articleTitle: Improved ADRC Based Speed Control for Dynamic Performance Improvement of Micro-Turbine System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The micro-turbine (MT) system plays an important role in the gas-electricity combined system. For an isolated gas-electricity combined system, effective speed-tracking control is critical for a stable power supply. This study employs a linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) technique to achieve precise speed-tracking for the MT system with a permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG). Beginning with looking into the MT system's internal structure, the mathematical model of the speed control loop is derived. A third-order extended state observer (ESO) is established to manage lumped model disturbances. Leveraging the ESO, the proposed LADRC-based speed controller facilitates accurate speed tracking. Recognizing the limited observer bandwidth in extensive time-lag systems, an enhanced version of the regular ESO is introduced, leading to an improved LADRC with a smaller control input gain, bigger bandwidth, and enhanced disturbance rejection capabilities for speed control. Simulation results demonstrate the improved control performance of the LADRC-based speed controller for the MT system.

articleTitle: Research on Condition Assessment Methods of In-Service 110kV and 220kV XLPE Cables
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: XLPE cables have been operational for decades within urban transmission and distribution networks. Influenced by various stresses in the underground environment, the insulation performance of these cables has significantly deteriorated, resulting in increased accidents. Therefore, it is necessary to assess the condition of operating high-voltage XLPE cables. This study focuses on 13 high-voltage XLPE cables with different operating periods. Fourier transform infrared spectroscopy, differential scanning calorimetry, X-ray diffraction, broadband dielectric spectroscopy, AC breakdown test, and tensile test were used to analyze the changes in electrical characteristics, physicochemical properties, and mechanical performance of the cables. Additionally, the dependency of each performance parameter on the aging state was evaluated. Finally, parameters such as melting temperature, elongation at break, relative permittivity, breakdown field strength, and Gibbs free energy were selected as input variables to establish a cable condition assessment method based on fuzzy diagnosis. The accuracy of this method was confirmed through case studies.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Transformer Explosion in the Offshore Platform Based on FLACS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The offshore platform power transformer is an important hub equipment in the power system. Once the explosion failure occurs, it will seriously affect the normal production and operation of the platform and cause significant economic losses. Therefore, it is very important to ensure the safe and reliable operation of the offshore platform transformer. This paper takes a new central platform as an example, by conducting the explosion numerical simulation analysis of the high-voltage oil-immersed transformer set on the platform, using FLACS software to 3D model the joint platform, and analyzed the whole process of transformer primary explosion and secondary explosion. According to the calculation results, the maximum over-voltage of the indoor room is 0.73bar, and the maximum over-voltage of the transformer door is 0.71bar, which will have a certain impact on the production facilities of the platform. In order to reduce the explosion over-pressure in the transformer room, this paper optimizes the original design scheme and adds an explosion relief area in the transformer room, The numerical simulation analysis shows that after adding an explosion relief, the room explosion over-pressure is significantly improved and reduced to 0.148 bar. To further improve the overall safety performance of the offshore platform, the transformer rooms are designed with the anti-explosion load of 0.15bar. which greatly reduces the impact of explosion over-pressure on the surrounding oil and gas facilities.

articleTitle: Integrated Energy System Planning and Optimization Configuration for a Park in Shandong Province
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Developing wind and solar new energy resources and constructing an integrated energy system align with the country's industrial policies and sustainable development strategies. However, the current integrated energy planning overlooks the optimization of energy storage systems, resulting in low utilization rates and the wastage of wind and solar energy. This paper, in response to the requirements of the investor, outlines a plan for the integrated energy system. The cost-benefit analysis indicates that establishing a wind-solar storage integrated energy system can effectively reduce electricity expenses and enhance enterprise profits. Additionally, the paper provides a configuration plan for the integrated energy system, aiming to further increase the utilization of new energy and improve the return on investment.

articleTitle: Adaptive Model Predictive Control Using Artificial Neural Network for Power Converters Under Parameter Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: There has been an increasing interest in using model predictive control (MPC) for power electronic applications. However, the demand of accurate system model and the common issue of inevitable system parameter uncertainties hinders the practical adoption of this highly promising control technique. In this paper, a new adaptive MPC using an artificial neural network (termed ANN-AMPC) is proposed to overcome these barriers. A power converter with a supervisor MPC controller is first designed and operated using matched model parameters. An ANN is then built and trained offline using the operating data of the supervisor MPC controller. In addition to the input components of the supervisor MPC, its previous output control signals are also added to the input vector of ANN. Next, an actual FPGA-based adaptive MPC controller is designed using the trained ANN to control the actual operation of power converter in real time. The trained ANN-AMPC can adaptively track the variation of system parameters and achieve the optimal control performance without extra identification part of system parameters. The basic concept, ANN structure, off-line training method, and online operation of ANN-MPC are described in detail. The dynamic response of the ANN-AMPC and conventional MPC under step changes in load parameters are analyzed and compared. The ANN-AMPC concept is validated by both simulation and experimental results on a kW-class 3-phase voltage source inverter (VSI) as the case study. It is demonstrated that the FPGA-based ANN-AMPC controller offers better dynamic performance in the presence of uncertain parameters while utilizes reduced FPGA resource requirement compared with the observer based MPC controller.

articleTitle: Design and Primary-Side Control of Wireless Power Transfer Device for Brushless Excitation of High-Speed Flywheel Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper analyzes the design method and control strategy of the inductive power transfer (IPT) based brushless excitation system for flywheel electrical excited synchronous machines. Both advantages and disadvantages of multiple compensation network topologies for the IPT system are discussed, and the electrical parameters of the coupler are designed based on efficiency and robustness principles. For the specific application of non-contact power supply to rotating components, a method for estimating field current based on primary-side information is proposed, and a double closed-loop current control algorithm based on current prediction control and reduced-order linearized dynamic model is designed. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Incremental Iterative Mapping Mechanism and Self-Consistent Evolutions in the Dynamic Process of Grid-Connected Converter System with LC Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The power system is gradually becoming electronic. At the same time, the oscillation problem of unknown mechanism in the system is frequent, the oscillation frequency coverage is wide and the oscillation hazard is large, so it is urgent to understand the dynamic process of power electronic power system. Whether it is a traditional power system dominated by synchronous devices or a new power system with power electronic devices as an important component, the basic operation goal of the system is still to maintain the stability of voltage amplitude/frequency and the stable transmission of power, so the role of the device is to adjust the internal voltage amplitude/frequency according to the unbalanced active/reactive current, and the role of the network is to readjust the active/reactive current at each device port when the internal voltage amplitude/frequency changes. In this paper, an incremental iterative mapping mechanism based on the internal voltage amplitude/frequency and the active/reactive current is proposed to describe the dynamic process of the grid-connected AC system of the converter, and the self-consistent evolution of the relevant electrical quantity with a complex exponential function is clarified when the increments are small, and then the relationship between the device and the network based on the active/reactive current increments and the internal voltage amplitude/frequency increments is deduced, and finally the possibility of linearization of this relationship is discussed.

articleTitle: Optimization Configuration of Edge Containers in Digitalized Substations in Intelligent Auxiliary Equipment through Multi-Service Collaboration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Addressing the challenges associated with information linkage in intelligent auxiliary equipment within digital substations, this study presents a sophisticated approach to optimize edge container resources through multi-service collaboration. Initially, we establish precise functional relationships among audio, text, video, DLT860 message data, and the parameters governing the interconnection of auxiliary devices. Based on Leveraging Kubernetes and a heterogeneous network architecture, we meticulously define the configuration parameters for container instances within the substation's edge computing platform. Subsequently, constraints related to real-time performance, uniqueness, and scope are formulated. These constraints are strategically designed to optimize security and reliability in the context of multi-service collaboration, while simultaneously minimizing the overall cost of container configuration. Finally, the effectiveness of this approach is validated through simulation results, confirming its capability to enhance the performance of the edge computing platform, meet the diverse demands of various business processes, and concurrently reduc container configuration expenses.

articleTitle: Power System Dominant Instability Mode Identification Based on Improved Multi-Head Attention and CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Ensuring the regular operation of the power grid and maintaining energy supply relies on the transient stability of the power system. Formulating emergency control strategies requires identifying the system's dominant instability mode. This paper introduces a method for rapid and accurate identification of the dominant instability mode, employing an improved multi-head attention mechanism and convolutional neural network (CNN). Constructing a characteristic matrix reflecting the power system's operation state is the first step, followed by building a deep neural network that combines the improved multi-head attention mechanism and CNN. CNN can extract the feature information of transient electrical quantities with the most significant correlation with the dominant instability mode. Combined with the multi-head attention mechanism, it focuses on the critical information in different positions and different characterization subspaces of the input data, learns the global features in electrical quantities, and introduces the deep residual network structure to capture long-term dependencies. The weighted cross entropy loss function enhances the training effectiveness with unbalanced samples. Subsequently, the proposed method undergoes analysis using a modified IEEE-39 node test system example. The obtained results confirm the accuracy, effectiveness, and interpretability of the method in identifying the dominant instability mode of the power system.

articleTitle: Study on Construction Methods and Electrical Properties of Super Electrical Insulating Materials With Nanopores
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The breakdown field strength and dielectric loss are the most important indexes to evaluate insulating materials. In the past two decades, the electrical properties of materials have been significantly improved by the nano-doping technique, which has been achieved milestone achievements. However, the challenge such as nanoparticles agglomeration and interface control have restricted the industrial application of nanocomposite dielectrics. It is theoretically suggested that the breakdown field strength of dielectric samples can be significantly improved by constructing nanopore structures, based on it, we designed and fabricated two kinds of insulating materials with extremely high electrical performance, that is, siloxane-based nanoporous polymer insulating material (SNPIM) and polysiloxane biocomposite insulating material (PBIM). The characteristics of pore structures and electrical performances (breakdown field strength, permittivity, and dielectric loss) were obtained, and the influence of pore structures characteristics on electrical performances was analyzed. The results indicate that the breakdown field strength of SNPIM and PBIM in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${{S}_6}$</tex> are much higher than that of industrial ceramic fiber insulating papers (ICFIP), and the corresponding increase percentage is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$261.51{{\% }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$325.47{{\% }}$</tex>, respectively. Besides, both SNPIM and PBIM have excellent dielectric performances whose permittivity is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$53.2{{\% }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$57.6{{\% }}$</tex> lower than that of ICFIP, and the corresponding decrease percentage of Tan <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\delta$</tex> were <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$76.2{{\% }}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$73.8{{\% }}$</tex>, respectively.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy for Distributed Grid-Forming Energy Storage Considering Multi-Security Operation Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Regarding the dynamic response and active support ability needs of the new power system for distributed energy storage, a coordinated control strategy for distributed grid-forming energy storage considering multi-security operation constraints is proposed. Firstly, it is revealed that the power allocation of distributed grid-forming energy storage is inversely proportional to both the droop coefficient and line impedance. By introducing fuzzy control, the droop coefficient can adaptively change within a reasonable range according to the frequency deviation, energy storage SOC, and frequency dead band, achieving balanced active power allocation of distributed grid-forming energy storage and stable frequency regulation of power systems. Finally, the overload capacity of the proposed control strategy is verified.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Graph Completion Method for the Power Transformer Based on Graph Neural Network and TransR
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With a high proportion of new energy access in the power grid, the risks and the latent dangers of the operation of the power equipment increase. At present, the prediction of the latent failure of the power equipment largely depends on the experience and the expertise of the maintenance personnel. A completed construction of the knowledge graph for the power equipment provides a more objective way for the maintenance personnel to make a more accurate judgment and decision. In order to further mine the hidden knowledge in the knowledge graph of the power equipment and improve the integrity of the knowledge graph of the power equipment, a dynamic completing method for the knowledge graph of the power transformer maintenance based on Learning Entity and Relation Embeddings for Knowledge Graph Completion (TransR) and graph neural network is presented. A graph neural network is designed for the graph embedding of the triples and obtaining the representation ability of the out-graph entities from the triples. The external knowledge triples were scored by the TransR scoring algorithm, which determines whether a new triplet is added to the knowledge map or not. The testing results show that the proposed method has a better effect on the completion and the extension of the knowledge graph.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimal Planning of Coal-Fired Plants Flexibility Retrofits Considering Multi-Technology Options
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Retrofitting coal-fired power plants (CPPs) is a way to accommodate ever-increasing variable renewable energy (VRE) in coal-dominated power systems in countries like China and India. Yet, how to retrofit the CPPS cost-effectively is an important issue to address. This paper proposes a multi-objective two-stage planning approach based on the none-dominated sorting genetic algorithm II (NSGA II). It considers both economic and flexibility requirements for the power system. At the planning stage, optimal technical options considering investment constraints and technical constraints are generated. At the operation stage, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) based model considering the detailed start-up and shut-down processes of the CPP is established. Then the optimal solution is selected from the Pareto solution set using the Technique for Order Preference by Similarity to an Ideal Solution (TOPSIS). Finally, case studies demonstrate the proposed approaches and show the potential of retrofitting CPPs to enhance power system flexibility.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of V2G Microgrids with Pumped Storage and Uncertain Wind Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper introduces a novel optimization model for a V2G microgrid, effectively integrating pumped-storage and fluctuating wind energy. The study delves into a two-tiered framework, where the upper level harnesses Particle Swarm Optimization to streamline load variance and user charging expenditures. With emphasize on comprehensive load management, it addresses critical challenges like peak-to-valley disparities and enhances cost-efficiency. Concurrently, the lower level strategically fulfills diverse energy demands, focusing on economical resource allocation to curtail the microgrid's operating expenses. The model adeptly navigates wind power's unpredictability and hydropower spillage risks, through employing EPNS and EPC indexes for risk assessment and economic impact minimization.

articleTitle: A Capacity Optimized LC-Filter CHB STATCOM and Its Control Method for the Unbalanced Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Cascaded H-bridge static synchronous compensator (STATCOM) with delta-connected configuration is an effective solution to compensate reactive current and negative-sequence current. In this paper, a capacity optimized LC-filter CHB STATCOM and its comprehensive control method are proposed. Firstly, operating principle of CHB STATCOM for unbalanced compensation is introduced. On this basis, the working modes of L-filter STATCOM and LC-filter STATCOMs are derived according to the vector analysis. At the same time, the mathematical models of three kinds of STATCOMs are carried out to quantitatively analyze the voltage stress. Comparison results demonstrate that proposed LC-filer CHB STATCOM has advantages of lower DC-link voltage and rated power. In order to eliminate the DC component of phase-cluster power in unbalanced compensation stage, two methods of circulating current injection are proposed and the analytical expressions of circulating currents are derived. Moreover, the comprehensive control methods for LC-filter CHB STATCOM are proposed, where AC or DC circulating current can be adopted and controlled for cluster voltage balance for negative-sequence compensation. Finally, the results of experiment effectively verify the proposed structure and control method.

articleTitle: Design and Research of a 10 kV Dynamic Voltage Restorer based on Cascaded H-Bridge and Supercapacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Voltage sag has become one of the key power quality problems for sensitive loads. To cope with high voltage level and large capacity demand for 10kV voltage sag mitigation schemes, this paper proposes and studies in detail a 10kV hybrid Dynamic Voltage Restorer (DVR) based on back-to-back cascaded H-bridge converter with supercapacitors as energy storage elements. The optimization on topology makes it suitable for sag compensation scenario. The optimized design of injection power coordination control enlarges DVR compensation range by rationally manage the rectifiers' power absorption from grid and supercapacitors' discharging. The design of redundant operation control contributes to a flexible operation and back-up redundancy for converter submodules. The simulation result based on PLECS environment together with a down-scaled experimental prototype have verified the correctness and effectiveness of proposed control schemes, the comparison among parallel energy storage scheme, series DVR scheme and proposed scheme proves the advantages of larger compensation range, better grid adaptability and less energy storage consumption.

articleTitle: Research on Energy and Efficiency Drop Issue of Underwater Wireless Power Transfer Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Underwater wireless power transfer (UWPT) technology provides a feasible way to solve the problems of poor safety, low lifespan, and complex maintenance of the traditional plug-and-play charging method for unmanned underwater equipment because it can realize energy supply in the sea through non-electrical contact. However, the UWPT system faces more challenges than land-based wireless power transfer (WPT) due to the complex marine environment. Currently, UWPT systems based on magnetically coupled resonance technology suffer significant power and efficiency drops in real project applications compared to air environments. Although it is believed to be due to the difference in electrical parameters between the marine environment and air, few studies have analyzed and investigated the mechanism of this problem. In this paper, the additional eddy current loss and resonance drift problems that affect the energy efficiency of UWPT systems are investigated and analyzed. Furthermore, the design method of UWPT frequency optimization and the on-line and off-line compensation correction methods of system topology are proposed. Finally, the influence mechanism of the seawater medium and the correction effect of the design method are verified by experiments. Prominently, the proposed pre-compensation methods and calibration ideas are conducive to advancing the energy efficiency improvement, reliability, and commercialization and engineering progress of UWPT technology.

articleTitle: Research on the Preprocessing Method of Switchgear Operation Data Based on Clustering Algorithm*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Considering the high requirements for the safety of switchgear equipment and the extremely large amount of data in the process of equipment condition monitoring, a preprocessing method based on K-means clustering of switchgear equipment operation data is proposed. The method firstly selects evaluation parameters from multiple fault problem aspects to ensure the reliability of condition monitoring; then it considers the characteristics of different data volumes, quantifies the non-data volume information, and forms a unified data format; finally, it concentrates the massive operation data through K-means clustering algorithm. Using this method to analyze the switchgear operation data of a city in North China, an accuracy index is introduced to evaluate the performance of the algorithm in the clustering task, and the experimental results show that the method can realize the normalization and effective compression of switchgear equipment operation data.

articleTitle: Teaching Learning Based Optimization Algorithm for Fault Recovery of Distribution Network with Distributed Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the application of Distributed Generation (DG), more and more DGs have been connected to the Distributed Network (DN) in recent years. As a result, the traditional DN has turned into an active one, and its topology and operation mode have been changed. Extreme events often cause power outages, which brings great challenges to the problem of system failure recovery. In this paper, a two-stage fault recovery strategy of distribution network with distributed generation is proposed by using teaching learning based optimization algorithm. Specifically, in the first stage, the faulted distribution network is divided into several islands with breadth-first search first and then depth-first search. In the second stage, teaching learning based optimization algorithm is utilized to solve the optimization problem of fault recovery for distribution network with distributed generation. To evaluate the proposed approach, the IEEE33-node distribution network is used for case study. The experimental results show that the proposed fault recovery strategy can derive the optimal solution for distribution network fault recovery while meeting the load of user demand and guaranteeing the uninterrupted power supply to essential loads, which verifies the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: A Systematic Review of Causal Analysis in Power Systems: Principles, Application, and Prospects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Causal relationships are a scientific research method used to describe relationships between variable data, allowing for the excavation of the deep logic and operational mechanisms behind phenomena. The integration of causal relationships as a means of data analysis in the field of power systems improves the accuracy and efficiency of power systems analysis and operation. This paper presents the definition and origin of causal relationships and the principles of main causal analysis models. It overviews the application of causal relationships in power systems fault diagnosis, energy prediction, stability analysis, and the electricity market. Finally, it looks forward to the development prospects of causal relationships in combination with power physics models and artificial intelligence, promoting the construction of a reliable and intelligent new power systems under the penetration of renewable sources.

articleTitle: An Inverse Study of Transient Response of a No-Insulation Coil with AC Currents Based on Simplified Equivalent Circuit Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the ability to bypass current, no-insultation (NI) superconducting coils can tolerate small over-critical currents, local defects and hotspots, which improves its stability and simplifies quench protection system. To describe the overall behaviors of the NI coils, inductance, variable resistance of superconductors, and characteristic resistance are the three necessary parameters. In general, the variable resistance of superconductors is neglected when the supplied current is below critical current. Besides, the inductance and characteristic resistance are regarded as constants during the transient process, for instance, charge and sudden discharge process. However, many tests have demonstrated that the time constant which is only related to characteristic resistance and inductance changes with different ramping rates or frequencies of AC currents, or even amplitude of current can affect its values. In order to better analyze the transient response of the NI coils, and to figure out how and why the abovementioned three parameters change with frequency, a NI coil was tested under DC biased AC currents with frequency range of 0.5 Hz-200 Hz. An inverse calculation of these parameters based on the simplified equivalent circuit model from the measured center magnetic field, terminal voltage and supplied current is carried out. Two widely used simulation models, a more complicated circuit model meshing with radial and azimuthal elements and a finite element model with rotated anisotropic resistivity, are employed to validate the inverse calculation and to investigate the current density distribution or current distribution in turn level. It is found that the variable resistance of superconductors under AC conditions are non-neglectable, and it increases with frequency. Moreover, the inductance and characteristic resistance are not constant with AC currents and change with frequency.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of a New Type of Polymer-Magnet Permanent Magnet Fault-Tolerant Vernier Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This study focuses on the Spoke Array Fault-Tolerant Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine (SAFTPMVM) which, due to its magnetic concentration effect, has a high torque density. However, an increase in air gap length significantly affects this magnetic concentration, thereby drastically reducing the motor's torque density. To address this issue, a new structure called the Fault-Tolerant Concentrated Flux Permanent Magnet Vernier Machine (FCFTPMVM) is proposed. This structure enhances the fundamental and low-order harmonic of the air gap magnetic density, thus increasing torque density without additional permanent magnet material. The principle of torque enhancement was analyzed using the equivalent magnetic circuit method, and the impact of structural parameters on torque performance was studied using finite element methods. This led to the design of optimal motor structural parameters. A comparative analysis of the electromagnetic performance of surface-mounted, spoke array, and the new concentrated flux structure motors was conducted using finite element analysis. The results demonstrate that the proposed FCFTPMVM motor exhibits high output torque, low torque ripple, high efficiency, and strong fault tolerance capabilities.

articleTitle: Discussion of Domestic VPP Development Trend and Comparison of Domestic and Foreign VPP Development Models and Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The transition of virtual power plant (VPP) from being a technical term to becoming a hot trend in policy, business, and energy industries has rapidly evolved in recent years. VPP has become highly important to build clean, low-carbon, safe, and efficient modern energy systems. Due to the lack of sufficient guidance regarding VPP in China, this paper investigates the development trend, development models and characteristics of VPP from the Chinese perspective. The development trend of domestic VPP is further depicted based on three dimensions of VPP: three generations, three stages, and the overall situation. Based on that, through the vertical and horizontal depth comparison of VPP characteristics at home and abroad, it is concluded that the domestic VPP model is similar to the European and American models in terms of energy structure and market mechanism. This comprehensive research and analysis provide significant guidance for the rational and convenient rapid development and commercial application of domestic VPP.

articleTitle: Study on State of Health of Power Battery Prediction Using Denoising Autoencoder and Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The capacity of a power battery gradually decreases with long-term use and is reflected by the state of health. Accurately predicting the state of health of a power battery is critical to ensuring reliability in battery use. To improve the accuracy of state of health prediction for power batteries, a hybrid model is proposed in this paper to cope with the effects of noise and nonlinear degradation in the data on state of health prediction. Firstly, feature learning and extraction of the power battery data are performed using a denoising auto encoder, which is able to extract key information and capture variations over time from the data. Subsequently, the extracted features were modeled using a bidirectional long short-term memory network to capture complex patterns and nonlinear dependencies. The model proposed in this paper has been tested and validated on a public dataset, and the experimental results show that none of the evaluation metrics exceed the 3% error range, which aligns with the accuracy requirements of the battery health state prediction task. Therefore, it is verified that the model proposed in this paper can effectively improve the accuracy of the state of health prediction of power batteries.

articleTitle: Efficient anomaly intrusion detection using Transformer based GAN network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid development of power grid terminals technology and the continuous increase in threats of network attacks, network anomaly intrusion detection for power grid terminals has become more complicated and crucial. However, due to the large number of network protocol fields and diverse network behaviors, existing methods still face challenges. Therefore, this text proposed a network anomaly intrusion detection method based on TransGAN, which combines the ideas of generative adversarial networks and Transformer models, to learn the correlation between different types of network intrusion behaviors and capture the dependency relationship of the network data. Besides, XGBoost was utilized for feature extraction to reduce computational cost without compromising detection performance. The experimental results show that the proposed anomaly detection method achieved an accuracy of 84.64<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> on NSL-KDD, while reducing the computational cost of training and testing by 9% and 6% respectively. It makes a valuable contribution to the research and practice of network security in the field of power grid terminals.

articleTitle: Overview of Photovoltaic Power Forecasting Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Guided by the dual-carbon target policy, China's photovoltaic penetration rate has experienced a consistent upward trend, integrating a growing amount of photovoltaic energy into the power grid. Nevertheless, the intermittent and unpredictable nature of photovoltaic generation poses significant challenges to grid stability. To ensure optimal unit commitment and economic scheduling, accurate solar power forecasting has become a crucial task. Currently, numerous domestic and foreign research institutions, companies, and other entities are actively exploring photovoltaic power generation forecasting. This paper presents a comprehensive review of power forecasting, focusing on generation-related effects, forecasting methods, and evaluation criteria. Initially, we introduce the principles of photovoltaic generation and the influencing factors that affect it. Subsequently, we summarize several widely used forecasting methods and discuss the innovative aspects of each. Furthermore, we compile commonly employed accuracy evaluation criteria. Finally, drawing upon relevant research findings and considering future trends, we offer insights into potential directions for overcoming current challenges in photovoltaic power prediction.

articleTitle: Controllable fractal modelling method based on soil statistical parameters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Internal structure of soil is disorder and with statistical self-similar fractal attribution. How to construct its micro-structure model is very important for the study of electrical properties, thermal properties and hydrodynamics. So, this paper presents a controllable modelling method for soil. This paper firstly introduces the development process from the classical soil fractal model (Sierpinski carpet model) to randomized Sierpinski carpet model, and analyses the difference between the latter and actual soil. A Lower-weighted Non-uniform Iterative Fractal (LNIF) method is proposed to reduce the influence weight of first fractal by introducing Initial Scale Reduction Factor(ISRF). X<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> test is used to verify that the porosity of soil model established by LNIF method conforms to normal distribution regularity when ISRF is large enough. Furthermore, this paper studies the control strategy of model parameters aimed to make LNIF model closer to measured parameters in actual soil. The numerical relationship between soil solid particle size, porosity and its deviation range and LNIF model input parameters is established. Then the paper proposes a fractal modelling strategy based on actual soil structural parameters, and presents a Controllable Fractal Modelling(CFM) method based on soil statistical parameters. This method can not only make soil model porosity conform to the statistical regularity of normal distribution, but also take the distribution of soil particle size, the average and error range of measured porosity as control variables to realize the control of solid particle size and porosity in the model, which leads to the established soil microstructure model have the same statistical regularity as the actual soil. Finally, this paper presents the specific operation process taking the Leached Cinnamon soil as an example.

articleTitle: Microgrid Protection Criterion Based on Positive Sequence Component of Fault Current*
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: According to China's grid connection standard, the access of doubly-fed wind turbines of small and medium capacity causes the topology and operation mode of the distribution network, and the complexity and variability of the current level and direction of flow, which brings great challenges to the protection of microgrids. In this paper, based on the low-voltage ride-through operation characteristics of DFIG, the distribution characteristics of the positive sequence component of fault current in microgrids with doubly-fed turbines are analyzed in depth, and a longitudinal protection principle for microgrids based on the positive sequence component of fault current is proposed. This principle not only reduces the requirement of longitudinal protection on the data synchronization of communication equipment by using fault component amplitude transmission, but also eliminates the influence of load current and improves the action characteristics of protection. Finally, simulation is carried out by MATLAB/Simulink to verify the feasibility of the proposed protection principle.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Traffic Flow-Based Simulation Method for Charging Demands of EVs Considering Various Uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the large-scale application of electric vehicles (EVs), the stable operation of power grid is significantly affected by the increasing of uneven charging demand distribution. Considering the real-world traffic conditions under time-varying multiple uncertainties, this paper proposes a dynamic traffic flow charging load simulation method to analyze the variable charging demands. First, the characteristics of multiple uncertainties are depicted by the probability models, including the link capacity, travel demand and EV operation states. Then, the dynamic traffic flow assignment problem under multiple uncertainties is established by considering the congestion effect of EVs. The optimal path generation model is used to construct the available path sets. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by the simulation results in case studies.

articleTitle: Molecular Simulation Analysis of the Influence of Resin Matrix on the Properties of Composite Foam
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Epoxy composite foams, as a lightweight and highly insulating composite material, have been widely used in insulation filling of electrical equipment. This paper uses 2021P alicyclic epoxy resin to co-blend to change the performance of DGEBA, methyl hexahydrophthalic anhydride (MHHPA) as curing agent, the mixed epoxy resin and the curing agent MHHP A cross-linked with DGEBA and 2021P in four different ratios to form the epoxy resin system was studied. PMMA was selected as the organic microsphere. An amorphous hybrid model of DGEBA/2021P and MHHP A monomer molecules was built in the module of Materials Studio, and the program of automatic cross-linking reaction and annealing written was imported. The models were automatically cross-linked and annealed to generate the models after the reaction between epoxy resin and curing agent, and the cross-linking degree of all four models was above 85%. The four cross-linked epoxy resin models were merged with the same organic microsphere, and the structure of the model was analyzed. The mechanical and thermal properties of the two-layer model of epoxy resin and organic micro spheres were analyzed and calculated by molecular dynamics simulation. Research shows the glass transition temperature of the original resin system increases to 373 K when 10% of 2021P is added, but further increasing the content of 2021P, the glass transition temperature of the material decreases and is lower than that of the model without the addition of 2021P. The bulk modulus, Young's modulus and shear modulus of the system with 30%2021P are the highest.

articleTitle: Assessment of the Renewable Energy Accommodation Capability of the Power Distribution Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Against the backdrop of China's ambitious goals to achieve carbon peak and carbon neutrality, the construction of the energy internet is advancing steadily. Concurrently, the pace of substituting electricity for other forms of energy consumption is accelerating. In this evolving power system, there is a significant deployment of facilities such as electric vehicles and energy storage, alongside the continual emergence of comprehensive energy service providers. Moreover, the market entities involved in the distribution and sale of electricity are rapidly diversifying. Set against this comprehensive background, this article delineates the operational characteristics of distributed energy resources and establishes a model for distributed power generation. This model is based on the aggregation and interaction of multiple distributed energy resources. It proposes evaluation metrics and methodologies for assessing the carrying capacity of distributed power sources. Further, it analyzes the capacity and optimal locations for integrating distributed power sources. The article also puts forward management and operational strategies for distributed power sources, aimed at promoting their development. This is with the objective of achieving cost reductions and efficiency enhancements within the power system.

articleTitle: Multi-level Optimization and Scheduling Strategy for Power Grid Considering Adjustable Resource Participation in Real-time Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The access of a large amount of adjustable resources to the power grid for participation in dispatching has promoted the transformation of the traditional ‘source-following load’ mode to a collaborative ‘source-load interaction’ mode. A multi-level optimization scheduling strategy for power grids considering the participation of adjustable resources in real-time regulation is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the adjustment characteristics of different types of adjustable resources are analyzed, and based on historical output data, the output situation of various resources during different time periods of the day is predicted. Then, a dispatching model is constructed with the goal of minimizing the comprehensive operating cost of the system, and the scenario-based stochastic programming (SSP) method is used to obtain the day-ahead dispatching plan. Secondly, based on the day-ahead dispatching plan, the intraday optimization is carried out with the goal of minimizing the dispatching cost. The Niche Chaotic Particle Swarm Optimization (NCPSO) algorithm is used to solve the multi- objective optimization problem, and the intra-day dispatching plan is obtained. Based on the day-ahead and intra-day dispatching plans, the demand for real-time regulation of the power grid is considered, and a model is established with the goal of minimizing the deviation between the dispatchable amount and the dispatching demand. The Model Predictive Control (MPC) is used to formulate the real-time optimization dispatching strategy for adjustable resources. Finally, the feasibility of the method proposed in this article is verified through case analysis.

articleTitle: Low-Carbon Economic Dispatch of Power System with Wind Power Considering Dual Demand Response and Ladder-Type Carbon Trading Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Low-carbon, clean, efficient and energy-saving is the development trend of the power industry. Building a new power system with new energy as the main body, developing a carbon trading market, and giving full play to the scheduling potential of user-side resources are important measures to achieve low-carbon and safe operation of the system. Therefore, the paper proposes a system low-carbon economic dispatch model considering demand response and carbon trading mechanism. Firstly, the price-based demand response and incentive-based demand response models are established based on the user-side load characteristics under different driving modes. Secondly, the baseline method is used to allocate carbon quotas to the system, and the ladder-type carbon trading mechanism is proposed to construct a carbon transaction cost model to control the carbon emissions of the system. Finally, based on the dual demand response model and the carbon transaction cost model, an optimization model is established to minimize the sum of coal consumption cost and start-stop cost of thermal power units, operation and maintenance cost of wind turbines, carbon transaction cost, compensation cost of incentive demand response, wind curtailment and load loss cost, and the Cplex solver is used to solve the model. The results show that the proposed model can effectively reduce the cost and carbon emissions of the system while taking into account the low carbon and economy of the system.

articleTitle: Comparative Evaluation of 10 kV SiC MOSFET Power Module Insulation Ability Through Chip Neighborhood Range Electric Field Modelling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Insulation failure is the primary problem of medium-voltage (MV) silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET power modules restricting the advanced performances of SiC chips, which is induced by the electric field concentration caused by both the packaging and SiC chips. This paper establishes the insulation ability comparative evaluation of 10 kV SiC MOSFET power module through proposed chip neighborhood range (CNR) electric field model based on technology computer-aided designer (TCAD), where the model is defined and calibrated as prerequisite. The influence of chip and packaging structure variation on the electric field distortion on the insulation weak point at the interface between chip and encapsulation material as well as the insulation enhancement method are comparatively evaluated, demonstrating that bonding wires will significantly weaken the insulation ability regardless of protection. Three types of 10 kV half-bridge SiC power modules are fabricated and partial discharge test is carried out to effectively verify the evaluation results, showing that apparent charge of module with ten bonding wires of 20.7 pC is much larger than that with four bonding wires of only 1.2 pC.

articleTitle: A Quick Sensorless Startup Method for Ultra-High-Speed PMSM Using Predictive Current Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Sensorless control is indispensable for ultra-high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor due to installation issues. And the startup process must be finished as quick as possible in consideration of useful life of air bearings. A predictive current model based position observer is proposed in this paper to give accurate estimation results at low speed and realize quick startup of ultra-high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor. The proposed method utilizes the current model in the estimated rotating reference frame to obtain the position estimation error, which is later sent to an extended state observer to acquire accurate estimation results of electrical speed and position. With the help of additional position pre-locating and inverter nonlinearity compensation, the proposed predictive current model based startup method can realize quick startup from standstill to 30000 rpm within 1 second. Furthermore, the proposed position observer is quite efficient and takes less than half execution time of traditional observers in embedded developing. An experimental platform is built to validate the properties of the method. And experimental results show that performance of the proposed observer is desirable at low speed and can realize quick and reliable startup of ultra-high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor.

articleTitle: Voltage Coordinated Control Strategy for Distribution Network With Controllable Devices Based on Different Time Response Scales
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In response to the current challenges of high penetration of renewable energy and excessive complexity of loads, this paper proposes an effective coordinated control strategy by integrating controllable devices with different time response scales in low-voltage distribution networks. Firstly, the controllable voltage regulation devices with different response time scales are analyzed. Then, a coordinated control strategy for multiple controllable voltage regulation devices is presented. Finally, MATLAB/SIMULINK is used to simulate and validate the proposed strategy in both an improved IEEE 33-node system and a practical low-voltage distribution system in a city in Zhejiang Province. In the improved IEEE 33-node system, the voltage deviation is reduced to 3%, and the voltage deviation improvement reaches 95.07%. In the practical low-voltage distribution system of the city in Zhejiang Province, the voltage deviation is reduced to 1.7%, and the voltage deviation improvement reaches 99.04%. These results effectively address the issues of voltage violations caused by renewable energy integration and the complexity of loads, providing assurance for the safe and stable operation of low-voltage distribution networks.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Single-Phase Current Source Inverter for Standalone Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, a single-phase current source inverter (CSI) is proposed for standalone applications, leveraging its intrinsic boost capability for a single-stage power conversion. While the existing literature reports a typical voltage gain of 3–4 times for the CSI, the upper limit of its voltage gain and the factors influencing it remain unexplored. In this article, the upper limit of the voltage gain and the factors affecting it are discussed and a mathematical model is presented to estimate the voltage gain of the CSI. To regulate the output voltage, a proportional-integral (PI) based feedback control system is proposed and performance of the CSI with the controller is discussed. The proposed single-stage system effectively tracks the reference voltage and simulation results demonstrate that the CSI can offer high voltage gain and can serve as a promising single-stage solution for standalone applications.

articleTitle: IGBT Fault Diagnosis Method Based on Information Gain and Least Squares Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This study proposes an IGBT fault diagnosis method based on Information Gain and Least Squares Support Vector Machine (LSSVM). Considering the significance of IGBTs in power systems and the severe consequences that their faults can cause, this paper employs Information Gain technology for feature selection to effectively extract fault characteristics. Moreover, an improved Chimpanzee Optimization Algorithm (ICOA) is introduced to optimize the parameters of the LSSVM model, aiming to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of fault diagnosis. Experimental results demonstrate that this method achieves a high accuracy rate and good generalization ability in IGBT fault diagnosis, verifying its practical value in enhancing the stability and reliability of power systems.

articleTitle: Optimization Method for Low-Carbon Economic Dispatch of Carbon Capture Power Plants Considering Market Power Constraint in Carbon Trading Market
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The phenomenon of market power abuse in carbon trading, leading to deviations in carbon quota prices from normal competitive levels, poses a significant challenge to the economic dispatch of carbon capture power plants. In response, this paper introduces a comprehensive market power assessment methodology tailored to the carbon market environment in China, encompassing pre-market, mid-market, and post-market phases. Furthermore, it proposes market power restraint measures based on the incentive compatibility principle. Comparative analysis is conducted to validate that the implementation of market power restraint can prevent the masking of true cost information, thereby enhancing the low-carbon operational efficiency of carbon capture power plants.

articleTitle: Design of Symmetrical Magnetic Integrated Filter with Balanced Flux Paths for the Grid-Connected Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Magnetic components such as inductors constitute a major proportion of the overall size and volume of grid-connected inverters. This paper presents an exploratory investigation into the magnetic integration of a three-phase LCL filter induction system, employing a Y-configured core that achieves equal magnetic flux pathways. Compared to using a conventional rectangular core, the proposed Y -shaped core configuration demonstrates a volumetric reduction of over 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for the three-phase inductors, while preserving the integrity of LCL filter functionality. The magnetic circuit analysis of the Y -shaped core is complemented by three-dimensional Finite Element Analysis (FEA) simulations to validate the theoretical calculations and reduced volumetric size. By enhancing the symmetry of magnetic flux distribution, this integrated inductor design significantly contributes to the miniaturization of three-phase grid-connected inverters without compromising their filtering performance.

articleTitle: Capacity Assessment of Distributed Generation in New Generation Distribution Networks Based on Different Load Levels
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the changing energy structure in our country, the rapid development of distributed generation (DG) represented by photovoltaic and wind power has become a trend, and large-scale integration into the distribution network is underway. However, if the scale of distributed generation integration exceeds the carrying capacity of the distribution network, it can lead to a series of problems, such as fluctuations in grid frequency and voltage, destabilizing the power system, and potentially causing equipment failures, outages, or power interruptions, thus deteriorating power quality. Therefore, in order to ensure the coordinated development of distributed generation, loads, and the power grid, it is necessary to determine the allowable capacity margin for distributed generation integration, providing guidance for the planning and construction of distributed generation systems and distribution networks. This study proposes a data-driven assessment method to determine the carrying capacity of distributed generation under different load levels. By considering various influencing indicators of carrying capacity and using data processing techniques such as the time probability distribution matrix, an improved entropy weighting method is employed to determine the key indicators. Based on the nature and context of different loads, the loads are classified into different levels, and based on the parameter limits of the loads, the thermal stability evaluation is conducted in the actual operating state and safety boundaries of the distribution network. By calculating the maximum injection of DG through reverse load factor and progressively reducing it in stages to meet the specified criteria, the carrying capacity of the distributed generation system is determined.

Author Keywords: Combination of subjective and objective weighting

articleTitle: Preventive Maintenance Strategy for Air Conditioning Systems Based on Health Index Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Constructing a health index (HI) that accurately describes the degradation process and accurately predicting the HI are two prerequisites for developing preventive maintenance (PM) strategy for air conditioning systems (ACS). Existing research primarily relies on single indicators when constructing the HI, which may fail to authentically reflect the system's health states. Moreover, an unreasonable HI can also render prediction model ineffective. To address the issue, this paper proposes a method that integrates multi-source data to construct and predict HI, which can help in conducting condition-based PM strategy. Specifically, a combination weighting method is employed to construct an HI using the set of monitoring parameters related to system condition, which provides a more reliable indicator for predicting health states. On this basis, the constructed HI is utilized as the label for the dataset, and long short-term memory (LSTM) neural networks are employed to predict the future HI of the system. Based on the predicted results of HI, corresponding maintenance measures are taken at different thresholds. The effectiveness of the proposed method is demonstrated through a practical example of ACS.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Evaluation Method for Pressure Pulsation of Variable Speed Pumped Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the case of a large number of intermittent new energy sources such as solar and wind energy being connected to the power grid for operation, pumped storage technology as a large capacity energy storage is the most economical means to solve the problem of peak shaving and frequency regulation in the power system. The doubly fed variable speed pumped storage unit has the characteristic of adjustable pumping power, and has more technical advantages in terms of unit performance and hydraulic characteristics. However, there are currently no operational doubly fed variable speed pumped storage units in China, and their hydraulic performance is not yet clear. This article constructs an evaluation method for pressure pulsation intensity of pumped storage units under variable speed operation, and explores whether it is possible to reduce pressure pulsation of pump turbines through variable speed operation. By evaluating the pressure pulsation of variable speed pumped storage units under different operating conditions and transition processes, the law of pressure pulsation can be studied, reasonable operating strategies can be formulated, and the restricted range of variable speed operation of the unit can be avoided.

articleTitle: Learning-Aided Adaptive Lyapunov Optimization for Wind Farm-Equipped Storage Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the growing integration of wind power into the energy supply, the grid's stability faces heightened challenges due to the unpredictable nature of wind energy. For the wind farms, additional electricity penalty costs will be charged because of the real-time discrepancies between the committed and actual supplied wind power. Equipping wind farms with energy storage systems can help alleviate these power discrepancies. However, implementing an optimal online storage control policy is practically challenging due to time-varying penalty costs and energy mismatches. To address this issue, we propose a storage control algorithm based on the Lyapunov optimization frame-work. To further improve the performance of the time-invariant Lyapunov function, we employ a deep neural network (DNN)-driven parameter-learning approach and design a novel time-adaptive Lyapunov optimization framework. Simulation results demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: A Novel Substrate-Baseplate Structure for Medium Voltage SiC MOSFET Device
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This study presents a novel substrate-baseplate structure tailored for medium-voltage SiC MOSFET devices. The proposed configuration combines an asymmetric DBC substrate with a metal baseplate featuring voids, creating a sealed cavity that achieves phase-change heat spreading. This innovative design significantly improves the thermal dissipation efficiency of the device while effectively reducing common-mode capacitance. Additionally, the application of a low CTE polyimide film on the substrate ensures compliance with the 10kV voltage rating. Simulation and experimental results robustly validate the exceptional electrothermal performance of the proposed structure. In comparison to conventional substrate-baseplate configurations under identical DBC upper copper traces, the proposed structure demonstrates a 56.41% reduction in common-mode capacitance and a 13-degree decrease in the maximum junction temperature at a single-chip heating power of 30W.

articleTitle: A Nonlinear Dynamic model for Giant Magneto-strictive Actuator Incorporating Temperature Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In giant magnetostrictive actuators (GMAs), giant magnetostrictive materials (GMMs) and permanent magnets would suffer from rising or fluctuating temperature. Temperature effects on the two materials are significant, indicating that dynamic behaviors of the GMA would be strongly affected. In this paper, a magneto-elastic system-level model is presented to characterize the dynamic behaviors of the GMA at distinct temperatures. Temperature effects on the magnetic field of the GMA, especially the reversible demagnetization of the permanent magnets in the presence of rising temperatures, are included in the proposed magnetic equivalent circuit (MEC), which comprehensively takes into account magnetic leakage, fringing effect, and eddy current effect. Combining the modified Jiles-Atherton model, a magnetoelastic model, and a single-degree-of-freedom dynamic model sensitive to the excitations, the variation of the GMA's dynamic performance as a function of temperature can be predicted. For validation, a finite element model is set up, and an experimental platform is established. Results from the simulations and experiments indicate that the proposed model can accurately characterize the magnetic field distribution and capture the dynamic behaviors of the GMA. With the temperature effects on the magnetic field and the hysteresis behaviors of the GMM included, accuracy of the proposed model is greatly improved.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Cascaded Transmission System Suitable for Large-scale New Energy Long-distance Island Transmission
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to meet the collection and long-distance transmission of large-scale wind power, photovoltaic and other new energy sources in Northwest China, this paper proposes a sending-end hybrid cascade transmission system suitable for stable transmission of large-scale wind power bases. Firstly, the topology and operation characteristics of the sending-end hybrid cascaded transmission system are introduced. This system has a double-layer structure. The high-voltage valve group adopts the grid commutation converter, and the low-voltage valve group adopts the modular multilevel converter, which can realize the access and stable delivery of large-scale wind power bases. Then, the coordinated control strategy of LCC and MMC is introduced, and a coordinated start-up strategy suitable for large-scale wind power base access is proposed. Aiming at the output fluctuation of wind power base, the maximum transmission power of LCC and MMC converters is analyzed respectively. And the adaptive distribution control strategy of valve group power is designed for the system to ensure the stable and reliable operation of the system. Finally, the simulation model of the sending-end hybrid cascaded transmission system is built in PSCAD / EMTDC to verify the effectiveness of the control strategy.

Author Keywords: adaptive power distribution of valve group

articleTitle: Multi-Time Scale Low-Carbon Economic Scheduling of Electric-Hydrogen Coupled Integrated Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the continuous advancement of China's carbon neutrality goal, low-carbon electricity will promote the development of a low-carbon economy in China. This paper proposes a multi-time scale low-carbon economic scheduling model of electric-hydrogen coupled integrated energy systems (EH-IESs). Firstly, the carbon trading mechanism is introduced to control the system's carbon emissions. Secondly, the operation strategy of hydrogen production, storage, usage, and the equipment with adjustable thermoelectric ratios are introduced to improve the energy utilization efficiency and low carbon levels. Finally, the spinning reserve market is considered to enhance the benefits of EH-IES. The simulation results show that the proposed multi-time scale low-carbon economic scheduling model of EH-IES can effectively reduce carbon emission and improve system economy, energy utilization efficiency, and renewable energy absorption capacity.

articleTitle: Maximum Power Point Tracking Control for Full-Speed Range Power Generation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Wind power generation systems operate long-term in environments with random fluctuations in wind speed, unknown input disturbances, and non-zero and unmatched uncertainties. In response to this operating condition, to enhance the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) performance of wind power generation systems, this paper first introduces the overall structure and generation principles of a brushless DC wind power generation system. It establishes a mathematical model for a back-to-back inverter. Secondly, it investigates the power control of a variable-speed variable-pitch brushless DC wind power generation system across the entire wind speed range. Addressing the issue of slow dynamic response in the low wind speed range when using traditional power feedback control, an improved power feedback method is proposed to accelerate the maximum power tracking speed and improve the overall power generation efficiency. To address the problem of the inability to achieve power control through pitch control in the high wind speed range for a variable-speed variable-pitch turbine, a mechanical power outer loop is introduced to reduce the turbine speed, enabling constant power control in the high wind speed range, simulation results validate that the proposed power control strategy across the entire wind speed range exhibits excellent performance in a brushless DC wind power generation system based on a back-to-back inverter structure.

articleTitle: Active Thermal Control of Dual Three-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Improved Bayerer's Lifetime Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors (DT-PMSMs) are widely used in transportation electrification because of simple structure, high power density, good fault tolerance and low torque ripple. However, power semiconductor devices within the motor drive circuits are among the most vulnerable and failure-prone components in the entire motor system. They play a crucial role in determining the redundancy and reliability of the motor system. To address this issue, this article elucidates the failure mechanisms of power semiconductors and proposes an active thermal control algorithm based on improved Bayerer's lifetime model, establishes a mathematical model for power compensation, and thoroughly analyzes it to obtain optimized current references. Theoretical analysis also ensures the enhancement of power semiconductor lifetime. Furthermore, this control strategy does not require iterative computations, ensuring high computational efficiency and validation on the laboratory DT-PMSM experimental platform. The control performance under various load conditions is discussed and tested. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed control algorithm can extend the overall lifetime of power semiconductors within the drive circuit, enabling active thermal control of DT-PMSM.

Author Keywords: Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors (DT-PMSMs)

articleTitle: Research on Closed-Loop Control of Single-Stage Hybrid Three-Level DAB Type Resonant AC-DC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to expand the application of single-stage isolated AC-DC converter and improve its current characteristics, a new topology with half-bridge three-level structure on the AC side is proposed, the working principle and steady-state characteristics of the converter are analyzed in detail based on the three-phase shift modulation strategy, the rms value of the minimum resonant current is realized through the relationship of the three phase-shifting angles. The converter reduces the voltage stress of the AC-side switch to half the AC voltage, helping to reduce power loss and cost. Furthermore, a closed-loop control strategy of grid-side current for proportional resonant complex odd-harmonic repetitive control is proposed., and the grid-side current fundamental component is realized by the proportional resonance controller to achieve static difference closed-loop control of the fundamental component of the grid-side., and the odd-order harmonics of the grid-side current caused by grid voltage harmonics are eliminated by the odd-harmonic repetitive controller. Detailed experimental results verify the correctness and feasibility of the proposed topology and closed-loop control strategy.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Energy Optimization Strategy for the Multi-Energy Microgrid with the Carbon Trading under the Step Price
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: It is promising to reduce carbon emission by incor-porating carbon trading into the multi-energy microgrid which can exploit the complementary advantages among various energies. Currently, most carbon trading uses the fixed price, limiting the prohibition effect on carbon emission. Introducing the step price can bring the indifferentiable characteristic of the cost function, which is difficult to solve. To address the issue, in this paper, an energy optimization strategy is proposed for the multi-energy microgrid based on the intelligent meta-heuristic algorithm. Firstly, the models of the electric, heat, gas devices, and energy converters are constructed. Then the energy optimization problem for multiple energies with the carbon trading under step price is formulated. Afterward, an improved grey wolf optimization algorithm with fast convergence is utilized to reduce the operation cost under the lowest carbon emission. The Simulations conducted on the real-world data verify the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Enhanced Thermal Conductivity and Insulation Properties of Mica Tape with BN-Coated Meyer Bar Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In high-voltage generator, mica tape is the most critical and main stator coil insulation material. The improvement of its thermal conductivity and insulation properties can extend the service life of the generator while improving the operational stability of the main insulation structure of the high-voltage generator. Consequently, improving the thermal conductivity and insulation properties of mica tapes has a decisive role in improving the reliability of the main insulation of high-voltage generator. In this paper, a Meyer bar coating method is used to uniformly coat boron nitride (BN) with high thermal conductivity and excellent insulation properties onto the mica tape surface using polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) as the binder. With the increase of BN content, the thermal conductivity and breakdown strength of mica tape are improved. At 25 °C, the out-of-plane thermal conductivity increased from 0.171 W/(m.K) to 0.265 W/(m.K) when the BN content reached 2 wt. %, an improvement of 55%, and the DC breakdown strength increased from 93.13 kV/mm to 101.24 kV/mm, an improvement of 8.71%. The thermal stability and dielectric properties are almost constant. This work provides a reference for improving the electrical and thermal properties of the main insulation of generator and further developing high thermal conductivity insulation materials.

articleTitle: Thermal-Electrical-Risk Coupled Modeling of Battery Energy Storage System Considering Stabilizing Intermittent Power Fluctaution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To address the issue of uncertainty in the output of energy storage systems resulting from the integration of new energy sources into the grid, a thermal-electrical-risk coupled model for energy storage is established. This model employed Automatic Generation Control (AGC) to regulate the power output of energy storage systems, thereby managed their stochastic output. By operating the energy storage model under uncertain output conditions, parameters related to temperature, capacity degradation, and internal resistance increase are obtained, facilitating a comprehensive analysis of the electrical, thermal, and safety performance of the energy storage system. Furthermore, under the condition of equal input and output electrical energy, the thermal-electrical-risk coupled model of energy storage is controlled for constant-power charging and discharging. A comparison is made between the temperature and performance degradation indicators of the energy storage system under the two scenarios, aiming to analyze the impact of output uncertainty on temperature and risk when integrated into the grid. The results indicate that compared to constant-power charging and discharging, uncertain output leads to significant temperature fluctuations and the occurrence of excessively high temperatures, thereby accelerating the performance degradation of the battery.

articleTitle: Interpretable XGBoost Based Cold Load Pickup Behavior Identification Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to provide decision support for load restoration optimization in distribution networks, taking the constant temperature control load of air conditioning as an example, which is the most likely to induce cold load recovery phenomena, we investigate the outage duration dependency characteristics of cold load recovery.
