We then use the Shapley Additive Explanation (SHAP) method to construct an interpretability mechanism for an XGBoost machine learning model, SHAP defines the average contribution of a feature value to the prediction in different coalitions. We select features that influence load parameters as inputs and cold load recovery power as output, and train a cold load recovery power prediction model. By comparing it with mainstream machine learning models, the interpretable XGBoost algorithm has best behavior, achieving a mean absolute error of 0.380%, a mean squared error of 0.030%, and a mean absolute percentage error of 0.445%. Finally, we uncover the feature correlations that affect cold load pickup power prediction, elucidating the decision-making process of the machine learning model at a global level.

articleTitle: Active and Reactive Power Collaborative Optimization of Photovoltaic Distribution Network Based on Two-Stage Decision-Making
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The penetration of distributed PV in distribution networks is increasing. The randomness and uncertainty of distributed PV output can lead to voltage fluctuations in the distribution network. Thus, for a PV distribution network, this research suggests a two-stage joint optimization approach for active and reactive power. Reducing voltage fluctuations and increasing the distribution network's economy of operation are the goals. In the first stage, a reactive power compensator planning model is established. The reactive power compensator's capacity and position are established based on the cost optimization goal function and loss sensitivity indicators. In the second stage, the results of the devices are derived based on a multiobjective improved particle swarm algorithm. And the collaborative optimization model of active and reactive power is established. Finally, the network loss and voltage optimization results are obtained. The IEEE 33-bus distribution network was the basis of several simulations and comparisons. The approach lowers operating costs and enhances voltage stability of the distribution network with photovoltaic access, according to the results. The effectiveness of the proposed strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Switching Harmonic Attenuation of Grid-Tied Converters Using LLCL Filters and MPC-SVPWM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper introduces an enhancement in grid-tied converter technology by incorporating a Model Predictive Control (MPC)-based space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) along with an advanced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$LLCL$</tex> filter. This approach aims to improve the conversion efficiency in grid-tied applications to three-phase ac, offering better harmonic attenuation than standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$LC$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$LCL$</tex> filters. The implementation of dual-mode control for dc voltage stabilization and the use of quadratic programming for inverter switching optimization is proposed to reduce switching losses, thereby augmenting system efficiency. Comparative simulations demonstrate a measurable efficiency improvement over traditional linear inverter methods, indicating a notable advancement in grid-tied converter technology, especially in terms of harmonic reduction and overall system performance enhancement.

articleTitle: Capacity Planning and Economic Analysis of Off-grid Offshore Wind-Hydrogen Storage Integrated Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Hydrogen production from offshore wind power is an effective means to solve the problems of grid connections and consumption difficulties of large-scale offshore wind farm, and the high cost of power delivery in the deep and distant sea. At present, the offshore wind power hydrogen production industry is still in the exploratory start-up stage, lack of industrial top-level design, demonstration project experience and mature business models, there is an urgent need to carry out the development of offshore wind power hydrogen production project strategic planning and technology research and development, to explore and study the scientific and reasonable, locally adapted offshore wind power hydrogen production system program. In this paper, the off-grid offshore wind hydrogen storage integrated system is taken as the research object, and the mathematical model of the system is constructed. Meanwhile, according to the different types of collector and hydrogen production methods, four schemes are designed for comparison, and with the minimization of Levelized Cost of Hydrogen (LCOH) as the objective function, the capacity planning of electrolysis capacity and storage tanks is carried out for each scheme. The system construction scheme combining the AC collector system and the PEM hydrogen production technology has the lowest LCOH cost, and has the largest NPV, which is competitive among the four schemes at the hydrogen selling price of 6.6€/kg.

articleTitle: A Novel Sensorless Position Sensing for Free-Piston Engine Generation Using Observation Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The accurate observation of mover is crucial for the effective operation and control of free-piston engine generator (FPEG). The conventional position sensors have drawbacks such as high cost, limiting the development of FPEG. This study introduces a novel sensorless position observation technique based on the structural characteristics of FPEG. The proposed approach employs an observation coil to establish the relationship between the flux and the displacement for observing the position of the mover in real time. This paper presents the establishment of an equivalent magnetic network model and a finite element model for the analysis of flux. A series of displacement observation experiments were conducted on a test bench. It is found that the calculated flux value has a linear connection with the actual position. The difference between the model results and the linear model results obtained from the testing is less than 3%. This approach can acquire instantaneous the observed position of the mover in real time during the test within a ±5mm range. The sensorless position observation approach can achieve a position detection error of less than 5%. This novel sensorless approach provides essential guidance for optimizing the performance and improving the commercial viability of FPEG.

articleTitle: An Improved Current Sensor Fault Diagnosis and Fault-tolerant Control for Multisector Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Multisector in-wheel motors have been widely used in the fields of electric vehicles and electric aircraft due to their high torque density, high power, and strong reliability. As the core component of the current controller and various observers, the current sensor plays a vital role in the stable control of the motor, thus the fault diagnosis and fault-tolerant control of current sensors is essential. However, the characteristics of both single-phase open-circuit faults and current sensor break faults are similar, making it difficult to distinguish between the two faults. In addition, for current sensor faults, the winding is usually directly cut off and controlled as a phase fault condition, which limits the output capability of the system. How to fully utilize the healthy windings after the current sensor fault is critical. Aiming at the above problems, this paper firstly analyzes the differences in the mechanism of current sensor fault and phase break fault and proposes a fault diagnosis algorithm based on a neutral point voltage observer. Secondly, to improve the robustness of the proposed method under the inaccurate motor parameters, an improved diagnostic algorithm by compensating the neutral voltage observation of the health sector is proposed. Finally, for fault-tolerant operation after current sensor failure, an extended Kalman observer which integrates the information of healthy and faulty sectors is proposed to realize the observation of faulty-phase current and fault-tolerant operation. The experiments with a four-sector in-wheel motor drive finally prove the evidence of the proposed algorithm.

articleTitle: Study on Reactive Power and Voltage Fluctuations Characteristics of Power Transformer Models Under Simulated Extreme Geomagnetic Disturbances Induced Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The advancement of China's energy transformation requires building a new power system. New power system has unique technical characteristics, and it faces new development opportunities and challenges. In addition to traditional accidents that damage the stability of power systems., non-traditional safety accidents such as extreme weather., geomagnetic storms., and electromagnetic attacks also require great attention.., . In this paper., we discuss the possible geomagnetic induced current (GIC) that may occur in the power system which potentially caused by solar storms extreme geomagnetic disturbances (SS-GMD)and high-altitude electromagnetic pulses late time effects (HEMP E3). The impact path and mechanism of GIC on the power equipment was firstly analyzed. Then., a HEMP E3 effect injection experimental circuit was proposed., and verified through simulation. Based on that., a HEMP E3 GIC source was developed to conduct relevant effect experiments. Finally., a PSCAD/EMTDC model was developed to simulate the partial electromagnetic effects of power transformers under extreme GIC injection., including harmonic distortion., sudden increase in reactive power loss., and bus voltage drop. This work can provide reference and data support for future effect experiments.

articleTitle: Coordinate Frequency Control Strategy for Multiple Wind Farms Considering Wind Speed Differences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem that the existing wind farm frequency control strategy cannot take into account different wind speed conditions to achieve primary frequency regulation, this paper proposes a coordinated frequency control strategy for multiple wind farms considering wind speed differences. Firstly, the theoretical equation of system counting and wind power square wave inertia command frequency dip depth is derived, and the factors affecting primary and secondary dip depth are analyzed. Further, to address the problem of differential frequency control capability of wind farms at different wind speeds, the constraints such as power dip at the exit moment, minimum rotor speed limit and system frequency frequency change rate are considered comprehensively to realize online optimal square-wave inertia power command optimal adjustment for different wind farms, and each wind farm participates in the system frequency control according to the stepwise timing sequence of command value; finally, a multi-wind farm coordinated frequency control strategy based on MATLAB/Simulink simulation model of multiple wind farms is built, and the simulation results of this paper can effectively improve the system frequency response characteristics, suppress the depth of the second drop, and improve the system frequency stability.

articleTitle: Research and Analysis on Management Methods of Line Loss for High Permeability Distributed Photovoltaic Access Transformer District
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of excessive line loss in high permeability distributed photovoltaic access transformer district, we proposed a line loss control method for distributed photovoltaic access transformer district based on the krill swarm algorithm. Firstly, the minimum objective function of active power loss and voltage offset at the node of photovoltaic access transformer district area is constructed, and the optimal solution of the objective function is obtained by using the improved krill swarm algorithm. Secondly, a high permeability distributed photovoltaic transformer district lumped total equivalent analysis model is established, besides, a coordinated control method for total active and reactive power output of photovoltaic that meets the optimal objective function is proposed. On the above basis, the cosine decreasing step evolution method is used to further optimize the improved krill swarm algorithm, and the optimal power allocation values for each distributed photovoltaic system in the transformer district were also obtained. Finally, a typical high permeability distributed photovoltaic transformer district area is selected for simulation and comparative analysis,proving that this line loss control method can achieve refined management of line losses in photovoltaic transformer district.

articleTitle: An Online Impedance Spectrum Measurement Method Based on Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: An online impedance spectrum measurement method based on a dual active bridge (DAB) converter is proposed in this article. This work integrates AC impedance measurement technology into the DAB converter in the charging interface device, and achieves online measurement of the AC impedance spectrum by applying sinusoidal disturbance signals of different frequencies to a given part of the PI controller. Through frequency sweep verification and PI controller design, high-quality sinusoidal disturbance signals are achieved. A high-bandwidth operational amplifier was used to build a signal conditioning circuit, and the USB-6211 data acquisition card was used to implement signal acquisition. The fast Fourier transform (FFT) algorithm was used to extract the amplitude and phase information of the impedance. The experimental results show that the error rates of the impedance measurement results are less than ±10%, confirming the functionality and feasibility, and providing a basis for online AC impedance spectroscopy. At the same time, it also provides a low-cost and practical solution strategy.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Microgrid Simulation Based on Hardware-in-the-Loop Simulation Software
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As the modern power industry expands, environmental pollution and resource demand also increase. Photovoltaic power generation technology stands out among other renewable energy sources due to its eco-friendliness and ease of utilization. However, when photovoltaic systems are integrated into the grid, a challenge arises: the inability to compensate for inductive reactive power, which can lead to voltage dips and impact the stability of the power grid. To address this issue, this study proposes the installation of a reactive power compensation device in the simulation design. Initially, the optimal capacity of the Static Var Compensator (SVC) is determined. Subsequently, the SVC's capacitor switching is controlled using both manual methods and a genetic algorithm, ensuring that the power factor meets the grid's stringent requirements upon interconnection. Furthermore, an energy storage battery is integrated into the simulation design to enhance the reliability and economic efficiency of power supply. This innovative solution offers dual advantages: rapid reactive power compensation and guaranteed power supply reliability. Its implementation is validated on the Real-Time Digital Simulator (RTDS) platform, demonstrating its feasibility and potential for widespread application in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Power Supply Restoration Optimization Considering Topology and Faults of the Upper-Level
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The adjustment of the power grid operation is achieved by changing the network topology through switch state switching, thereby enabling the transfer of loads within the power grid. This provides a solution to effectively alleviate issues of transmission congestion and equipment overload that arise during peak load periods. The paper begins with an analysis of the typical structure of a 220kV/110kV transmission system, deriving active power balance equations for various typical topologies and generalizing them in the form of the linear matrix. Building upon this foundation, the paper considers scenarios where a 220kV substation experiences voltage loss during a fault, leading to a loss of power supply to the 110kV substation it serves. A power supply restoration optimization model is developed, taking into account power backflow, to restore power supply to the loads served by the 220kV substation through power backflow from the unaffected 110kV lines. The problem is formulated as a mixed integer linear programming problem and solved using CPLEX. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed model is validated through optimization tests and analysis conducted on a real power grid.

articleTitle: Development of a Three-Dimensional Optical Waveguide Sensor for Pulsed Electric Field Measurement
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Non-contact electric field sensing technology is currently a solution for voltage measurement at critical nodes in power systems. This study focuses on the development of a small-sized, high-resolution, and wide frequency range three-dimensional(3D) pulsed electric field measurement technique. A three-dimensional integrated optical waveguide electric field sensor(OWEFS) based on the Mach-Zehnder interference effect is proposed. An asymmetric waveguide structure with two conical electrodes and one segmented electrode is introduced. A 3D electric field measurement probe is designed, and simulation studies and experimental verification are conducted to assess its measurement range, directionality, and temporal waveform measurement capabilities. The volume of this 3D probe is approximately 3 cmx I cm> 10 cm, which is about 10 times smaller than conventional probes, thus improving the spatial resolution of electric field measurements. After assembling the electric field measurement system, calibration of the proportionality coefficients for each direction in the three-dimensional coordinate system is performed. Experimental results demonstrate that the probe accurately captures the temporal waveform of the tested lightning-induced pulsed electric field and exhibits good directionality. Under lightning-induced pulsed voltage, the comprehensive measurement error of the sensor is less than 3%.

articleTitle: Hybrid Compensation Topology With Phase-Shift Modulation for DWPT System CC/CV Charging
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A receiver-based hybrid compensation topology for the dynamic wireless power transfer (DWPT) system of electric vehicles (EVs) is presented in this paper. And the proposed hybrid compensation topology consists of a series/series (S/S) compensation network and a series/inductor-capacitor-capacitor (S/LCC) compensation network to realize the constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) charging for EVs. All the compensation components of the S/S compensation network are contained in the S/LCC compensation network, which allows cost saved. Besides, a segmentation-based phase-shift modulation (PSM) strategy is introduced into the hybrid compensation topology to suppress the output fluctuations caused by discontinuous conduction mode (DCM), misalignment and load variation. Finally, a 2-kW prototype is established to validate the feasibility of the proposed hybrid compensation topology and control strategy. And the experimental results show that the output current/voltage are constant during 25cm misalignment when the load varies from 6 to 200Ω.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Dimensional Evaluation Index System of High Proportion New Energy Power Grid Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The increasing proportion of new energy access intensifies the volatility and uncertainty of the power grid., thereby creating a greater demand for grid flexibility., which significantly impacts the safe and stable operation of the power grid. Studying the operational characteristics of the power grid under high proportions of new energy access can provide guidance to ensure reliable power supply., promote consumption., and maintain safe and stable operations. To address this issue., this paper proposes a multidimensional evaluation index system for high-proportion new energy power grid operation. Firstly., it analyzes the adverse effects of a high proportion of new energy access on power grid operation from multiple time scales. Secondly., it presents a framework for a multidimensional evaluation index system based on time scale and establishes a multidimensional analysis model for high-proportion new energy systems that includes four indices: multi-time scale volatility., confidence level., multi-time scale complementarity., and peak load characteristics. Finally., using actual operational data from provincial power grids as an example., quantitative analysis is conducted on the operational characteristics under different time scales (hours., weeks months., and years) with significant levels of new energy access. The results demonstrate that the proposed evaluation system can quantitatively reflect the impact of large-scale integration of new energy sources on power grid operations from various perspectives.

articleTitle: Optimal Operation of Agricultural Park Considering Carbon-Green Certificate Joint Trading and Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the context of the dual-carbon goal of “peak car bon and carbon neutrality”, to realize the low-carbon economic o peration of agricultural park, This paper proposes a method for optimizing the operation of agricultural park considering carbon -green certificate trading and demand response. Firstly, the multi -energy coupled conversion characteristics of an agricultural par k in a certain place are comprehensively considered for its fine m odeling. Secondly, a carbon and green certificate trading mechani sm should be introduced, linking green certificate trading with ca rbon trading based on the carbon emission reduction represented by the green certificates. At the same time, it optimizes the load-s ide energy use behavior through demand response to reduce the peak-to-valley load difference. Finally, a low-carbon economic sc heduling strategy under the carbon-green certificate trading mar ket is proposed to minimize the sum of the system's operating cos ts, simulation results show that this method can effectively reduce the system operation cost and increase the rate of renewable ene rgy consumption.

articleTitle: Research on Hierarchical and Gradual Cooperative Voltage Regulation Strategy Based on OLTC and MDT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The voltage fluctuation on the low voltage side caused by the distributed generation (DG) in the new distribution network is the key factor affecting the power quality of users. this paper proposes a hierarchical and gradual cooperative voltage regulation control strategy based on on-load regulation transformer (OLTC) and modular distribution transformer (MDT) under the condition of sufficient reactive power. In this strategy, the concept of voltage cross section quality is first proposed and the model is given. Then the voltage fluctuation range is divided into three intervals: Interval 1 is the normal region, interval 2 is the slight over-limit region, and interval 3 is the serious over-limit region. Considering the economy and fast response of MDT, the strategy uses MDT as the main adjustment mode and OLTC as the backup adjustment means. Finally, the simulation not only verifies the feasibility of this strategy under normal conditions but also demonstrates its ability to prioritize the voltage quality of important loads during emergency situations.

articleTitle: Risk Analysis and Countermeasures of Start-Up Failure and Unplanned Outage of Pumped Storage Units
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the proposal of the dual-carbon target, the functional positioning of pumped storage in the new energy system has changed greatly, and it will become an important support for the new energy system. Start-up failure and unplanned outage of pumped storage units will not only lead to power loss and increase maintenance costs, but also cause disturbance to the power grid system and destroy the stability of the power grid system. This paper analyzes the startup failure and unplanned outage of pumped storage units, and puts forward corresponding countermeasures to provide reference for the safe operation of units and improve the operation reliability of units.

articleTitle: A Multi-objective Two-layer Collaborative Optimal Configuration Method for Ship Hybrid Energy Storage System Based on NSGA II
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To solve the problems of power quality degradation of ship power grid and power allocation of hybrid energy storage system (HESS) under complex operating conditions, a multi-objective two-layer collaborative optimization method based on the non-dominated sorting genetic algorithm (NSGA II) for all-electric ship hybrid energy storage system is proposed. The method first uses low-pass filtering(LPF) and variational modal decomposition (VMD) in the lower-layer operation model to realize the initial allocation and reallocation of the shipload power, and then takes into account the coupling characteristics between the energy management strategy and the capacity allocation of the HESS, and establishes a multi-objective optimal configuration model of the HESS that takes into account both the economy and technology in the upper-layer fixed-capacity model and then employs the NSGA II to solve the optimal power allocation strategy and the optimal capacity allocation. The optimal power allocation strategy and optimal capacity allocation are solved using NSGAII. The simulation results show that compared with two typical multi-objective algorithms, the proposed method realizes a reasonable power allocation between the diesel generator unit and the energy storage unit, and effectively suppresses the power fluctuation of the diesel generator unit under the premise of cost reduction.

articleTitle: Transmission Distance Extension Method for PT Symmetric Wireless Power Transmission System Based on Variable Capacitance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The Parity-Time (PT) symmetric wireless power transmission system can achieve stable operation of constant power and constant efficiency in its PT symmetric region. However, when the transmission distance of the system exceeds its critical coupling distance, power instability and efficiency degradation will occur, which limits the further improvement of its transmission distance. Therefore, in order to extend the transmission distance of PT symmetric wireless power transmission system and improve its practicability, this paper proposes a transmission distance extension method based on variable capacitance from the analysis of circuit theory. Firstly, the transmission characteristics of PT symmetrical wireless power transmission system are analyzed based on circuit theory. Next, to further extend the transmission distance and to avoid the problem of reduced system efficiency after improvement, a transmission distance extension method based on variable capacitance is proposed. The control parameters and control strategy of the variable capacitor are determined by simulation and theoretical analysis. The results show that the proposed method and control strategy can effectively extend the transmission distance of the system by increasing the operating frequency of the system, and can compensate the detuning of the primary and secondary capacitors of the wireless power transmission system.

articleTitle: Intelligent Bidding Strategy of Energy Hub in Under Multiple Electricity Market Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the promotion of power system (PS) reform in China and development of Energy hub (EH) technology, the research of Energy hub bidding strategy participating in the electricity market at distribution level emerges a great requirement. In view of this, the paper proposes a bi-level bidding optimization model of energy hub at distribution level is proposed, which considers the benefits of each participate under the energy market and ancillary service market environment. In the upper level, the Energy hub agent aims to develop an optimal bidding strategy to maximize its total benefits with the consideration of various characteristics of flexible energy resources. In the lower level, the power system owner conducts the electricity market clearing to minimize the operation cost considering the system topology and power flow security. The simulated annealing hybrid genetic algorithm (SA-GA) is adopted to obtain the Energy hub bidding decisions of the proposed bi-level optimization model. The proposed strategy is validated by case studies of a real system and the optimization results and analyses are presented under different scenarios, which indicate a promising application of the proposed Energy hub bidding strategy.

Author Keywords: thermal inertia simulated annealing hybrid genetic algorithms

articleTitle: Midpoint Voltage Balanced Control for Three-Phase Four-Wire Inverter Based on Three-Phase Generalized Coordinate Transformation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The primary objective of this study is to implement three-phase generalized coordinate transformation on a three-phase four-wire inverter, each phase of which supplies an independent load, aiming for a simple control structure and enhanced control effect. In the condition where the three-phase four-wire inverter operates in an isolated manner, the three-phase unbalanced loads leads to current fluctuation in the neutral line. The fluctuation subsequently offsets midpoint voltage of the split capacitors. The issue can be addressed by increasing the capacitor size. However, it inversely impacts the power density of the PWM inverter due to the increased volume. To address these challenges, an effective approach involves continuously adjusting the amplitude ratios and phase differences of the inductor currents based on the amplitude ratios of the capacitor voltages. This adjustment not only ensures equal capacitor voltages amplitudes, but also regulates the zero-sequence current to zero, thereby achieving minimal the midpoint voltage fluctuation of the split capacitors, and allowing for a significantly reduced thickness of the neutral line and smaller sizes of the split capacitors. Finally, the efficacy of the proposed scheme is validated through simulations.

articleTitle: A Data-Driven and Physics-Guided Modeling Approach for Bottom-Level Equipment in Integrated Energy System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid development of integrated energy system (IES), it is crucial to model subsystems and key equipment at different levels to meet the needs of characteristic analysis, planning and design, and operation control. In this paper, a modeling method for the underlying equipment in an IES is proposed. The core of the method is the fusion of convolutional neural network (CNN) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU). On this basis, the physical model of the equipment is used to guide the modeling and avoid the physical inconsistency. Finally, the experimental data of the vortex expander are collected through the miniature compressed air energy storage system to verify the accuracy and practicability of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Model Predictive Control of Alkaline Electrolyzers to Provide Ancillary Services
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Grid-connected power-to-hydrogen (P2H) plants are required to provide ancillary balancing services to the utility power systems. In this context, electrolyzers in the P2H plant must track regulatory load commands such as the automatic gen-eration control (AGC) or peak shaving signals. Large-scale P2H plants commonly use alkaline electrolyzers (AELs). However, the AELs are subject to complicated process constraints related to electrochemistry, thermal balance, and impurity accumulation. If they are not properly controlled in tracking the fast-varying regulatory commands, safety limits can be violated. To address this challenge, this paper proposes a nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) approach for the AELs to track the regulatory command, considering comprehensive process constraints. In the meantime, the proposed controller optimizes energy conversion efficiency by coordinating the AELs' load levels, temperatures, and hydroaen-to-oxygen (HTO) impurities. Simulation on two 1,000 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${\mathrm{N}}\mathrm{m}^{3}{/}\text{hr}$</tex> AELs responding to an AGC signal validates the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Research on Key Points and Evaluation Strategies for Interruption Performance of Circuit Breakers Under High Current Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The reliable operation of circuit breakers is crucial for maintaining the safety and stability of the power grid. This article focuses on the evaluation of the breaking capacity of circuit breakers under high current conditions. By establishing a magnetohydrodynamic model, the evaluation method of the breaking capacity of circuit breakers is systematically explored. The key areas of airflow field regulation and the role of zero front resistance in the evaluation of breaking capacity were studied with emphasis. Firstly, the paper discusses in detail the two key areas of airflow field regulation, namely the highest flow velocity area and the cyclone formation area, and points out design criteria to optimize the airflow field, increase flow velocity, and avoid unnecessary airflow movement. Secondly, this article analyzes the importance of zero front resistance in evaluating the breaking capacity of circuit breakers. Through a thermodynamic based thermal breakdown model, the temperature field thermal breakdown mechanism and dielectric recovery characteristics were studied, and the important embodiment of zero front resistance in key performance such as reaction interruption time and arc voltage was demonstrated. Overall, this study explores the key roles of airflow field regulation and zero front resistance in circuit breaker performance evaluation, filling the existing research gap in evaluating the breaking capacity of circuit breakers under extreme operating conditions. This provides important theoretical guidance for improving the design and performance of circuit breakers.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Dispatch Strategy for Distribution Network Based on Hierarchical Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the integration of massive distributed resources into the distribution network, the traditional centralized control approach struggles to meet the extensive energy and information interaction demands of numerous nodes. To address the developmental needs of new-generation distribution networks, this paper introduces a hierarchical control strategy based on source-load clusters. Initially, the paper defines the concept of source-load clusters and establishes a multi-tier control architecture consisting of distributed source-loads, distributed source-load aggregators, source-load cluster energy management centers, and distribution network operation centers. Subsequently, it designs a method for autonomous and hierarchical operation in each source-load cluster region, allowing each cluster to develop a day-ahead operation plan based on its unique source-load characteristics. Finally, through case studies, the paper demonstrates that the proposed control strategy effectively implements hierarchical energy control, reduces the control burden on distribution network operators, and achieves orderly power dispatch and maximal resource utilization.

articleTitle: The Key Construction Points of Electromagnetic Shielding Environment in The Anechoic Chamber
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The microwave anechoic chamber is an important laboratory and electromagnetic shielding test environment in the field of electromagnetic compatibility, and the electromagnetic shielding project is the premise and foundation of it. Unlike general construction projects, there are many key aspects of construction relationships, the technical points are complex, the process is irreversible, the investment cost is high, and multiple disciplines are involved. The size of the anechoic chamber usually follows the principle of 3 m and 10m, and most of them take the form of an anechoic chamber built separately in the main building, i.e. “room within a room”. In recent years, there is still not much practical experience in constructing the electromagnetic shielding test environment of a large anechoic chamber that is completely welded and integrated with the main building. Taking the example of the construction of a large-scale electromagnetic shielding test project of microwave anechoic chamber, the paper analyzes and calculates the weak points that affect the shielding index of the anechoic chamber, such as filters, shielding doors, waveguides, and waveguide windows, discusses the main technical practices and design to achieve the shielding index of the anechoic chamber and meet the user's requirements, and provides reference experience for similar projects.

articleTitle: A Two-Stage Robust Optimal Economic Scheduling Method for an Electricity-Hydrogen Coupled Microgrid with Local Hydrogen Sales
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: For the electricity-hydrogen coupled microgrid containing renewable energy, the uncertainty of renewable energy and load power prediction will lead to the weakening of the ability to resist intraday electricity market price fluctuations, which will increase the actual operating cost of the microgrid. In view of the above problems, this paper proposes a two-stage robust optimization economic scheduling model for electricity- hydrogen coupled microgrid. In the model, the time-of-use electricity price of the power grid and the hydrogen sales revenue of the microgrid are considered, and the uncertainty adjustment parameters of photovoltaic power generation and load power are introduced, which can flexibly adjust the conservatism of the scheduling scheme. Based on the column constraint generation (CCG) algorithm and the strong duality theory, the two-stage robust optimization problem is transformed into a mixed integer form of the main problem and the sub-problem to obtain the optimal solution of the original problem. Finally, under different prediction errors, the robust optimal scheduling model is simulated and compared with the deterministic economic optimal scheduling model. The larger the prediction error, the more significant the economy of the robust optimal scheduling scheme, which verifies that the two-stage robust optimal scheduling has stronger ability to resist intraday electricity market price fluctuations.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method of Renewable Energy Consumption Capacity of Integrated Heat and Power Energy System in Heating Season Based on Time Series Production Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A round of energy reform characterized by large-scale development and utilization of new energy sources such as wind energy and solar energy is booming around the world, and since the promulgation of the “ Renewable Energy Law, ” China's domestic new energy development momentum has been rapid. However, due to the need for heating in windy areas in winter, the northeast and northwest China have a high proportion of combined heat and power units, resulting in frequent wind curtailment during the winter heating season. In order to reduce the phenomenon of wind curtailment and increase the proportion of renewable energy generation, this paper focuses on the thermal-electric joint planning technology to improve wind power consumption from the planning level and studies the technical and economic model of various heat sources, and uses the time series production simulation model to resolve the problem of augmenting the large-scale wind power consumption capacity. Through the research on the above problems, the study puts forward a reasonable basis for the consumption of wind power by each heat source, improves the thermal-electric joint planning method of wind power consumption and develops a simulation platform. On this basis, the thermal-electric joint planning scheme and operation mode for improving wind power consumption are proposed.

articleTitle: Research on Protecting and Operating 5G Radio Base Stations Using Lightning Strikes Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This article mainly introduces researching results on using lightning strikes data obtained from lightning location systems (LLS), to protect and operate the fifth generation(5G) Radio Base Stations (5G RBS). The purpose of this article is to give guidance for data utilization of the LLS data to prevent damage from lightning strikes and to protect telecommunication facilities. This means that data is not only limited to maintenance situations, but also can be applied to design or installation situations. Moreover, how to use LLS data for 5G RBS risk assessment are introduced in related content.

articleTitle: Short-Term Wind Power Interval Prediction Based on TCN-DBG-PSMAT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the increasing proportion of new energy access, the accurate prediction of wind power is increasingly important for the stable operation and flexible scheduling of the integrated energy system. In view of the traditional prediction model, it is difficult to fully explore the potential dependence between variables, which cause problems of low prediction accuracy of wind power under high dimensionality and large amount of data. In this paper, we propose a short-term wind power interval prediction model based on hybrid deep-learning. The model integrates a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN) with a Deep Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Unit (DBG) and Prob-sparse Multi-head Self-attention mechanism (PSMAT). Based on this, Quantile Regression (QR) and Kernel Density Estimation (KDE) are combined to obtain interval predictions of future values at different confidence levels. The method is validated on the output dataset of a wind farm in Australia. The experimental results show that the network proposed in this paper has better performance and can more accurately characterize the uncertainty of wind power output compared to other prediction models, laying the foundation for subsequent research on integrated energy system scheduling.

articleTitle: Multi-Period Coordinated Optimization of Coupled Traffic-Power Systems via Pricing Incentives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The rapid growth of electric vehicles (EV s) and fast charging stations couples the urban power network and traffic network and brings spatial-temporal flexibility resources. Through the coordination of price incentives, the EV traffic flow and charging load distribution can be improved to relieve the congestion phenomenon in the coupled traffic-power systems. In this paper, a multi-period coordinated optimization framework of the coupled traffic-power systems based on pricing incentives is proposed and implemented in two steps. Firstly, in an aggregated manner, the multi-period optimal traffic-power flow is calculated to minimize the total network operation costs. The temporal and spatial flexibility of EV s is described by a multi-period traffic assignment model, which is formulated as cone optimization to accelerate the solution. Secondly, in a disaggregation manner, the best pricing strategies, i.e., road toll and charging prices are identified to track the flow target above while minimizing total taxes imposed on EV users. Case studies validate the effectiveness of the proposed framework and methods. The two-step pricing framework is proven to effectively improve traffic-power flow and reduce computational burden.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Stochastic Optimal Dispatch of Integrated Electricity and Heat Energy Systems Considering Uncertainty of Wind Power
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The integrated electricity and heat energy systems (IEHS) realize the coupling of electricity system and heat systems, which can make full use of the characteristics of different energy flows, and helps to improve the energy efficiency of the system and the consumption of renewable energy. In order to cope with wind power's uncertainty, this paper establishes a two-stage stochastic optimal dispatch method for IEHS. Typical wind power scenarios are obtained by Monte-Carlo sampling and scenario reduction method. The two-stage optimal dispatch model is constructed based on the direct-current power flow model and dynamic thermal model, and the relationship between day-ahead dispatch and realtime adjustment strategy. In order to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method, a case study is carried out based on an IEHS consisting of a 6-node electricity system and a 12-node heat system, and the impact of the CHP units' participation in the second stage optimization on the dispatch results is analyzed in detail.

Author Keywords: integrated electricity and heat energy systems

articleTitle: Distributed Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Coordination: An Efficient and Cost-Effective Framework Based on Multilevel Game Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Due to the multiple attributes of transportation and energy storage device, electric vehicles (EVs) are expected to play an important role by vehicle-to-grid (V2G) interaction in future power system to cope with the high penetration of intermittent renewables. In order to improve the control efficiency while maintaining the cost-effectiveness of massive EV fleet scheduling, a hierarchical framework is proposed in this work, utilizing game theory to carry out economic incentives and control at three levels. The mean-field game and leader-follower Stackelberg game are combined in the lower and middle levels to model the competitive coordination among virtual power plants (VPPs) that aggregate the distributed EVs and to approximate the system state for extensive EV response. The evolutionary game is further employed in the upper level to examine the continuous configuration change with V2G adopted. Also, EV characteristic models of travelling features and battery degradation are established and simplified for efficient calculation. Case studies are implemented to verify the feasibility and performance. Results show that the required solution time can be reduced by distributed scheduling based on game method with similar and even better general utility achieved.

articleTitle: Real-Time Risk Zoning Research on Rainfall Induced Disasters in Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Starting from the three types of rainfall-related disasters affecting power grids, this article considers the combined effect of multiple factors in the natural disaster risk assessment system to construct a real-time risk assessment index system for rainfall-induced disasters on transmission lines. Large-scale data such as elevation, water systems, and vegetation coverage in a specific region are comprehensively selected and used in conjunction with rainfall data as dynamic variables in the evaluation method to obtain a real-time risk assessment map for different types of disasters. From the analysis of risk zoning, high-risk areas for rain-flash accidents in the region are mainly caused by short-term heavy rainfall, while high-risk areas for urban waterlogging and secondary disasters are mainly caused by geographical features. Targeted recommendations are proposed to provide effective information for disaster prevention and mitigation decisions and to ensure power grid safety to the greatest extent possible.

articleTitle: Adjustable Capacity Computing Model for Energy Storage and EV Participating in Valley Filling Demand Response in Virtual Power Plant Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The calculation model for the adjustable capacity of energy storage and electric vehicles (EVs) involved in valley filling demand response in virtual power plant mode is proposed in this paper. Firstly, calculation method for the adjustable capacity of individual flexible adjustable charging load resources for energy storage and EVs is constructed to achieve quantitative calculation and classification of its adjustable capacity. Then, the method of calculating adjustable capacity of the polymer flexible adjustable charging load resource is proposed to realize calculation of adjustable capacity. Secondly, adjustable capacity of the reserve regulation pool is judged and calculated to realize the deep utilization of the flexible adjustable charging load resources of the reserve regulation pool. Finally, the ability of flexible adjustable charging load in load aggregator to participate in the valley filling demand response is calculated, and the demand response timing strategy is proposed. The model and method proposed in this paper can calculate the adjustable capacity of individual and aggregate resources, which is conducive to the accurate assessment of the initial response capacity of load aggregators when they participate in the demand response of filling.

articleTitle: Investigation and Experimental Verification of Decomposition Components of GIS Gas Mixture under Partial Discharge Defects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The mixed gas technology of sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas and nitrogen (N2) gas for gas insulated switchgear (GIS) has been proven to be an effective method to the traditional GIS with single sulfur hexafluoride (SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf>) gas, which can effectively reduce carbon emissions. However, for GIS equipment using mixed gas technology, the characteristic components of internal decomposition products under different partial discharge types are not clear. A rapid diagnosis and analysis method of internal decomposition products after partial discharge in GIS field is proposed, and four typical partial discharge defects of GIS equipment, namely metal protrusions, metal contamination on insulator surface, air gap between metal and insulator, and suspension discharge, are investigated by building a test platform, respectively. Characteristic components and the trend of discharge voltage and discharge amount, which provide a potential solution for accurate and rapid evaluation and diagnosis of equipment defects.

articleTitle: Combined Peak Load Scheduling for Power Dispatching with Price Demand Response
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As renewable energy technologies continue to advance, the integration of an increasing amount of new energy power generation into the grid is observed.However,the inherent instability of these renewable sources poses challenges to the safe and efficient operation of power systems. This research employs an elastic matrix method to adjust the load demand curve on the load side.And establishes a model for minimizing total cost under conditions of wind power integration.Within this model, the outputs of thermal power units and wind turbines are optimized and coordinated,considering various operational constraints Various operational scenarios are established to compare and analyze the cost advantages of a joint source-load peak shaving approach, as well as to assess the impact of different peak shaving states of thermal power units on the integration and efficiency of the wind power grid.

articleTitle: Pattern Recognition for Partial Discharge Ultrasonic Signal in Oil-Immersed Transformer Based on EEMD-LSSVM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Effective identification of partial discharge types is an important prerequisite for accurately assessing the insulation state of oil-immersed transformers. In this paper, a classification combined identification method is proposed for localized discharge ultrasonic signals of oil-immersed transformers based on ensemble empirical modal decomposition (EEMD) and least squares support vector machine (LSSVM). First, the EEMD algorithm is used to analyze the time-frequency of the local discharge ultrasonic signals, then the intrinsic modal function (IMF) obtained by calculating the EEMD decomposition is used to select 11 feature parameters to form a hybrid feature vector, and finally, the LSSVM classification algorithm is used to classify and identify the type of discharge. In order to verify the accuracy of the algorithm, an experimental platform is set up for collecting four different types of local discharge ultrasonic signals. By performing feature extraction and pattern recognition on four types of Partial Discharge (PD) ultrasound signals, the recognition accuracy was 94.38%. The comparison experimental results show that the method proposed in this paper can effectively extract the characteristic parameters of local discharge ultrasonic signals and accurately identify the type of discharge, which is of good value for engineering applications.

articleTitle: Effect of BaTiO3 Doping on the Surface Insulation Properties of Alumina in SF6 Under DC Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Ceramic materials have high mechanical strength, excellent temperature stability and aging resistance. Compared with epoxy resin, it is more suitable for the alternative material solutions of surface insulation in complex working conditions of strong electric field and large temperature gradients. However, there is still a certain distance between the surface insulation performance of alumina-based ceramic insulation materials used in the field of external insulation of power industry and the actual requirements of internal insulation pillars for UHVDC equipment, and its key electrical properties need to be regulated. Therefore, a new type of Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>/BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> composite ceramic material was prepared by using ion doping technology in this paper. It is found that the electrical properties of ceramics doped with 3% BaTiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> are excellent. The volume resistivity at room temperature is <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.01\times 10^{15}\Omega\cdot \mathrm{m}$</tex>, and the average surface charge density under positive and negative DC voltages is 0.43 pC/mm2 and 0.42 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{pC}/\text{mm}^{2}$</tex>, which is 32.59% and 27.40<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> lower than that of pure alumina ceramics, and the flashover voltage is 19.15% higher than that of pure alumina ceramics. Doping Ba<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>+ with high ionic radius will hinder the movement of weakly bound carriers, increase the conduction barrier, thereby increasing the volume resistivity, slowing down the migration rate of internal carriers, and reducing the charge from solid to gas-solid surface, thereby inhibiting the accumulation of surface charge, and weakening the distortion of local electric field on the surface, thereby increasing the flashover voltage to a certain extent. The research results provide a theoretical basis for the regulation of surface insulation properties of ceramics in SF6 under DC voltage by ion doping based on large ion suppression effect.

articleTitle: Role and Value Embodiments, Application Challenges and System Design Suggestions of VPP in the Context of New Type Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Virtual power plant (VPP) is a new type of power coordination and management system, which can effectively integrate and optimize the use of resources, realize the grid to cut peaks and fill in the valleys and improve the reliability of power supply, as one of the important components of the new type power systems, it is more and more concerned by all walks of life in the society. Firstly, role embodiments of VPP in the context of new type power systems is analyzed in detail from 8 aspects including power balance management, energy efficiency improvement, flexible load management, etc. Secondly, the important value embodiment of VPP from the perspective of power supply, power grid, power consumption, regulatory, industry, and market are summarized. Finally, large-scale application challenges of VPP in the context of new type power systems are discussed, and supporting VPP policy system design suggestions are given. The VPP is of great value in the different participants. it can be expected that under the background of the “3060 dualcarbon” goals and the acceleration of the construction of new type power systems, the future VPP technology development potential is huge and the application prospect is broad.

articleTitle: Study of the Economic Efficiency and Carbon Emission of a Wind-solar-coal Integrated Hydrogen Production System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The trend of energy transformation provides an opportunity for the development of hydrogen energy, which will become an important component of the future energy system. Due to the carbon reduction requirements under the dual carbon target, the demand for using clean electricity to produce green hydrogen has greatly increased, and the coordinated development of hydrogen and electricity has become increasingly important. This paper proposed a wind-solar-coal integrated system, by using the stable and adjustable power generation capacity of coal-fired power plants to balance the volatility of wind and solar power generation, it improves the efficiency of hydrogen production in electrolysis tanks, and thus enhance the overall economic efficiency of the system. At the same time, this article also calculated the system's carbon emissions. By taking an integrated combination in northwest district, this paper simulates the realtime hourly operation condition. The results show that the coal-fired unit has great cooperation ability with wind and solar PV, the cost is nearly 6–9 CNY lower than the average level, and the carbon emission intensity is at acceptable level. Two more scenarios with different proportion of coal electricity is analyzed, the results show that the integrated system proposed in this paper has utility value.

articleTitle: Robust Optimal Dispatch Model for Multi-Area Interconnected Power System Considering Flexible Operation Mode of Carbon Capture Power Plants
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A decentralized coordinated low-carbon optimal dispatch model of interconnected power system with multi-flexibility resource access is proposed to effectively promote new energy consumption in the sending area and improve the problem of insufficient flexible regulation capacity in the receiving area. Firstly, a mathematical model of carbon capture power plants (CCPPs) with integrated flexible operation approach is established to analyze the net output power operation range and to explore the “energy time-shift” characteristics of CCPPs with the flexible operation mode. Secondly, according to the actual power supply composition of China's sending and receiving areas, taking into account the operating characteristics of tie-line, a fully decentralized optimal dispatch model of interconnected power system is constructed based on alternating direction method of multipliers (ADMM). Finally, the example analysis verifies that the proposed dispatch model is able to coordinate and optimize the flexibility regulation resources in the sending and receiving areas, reduce carbon emissions, and improve the economy of system operation.

articleTitle: Fault Detection for Battery Energy Storage Systems in Microgrids Under Event-Triggered Protocols: An Interval Observer Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, we investigate a method to realize fault detection using interval observer for battery energy storage systems containing actuator faults in microgrids. In order to reduce the data communication burden of the battery energy storage system, an improved event triggering mechanism with time-varying threshold is proposed to control the received signal of the interval observer. In addition, the desired interval observer gain is obtained by solving a matrix inequality. The output of the interval observer is utilized to construct the upper and lower bounds of the output of the system when the system does not contain actuator faults, and the actuator fault detection is achieved by whether the output of the system exceeds the constructed upper and lower bounds. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method are verified by numerical simulation.

articleTitle: Review of Carbon Emission Accounting in Typical Industry and Associated Emission Reduction Application
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The use of fossil fuels has increased significantly since the Industrial Revolution, leading to a rise in CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emissions and causing environmental pollution and climate change. To combat global warming and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, efficient carbon accounting methods must be developed, especially in high-emission industries such as manufacturing, construction, and high-tech industries. China has set goals to peak carbon emissions by 2030 and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060 by improving energy efficiency and upgrading industries. However, without a comprehensive national product carbon emission accounting database, the accuracy of carbon accounting will be challenged, which is crucial for governmental policy-making and corporate sustainability. It's also essential to develop a carbon accounting strategy for typical industries' products to achieve efficient carbon emission reduction. Various methods of Virtual power plants (VPPs) are being explored for carbon accounting integration and carbon emission management. This review synthesizes a multitude of studies in the field of carbon accounting and focuses on the construction of carbon emission databases in typical industries, and their significance in reinforcing efforts toward a sustainable and environmentally responsible future.

articleTitle: Fully Distributed Energy Management Scheme for Multi-Source Hybrid Power Systems in Fuel Cell Ships Based on Extended Droop Control Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Conventionally, energy management systems (EMSs) for fuel cell (FC) ships are usually implemented with centralized or hierarchical control, which causes high costs, low reliability, and poor scalability. In this paper, a fully distributed EMS (FD-EMS) applied to shipboard multi-source hybrid power systems consisting of parallel FCs, batteries (BATs), and supercapacitors (SCs) is proposed to solve the problems of mismatch load power, inconsistent performance of multi-stack FCs, and unbalanced State-of-Charges (SoCs) between parallel BATs and SCs. The proposed FD-EMS is realized based on a novel extended droop control strategy, which is achieved by using virtual inductive, resistive, and capacitive droop control for FCs, BATs, and SCs, respectively, in order to ensure automatic split-frequency response of the load power among the three types of power sources. On this basis, adaptive virtual inductance, resistance, and capacitance droop coefficients are individually designed to achieve the objectives of multi-stack FC performance consistency, dynamic equalization and adaptive regulation of SoCs for BATs and SCs, and stable bus voltage control. Moreover, the proposed strategy allows for maintaining the normal system operation in the case of power sources failures, and does not depend on a centralized communication network. Finally, simulation results based on Matlab/Simulink verify the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: Input Series Inverter Topology to Suit the Application Scenario of High Input Voltage Driving Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper has studied a high power motor drive architecture with multi-three-phase winding and high DC-link voltage. The high DC-link voltage of the inverter makes it difficult for the inverter to select suitable switching devices. In this paper, a series inverter topology is proposed, in which the DC sides of three-phase inverters are connected in series and connected to the DC bus, and the DC side voltage of each inverter is reduced by series connection. Each sub-module of the inverter can drive the corresponding three-phase windings and generate torque. However, when the parameters of the motor side are not equal or the capacitance of the DC side of the series inverter is not equal, the input voltage of each inverter will be unequal. Therefore, this paper puts forward a three-loop control method of voltage sharing loop, speed loop and current loop to ensure the DC side capacitor voltage balance of each inverter and the stable operation of the motor. The simulation results show that the capacitor voltage on the DC side of the series inverter can keep balance. This new architecture can be applied for high power motor drives in shipboard and so on.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy to Improve the Frequency Stability of Large-Scale Wind Power Connected to the Grid Through UHVDC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problems such as the decrease of frequency regulation ability of the sending end system caused by large-scale wind power transmission through UHVDC and how to coordinate and utilize various frequency regulation resources, a coordinated control strategy of multi-agent active support frequency based on wind power and UHVDC is proposed, which effectively improves the frequency stability of the sending end system. Firstly, according to the reserve capacity of each frequency regulation resource of the sending end system and the unbalanced power caused by power disturbance, the power support demand of the sending end system under different scenarios is analyzed, and a multi-time scale coordinated control strategy of frequency support for wind turbines and UHVDC systems considering the dead zone of frequency regulation is proposed, so that both wind turbines and UHVDC systems have the ability of inertia support and primary frequency regulation at the same time. Combined with the maximum reserve capacity of synchronous unit and wind turbine frequency regulation, the dead zone values of frequency regulation control strategies of wind turbine and UHVDC system are designed respectively, so that the two can automatically switch inertia support and primary frequency regulation according to the size of unbalanced power, so as to improve the frequency stability of the sending end system and make full use of the frequency regulation ability of synchronous unit and wind turbine. Finally, based on the RTLAB real-time digital simulation platform, a simulation model of large-scale wind power transmission system through UHVDC is built to verify the effectiveness of the proposed frequency active support coordinated control strategy.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of an LCC-S Compensated Topology in Wireless Power Transfer System With Constant Current and Voltage for Battery Charging Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a unified approach to parameter design, aimed at achieving load-independent constant current (CC) and constant voltage (CV) outputs under zero phase angle (ZPA) conditions which can be used in most topologies. A systematic set of parameter design techniques has been developed to facilitate this goal. This approach offers high design flexibility, thereby allowing extensive adjustability across various system components. This approach has the advantage of producing multiple viable solutions for a given set of parameters, distinguishing it from other methods. To verify the theoretical analysis, a 500W LCC-S compensated wireless power transfer (WPT) system for battery charging applications was designed and manufactured. The system operates at two different frequencies enabling both CC output with ZPA and CV output with ZPA. Details of the hardware design and laboratory prototype are presented, complemented by experimental results.

articleTitle: Optimization of Magnetic Coupling Structure based on Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To achieve high misalignment ability and avoid the time cost brought by the exhaustive method, a non-resonant wireless charging system (WCS) and a multi-objective optimization method for magnetic coupling structure are proposed. First, the working principle of WCS with non-resonant SS compensation is analyzed to illustrate the system's anti-misalignment ability and the necessity of multi-objective optimization. Then, the Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm-II (NSGAII) is analyzed and used to optimize the design of nested coils. The principle of NSGAII is analyzed, and the mutual inductance fluctuation and aligned mutual inductance are optimized. Finally, the simulation result shows that the optimized WCS has a high anti-misalignment performance and can maintain the output power within the misalignment range of 120 mm.

articleTitle: Second Harmonic Current Suppression Applied for Single-Phase Converter of Hybrid System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The power decoupling-based method stands as an effective strategy for mitigating the second harmonic current in single-phase power electronic devices. To successfully curb the ingress of second harmonic power into these devices, the control strategy for the second harmonic current compensator becomes pivotal. In an effort to assess the efficacy of the second harmonic compensator within multi-cell hybrid systems, a compensator tailored for the fundamental double closed-loop control of fuel cell and battery hybrid systems is formulated. This method demonstrates commendable steady-state and dynamic performance, along with robust stability. The design process and simulation results presented in this article substantiate the effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Necessity and Optimal Design of Magnetic Shielding Structure for Leakage Current Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Leakage current is inextricably linked to the insulation state of power equipment, leakage current refers to the current formed inside the insulation and on the surface of the insulation between the high potential and the low potential under the condition of applied voltage. Leakage current is an essential basic parameter for the perception of insulation state of power equipment, and to improve the reliability of the perception of insulation state of power equipment, it is necessary to ensure that the leakage current measurement results are accurate, stable and reliable. Therefore, it is of great significance to study the magnetic shielding structure of microcurrent sensors and improve the shielding structure's ability to resist the interference of industrial frequency magnetic field. In this paper, by optimizing the design of magnetic shield structure, increasing the thickness of magnetic shield extension structure and magnetic shield gap, the shielding efficiency of the shielding device can be effectively enhanced. Through the study of micro-current sensors in the complex system substation environment by the external magnetic field interference on the influence of its working magnetic field characteristics, aimed at solving the micro-current sensors in the face of industrial frequency magnetic field interference in the weak anti-interference ability of technical problems.

articleTitle: Small-Signal Stability Analysis Based on Impedance Network Matrix of Multiple Grid-Connected Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the ever-increasing renewable energy in a power system, many small-signal stability issues occurred in a system when these sources are connected to a weak grid through power electronic converters (PECs) with unreasonable parameters. However, the traditional impedance analysis has some limitations in the small-signal stability analysis for a multiple grid-connected converters (MGCCs). To overcome these limitations, in this paper a new stability analysis method is proposed. Firstly, the concept of impedance network matrix is obtained by extending traditional impedance ration form single grid-connected converters (SGCCs) to an MGCCs. Furthermore, the equivalent open-loop transfer function is derived to analyze stability, then stability indexes-evaluation factor and influence factor are used for locating the stability of the subsystem. Finally, the validity of the criterion and stability indexes is verified by a 7-PECs system. Both theoretical analysis and time-domain simulation show that the proposed method has the potential to analyze the high-order system stability.

articleTitle: Prediction of Medium and Long Term Power Grid Energy Loss in the Central of China Based on Simulation Calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The formulation and prediction of line loss rate has always been one of the important tasks for power grid enterprises. By studying the trend of power grid energy loss and line loss rate in the medium and long term, loss reduction goals are proposed, which are conducive to achieving carbon peaking and carbon neutrality goals. This article considers the influence of factors such as power grid structure, operation mode and load growth on power grid energy loss, and proposes a prediction method for medium and long-term power grid energy loss based on simulation calculation. This article also presents the prediction results of the trend of medium and long-term power grid energy loss in the Central of China. It is expected that the power grid energy loss is mainly related to the changes of power grid structure and inter-provincial electric quantity. Finally, this paper proposes practical and feasible measures to reduce power grid energy loss.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis and Impedance Reshaping Methods for DC Distribution Systems with Multiple Voltage Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In recent years, impedance-based stability analysis and improvement methods have become very popular in DC distribution systems. However, the existing stability criteria such as the impedance-ratio and impedance-sum criteria, require the additional calculation of the number of right-half-plane (RHP) poles when applied in the DC distribution systems with multiple voltage sources, which makes the stability analysis complex. In this paper, a stability analysis method for a DC distribution system with two voltage sources and one converter-based load is proposed, which does not require evaluating the RHP poles. On this basis, an impedance reshaping strategy based on the first-order high-pass filter is proposed to suppress system oscillations. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed methods is verified through impedance analysis and experiments.

articleTitle: Influence of 16k-30kHz Sinusoidal Voltage on the Partial Discharge and Breakdown Characteristics of Parallel Wires at Low Pressure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Due to the requirements of certain special communication frequency bands (Very Low Frequency, VLF) for high-altitude platforms, the internal insulation design of power source faces challenges posed by low air pressure and voltage frequencies in the range of 3–30 kHz. Presently, limited research exists on the partial discharge and breakdown characteristics within the VLF band, particularly concerning the impact on discharge characteristics under low pressure conditions.
