In this study, we established an experimental platform where a 16k-30kHz VLF sinusoidal voltage was applied to a parallel conductor gap. We measured the Partial Discharge Inception Voltage (PDIV) and breakdown voltage within the pressure range of 19.4kPa to 57.8kPa. The results indicated a notable decrease in PDIV with voltage frequency for a 10 cm air gap. For a 2 cm gap distance, the breakdown voltage under 50Hz voltage was marginally lower than that under VLF frequency at low pressure, although they exhibited similarity at atmospheric pressure. As the gap distance increased to 3cm, the breakdown voltages under the two voltage types became comparable under low pressure conditions. Upon reaching atmospheric pressure, the breakdown voltage under VLF frequency was markedly lower than that under power frequency conditions.

articleTitle: AC Breakdown Characteristics of Air in Non-Uniform Electric Fields at Low-Pressure Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the development of the power grid at high altitudes, more and more transmission and transformation projects are being implemented at altitudes close to 5000 meters. As the altitude increases, the air pressure decreases, resulting in a decrease in the insulation performance of the air gap and requiring corresponding adjustments to the insulation structure of power equipment. This paper investigated the AC breakdown characteristics of air in non-uniform electric fields at pressures of 50~100 kPa. The relationship between maximum breakdown field strength and electric field non-uniformity factor at different pressures was analyzed. The applicability of streamer criterion in low-pressure air gap was also analyzed. The results show that the breakdown voltage increases with increasing pressure and electrode distance for different electrode radius. At the same air pressure, the maximum breakdown field strength increases with the decrease of the electrode radius. When the electrode radius <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$r$</tex> ≥ 1.0 cm, the streamer criterion can accurately calculate the breakdown voltage of short air gaps at low pressures.

articleTitle: The Influence of Insulation Distance and Electric Field Component on Surface Charge Accumulation on Insulators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Surface charge accumulation is an important factor to consider in the insulation design of direct curren (DC) gas-insulated lines (GILs). The proportion of normal and tangential electric field may vary due to different insulation dimensions, leading to significant changes in the surface charge accumulation pattern. To clarify the dominant charging pathways under different insulation dimensions and electric field components, this study examines two cases: a mixed electric field distribution (Case 1) and a tangential electric field dominant distribution (Case 2). Surface charge distributions are measured, and the transition in charge accumulation modes are analyzed. The results indicate that in Case 1, positive charge accumulation is the predominant distribution pattern, with gas conduction and high voltage (HV) electrode injection being the main sources of positive charges. As the insulation distance increases, the positive charge density gradually decreases due to weakened gas conduction process. In Case 2, negative charge accumulation becomes the primary distribution pattern, primarily attributed to gas conduction. With an increase in insulation distance, the negative charge density gradually increases, mainly due to the reduced tangential electric field weakening the injection process of HV electrode.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Deep Dielectric Charging Models of Spacecraft Slip Ring Assembly
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Numerical simulation is widely used as an important means for the design, evaluation, and qualitative analysis of deep dielectric charging in spacecraft. In this paper, for the commonly used radiation-induced conductivity (RIC) model and the charge conservation law (CCL) model, a comparative analysis is conducted from the perspective of control equations and physical meanings. The RIC model is a microscopic expression considering free charge and trapped charge, and the CCL model is a further simplification of the RIC model. Based on the RIC model, a typical back-grounded plate example is calculated to explore the internal charging of the medium under different particle energies. Based on the CCL model, utilizing a combination of Monte-Carlo particle transport simulation and finite element calculation, the 3-D distribution of the electric field intensity inside the solar array drive assembly (SADA) slip ring is accurately described. It can be seen from the calculation results that the two results are basically consistent, but the three-dimensional calculation can more accurately describe the internal electric field intensity distribution of the medium. The maximum internal electric field intensity is about − 1.81 × 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">7</sup> V/m, which is close to the internal breakdown threshold of the dielectric.

articleTitle: First-Principles Study in Graphene-Based Single-Atom Catalysts for Hydrogen Evolution Reactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Electrochemical water splitting is the most promising process for producing hydrogen as an energy carrier. The electrocatalysts, as the main step in hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) of water electrolysis, are crucial for reducing the energy barrier and improving reaction efficiency. This motivates us to design low-cost and highly active HER electrocatalysts. Herein, we utilize density functional theory (DFT) calculations to explore the HER activity on the surface of graphene doped with single atoms of copper, iron, and platinum, respectively. We explore the HER activity of graphene with two different doping sites, in-plane and out-of-plane. The absolute value of the hydrogen adsorption Gibbs free energy change of each sample are less than 1 eV, showing good hydrogen adsorption performance, which are close to the HER performance of noble metal catalysts. Meantime, electronic structure analysis shows that the energy of the bonding orbital of Fe in-plane site is greatly reduced, and the antibonding orbital is not filled with electrons.

articleTitle: A Fault Diagnosis Method for Silicon Carbide (SiC) Converters Based on ResNet
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: One of the impediments to the widespread application of Silicon Carbide (SiC) Metal-Oxide-Semiconductor Field-Effect Transistors (MOSFETs) is the insufficient research on their safety and reliability. This paper proposes a ResNet-based fault diagnosis method for SiC converters to address the inadequacies in the research on fault diagnosis of SiC MOSFET converters. Firstly, driven by data, electrical quantities of SiC MOSFET converter are extracted as inputs for the diagnostic model. Subsequently, a one-dimensional ResNet network is constructed to uncover hidden information in the fault data, ultimately yielding diagnostic accuracy for various open-circuit fault modes. The effectiveness of this approach is validated on a simulation platform for SiC MOSFET converters.

articleTitle: Capacity Estimation of Cross Domain Lithium-ion Battery Based on Semi-Supervised Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The state-of-health (SOH) estimation algorithm for lithium-ion batteries is crucial for ensuring the safety and cost-effectiveness of batteries, garnering widespread research and attention. However, data-driven models face challenges in generalizing models established on one type of battery to others, mainly due to the assumption of independent and identically distribution. Therefore, this paper proposes a semi-supervised transfer learning approach to address this issue. By leveraging trace amount of labeled data and unlabeled data from the target domain, the proposed method designs a semi-supervised transfer process and loss function for the source model through fine-tune and a domain adaptation method based on Maximum Mean Discrepancy (MMD). This facilitates the development of a capacity estimation model that can be universally applied to batteries with different chemistries and operating conditions. Cross-validation results indicate that, compared to original models and other benchmarks, the proposed method achieves the generalization of the capacity estimation model to lithium-ion batteries with different data distributions. These efforts contribute to enhancing the practical applicability of SOH algorithms in real-world scenarios.

articleTitle: Adaptive Compensation Method for D-Axis Current Reference for Speed Sensorless Induction Motor Drives with Virtual Voltage Injection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Induction motor sensorless control technology enjoys widespread application across various fields today due to its numerous benefits, including low cost, high reliability, and ease of maintenance. However, its practical application is significantly hindered by poor stability and insufficient load capacity within the low synchronous speed range. The virtual voltage injection method fundamentally addresses the instability issues in the sensorless control of induction motors at low synchronous speeds, without causing torque pulsations and current ripples typically associated with traditional signal injection techniques. Nevertheless, virtual voltage injection leads to an increased requirement for the d-axis current reference in induction motor control, which in turn elevates no-load and light-load losses. To counter this drawback, this paper proposes an adaptive compensation scheme for the d-axis current reference in sensorless control of induction motors with virtual voltage injection. This scheme allows the d-axis current reference to vary adaptively with the load, thus reducing no-load and light-load losses.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Vibration Analysis of Nine-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper investigates the electromagnetic performance and vibration characteristics of a nine-phase, 8-pole, 72-slot permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). Firstly, the expression of the air-gap magnetic density of the motor is obtained by using the method of magnetic potential multiplied by magnetic permeability. Then, the formula of the radial electromagnetic force density (EFD) of the motor is deduced by Maxwell's stress equation, and the sources of radial EFD at each order and frequency of the motor are further generalized. In order to verify these conclusions, the results of the spatiotemporal distribution of the radial EFD of the motor are obtained by using finite element simulation, which verifies the correctness of the deduced results. The electromagnetic multi-physics field coupling model is constructed through the Workbench platform, and the modal and harmonic response simulation are performed to analyze the vibration characteristics of the studied permanent magnet motor.

articleTitle: A Novel Inverter Structure Resilient to Commutation Failure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A thyristor commutation module with controllable output voltage and adjustable impedance during commutation is proposed to comprehensively address the commutation failure issue in Line-Commuted Converter-based High Voltage Direct Current (LCC-HVDC) transmission systems. This module is cascaded to form a novel inverter topology that effectively resists commutation failure. Through analysis and validation in PSCAD/EMTDC, the results indicate that the proposed novel inverter not only completely resolves the commutation failure problem but also retains a specific power transmission capability during fault conditions. The parameter design method is deemed reasonable, and the stresses on the components of the commutation module are within the allowable design range.

articleTitle: Position Sensorless Control of Multiphase PMSM Based on Harmonic Back-EMF Observation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Position sensorless control not only reduces the cost and size of motor control systems, but also enhances control system stability. These advantages have made it a prominent research topic in the realm of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) control. This paper proposes a strategy for position sensorless control of a multiphase PMSM, where the mathematical model of a nine-phase PMSM is derived in different coordinate systems, and the rotor position is extracted by observing the harmonic back-EMF. The sensorless control system of the nine-phase PMSM is designed in detail, and the proposed method in this paper is verified by experiments.

articleTitle: Mutual Inductance Identification of Wireless Power Transfer Based on Second Harmonic
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel method for identifying mutual inductance in wireless power transfer systems. When the input voltage of the uncontrolled rectifier on the receiver side is a square wave with a 50% duty cycle, the voltage comprises only the fundamental frequency and odd harmonics. if a second harmonic is introduced into the voltage on the transmitter, the equivalent circuit for the second harmonic can be considered a short circuit on the receiver. By measuring the amplitude of the second harmonic in the current and voltage output from the inverter, the input impedance of the second harmonic can be obtained. Integrating the input impedance with the coil's self-inductance and resonant capacitor parameters allows for the direct calculation of the system's mutual inductance using the impedance formula. This method is simpler and requires less computational effort compared to traditional mutual inductance identification methods.

articleTitle: Research on Safety Distance Between HVDC Grounding Electrode and Oil or Gas Pipeline
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The grounding current of the HVDC grounding electrode can cause interference on nearby oil and gas pipelines. The oil and gas pipeline should maintain a certain distance from the grounding electrode to avoid excessive pipeline voltage caused by the grounding current. The paper establishes an interference model of buried pipelines under grounding electrodes current based on CDEGS simulation software, and analyzes the main factors affecting safety distance; Studied the safe distance of buried pipelines in different uniform soils and multi-layer complex soils; A method was proposed to obtain the safe distance of complex soil by using the maximum pipe to ground potential and coefficient correction. The research results indicate that soil resistivity has the greatest impact on safe distance; If the safe distance in the uniform soil resistivity is less than 8km, it is recommended to use a correction factor of 0.85 to obtain the safe distance for complex soils; If the safe distance in the uniform soil resistivity is between 8km and 12km, the correction coefficient and the safe distance follow a power function relationship; If the safe distance in the uniform soil resistivity is greater than 12km, it is recommended to take a correction factor of 0.53.

articleTitle: Promoting The Wind Power Accommodation Considering Demand Response Exchange
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of wind power in power system, the problem of wind power consumption is becoming increasingly serious. By developing smart grid technology in recent years, it is possible to utility demand response to improve the consumption of wind power. This paper proposes a novel method based on security constrained unit commitment (SCUC) including demand response exchange to promote wind power consumption. In this article, demand response mainly includes interruptible load and transferable load. In particular, for the transferable load, the incentive compensation price is determined by the demand response exchange market, where the transferable load customers could bid through the linear supply function. The results of this paper show that the proposed model can effectively promote the consumption of wind power and reduce the operating cost of whole system. Meanwhile, the demand response exchange market improves the enthusiasm of customers to participate in demand response effectively.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Three-Coil Wireless Power Transfer System with Split Transmitting Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) technology is helping the electric vehicles (EVs) to solve several issues brought by cable charging. Three different WPT networks, namely series-series (SS), three-coil, and inductor-capacitor-capacitor-series (LCC-S), are the possibilities for different application scenarios. This paper analyzes the three-coil WPT system and compares it with the other two networks. We find that the three-coil network is combining the advantages of the other two networks, including high efficiency and better misalignment tolerance. Then, we have concluded several conditions to guide the design of three-coil WPT system. Next, we propose a design method, that is setting the turn ratio to split the transmitter coil of an SS network into two independent coils and the compensation capacitors to meet the conditions above. Finally, we obtain experimental results with 3.3kW output and 96.67% total efficiency, using a split transmitting three-coil network.

articleTitle: Real-Time Monitoring of Low-Voltage Power Load Using Bluetooth mesh IoT Technology: A Shift From Macro to Micro
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To maximize the effectiveness of smart grids and integrated energy systems, it is essential to acquire accurate data on electricity consumption loads. However, current smart meters are still unable to collect specific power consumption data from individual electrical devices. Therefore, to address the issue, a low-cost, real-time remote monitoring load monitoring system based on Bluetooth mesh wireless network and IoT technology has been developed in this work. The Bluetooth mesh network consists of multiple client nodes, one server node and relay nodes (if necessary). The server node comprises a power metering chip and an ARM architecture Bluetooth microcontroller. It is responsible for measuring data, conducting initial filtering and processing on voltage and current signals, and transmitting the processed data to the service port via the Bluetooth mesh network. The client node, composed of a Bluetooth microcontroller and an ESP32 module, consolidates diverse data and transmits it to the cloud platform for storage via WIFI. Simultaneously, the coverage of the wireless power data collection system can be extended further through Bluetooth mesh relay nodes. A simple WeChat mini program display interface was developed to enable users to view the power detection status at any time during actual use, providing underlying data support for the deployment of users or power departments.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Time Energy Management Techniques for Shared Mobile Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In response to the significant seasonal load characteristics and tight electricity demand in certain regions, a shared mobile energy storage system planning configuration and optimal dispatch method considering multiple time scales with power region characteristics is proposed. This method enables the optimal dispatch of multiple energy systems, taking into account specific application scenarios and considering cost comprehensively. Firstly, on a long-term time scale, the shared mobile energy storage systems are configured for seasonal loads on a monthly basis to maximize profits for the distribution. And it determines the capacity, power, and quantity of individual shared mobile energy storage units within the region. Then, on a short-term time scale, the method optimizes charging and discharging power of the mobile energy storage units and the connected nodes in the distribution network on a daily basis. This optimization aims to maximize the gains from peak-valley arbitrage and reducing network losses. The results of the case study demonstrate that the proposed method can significantly increase economic benefits while improving the spatiotemporal utilization of the energy storage system.

articleTitle: Study on Electrode Damage Behavior of Metallized Film Capacitors Based on Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Due to the winding structure of the metallized film capacitor (MFC), it is difficult to obtain the multi-physical field distribution characteristics of the metallized electrode after self-healing breakdown in the experiment. Based on this, this paper uses the finite element method to simulate the local electric field of MFC. According to the hole morphology after self-healing breakdown of the electrode, holes with the same morphological characteristics are set proportionally on the electrode of the geometric model. The physical field distribution characteristics of the electrode damage area are analyzed. The results show that the hole on the electrode causes the current direction to change, and the current concentration is caused at the upper / lower edge of the hole notch, resulting in higher current density and power density in this region than in other regions.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of Paralleled Grid-Following Inverter and Virtual Synchronous Generator Considering Transient Mode Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid evolution of the power system towards a high proportion of renewable energy and a high proportion of power electronics, the grid-following (GFL) inverter and the grid-forming (GFM) inverter have been widely used. However, due to the limited overcurrent capability of the inverter, current limiting measures are usually taken in the GFM inverter, which may cause the GFM inverter to stabilize in current limiting mode without successfully recovering from a fault. In order to understand this phenomenon of the GFM inverter in the parallel system, this paper aims to analyze the fault recovery process of the GFM inverter in the parallel system. First, the mathematical model of the paralleled GFL inverter and GFM inverter system is established, and the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control is adopted for the GFM inverter. Next, the formula about the output current of the VSG in the parallel system and the output active power of the VSG in current limiting mode are derived. Then the effect of the parameters of the GFL inverter on the mode switching angle of the VSG is analyzed based on the current limiting inequality. Finally, the switching rules are verified by simulation. This paper provides a reference for the parametric design of the GFL- VSG parallel system to improve transient stability when considering current limiting.

articleTitle: Research on The Relationship Between Carbon Emissions and Renewable Energy Consumption Based on New Energy Vehicles Big Data
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to cope with climate change and reduce greenhouse gas emissions, various countries and regions around the world have agreed on carbon peak, carbon neutrality plans and formulated their own policies. This paper is a data analysis and research on the relationship among electric vehicles (EVs), renewable energy and carbon emissions. By studying the renewable energy installed capacity, power generation and carbon emissions in the top ten countries of global EV sales, the development enlightenment of EVs is obtained, while promoting renewable energy consumption and effectively reducing carbon emissions.

articleTitle: Modulation-Index-Adjustment-Based Dead-Time Compensation Method in Voltage Angle Regulation for PMSM Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The field-weakening control method with voltage angle regulator (VAR) has the advantages of better efficiency and power capacity by improving the voltage modulation index (MI). However, the control error of MI, which is mainly caused by the dead-time effect, results in the current operation points deviating from the optimal ones. It increases motor thermal loss and reduces system efficiency. But the applications of dead-time compensation methods are limited by the difficult problem of current polarity judgment. To solve this problem, a modulation-index-adjustment-based (MIAB) dead-time compensation method is proposed in this article, where the current polarity judgment is not necessary. Firstly, the quantitative relationship between MI and dead time is analyzed. Then, it provides the theoretical foundation of the target MI adjustment to eliminate the control error of MI, allowing the current operation points return to the optimal ones. Therefore, the influence of dead-time effect on MI is suppressed. Finally, the adaptability of the proposed method is verified by PMSM bench experiments.

articleTitle: Feasibility Study on the Application of Semiconductor Refrigeration Technology in Local Heat Dissipation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Traditional cooling methods are difficult to solve the local heat dissipation of motor. Semiconductor refrigeration technology based on the thermoelectric effect has significant advantages on this issue. In this study, an experimental platform for local heat dissipation based on semiconductor refrigeration technology was constructed. An electric heating device was used as a heat source to simulate local heating. The heat dissipation performance of three different models of semiconductor refrigeration chips was studied through experiments under constant heat source. And the results indicate that semiconductor refrigeration technology exhibits good heat dissipation performance for local heat resource. So it can be applied to solve the problem of local heat dissipation in motor.

articleTitle: Analysis and Optimization on Motor Vibration Noise Associate with Inverter Switching Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: On the one hand, the application of permanent magnet motors in various high-end industries has promoted the improvement of the design and manufacturing level of permanent magnet motors. On the other hand, it has also put forward increasingly higher requirements for the performance of permanent magnet motors. Among them, vibration noise has gradually become an important indicator to measure the performance level of permanent magnet motors. It is widely concerned in various industries. Therefore, conducting research on the electromagnetic vibration of permanent magnet motors has important scientific value and application value. This paper mainly analyzes the source of motor vibration noise from the perspective of the switching frequency of the motor controller, derives the analytical expression of the electromagnetic force that causes vibration noise, and verifies the impact of switching frequency on vibration noise through experiments. Combined with theoretical analysis. A method to suppress vibration noise by changing the switching frequency has been presented by this article.

articleTitle: Semi-Physical Simulation of EHA Electric Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Electro-hydrostatic actuator (EHA) electric drive system is commonly used in more electric aircraft (MEA) and can improve aircraft performance. This article designs a high-speed permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) with a rated speed of 12,000 rpm for EHA. It establishes the design and system simulation of a semi-physical real-time simulation model based on the EHA electric drive model, verifying the normal operation of the EHA electric drive system's load spectrum. This provides a reliable basis for the highly integrated and high-performance design of the EHA system, thus improving the research and development efficiency.

articleTitle: Comparison of Structural Design Performance between 30 kV Oil-immersed Transformer and Dry-type Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The high-voltage pulse power supply was characterized by its high output voltage, narrow pulse width, large output current, and high frequency, rendering it extensively utilized across various fields. The transformer stood as a pivotal component within this system. In order to minimize the transformer's size, both oil-immersed and dry-type transformers utilizing the same transformer body were designed and compared. Simulation tools were used to analyze aspects such as appearance size, leakage inductance, temperature rise, and mechanical strength of the two transformer types. Under the condition of voltage with 30 kV, the dry-type transformer required a significantly smaller volume, approximately one-quarter of the oil-immersed transformer. Moreover, the temperature rise and mechanical strength of the dry-type transformer met the necessary requirements for operation.

articleTitle: Radial and Axial Leakage Flux Characteristics of Induction Motors with Stator Inter-Turn Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Inter-turn fault (ITF) will cause the change of the motor magnetic field, and the external leakage flux detection of the motor as a non-invasive measurement method has certain advantages compared with the internal invasive magnetic field measurement. In this article, the radial and axial leakage flux detection coils are used to measure the external leakage flux of the motor. Through theoretical analysis, the frequency characteristic components of the leakage flux before and after the fault are clarified, and the radial and axial leakage flux of normal motor and motors with different fault degrees are measured under different load conditions. By means of RMS and spectrum analysis of leakage flux signal, the influence of ITF on leakage magnetic field is obtained, and the fault characteristic, which can be used to effectively diagnose the fault under no-load, light load, and rated load conditions is found. In addition, a new feature that can be used for fault diagnosis is obtained from the analysis of axial leakage flux signal, providing a new method for non-invasive detection of ITF.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Transformation of Insulation Monitoring System for DC Power Supply in 500kV Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: DC system is an important public system in substations, especially for 500kV main grid substations, providing protection power supply for the protection and safety automatic device of the whole station and stable operation power supply for the control system. With the increase of equipment operation years and the development of insulation monitoring technology, some insulation monitoring systems have frequent problems. In order to ensure the safe and stable operation of the power grid, it is necessary to transform the insulation monitoring system of the DC system. This article analyzes the current situation and existing problems of the insulation monitoring system, proposes an optimized ripple monitoring method based on the fast Fourier transform algorithm, optimizes the AC intrusion DC monitoring means and DC bus monitoring algorithm. Discusses the key links of non-power transformation of insulation monitoring systems to provide reference for similar substation transformations.

articleTitle: Study on levelized cost of new coal-fired units in Yunnan Province
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In recent years, the operation of aluminum-silicon production projects in Yunnan Province will bring a substantial increase in power load and power consumption. The new wind power and photovoltaic units are limited, and the output of new energy is difficult to predict, which may lead to a power gap in Yunnan Province. Therefore, Yunnan Province plans to build 4.8 million kilowatts of coal-fired units, and strive to put the first batch of units into operation in 2024. In this paper, based on the analysis of the cost composition of coal-fired units, combining the research results of LCOE model at home and abroad and the principle of LCOE analysis, the LCOE analysis model suitable for China's coal burning mechanism is established. The model is used to measure the levelized cost of coal-fired units in Yunnan Province, and the sensitivity analysis is carried out on the important factors affecting the LCOE of coal-fired units, to find out the key factors, and to focus on control from the whole life cycle.

articleTitle: Parameter Design Method with Anti-Misalignment Ability for Electric-Filed Coupled WPT System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of coupling misalignment of electric-field coupled wireless power transfer (EC-WPT) system, this paper proposes a parameter design and optimization method, which can achieve anti-misalignment ability. Taking the double-sided LC-compensated EC-WPT system as an object, the mathematical model of the system is established under the consideration of inductor equivalent series resistance (ESR), and the expression of the system output voltage is derived. Considering the constant voltage characteristic and coupling capacitance variation, a nonlinear planning model for the design of the system parameters is established. Therefore, the parameter design method of the system is given. The simulation model of the system is established, and the simulation results show that the output voltage of the system has a maximum variation range of 0.9% under the maximum misalignment of 85% of the receiver plates when the value of the coupling capacitance varies within the interval of [11.5pF, 63pF]. The simulation results demonstrate the system has a constant-voltage output characteristic under the condition of misalignment of the coupler of the un-manned aerial vehicle.

articleTitle: Optimization and Analysis of Transient Temperature Calculations for Frequency Converter in Changing Working Condition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to realize the application of digital twin technology, it is necessary to study the transient physical field of the research object. For frequency converters, their transient temperature is the focus of attention. Finite element transient simulation calculations generally require a lot of time. To address this problem, this study proposes a quick calculation method that combines fluid field simulation and heat transfer theoretical calculations. It first calculates the fluid field inside the frequency converter through simulation software and obtains the boundary conditions of the heat source. Then use the theory of heat transfer to establish a heat transfer model for the frequency converter, thereby obtaining the transient equation of the temperature change of the frequency converter with time. This calculation method does not require energy calculations, and can also avoid repeated iterative processes of transient calculations, which can significantly reduce the solution time. Finally, this paper verifies the accuracy of the calculation method through experiments. The accuracy of this method meets the engineering needs and can provide certain reference significance for the transient temperature analysis of electrical cabinets.

articleTitle: Characteristics of Electrical Tree Morphology in Power Module Package Insulation Under High Frequency Unipolar Square Wave Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Power module is the most significant equipment in modern electrical grid. Electrical tree growing on the gel-substrate surface is the main form of insulation failure in power module packages, which seriously threatens the stable operation of power module. However, treeing behaviors along the surface are currently unclear. In this research, electrical tree morphological characteristics growing on the gel-substrate surface under unipolar square wave voltage with a frequency of 1 kHz∼20 kHz were investigated. Moreover, the effect mechanism of frequency on electrical tree morphology were analyzed. The morphologies of electrical tree growing on the gel-substrate surface are different significantly from that in conventional solid media. The results show that the electrical trees show branch-like, bush-like and pine-like and the branching type can be classified into pearl-chain type, microcavity-cloud type and smoky type at different frequencies. The electrical tree morphology during the initial stage becomes denser with increasing frequency. At lower frequencies, the morphology gradually transitions from branch-like to jungle-like, while from jungle-like to pine-like at higher frequencies. The carbonization of the electrical tree is more severe at higher frequencies. The carbonized branches inhibit PDs and change the electric field distribution, which, in combination with the self-healing effect of silicone gel, the electrical tree develops towards pine-like structure at higher frequencies. The research is expected to provide a theoretical and experimental basis for package insulation performance improvement of power modules.

articleTitle: Adaptive Inertial Control of Marine Energy Storage for Pulsed Power Load
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper investigates an adaptive inertia control of marine energy storage for impulse load. A small-signal model of the marine energy storage device containing multiple groups of flywheels and converters is established, and the power allocation rule of multiple power sources is revealed. By introducing the real-time rotational speed of the flywheel in the inverter control, the adaptive change of virtual synchronous generator control parameters is realized, thus the marine energy storage is able to reasonably allocate the power in the case of unbalance of rotational speed of each group of flywheels, and it can also adjust the support capacity of marine energy storage according to the residual energy of the marine energy storage group, which ensures the stability of the ship's electric power system containing the pulsed power load. The experimental results present the simulation results of the marine energy storage adaptive inertia control under impulse load, which verifies the effectiveness of the control algorithm.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Multi-Load Single-Wire Power Transfer System Based on Rebar Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) can supply power to sensors embedded in reinforced concrete for structural health monitoring (SHM) systems in a non-destructive manner. However, in many cases, multiple sensors are needed to operate simultaneously within a single monitoring area. Achieving widespread power distribution to multiple loads with small receiving coils, as in traditional WPT systems, presents a significant challenge. The primary objective of this paper is to experimentally explore the feasibility of using the rebar array as a “single wire” in single-wire power transfer (SWPT) to achieve power supply to multiple loads. Mainly through experimental methods, the operating frequency and capacitance value of the system are obtained through a Vector Network Analyzer. Firstly, a single copper wire is used as a single conductor to verify the transmission of electrical energy by observing the brightness of the small light bulb. Then, different kinds of shaped rebars are used as single conductors for testing. Replacing a single copper wire and using different rebar structures as single conductors in the system can light up small light bulbs. The experimental results indicate that using a small volume transmitting and receiving mechanism and using a rebar network as a single conductor can achieve the transmission of electrical energy, which is feasible for supplying power to deep buried sensors.

articleTitle: Numerical Investigation on the Czochralski Crystal Growth and Oxygen Concentration with CUSP Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: High quality single crystal silicon can help improve product performance and increase enterprise's profitability. Superconducting magnetic fields have been imported to the semiconductor industry as a way to decrease the impurity content during single crystal silicon growth process. In this article, a 2D numerical simulation on the Czochralski crystal growth method furnace heat transfer and melt flow is conducted, along with the effect of an external CUSP magnetic field. The results show that the natural convection melt flow under the magnetic field has been suppressed. And the oxygen concentration is reduced, hence the crystal quality is ameliorated.

articleTitle: Cogging Torque Reduction of Axial Flux Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors For Gravity Energy Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor (AFPMSM) has the characteristics of simple structure, small volume, high torque density, and high efficiency. Thus, it is suitable for the gravity energy storage systems. But the inherent cogging torque problem may cause mechanical vibration and noise, which in turn affects the performance of the total system. In order to effectively suppress the adverse effects of cogging torque, both theoretical analysis and finite element simulation is done to optimize the cogging torque of AFPMSM in this paper. Firstly, the theoretical analysis for the cogging torque of surface mounted type AFPMSM is elaborated; Afterwards, the 3D motor model is reduced to a 2D equivalent model using the equivalent simplification method; Finally, taking a 10 pole 12 slot double stator single rotor surface mounted AFPMSM as an example, some main parameters were selected for simulation analysis and comparison, including stator slot pole shoes, stator slot misalignment, permanent magnet pole arc coefficient, and permanent magnet shape. Finally, a minimum cogging torque model was obtained.

Author Keywords: Axial flux permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant Scheme of Multi-Level Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Multi-level dual active bridge (DAB) converter is more susceptible to switch open-circuit fault (OCF) than the conventional DAB, which leads to negative effects such as DC bias and overcurrent. Therefore, fault-tolerant control of this converter is important, and a fault tolerant scheme to eliminate the negative influence of OCF is proposed. First, all single-switch and dual-switch faults of multilevel DAB are analyzed. Based on the analysis, aiming at fault occurs, the corresponding fault tolerant strategies for primary-side and secondary-side faults are proposed, respectively. The scheme can mitigate the negative effects while maintaining the output power as much as possible. Finally, simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Secondary Control of Islanded Microgrids With Variable Topology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A fault in the lines between different distributed units in the microgrid(MG) will trigger the relay protection system to remove the faulty line, causing the distributed power generation units to be reconnected and changing the topology of the MG. MG need to adjust the control strategy of distributed power generation units in real time to adapt to new operating conditions, especially to suppress the reactive power imbalance caused by line impedance mismatch to ensure stable and safe operation of MG under the new topology. Aiming at the fault tolerance problem under non-directional switching topology, a distributed secondary control method is proposed, and a variable topology island MG model based on inverter droop control and distributed secondary control is established. The simulation model and mathematical model of the variable topology island MG system were built in MATLAB/Simulink to verify the effectiveness of the proposed control method.

articleTitle: Transient Mathematical Modelling and Parameter Optimization Method for Reactive Power of VSG Controlled DFIG Under Voltage Fault
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The application of virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control strategy has enhanced the active support and stability capability of doubly-fed wind generator (DFIG) for the grid-connected operation. The voltage support capability of the DFIG is closely related to the VSG reactive power control loop. In order to analyze the factors affecting reactive power output, it is essential to model the reactive power characteristics of VSG controlled DFIG when the grid voltage dips. This paper establishes a mathematical model and a parameter optimization method for the transient reactive power of VSG controlled DFIG. The method is aimed to suppress the maximum reactive power surge and ensure the ability of reactive power response.

articleTitle: A Generalized Model Framework of Electrolyser
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As electrolysis systems scale up to megawatt and gigawatt capacities, the imperative for dynamic characterization and grid-connection analysis becomes increasingly pressing. Unlike conventional loads, electrolysis systems' Balance of Plant (BoP) incorporates temperature and gas pressure control processes, amplifying model complexity. This paper consolidates the dynamic behaviors of various electrolyzers across diverse transient processes and formulates a comprehensive, generic electrolyzer dynamic pattern. Then, a generalized three-layer model architecture for electrolyzers based on the equivalent BoP control loop is proposed. A simulation in MATLAB/Simulink has been built and the simulation results verified the feasibility of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Data-Based Soft Fault Diagnosis of a Three-Phase DC/AC Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the widespread use of power electronic equipment, accurately identifying soft faults in power electronic converters is crucial for the stable and reliable operation of power electronic equipment. This paper proposed a soft fault diagnosis method for three-phase DC/AC converter using a data-based approach. Firstly, simulation analysis is conducted on the soft faults of three-phase DCI AC converter, and appropriate test signals are selected as data sources. Then, the LSTM neural network and its variants are used to obtain fault diagnosis models. Finally, the method is validated through experiments, and the results show that it has good performance in soft fault diagnosis of the three-phase DCI AC converter.

articleTitle: A Novel Smooth Switching Method Between Voltage Source and Current Source of DFIG Based Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Doubly-fed wind turbines present current source characteristics under vector control, and the phase-locked loop section relies on grid phase information, which is suitable for operation under strong grid; and present voltage source characteristics under virtual synchronous control, which can provide frequency and voltage support for the grid, which is more suitable for operation under weak grid. In order to meet the needs of grid operation under different short circuit ratios, it is of great practical significance to study the control mode switching of doubly-fed wind turbines. This paper proposes a smooth switching control strategy for doubly-fed wind turbine voltage-current source dual-mode operation, which realizes the smooth switching of phase and current commands through the joint action of controller state following and numerical soft starter, and effectively suppresses current impact and power fluctuation in the switching process of doubly-fed wind turbine operation mode. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy is verified by theoretical analysis and simulation results.

articleTitle: A rotor position detection method for synchronous motors based on high-frequency injection voltage estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A rotor position detection method based on high-frequency injection is proposed in this paper to solve the related problems of rotor pulsation during low-speed starting. Considering the characteristics of the electrically excited synchronous motor, high-frequency voltage signal is injected into the excitation to generate a high-frequency excitation current. The high-frequency voltage signal have rotor position information is collected. After filtering and coordinate transformation, effective rotor position information is collected. Finally, a phase-locked loop is employed to lock the rotor position. In a thyristor driven system, during the current commutation, the motor's back electromotive force of the motor is distorted, leading to significant high-order harmonics in the terminal voltage. Accurately collecting effective high-frequency signals becomes challenging. Therefore, a rotor position detection method for synchronous motors based on high-frequency injection voltage estimation is proposed in this paper. The estimated voltage is used as the input signal for the phase-locked loop during commutation to prevent distorted high-frequency harmonic from entering the phase-locked loop. The simulation results show that adding voltage estimation effectively avoids the harmful effects of commutation voltage distortion on rotor position detection and improves the accuracy and reliability of high-frequency injection rotor position detection.

articleTitle: Research on Multipath Balancing Topology Based on Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As the voltage and power levels of the energy storage system continue to increase, the number of cells in the series-connected battery pack increases, and the imbalance between the battery packs becomes more and more complex. For this reason, a transformer-based direct equalization topology for multipath series-connected battery packs is proposed. The topology, which uses a transformer as the energy transfer carrier, is able to switch between buck-boost and flyback modes, and can achieve equalization between any battery cells by controlling a low-conduction bidirectional switching array. This topology has multiple equalization modes, flexible equalization paths and faster equalization speed. In order to achieve effective energy distribution and improve the equalization efficiency, a fuzzy control strategy with SOC (State of Charge) as the equalization index is designed. Finally, a series of simulation experiments are carried out to verify the effectiveness of the proposed topology and its control strategy under different working conditions. The results show that the balancing topology and control strategy proposed in this paper are effective in improving the inconsistency of single cells in the battery pack and enhancing the capacity utilization of the whole series-connected battery pack.

articleTitle: Power Grids Partitioning by Detection of Electrical Communities
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In rapidly evolving power grids, effective partitioning strategies are critical for ensuring stability, reliability, and efficiency in subsystems and even the operation of the entire system. Community detection has been considered promising in power grids partition recently, but the electrical features were not well integrated with most conventional algorithms. This study proposes a novel Inversed Girvan-Newman Algorithm to partition power grids. Compared with traditional Girvan-Newman Algorithm, the updated electrical betweenness plays a totally different role in principle according to basic understanding of electrical community. Case studies in IEEE-lIS and IEEE-300 bus transmission networks are implemented to detect electrical communities, which has shown better performance in modularity, boundary flow, and subsystem operational cost.

articleTitle: Study on Surface Charge and Mechanical Properties of Epoxy Impregnated Paper Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Epoxy impregnated paper is the main insulation material of bushing capacitor core, which withstand electrical and mechanical stress for a long time. In this paper, the surface potential characteristics of epoxy impregnated paper and pure epoxy resin in the application environment of strong normal electric field components were compared, and the flashover and mechanical properties were tested. The results show that the conductivity of corrugated paper is higher than pure epoxy resin, and some defects are introduced into the composite material, which makes it easier for carriers to migrate. Thus the composite material has higher conductivity and local non-uniformity. Result in the accumulation of surface charge is large and the distribution is uneven. It leads to the distortion of electric field and the decrease of flashover voltage, which is the inducing factor of the actual flashover accident of bushing. In terms of mechanical properties, the corrugated paper can relieve part of the stress, and the tensile strength and elongation at break of the epoxy impregnated paper composite insulation material are increased by 41.74% and 48.31% respectively, compared with the epoxy resin. Because the surface of epoxy impregnated paper composite insulation material is mainly composed of epoxy resin, there is little difference in hardness between them. The conclusions of this paper can provide a reference for the operation of bushing capacitors core under mechanical and electrical stress.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Robust Optimization for Co-Evolving PV and ESS in a Rural Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the development of rural economic level, rural distribution networks face the issue of limited development. Among them, the problem of low voltage at the end of rural network lines and poor power quality is one of the key constraints to its development. In order to handle the issue of low bus voltage and lower the cost in rural distribution networks, this paper proposes a two-stage robust co-evolution for photovoltaics (PVs) and energy storage systems (ESSs). In the first stage, the construction cost and profit from carbon emissions are considered to determine the best configuration scheme. In the second stage, based on the probabilistic distribution of PV power generation, the model calculates the optimal scheme to minimize the bus voltage deviation and realize the co-evolution of PV and ESS. The numerical analysis of a rural distribution network in southern China demonstrates that the proposed method can lower cost, bus voltage deviations and reduce the carbon emissions resulting from electricity consumption.

articleTitle: Research on Demand Response with Passive Building Thermal Storage based on Co-Simulation of Beetle Antennae Search (BAS) Algorithm and EnergyPlus
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to fully investigate the economic benefits of demand response with passive building thermal storage, this paper proposes an optimization method to control of indoor temperature to reduce the air-conditioning operating cost based on Beetle Antennae Search (BAS) algorithm. A co-simulation between BAS algorithm and EnergyPlus is developed based on Python. A case study of an office building in Tianjin is conducted to demonstrate the effectiveness of the BAS algorithm and the flexibility of the co-simulation. Based on the electricity price policy in Tianjin, the indoor temperature setpoint of an office building is optimized. The results show that over 42% of cooling energy in the optimal scene is consumed during the valley-price time, and the operating cost of the air conditioning system is reduced by about 14%. So that, building thermal mass could provide flexibility to public power grid. More importantly, the BAS algorithm has highly search efficiency that can be used to guide building participation in demand response.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategy of Multi-Resource Participation in Frequency Regulation of Power Grid with High Penetration Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The continuous integration of high permeability renewable energy into the grid leads to a reduction in system inertia, a decrease in primary frequency regulation ability, and poses frequency safety challenges during power disturbances. Taking incorporation of frequency security constraints into the system optimization strategy becomes imperative to address this issue. In response to the frequency regulation requirements of a new energy power grid, this paper introduces an optimization strategy that considers frequency security constraints and integrates control for wind power. Initially, the paper derives system frequency security constraints based on the swing equation. Then, the unit commitment model is established, and the proposed method is tested on an IEEE 10-machine 39-bus system. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed method in achieving frequency regulation for new energy power grids while ensuring the secure and economical operation of the power grid.

articleTitle: Low Frequency Resonance Suppression in Servo Systems Based on Generalized Proportional-Integral Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Servo systems play an irreplaceable role in traditional industry and high-tech fields, and their performance directly determines the actual performance of industrial equipment such as CNC machine tools and robots. Industrial equipment often uses transmission devices such as shafts, transmissions, and couplings to connect motors and loads. These transmission devices are not ideal rigid bodies and are prone to mechanical resonance, which limits the improvement of dynamic performance of servo systems. Therefore, the suppression of mechanical resonance is very important. This article proposes to use generalized proportional-integral (GPI) observer (GPIO) based linear active disturbance rejection control (LADRC) to suppress low-frequency mechanical resonance, and improves the parameter tuning method of GPIO to make its disturbance observation have real bandwidth. The feasibility of the suppression method is analyzed theoretically, and verified through MATLAB/Simulink simulation and experiments.

articleTitle: Model-Free Approximate Fundamental Reactive Power Minimization for Modular Multi-Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Modular multi-active bridge (MMAB) converter is widely used in modern power grids to provide multiple ports for flexible power conversion and interconnection among grids, loads, and electric vehicles, etc. However, MMAB converters adopting traditional single phase-shift modulation are facing low-efficiency issues within a wide operation range. In order to address online optimization concerns brought about by the strong coupling of the converters, this paper proposes an optimization strategy to approximately eliminate the overall fundamental reactive power of MMAB converters without accurate model parameters, thus reducing the root-mean-square inductor currents and the overall conducting loss. The proposed optimization strategy is based on frequency domain and can be extended to multi-active bridge converters as well. Finally, the feasibility and the effectiveness of the strategy have been validated on a 4-port MMAB converter.

articleTitle: Study on the Grounding Characteristics of Power Transmission Tunnels in Complex Terrain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Power transmission through pipeline corridors assumes a pivotal role in overcoming challenges associated with the exportation of new energy, wherein the grounding system profoundly impacts the secure functioning of equipment. In this investigation, employing CDEGS modeling, a comprehensive examination was conducted to systematically scrutinize the influence of soil resistivity, corridor length, and the span distance between the through-conductor and the principal structural reinforcement on the electrical characteristics of the grounding system within power transmission corridors. The research outcomes reveal that an escalation in soil resistivity triggers a linear upsurge in ground impedance, manifesting a notably accelerated growth rate in shorter corridors. Furthermore, elongating the corridor length exhibits a mitigating effect on the system's ground impedance; nonetheless, the law of diminishing returns becomes discernible when the corridor length surpasses 4 km. The reduction of the cross-bonding distance between the through-conductor and the main structural reinforcement emerges as an effective strategy for diminishing the system's ground impedance, with a range of 100–125 m identified as the most optimal for cross-bonding. The study convincingly illustrates that within high-resistance, long-distance environments, the corridor grounding system adeptly governs the voltage distribution within the corridor. This not only furnishes theoretical underpinning for the refinement of grounding schemes in power transmission corridors situated in high-resistance regions but also substantively contributes to the assurance of the secure and stable operation of these crucial conduits for energy transmission.

articleTitle: A Novel Particle-Swarm-Optimization-Based Large Signal Analysis Method for Power Electronic Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Large signal stability evaluation is important for designing and optimizing power electronic systems. Less conservative large signal analysis method helps decrease weight and costs of power electronic systems especially in transportation and aerospace fields. With the development of power electronic systems, the traditional Takagi-Sugeno (TS) multimodeling method are hard to be used in large power electronic systems as accurate ranges of the nonlinear variables are required. Thus., in this paper., a large signal stability analysis method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed to fill this gap. Firstly, generate a particle swarm, and initialize randomly position of each particle. Position of particles should satisfy restrains of the linear matrix inequality (LMI). Secondly, calculate attraction domain index (ADI) of each particle. Thirdly, update individual and global optimal solutions of the particle swarm by searching the maximum ADI. Make sure the updated position of each particle satisfies the LMI restrains. Finally, find out the best matrix and calculate the candidate energy function of the studied system. Simulations and experiments verify the effectiveness of the proposed method. Compared with traditional TS multimodeling method, the proposed method is less conservative. The accurate range of the nonlinear variables is not required, which is promising to be used in transient stability analysis of higher-order power electronic systems.

articleTitle: Investigation of the Inverter Parameters on Losses for Flux Switching Permanent Magnet Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Pulse width modulation (PWM) inverters are widely used in electrical machines drives. Sine pulse width modulation (SPWM) and Space vector pulse width modulation (SVPWM) are two kinds of the most widely used modulation strategies. However, PWM inverters can result in loss increment and thus reduce efficiency of electrical machines. In this paper, we investigate a 12/10 Flux switching permanent magnet (FSPM) machine and analyze iron loss, eddy current loss and permanent magnet loss under two different modulation strategies. The influence of modulation index and carrier wave ratio on losses is also investigated by finite element analysis (FEA).

articleTitle: Magnetic Flux Uniformity Analysis of the Magnetic Core in the Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The magnetic flux uniformity in the core is an important figure of merit to design a compact and high efficiency magnetic coupler in a high power wireless power transfer (WPT) system. In this paper, the asymmetrical DD pads are studied which is widely adopted in the electric vehicle (EV) charging WPT system. The equivalent magnetic circuit model is derived to establish an equivalent model for the selected reference DD coil structure and provide theoretical guidance for obtaining magnetic core losses. The magnetic flux uniformity of the DD pad core on the transmitter side is investigated by the finite element analysis (FEA) model. The coefficient of variation (CV) with respect to magnetic flux density is proposed to quantitatively analyze the magnetic field distribution inside the core. It is found that the magnetic core utilization is low on the transmitter side due to the magnetic flux is concentrated in the middle of the core. This method is useful for the magnetic core optimization in order to obtain a high power density magnetic coupler structure.

articleTitle: DC Link Clamp Type High Step-Up Ratio Y-Source Inverter Grid-Tied Energy-Shaping Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Traditional grid-connected controllers often have complex structures, numerous control parameters, and limited stability, making them less suitable for practical applications. Therefore, it is crucial to design grid-connected controllers in a reasonable manner to enhance the grid-connected disturbance suppression capabilities of inverters. This paper begins by analyzing the pros and cons of traditional control methods, specifically focusing on the high-boost ratio Y-source inverter (DLVC-YSI-I) topology with DC link voltage clamping. Subsequently, the port-controlled Hamiltonian (PCH) model and energy-shaping control (ESC) method are employed to address the control problem of the improved Y-source grid-connected inverter from an energy perspective. By constructing a state average model based on the proposed topology's operating principle and converting the improved Y-source grid-connected inverter model into a PCH model using the state average method, an inverter grid-connected controller is designed based on ES theory. Finally, the proposed algorithm is validated on an experimental platform consisting of an impedance source inverter grid-connected system.

articleTitle: Research on Speed Fluctuation Suppression of a Dual-Sided Permanent Magnet In-Wheel Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The direct-drive hub motor stands as the central power unit in distributed electric vehicles, shaping the vehicle's power traits through its performance. With a direct linkage between the motor and the wheel, the challenge of motor speed fluctuation emerges as a crucial factor shaping the drive performance of the system. The paper, based on the requirements of vehicle hub direct drive applications, focuses on the study of a dual-sided permanent magnet hub motor with excellent “low-speed high-torque” capabilities. It specifically analyzes cogging torque, a significant factor causing motor torque fluctuations, and identifies the associated dominant harmonic orders. Confronting the intricate operational and challenging road conditions in hub direct drive scenarios, there arises a need to incorporate the “remarkable disturbance rejection capability” offered by Active Disturbance Rejection Control (ADRC) technology. The proposal involves the targeted introduction of a suppression component for the dominant harmonic of motor cogging torque within the error feedback control law of the ADRC. This introduces a quasi-resonant form error feedback control law, effectively mitigating the motor's speed fluctuations. Simulation results provide confirmation of the study's rationale.

articleTitle: Thermodynamic Study of Transformer Oil Thermal Decomposition Gases Considering Temperature Effects
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) in transformer oil is widely applied in the fault diagnosis of oil-immersed power transformers. Currently, research on dissolved gases focuses on revealing the microscopic dynamic characteristics of gas generation in oil through atomic-level molecular dynamics simulations, but is limited by the rationality of the established systems. In this paper, starting from a thermodynamic perspective, the temperature-dependent characteristics of thermodynamic parameters such as heat capacity, enthalpy change of reaction, and equilibrium constants are fully considered. Numerical calculations of dissolved gases in transformer oil are performed based on the theory of chemical equilibrium constants. Using 1 mol of propane as a typical alkane molecule for calculations, the results indicate that in the thermal cracking reactions of alkanes, chain-breaking reactions occur first with increasing temperature, followed by dehydrogenation reactions, producing small-molecule alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, and hydrogen. The evolution of the molar fractions of each substance aligns well with the actual gas content in the oil, providing a solution for calculating dissolved gases in oil.

articleTitle: An individual phase current control strategy for the single-stage medium-frequency isolated PET
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to ensure high-quality electrical energy output and alleviate the impression of electronic equipment when faults occur on the grid side, this paper applies the individual phase currert control strategy to the single-stage medium-frequency isolated power electronic transformer (PET) and verifies the feasibility and effectiveness of this control strategy. The PET in this paper uses a single-stage medium-frequency transformer to convert voltage and achieve electric isolation, replacing the traditional high-frequency transformer which can omit the convention control method of the isolation link, as well as run efficiently and flexibly. Firstly, the PET principle and advantages are introduced. Secondly, the control method of the individual phase current is described. Finally, the feasibility of the control strategy is verified through the simulation experiment under different power grid fault conditions.

articleTitle: Efficient Solution Methods for IGBT Electro-Thermal Coupling Models Based on Optimized Nonlinear Multigrid Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid development of power electronics technology, the application of IGBTs (Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors) in high-efficiency power conversion has become increasingly widespread. The electro-thermal coupling effect of IGBTs significantly impacts their stability and reliability. Therefore, accurately and quickly solving the electro-thermal coupling model is key to enhancing the design and application efficiency of IGBTs. This paper proposes a solution method based on an optimized Nonlinear Multigrid (NMG) algorithm aimed at improving the solution speed and accuracy of the IGBT electro-thermal coupling model. By introducing the hysteresis diffusion fixed-point iteration and successive over-relaxation iteration strategies, we optimized the traditional NMG algorithm to adapt to the specific requirements of the electro-thermal coupling model. Experimental results show that the optimized NMG algorithm not only significantly enhances the solution efficiency and reduces computation time but also improves the model's solution accuracy. Compared to traditional solution methods, our approach demonstrates clear advantages in the stability and efficiency of model solving. The successful implementation of this research provides a new perspective and tool for the efficient solution of IGBT electro-thermal coupling models, holding significant theoretical and practical significance for optimizing the thermal management design of power electronic devices.

articleTitle: Study on Hybrid Control Strategy of Bi-Directional LLC Resonant Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A hybrid control strategy combining variable frequency control and pulse width control is proposed to address the requirement of the LLC resonant full-bridge topology to achieve soft switching over a wide voltage range and improve the conversion efficiency. The mathematical model of the converter is established utilizing fundamental wave analysis method to derive the corresponding voltage gain characteristics. The hybrid control strategy is designed according to the voltage gain characteristic curve, and the parameters of the LLC resonant structure are optimised. The experimental results show that the proposed hybrid control strategy is able to operate efficiently over a wide voltage range and has good dynamic response characteristics.

articleTitle: Analysis and Simulation of Time-Frequency Characteristics of Dynamic DC Bias Current in Urban Power Grids caused by Metro Stray Current
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to better understand the dynamic DC bias caused by metro stray current, this paper analyzes it from the perspective of time-frequency characteristics. Firstly, 220kV Foshan Station, which is greatly affected by Foshan Metro, and 220kV Panyu Station, which is greatly affected by Guangzhou Metro, were selected for transformer neutral point current measurement. Then, the time-frequency characteristics of the bias current were extracted with wavelet analysis. Results show that the the dynamic DC bias current are mainly composed of low-frequency components, with a base frequency of 0.005Hz∼0.01Hz. In addition to the base frequency, the bias current also contains a large number of harmonic components, which may be formed by the superposition of stray currents generated by multiple metro trains. It can be inferred that there may be other intrusion paths with lower resistance than the earth that can cause significant superposition of stray currents besides. Simulation model considering the whole metro grounding system was established, and the 24h time-domain DC bias current generated by the simultaneous operation of multiple metro lines was simulated. The time-frequency characteristics of the simulated DC bias current are consistent with that of the measured ones. The results prove that the cable metal sleeve, drainage cabinet, and OVPD provide a low resistance path for stray current intrusion and superposition.

articleTitle: Guidance Strategy of Low-Carbon Charging Space for Electric Vehicles Based on Carbon Emission Flow
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A low-carbon charging space guidance strategy for electric vehicles based on carbon emission flow is proposed to utilize the electric vehicles' low-carbon properties fully. Firstly, considering the topological characteristics of the traffic network, the charging load model of an electric vehicle is established. Secondly, the node carbon potential of each charging station in the network is calculated using the power system's carbon emission flow theory, and the carbon emission cost caused by charging is charged according to this. Finally, considering the driving time, charging time, queuing time, charging load electricity cost, and the carbon cost, a charging station selection model is established with the minimum charging cost as the objective function to guide the charging of electric vehicles. The modified IEEE 30-bus system shows that the strategy reduces the carbon emissions of electric vehicle charging loads and charging costs.

articleTitle: Analysis on Abnormal Line Loss Rate of 1000kV UHV AC Transmission Line
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Through regular monitoring of the line loss rates of 1000kV ultra-high voltage AC transmission lines in the Central of China, it was found that the double-circuit 1000kV ultra-high voltage AC transmission line from Xiaoxiang to Ganjiang has experienced abnormal line loss rates for a long time since it was put into operation at the end of 2021. In order to find the reasons, this paper first studies the theoretical line loss rate, statistical line loss rate, power integral electricity consumption and daily average load rate, and finds that the main reasons are not technical issues. Further research indicates that the performance of electric energy metering device is a key factor.
