This paper presents a method for identifying and analyzing the abnormal line loss rates of transmission lines. This article also points out that corona loss may become the main technical factor affecting the fluctuation of line loss rate, especially for ultra-high voltage AC transmission lines, which requires attention and in-depth research in the future.

articleTitle: Optimum Trajectory Planning to Minimizing Loss of PM Linear Machines with Sandwiched Armature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To improve efficiency for free piston linear generator system, this paper presents an optimum trajectory planning method to minimizing loss for a novel PM linear machine with sandwiched armature. First, iron loss distribution characteristics considering magnetic field harmonics and rotational magnetization effects are analyzed by discrete parameterized method. And then iron loss and PM eddy current loss under different working conditions are calculated. Subsequently, by analyzing motion characteristics of mover, the mathematical description curve of operating speed is obtained. A speed trajectory planning method based on dynamic loss is proposed, and machines loss under four point-to-point speed curves is discussed. Finally, the optimal motion trajectory scheme can be obtained.

articleTitle: Mechanism Design of Green Electricity-Carbon Market Connection and User Cost Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To address the issue of duplicate calculation of environmental attribute costs in green electricity and carbon markets, this paper proposes a green electricity and carbon emission calculation mechanism to achieve mutual offsetting through the conversion relationship between green electricity and carbon emissions. By constructing a two-layer game model for users and aggregators, the impact of the designed green electricity-carbon market linkage mechanism on user transaction costs was analyzed. The results show that the proposed linkage mechanism can change the user's electricity consumption structure and reduce their electricity costs.

articleTitle: Research on Control Strategies for Photovoltaics Actively Building and Supporting the Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to achieve the future dual carbon goals, the proportion of new energy generation is increasing, and replacing fossil fuels has become an inevitable trend in future development. However, new energy grid connected generation has asynchronous properties and cannot actively support the power grid and provide inertia. Therefore, with the help of grid-forming converters, a active standby control strategy combining variable load shedding rate and virtual power frequency is proposed. By changing the load shedding rate, by deviating the maximum power point of the photovoltaic system and retaining a certain amount of active power reserve, virtual synchronous generator (VSG) control strategy with inertia frequency modulation characteristics is introduced into the MPPT control algorithm, so that the grid-forming photovoltaic converter can operate stably in the face of photovoltaic or grid frequency disturbances. The final results show the effectiveness of the control strategy designed in this paper.

articleTitle: Multiple Hybrid Load-Independent Outputs in Modular Reconfigurable Wireless Power Transfer System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a modular reconfigurable wireless power transfer (WPT) system with multiple hybrid load-independent outputs. The proposed system consists of a power module and several load modules in cascade. The introduction of a reconfigurable structure allows the loads to achieve constant voltage (CV) output or constant current (CC) output independently, while the system achieve zero-voltage-switching (ZVS) and high efficiency. Various decoupling methods are utilized to integrate the compensation inductors into the couplers. An experiment platform is constructed to verify the system viability. The output has the capability to achieve a CV output of around 20 V or a CC output of around 0.4 A, with a maximum variation rate of 4.64%. The power output can reach a maximum of 28.14 W, while the efficiency exceeds 97%.

articleTitle: Effect of Thickness and Frequency on Square Wave Breakdown of Epoxy Insulation for Solid-State Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The dielectric breakdown of insulating materials by high-frequency non-sinusoidal waveform voltage stress with high dV/dt is a new problem in the design and application of high-power electronic equipment. Here we discuss the frequency dependence of breakdown strength experiments. We constructed an insulation breakdown test platform at high frequency non-sinusoidal voltage, including high frequency and high voltage power supply, breakdown signal detection and boost unit. Measure measurement of specimens of different thicknesses (30 μm-100 μm) at different frequencies (50Hz-20 kHz). The results show that under the bipolar square wave, the dielectric breakdown strength (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_b$</tex>) of epoxy resin film decreases with the increase of frequency, and the rate of breakdown field strength decreases with the increase of frequency; the breakdown field strength (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_b$</tex>) decreases with the increase of thickness, showing a trend similar to the exponential rule. At the low frequency, with the increase of sample thickness, the breakdown field strength decreases and then increases. In addition to the internal local discharge and high dielectric heating, the spatial charge, trapping and polarization at the interface also play an important role under high-frequency stress. Further studies should focus on the interfacial effects behind the disruption mechanism.

articleTitle: Optimization of Dual-Drive Modeling for Large-Scale Offshore Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper introduced the new achievement from the research on optimization of dual-drive modelling technology for large-scale offshore wind farms. The dual-drive model consisted of data driven and knowledge driven respectively, and the iterative optimization is carried out by multi-parameter optimization neural network algorithm. Virtual twin model is a real-time simulation system formed by dual-drive simulation optimization algorithm, which takes multi-dimensional and multi-body dynamics modelling and multi-time scale simulation calculation as the basis, integrates multiple disciplines simulation and artificial intelligence algorithms, and combines renewable energy generation and integration as a significant result. The large-scale offshore wind farm real-time simulation model has improved the architecture of traditional electromagnetic transient digital simulation of power system.

articleTitle: Research on the Lightning Performance of ±800kV UHVDC Transmission Lines Erected on the Same Tower
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: At present, the transmission corridor to transmit electricity are gradually becoming limited. In order to improve the utilization efficiency of the existing transmission corridor, it is necessary to study technology of the UHVDC transmission lines erected on the same tower. Transmission lines are important parts of the power grids, so their safe operation is also very important. Transmission lines are widespread and easy to be stroke by the lightning, therefore the lightning protection research of the transmission lines should be paid great attention. In order to select the appropriate polar conductor layout, the lightning withstand level and flashover rate of ± 800kV double-circuit UHVDC line on the same tower under different polar conductor layout are calculated. In this paper, the shielding failure flashover rate under four different polar conductor arrangement were calculated by Electrical Geometric Model (EGM), and back flashover rate under four different polar conductor arrangement were calculated by traveling wave method. The calculation results under different polar conductor arrangement are compared with that of single-circuit line. By comparison, mode C (--/++) is the appropriate polar conductor layout when two UHVDC transmission line erected on the same tower. The research results can provide reference for lightning protection of ± 800kV double-circuit UHVDC line on the same tower.

articleTitle: A Model Reference Adaptive Control Strategy with Inertia Identification for Electric Winch System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper introduces a model reference adaptive control (MRAC) system for electric winch with inertia identification. Firstly, the influence of rotational inertia on the control system is analyzed. Then, as for the electric winch has the feature that the rotational inertia of the winch with the change of the number of wrapping turns of the cable. A MRAC algorithm for inertia identification is proposed to address the problem of inertia mismatch. Finally, the control effect of the inertia identification-based control algorithm is compared with the traditional control algorithm through simulation verification.

articleTitle: An Integrated Structure of Wireless Power Transfer, Onboard Charger, and Auxiliary Power Module in Electric Vehicle Charging Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The rapid development of electric vehicles has put forward higher requirements for various technologies of electric vehicles. One of the key components is the battery, which serves as the power source for electric vehicles. A suitable charging system can improve the safety and efficiency of electric vehicle battery charging, as well as extend the battery's service life and endurance. In this paper, an EV wireless charging system is proposed by employing an integrated solution for an electric vehicle charging system. The system can switch between different charging modes to meet the charging needs in different situations, including wireless power transfer (WPT), onbard charger (OBC), and auxiliary power module (APM). Different modes have different working frequencies. The leakage compensation model is used on the vehicle charging side, high-voltage receiving side, and low-voltage receiving side, while LCC compensation is used on the wireless charging side to achieve the required voltage ratio. The mathematical model of the integration of the WPT, OBC, and APM systems is established and verified in simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Living Object Detection Technology in Wireless Charging System of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Wireless power transmission(WPT) technology is the future development direction of electric vehicle(EV) charging method. To address the current problem of biological health hazards of strong magnetic fields between wireless charging coils of EVs, this paper proposes a method for living objects detection(LOD) in EVs based on a comb capacitor sensor, using two rows of 2n comb capacitors as sensing elements, while the upper and lower rows have different structures of sensing elements and matching them with different resonant inductors. The change in capacitance of the sensing elements is converted into an offset of the differential output voltage AU from the threshold value by means of resonant amplification, high-pass filtering, differential amplification and other active circuits. Simulations in COMSOL and Simuliink demonstrate that this method can effectively detect living objects in EV wireless charging systems and eliminate the detection blind area caused by conventional differential structures.

articleTitle: Research on Thermal Fault Diagnosis Technology of Generator Stator Winding Insulation Based on Graph Semi-supervised Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The diagnosis of early stator insulation thermal faults is crucial for the safe operation of steam turbine generators. Traditionally, the water outlet temperature of the cooling water system is monitored using a threshold, but this method has low accuracy and cannot effectively detect early anomalies. To achieve more accurate and timely insulation thermal fault detection, utilizing massive operational data through machine learning is an effective approach.,but there are problems such as vague physical meaning of dimensionality reduction features and high cost of sample preparation. Therefore, based on extracting the trend and temperature difference features of the water outlet, this paper adopts a graph semi-supervised method for fault diagnosis, which is conducive to intuitive understanding of the diagnosis results and reduces the dependence on the number of samples. Finally, experiments were conducted on the operational data of a steam turbine generator with model QFSN-660-2-22. The results show that the method has a diagnosis accuracy of over 98% for early stator insulation thermal faults, and is superior to traditional methods such as SVM and semi-supervised SVM under the same conditions. (Abstract)

articleTitle: Hierarchical Power Coordination Control Scheme for Non-grid-connected Hydrogen Production Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper explores the distinctive characteristics of off-grid hydrogen production systems (HPSs) that are dependent on photovoltaic (PV) renewable energy sources (RES), which function in off-grid mode during daylight hours and seamlessly interface with the grid during nighttime, thereby optimizing the cost-effective utilization of electricity. Considering this, this study devised a hierarchical power coordination control scheme employing an enhanced state machine design. At the device layer, the working mode and control plan are customized based on the distinctive characteristics of key devices within the system. Additionally, at the system layer, the adaptive adj ustment of the PV power proportion borne by the proton exchange membrane electrolyzer (PEMEL), facilitates uninterrupted state of charge (SoC) recovery of energy storage unit (ESU) while eliminating the necessity for an extensive array of operational modes and ensuring the system's reliable performance. Finally, the simulation cases verify that the proposed scheme can achieve the control objectives of reasonable consumption of PV power generation, stable bus voltage, and automatic maintenance of SoC. Consequently, the proposed approach enhances the stability and responsiveness of the system, thereby contributing to a more effective resolution of solar curtailment challenges.

articleTitle: A Multiport Power Flow Controller for Meshed High Voltage DC Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In multiterminal or meshed high voltage direct current (HVDC) grids, the power flow of each line cannot be accurately controlled by the voltage source converter (VSC) controllers. It may lead to unnecessary power losses and even damage the entire power transmission system. To solve this problem, the dc power flow controller (DCPFC) is introduced. This article proposes a novel multiport DCPFC topology which consists of three parts: series tapping block, energy transfer block and parallel tapping block. The proposed DCPFC topology can regulate one or more line currents in the dc grid. The line currents can be regulated independently. It is suitable for medium voltage (MV) or high voltage (HV) de systems due to its modular structure. Since the DCPFC only contains one stack, the costs and power losses can be reduced. Meanwhile, this article also elaborates on the topology structure, operation principle, and control strategy of the proposed topology. The theoretical analysis is verified by simulation results conducted in MATLAB/Simulink.

articleTitle: Reliability Evaluation of Distribution Network Considering Charging and Discharging Characteristics of Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Large-scale electric vehicles (EVs) will have a great impact on the reliability of distribution network. Aiming at the distribution network with EVs, this paper proposes a reliability evaluation method for distribution network, considering the charging and discharging characteristics of EVs. By simulating the charging and discharging behavior of EVs, the charging and discharging load power model of electric vehicles is obtained and compared from two aspects: type and intervention position, and the reliability of distribution system after electric vehicles are connected is comprehensively and accurately evaluated by sequential Monte Carlo method. Finally, the simulation results of the main feeder F4 of IEEE-RBTS Bus6 model verified the validity and accuracy of the proposed approach in this article.

articleTitle: Virtual Power Plant Analysis Task Offloading Strategy Based on Delay and Task Requirements in Cloud Edge Collaboration System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the virtual power plant scheduling system based on cloud edge collaboration, the edge computing effectively alleviates the computing pressure. And the effective computing offloading strategy can provide better analysis services. A virtual power plant analysis task offloading strategy based on delay and task requirements in cloud edge collaboration system is proposed in this paper. Analysis tasks in the edge cluster are realized by Docker containers. The completed information is sent up after the container calculation is completed. The same type of analysis tasks are unloaded to the container that has just completed the calculation according to the transmission delay. For tasks that need to build a new container, it is unloaded to the edge cluster server with the most abundant resources according to the different memory, storage and CPU requirements of the task. The strategy can improve the efficiency of analysis task execution. Its feasibility and advantage are verified by application example.

articleTitle: Impacts of Interactions between Grid-forming and Grid-following Converters on Stability of Hybrid System Connected to Weak Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper investigates the impacts of interactions between grid-forming and grid-following VSCs on the stability of hybrid system connected to weak grid. To begin with, the stability analysis model and the interaction analysis model of the hybrid VSCs system connected to the weak power grid are established. The self-influence and the inter-influence components are defined to quantify the interaction degree between grid-forming and grid-following VSCs. Then, combined with the Bode diagram and modal analysis method, the influence of the interaction between grid-forming and grid-following VSCs on the stability of system is analyzed by investigating self-influence and the inter-influence components with variations of operating points and control parameters. Finally, the above analysis results are verified by hardware-in-the-loop test platform.

articleTitle: Diagnosis Method for Electrical Contact Fault of Tulip Contacts in High Voltage Switchgear Based on Mechanical Thermal Coupling Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Early identification of electrical contact defects in tulip contacts using mechanical and temperature rise characteristics can ensure the safe and stable operation of high-voltage switchgear. This paper proposes a method for measuring the clamping force of the tulip contact spring in the KYN-28 switchgear and designs a testing system; We constructed a three-dimensional thermal-mechanical coupling simulation model for the tulip contact and analyzed the temperature field distribution of the tulip contact under different current and spring clamping force conditions; A fault diagnosis model for tulip contact electrical contact based on Adaptive-Network-based Fuzzy Inference Systems (ANFIS) and heterogeneous information fusion is proposed. This article establishes a finite element simulation model for the clamping force test system of the tulip contact spring in switchgear, and proposes a diagnostic method for the contact defect of the tulip contact based on the diagnostic concept of “pressure testing temperature simulation model prediction. This can effectively improve the accuracy of the electrical contact fault diagnosis of the tulip contact and provide reference for the operation and maintenance of the contact state of the tulip contact.

articleTitle: Optimizing Strategies for Rooftop Photovoltaic Installed Capacity Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: At present, the development of rooftop photovoltaic has become the main form of photovoltaic installed capacity, and there is no systematic planning strategy for the province's rooftop photovoltaic promotion. This paper studies the planning of installed capacity of rooftop PV by comprehensively considering various factors. The planning of installed capacity of rooftop PV is based on the installed capacity of rooftop PV, historical PV increase, light intensity, etc., and is generally divided into a system model for the planning of installed capacity of photovoltaic roof development considering the optimal economic benefit and the maximum social benefit.

articleTitle: Grid-Connected Current-Delayed Cascade Feedback Control Strategy for LCL Inverters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The rapid development of distributed renewable energy power generation and grid-connected technology is of great significance in promoting low-carbon transition and coping with climate change. As a bridge for new energy input to the grid, LCL grid-connected inverter can improve the quality of grid-connected current very well. However, it is easy to trigger current resonance during grid connection to destabilize the system, resulting in significantly poorer waveform quality of the grid-connected current. In addition, the weak grid environment containing grid impedance also affects the robustness of the inverter and triggers harmonic resonance. In this paper, the grid-connected current delayed feedback active damping control based on LCL grid-connected inverters uses cascaded delayed feedback links to improve the amplitude margin and enhance the system's adaptability and robustness to the dynamic impedance of the weak grid.

articleTitle: A Low-Power PWM Modulation Method for Suppressing Torque Ripple in Brushless DC Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Torque ripple stands as a prominent issue in brushless DC motors, significantly impacting systems requiring high precision and stability. A detailed analysis is conducted on the torque ripple during commutation periods using H_OFF-L-PWM modulation and an improved H_OFF-L_PWM modulation method, verifying the significant reduction of torque ripple achievable with the enhanced H_OFF-L_PWM modulation. Building upon this principle, an OFF-PWM-OFF modulation method is proposed, capable of entirely replacing the improved H_OFF-L_PWM modulation. This new method achieves equivalent suppression of torque ripple during commutation while reducing the number of switchings, thereby decreasing losses. Finally, a brushless DC motor wind power generation control system is developed on the PLECS simulation platform. Simulation results demonstrate a correlation between theoretical analysis and simulation outcomes, indicating that the OFF-PWM-OFF modulation method reduces current fluctuations and effectively suppresses torque ripple in brushless DC motors.

articleTitle: Research on Full Order Stator Flux Observer of Doubly-Fed Induction Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Accurate stator flux observing method is the foundation of doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) precise control. Detection precision of stator flux amplitude and stator flux phase will directly affect the operation of DFIG. Full order state observer is proposed to estimate DFIG's stator flux. Basic principle of full order state observer is analyzed. Full order stator flux observer of DFIG based on DFIG mathematics model is established. Simulation results show that the method gives accurate observation of DFIG stator flux.

articleTitle: A CLLC/S Compensated Wireless Charging System with Constant Output Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: During the charging of the battery, its constant current and constant voltage charging output and zero phase angle conditions are limited by changes in the equivalent load of the battery, making it difficult to achieve them simultaneously. Therefore, this paper proposes a new CLLC/S topology and its corresponding parameter tuning method. In this system, CC and CV charging modes can be obtained at two different frequency points respectively and achieve zero phase angle conditions. At the same time, the receiver adopts a minimalist design, which is in line with the WPT system principle of keeping the receiver compact and portable. Finally, the feasibility of the system was proved through simulation verification.

articleTitle: Effect of High-Frequency Square Wave Voltage on Space Charge Characteristics of Epoxy Insulation in Solid-State Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In renewable energy power systems, high-frequency transformers must withstand complex electric fields, which can easily cause discharge or degradation of solid insulation, leading to premature failure of the insulation system. This article focuses on the influence of high-frequency square wave voltage on the space charge characteristics of epoxy resin used in solid-state transformers. The space charge accumulation and dissipation characteristics of epoxy resin were studied by combining high-voltage polarization and short-circuit discharge. The space charge accumulation and dissipation characteristics of epoxy resin were studied by combining high-voltage polarization and short-circuit discharge. The results indicate that the charge accumulation under AC electric field is significantly lower than that under DC. Under high-frequency electric fields, space charges mainly accumulate near the electrode/insulation contact interface, with only a small amount of space charge accumulation inside the dielectric. In addition, as the frequency of the electric field increases, the average charge density decreases. The dynamic characteristics of space charge near the interface under a high-frequency electric field and the influence of frequency on the average charge density were analyzed using the theories of charge mobility and effective carrier migration distance under an AC electric field. The research results are of great significance for the insulation failure of solid-state transformers and the insulation design of high-frequency magnetic components.

articleTitle: Study on Fault Grounded Circulation Characteristics of Cross-Connected Box Under Different Phase Sequences
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Due to the complexity of the cable laying environment, the cross-interconnection box will have coaxial cable breakage, water failure in a box, water in two boxes and other faults due to man-made or natural factors, which will lay hidden dangers for the safe operation of the entire system. This paper analyzes the faults of the cross-interconnection box of high-voltage cables with double 110kV XLPE parallel arrangement, uses PSCAD for modeling and simulation, and analyzes and summarizes the variation characteristics of the ground current under different faults by calculating the ground current of the first end, which provides a theoretical basis for the fault detection of high-voltage cables.

articleTitle: Grid-Forming Control Strategy for Third-Harmonic Current Injection Two-Stage Matrix Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Compared with the conventional matrix converter, third-harmonic current injection two-stage matrix converter (3TSMC) simplifies the control strategy and has higher efficiency. This paper investigates the grid-forming control strategy for the 3TSMC. First, two possible configurations and the differences between them are discussed, the analysis reveals that the connecting the inverter-side to the grid is a more suitable method, compared to the rectifier side. Then the grid-forming control strategy is proposed for 3TSMC when the inverter-side is connected to the grid. Finally, all the considerations are verified by Simulation results.

articleTitle: Wireless Power Transfer System With Adaptive Current Following of Repeater Coils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, an exciter-quadrature-repeaters transmitter pad is proposed to achieve high two-dimensional misalignment tolerance of the wireless power transfer system. In the proposed wireless power transfer system, an inverter unit is needed to energize the exciter coil, which is magnetically coupled to three quadrature repeater coils. The currents in the three repeater coils naturally adjust based on the two-dimensional misalignment of the receiver pad to reduce the leakage flux density around the charging zone. The system can maintain the phase shift close to zero between excitation voltage and current and achieve constant current charging conditions with fixed compensation capacitors in the ± 50 mm two-dimensional misalignment range. According to the simulation results, the proposed wireless power transfer system has a near system efficiency and lower leakage flux density in extreme ± 50 mm two-dimensional misalignment case compared to the two-coil system.

articleTitle: Two-stage Optimal Operation of Low-Carbon Island Microgrid with High Penetration of Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Renewable sources can help island microgrid reduce carbon emissions. However, the increasing penetration of renewable energy poses a critical challenge to an economic and stable island microgrid, due to the intermittent and uncertain nature. In order to mitigate power fluctuations caused by renewables, a two-stage optimal operational model is proposed in this paper for an island microgrid, which is integrated with power generation, photovoltaic power generation, lithium-ion battery, and multiple hydrogen production devices. The goal of this model is to reduce cost and greenhouse gas emissions. A real-world data of Hengsha Isalnd in China is selected to verify the efficiency of the proposed optimization model. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed model guarantee the 100% renewable energy utilization under a lower emission and the economic performance of this island microgrid is improved by multi-energy integration.

articleTitle: A Low-Frequency Junction Temperature Swing Suppression Method Based on Varying Switching Frequency for Single-Phase PWM Rectifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Single-phase PWM rectifier is an important part in traction drive system. The low-frequency junction temperature swing of the power devices caused by the frequent changes of train operating condition, has a substantial impact on the reliability and service life of the system. In this paper, an active thermal control strategy based on varying switching frequency is presented to reduce the amplitude of the low-frequency junction temperature swing. Firstly, the power level is defined using the reference output power, and the relationship between the junction temperature information and switching frequency at each power level is revealed. The curve fitting method is adopted to obtain the fitting parameters among them. On this basis, a 3D lookup table is established according to these parameters, including the power level, switching frequency and junction temperature information. Then, a suitable switching frequency can be selected according to the 3D lookup table, to suppress the junction temperature swing during the dynamic condition. Finally, simulation result is presented to validate the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Least squares exponential fitting of surface potential
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The rated currents of the ground electrodes of the 800kV, 8000MW and 10000MW converter stations built in my country in recent years are 5000A and 6250A respectively. Due to the large ground current flowing into the DC ground pole, on the one hand, the ground potential (ESP for short) has a greater impact on the underground pipeline network; on the other hand, the ground potential (ESP for short) has a greater impact on the underground pipeline network. On the other hand., the distribution of DC near-earth potential is more complex due to the larger influence range and the differences in the electrical characteristics and structure of the earth. When the high-voltage DC ground electrode is operating., the ground surface potential increases., generating a DC bias voltage. DC bias can cause serious harm to the safe operation of power systems. The fundamental reason for the harm caused by DC bias lies in the uneven distribution of surface potential. To address this issue., this paper explores the mathematical method for finding multi-layer soil potentials and how different soil structure models use least squares exponential fitting to recover surface potentials.

articleTitle: Design of PCIe-Based Color Recognition and Tracking System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The tracking of target location plays an important role in animal behavior experiments. In order to meet the demand for high-speed transmission and fast processing of images in experiments, this paper designs an image transmission and processing system based on PCIe high-speed communication interface, which can track objects of specific colors within the screen in real time. By using the upper computer software designed based on the QT framework, the system is able to receive images containing calibration information in real time and make them available to researchers. The system's control and processing core uses Xilinx's Artix-7 series FPGAs, the Riffa framework to drive the PCIe high-speed communication interface data transceiver, and DDR3 SDRAM as the core of the high-speed memory module. The image acquisition device uses OV7670 CMOS, and the whole system realizes the complete process from image acquisition, processing, transmission to display.

articleTitle: Current Equalization Strategy for Three-Phase LLC Converter Based on Integral Phase-Shift Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid development of the new energy industry, the demand for high-performance power electronic devices is growing. The three-phase interleaved parallel LLC resonant converter has been widely used due to its characteristics such as high power density, low electromagnetic interference, high efficiency, wide input range, small output current ripple, and low component stress. However, differences in resonant parameters among the modules of the three-phase LLC converter may lead to uneven distribution of load currents. This paper proposes a novel control strategy suitable for the three-phase interleaved parallel LLC converter. The method controls by comparing the relationship between the three-phase resonant currents and adjusting the sizes of two phase-shift angles, thereby influencing the amplitude of the voltage fundamental wave. In this way, the resonant currents of the three phases can be balanced, achieving load current balance in the three-phase LLC converter. Finally, the effectiveness of this integral phase-shifting control strategy is validated through simulation and experimentation.

articleTitle: An Optimization Method for End Effect Suppression of Arc Permanent Magnet Torque Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Traditional rotary motors may encounter some problems when applied to large-diameter equipment due to the drawbacks of traditional transmission. The arc permanent magnet torque motor (APMTM) using stator splicing technology can improve the accuracy, efficiency and reliability of the equipment when applied to direct drive systems. It can be significant for overcoming the shortcomings of traditional rotating motors and promoting production. APMTM has the problem of large torque ripple caused by end effect. A method is proposed to suppress end effect from the perspective of adjusting the stator center angle and the stator adjacent angles, which can be used to suppress the torque ripple of APMTM. The mathematical derivation method and finite element method are used to analyze and calculate the end force of the motor. The proposed method of APMTM end effect suppression suitable for any number of unit motors is obtained. It can significantly suppress torque ripple caused by end effect in APMTM. This method provides experience for the structure design of the APMTM for the suppression of torque ripple.

articleTitle: Parametric Modeling and Sensitivity Analysis of a Hairpin Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor for Robust Design Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Aiming at the robust optimization design of a hairpin winding permanent magnet synchronous motor, the parametric modeling and sensitivity analysis are carried out considering manufacturing uncertainties. To consider the impact of manufacturing uncertainties more comprehensively in the motor design stage, a parametric model of the hairpin winding permanent magnet synchronous motor is developed considering both the geometric structure tolerance and property inconsistency. Then, sensitivity analysis of the design parameters is carried out to find the key parameters that have dominant influences on motor performance. To save the calculation time, the approximate model with a multi-level analysis strategy is used to quickly calculate the model response under different input parameters. Afterward, the proper modeling method is investigated to ensure robust optimization results validity with limited information on manufacturing uncertainties. Finally, the parameters that have dominant influences on motor performances and the performances that are susceptible to manufacturing uncertainties are identified.

articleTitle: Design of Feedback Linearization Controller for Boost Circuit Considering Digital Quantization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Boost circuits have different small-signal linearization models at various steady-state operating points. Traditional control methods involve designing a PI controller based on a specific operating point, making it challenging to achieve comprehensive control across all operating conditions. However, in the field of nonlinear control, feedback linearization can be employed to achieve control effectiveness across different operating points. This paper initially establishes an affine nonlinear model for the Boost circuit, employing an inductor current indirect feedback linearization control strategy. This achieves feedback linearization control of the current loop independent of the converter operating point. When using digital control, the impact of digital quantization on controller parameters is considered. Controller parameters applicable directly to digital control systems are derived and analyzed. Experimental results demonstrate that, compared to traditional PI control, the feedback linearization control exhibits faster current loop response, lower overshoot, and independence of controller performance from converter operating points.

articleTitle: DC Line Traveling Wave Protection Method Based on Improved Hausdorff Distance Comparison
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To improve the reliability of conventional protection using fault travelling wave, this paper proposes a line traveling wave protection method based on improved Hausdorff distance comparison. The traveling waves at the two sides of the line have different propagation laws and change characteristics during external fault and internal fault. First, the traveling waveform is processed by time matching and segmentation calculation. Second, splitting the long waveform into short waveforms and averaging the waveforms at both sides of the block processing, thus calculating the average Hausdorff distance. Last, using PSCAD building a bipolar DC transmission system for simulation verification, the results show that the improved method has high reliability.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Low-Frequency Noise and Vibration Control Technology in Distribution Room
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of structure-borne noise disturbance during the operation of distribution transformers., starting from the root cause of the vibration., taking power distribution equipment as the research target., A new type of equipment noise reduction measure was proposed.With the help of discrete element simulation tools., the preliminary design plan for particle damping is determined., and parameters such as the diameter of the particles and filling quantity are optimized to determine the final design plan. Through a combination of simulation and experiments., it is verified that installing particle dampers on distribution transformers can reduce the noise amplitude in distribution rooms by 14.6dB. The research in this paper provides a basis for the application of particle damping in noise reduction design in the power distribution field.

articleTitle: Optimal Design of Structural Parameters for Ladder-Type Secondary of Linear Induction Motor Based on Tabu Search Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to improve the performance of the long primary double sided linear induction motor (LP-DSLIM), the equivalent circuit of the ladder-type secondary LP-DSLIM is established under the condition of considering the longitudinal end effects. After determining the optimization variables of the ladder-type secondary of LP-DSLIM, the analytic expressions of thrust, efficiency, power factor and secondary weight and the multi-objective optimization function model are obtained. The thrust, efficiency, power factor and weight of the secondary are optimized under the constraints of the secondary thickness by the tabu search (TS) algorithm. The ladder-type secondary of LP-DSLIM 3D finite element model (FEM) is established, and the analytical optimization is compared with the finite element simulation, which proves the correctness of the optimization results.

Author Keywords: long primary double sided linear induction motor

articleTitle: Torque Ripple Suppression Strategy for Switched Reluctance Motor Based on Improved Active Disturbance Rejection Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The paper proposes an improved linear active disturbance rejection controller (ILADRC) for reducing torque ripple in switched reluctance motor (SRMs). A cascaded extended observer based on ILADRC is established to ensure accurate estimation of total disturbances and enhance system transient performance. Furthermore, theoretical analyses of ILADRC's performance are conducted. Finally, the proposed control method based on ILADRC is compared with the conventional proportional-integral-derivative (PID) control scheme through the MATLAB/Simulink platform. The results demonstrate that the proposed control scheme can reduce torque ripple in SRMs and exhibits commendable dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Decarbonisation Pathways for Empowering Telecom Networks Using Renewable Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As the number and power density of base stations throughout world have increased exponentially in recent years, so has the energy consumption of telecommunications networks in the country. The objective of this research is to assess the viability of integrating energy storage systems with wind and photovoltaic (PV) energy sources in order to provide telecommunication networks with uninterrupted power supply and cost-effectiveness. In addition, by employing an economic model that includes the Leontief and Constant Elasticity of Substitution (CES) production functions, this study assesses the likelihood of achieving sustainable energy generation for mobile networks. There is one potential power supply scenario incorporated in the proposed solution:2.5 kW per PV array and 2 kW per wind turbine. The results of the simulations indicate that both methods successfully met the power demands of the base stations across the nation by implementing a versatile control system for the energy storage system's charge and discharge. In addition, it was discovered that wind and PV energy have the potential to serve as sustainable energy sources for base stations, and that an energy storage system provides a critical energy supply guarantee.

articleTitle: Analysis of Abnormal Grounding Current in Converter Transformer Core
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The clamp grounding current of a converter transformer in the northwest region is around 2A for a long time. To accurately analyze the reasons, this article uses 3D simulation software and electromagnetic transient simulation software to analyze the impact of different working conditions on the grounding current of the iron core and clamp. On site testing of the clamp grounding current reveals that the excessive clamp grounding current does not affect the normal operation of the converter, as it is caused by harmonics rather than internal faults.

articleTitle: Common-Mode EMI Noise Co-Suppression on DC and AC Sides of Parallel Three-Level Inverters Systems with Balance Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Three-level neutral point clamped (3L-NPC) inverters are widely used in high-power parallel systems, where the common mode (CM) noise has a serious impact on the reliability of systems. As a CM noise suppression method, the balanced bridge technique has attracted much attention due to its low cost. However, the majority of balanced bridge research has focused on noise reduction on one side of a single converter. This paper investigates the CM noise of a parallel system, and an impedance balancing circuit is proposed to reduce the CM noise on the DC and AC sides. Firstly, a CM noise model is established for the parallel system with two 3L-NPC inverters. Then based on this model, a co-suppression method is proposed that can reduce the CM noise on both sides. Finally, simulation results show that the proposed co-suppression method can reduce DC and AC sides CM noise well.

articleTitle: Model Free Current Harmonic Suppression in PMLSM Drives Based on Linear Extended State Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the increasing precision requirements in industrial processing, Permanent magnet synchronous linear motor (PMLSM) are widely used in high-end manufacturing due to its high thrust and precision characteristics. However, the effectiveness of traditional control methods is influenced by the precise model of the PMLSM. In this paper, a model free control (MFC) strategy based on linear extended state observer (LESO) is studied. Under this control strategy, the parameter changes of PMLSM and other external disturbances of the system are considered as total disturbances. The total disturbance is observed by LESO and compensated in the current loop of the system, thus achieving the goal of improving the robustness and anti-interference ability of PMLSM. To further improve the current loop control performance, a quasi resonant controller (QRC) to suppress current harmonics is adopted in this paper. Considering that harmonic frequencies are not fixed, a frequency adaptive quasi-resonant controller is adopted. Finally, verified by simulation, this control strategy can effectively improve the dynamic response ability and anti-interference ability of the PMLSM.

articleTitle: Technical and Economic Research on Energy Saving Conductors for UHVDC Project
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: At present, The ordinary ACSR are widely used in DC projects, and the DC resistance is relatively high. Under different operation modes, the power loss on transmission lines can even reach 15%. In order to maximize economic and social benefits, it is necessary to study and analyze the energy saving characteristics of energy saving conductors. According to the technical principle of energy saving conductors and combining with the CSG UHVDC transmission lines from west to east calculated, compared the electrical performance, mechanical performance and economy of different types of energy saving conductors and ordinary ACSR. The results show that compared with ordinary ACSR, all kinds of energy saving conductors have better energy efficiency, low life-cycle cost, and better economic and social benefits. So energy saving conductors can be applied in the new UHVDC project.

articleTitle: A Multi-Fault Recognition Method Based on Excitation Voltage Information Fingerprint for the Generator Excitation System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to address the challenge of lacking diverse and accurate information sources for generator excitation system fault recognition, we have proposed a multi-fault recognition method solely based on the excitation voltage information fingerprint for the generator excitation system. Firstly, this method makes the recognition approach where the fingerprint code matches with the fault fingerprint database suitable for periodic excitation voltage signals, which enhances the robustness of fingerprint encoding against time shifts in signals. Meanwhile, this method effectively achieves the rapid and accurate identification of various fault types in the three-phase bridge rectifier circuit of excitation system. Through simulation validation, the generated fingerprint data in this method is minimal, enabling extensive storage and rapid matching for fault scenarios under different parameters. As a result, it demonstrates strong discriminative and noise-resistant capabilities for asymmetric fault states at different triggering angles.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis and Enhancement of Virtual Synchronous Generator with Current Limiter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The modern power system exhibits a double high characteristic, where the physical structure and control strategies of power electronic devices have altered the stability characteristics of the modern power system. This paper investigates the transient instability issue faced by virtual synchronous generators (VSG) equipped with a current limiter during grid faults. Firstly, the transient stability model of the VSG is established. Then, the equal-area criterion (EAC) is employed to reveal the mechanism of transient instability in VSG and elucidate the influence of the current limiter on the transient stability of VSG. Based on this analysis, current angle configuration methods are further proposed to enhance the transient stability of VSG. Finally, the correctness of the mechanism analysis and proposed methods is validated through simulation.

articleTitle: Nitrogen-Polymer Separator Composite Insulation Lightning Impulse Withstand Voltage Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Currently, there is limited literature on the study of the dielectric strength of insulating barriers under lightning impact in a nitrogen environment, especially concerning intermediate distances. In this paper, the lightning strike voltage withstand characteristics of nitrogen and polymer barrier composites were investigated using the environmentally friendly gas nitrogen. The experimental distances ranged from 10 cm to 35 cm, The study provides insights into the effects of barrier size, barrier location, barrier material and barrier surface conditions on breakdown voltage, providing insights into practical engineering challenges. The results show that an increase in the barrier size leads to a longer breakdown path and higher breakdown voltage in the presence of nitrogen. Variations in the effect of barrier placement on breakdown voltage were experimentally determined, with the highest increase observed when the barrier between the high voltage and ground electrodes was located at 0.2. Despite the presence of nitrogen, the study demonstrated the presence of space charge. Exploring the relationship between different barrier materials and space charge, it was found that space charge affects different material barriers differently, resulting in an increase in breakdown voltage. Barriers inevitably encounter deposits of dust or other contaminants. It was found that when the barrier surface was covered with conductive dust, the breakdown voltage was lower than that when it was covered with conductive copper plates. In order to verify whether iron dust causes surface roughness and reduces the breakdown voltage, a roughness comparison experiment was conducted. The results confirm that the breakdown voltage is independent of the surface roughness of the barrier. In conclusion, the study is based on practical considerations and provides a comprehensive examination of the lightning strike voltage resistance characteristics of nitrogen polymer barriers. The study contributes to an in-depth understanding of the effects of barrier size, location, material, and surface conditions on breakdown voltage and addresses practical engineering challenges.

articleTitle: Deloading Control Strategy of Permanent Magnet Direct Drive Wind Turbine with Adaptive Droop Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The growth of renewable power penetration in the grid and the deepening of the power electronics of the power grid have brought challenges to the frequency stability of the power system. The participation of wind turbines in power system frequency regulation is an inevitable requirement for future power systems. Deloading control for wind turbines can provide stable power for the set to participate in frequency regulation. Therefore, in this paper, the fixed-ratio deloading control strategy of direct drive permanent magnet wind turbine is designed by combining rotor overspeed control and pitch angle control in the full wind speed range. Meanwhile, considering the different power standby of the turbine under different wind speeds, an adaptive droop gain scheme for wind turbines is proposed. Furthermore, the effectiveness of the proposed scheme is verified by simulation.

Author Keywords: permanent magnet direct drive wind turbine

articleTitle: Data-Driven Short-Term Electric Vehicle Charging Station Demand Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) could effectively reduce the dependence of vehicle industry on fossil fuels; however, the complex charging behavior and large power consumption by EVs induce challenges to the operation of power grid. Accurate forecasting of power demand of EV charging station can provide important information for the operation planning of power grid. In this paper, a data-driven framework is proposed for short-term EV charging station demand forecasting. To fully mine the potential of machine learning algorithms in EV charging station demand forecasting, forecasting models based on different ma-chine learning algorithms have been developed including artificial neural network (ANN), support vector regression (SVR), and boosted regression trees (BRT). The performance of a machine learning algorithm highly depends on its hyperpa-rameters. To improve the forecasting performance, a hyperparameter opti-mization method is further developed based on Rao-l algorithm. To verify the effectiveness of the proposed data-driven framework for EV charging station demand forecasting, extensive computational experiments based on real data from different EV charging stations have been conducted. Experimental results illustrate that the proposed data-driven forecasting models perform much better than the widely considered persistence model while the ANN model and the BRT model outperforms the SVR model.

articleTitle: Five-Plate Coupler for Single-Side Shielding Applications in Capacitive Power Transfer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel five-plate capacitive coupler consisting of four power transfer plates and one shielding plate. It is designed for single-side shielding applications, such as wireless charging for electric ships. To achieve accurate modeling and analysis, a full-capacitance model of the five-plate coupler is proposed and then simplified into a two-port model. Finite element analysis results demonstrate that the equivalent capacitance of the five-plate coupler follows a similar trend to the four-plate and six-plate couplers, with comparable capacitance values. Additionally, the five-plate coupler achieves effective shielding of the receiving side electric field while utilizing one less shielding plate compared to the six-plate coupler. A 3-kW prototype is constructed to validate the high-power and high efficiency wireless power transfer capability of the proposed coupler, achieving a DC-to-DC efficiency of 94%. The five-plate coupler offers cost savings and simplifies the design process while ensuring electrical field safety requirements are met.

articleTitle: An Iterative FPGA Algorithm for IPMSM Rotor Position Estimation with GaN Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the inverter consisting of GaN semi-conductors, the switching frequency of the inverter can be significantly increased compared to an IGBT in-verter, which can certainly bring many benefits for the sensorless control of PMSM based on high-frequency (HF) carrier-signal injection. To take advantage of the benefits with higher switching frequency, the well known algorithms for HF signal injection and the rotor position estimation must be improved and implemented in an FPGA to achieve a higher frequency of the injected signal and more dynamic signal processing. In this paper, a sensorless rotor position estimation algorithm using HF square wave voltage is ultilized and improved for the FPGA programming. Using the HDL Coder (Hardware description language), the validated algorithm is successfully tested in a test bench consisting of a interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM), 3-phase-GaN-inverter and a real time computer.

articleTitle: Implementing Interval Prediction of PV Generation Using Bootstrap-Based Extreme Learning Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Power system operation facing renewable generation uncertainty has been investigated intensively, which requires the stochastic intervals of the uncertain variables for robustness. The interval prediction can be resolved based on statistical inference theory and artificial neuron networks. This paper provides the implementation of bootstrap-based extreme learning machines (BELMs) for PV generation interval prediction. First, the methodology of BELMs is revisited. Second, the implementation process, including data preprocessing, data selection, model fitting, hyperparameter tuning, and forecast and interval prediction, are explicitly presented. The proposed implementation is tested based on historical numerical weather and PV generation data. The results show that the application is effective in terms of reliability and sharpness.

articleTitle: Research on Frequency Characteristics of Errors in Low-Voltage Current Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: During the on-site calibration process of low-voltage current transformers (low-voltage CT), there may be a frequency deviation in the calibration current, which can lead to deviation in the calibration results. In response to the above issues, this article proposes a method for calculating low-voltage CT errors under different frequency currents. The use of this method can effectively eliminate the impact of frequency offset on low-voltage CT calibration results. Firstly, measure the magnetic permeability of the iron core material of the transformer at different frequencies, and apply the zero flux method to measure the impedance parameters of the secondary winding of the transformer. Based on the experimental measurement results, derive the parallel branch parameters in the T-type equivalent circuit of the transformer, and calculate the corresponding errors of the transformer at different frequency current ranges.

articleTitle: Enhanced Voltage Regualation Method in Wind Power Grid-Connected Systems Through Cooperation Control of Hybrid Transformer with Wind Farm for Minimal Compensation Capacity Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As the proportion of renewable energy power generation integrated into the grid continues to rise, the voltage stability at the point of common coupling (PCC) is facing challenges. The stochastic and fluctuating characteristics of wind power generation can lead to voltage fluctuations and overruns, influencing the safe and stable operation of the power system. It is urgent to propose a method to enhance the node voltage management capability at the PCC. Combined partially rated capacity converters and electromagnetic transformers, hybrid transformers (HTs) are considered a promising voltage regulation equipment with high efficiency and reliability. This paper presents an enhanced voltage regulation method in wind power grid-connected system through cooperative voltage compensation from both HT and wind farms to achieve the minimal compensation capacity requirements of hybrid transformers. By analyzing the working principle of HT, a mathematical model and control strategy of cooperative voltage compensation are established. A wind power grid-connected model was constructed in PSCAD, and the simulation results verified the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed strategy. The proposed strategy successfully compensates voltage sag at the PCC, fully utilizing the reactive power compensation capability of the wind turbine generations (WTGs). It reduces the total capacity requirement of the HT converters by about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$45{{\% }}$</tex> for the same compensation need.

articleTitle: Prediction for Thermal Ratings of Overhead Conductors Considering Correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The prediction of the thermal rating of overhead conductors is of crucial significance for the economic dispatch of power systems. In order to fully leverage the current-carrying capacity of overhead conductors, it is necessary to forecast their thermal rating. Presently, the data foundation for thermal rating prediction is primarily provided by dynamic thermal rating (DTR) measurement devices, leading to high prediction costs and challenges in acquiring effective data. Additionally, current research has not taken into account the temporal correlation of thermal ratings. This paper proposes a probability prediction method for the thermal rating of overhead conductors based on Numerical Weather Prediction (NWP) data, considering the autocorrelation of thermal ratings. Specifically, independent probability prediction of thermal ratings is conducted using NWP, and the application of the autocorrelation of thermal ratings into the prediction process is implemented to achieve the final probability prediction of thermal ratings. Simulation results indicate that utilizing NWP and applying the temporal autocorrelation of thermal ratings into the prediction can effectively enhance prediction accuracy, reduce energy wastage, and contribute to the economic and secure operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Voltage Support Technology of Photovoltaic System Based on Inertia Stiffness Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Because the photovoltaic output has the characteristics of volatility, intermittent and no moment of inertia, the photovoltaic system is prone to bus voltage fluctuations during operation, which affects the safe and stable operation of the entire system, and even leads to the action of the protection device. Therefore, how to improve voltage stability is the key problem that needs to be solved. In this paper, a voltage support technology of photovoltaic system based on inertia stiffness compensation is proposed. By adding inertia stiffness compensation device based on energy storage and virtual synchronous control to the system, active and reactive power support is carried out, the active power of the bus is quickly balanced, and reactive power is compensated to improve voltage. Finally, based on MATLAB/Simulink platform, the simulation results show the role of inertia and stiffness compensation and the influence of control parameters, and verify that the inertia stiffness compensator can effectively improve the voltage quality of the photovoltaic system.

articleTitle: Effect of micro-nano particles on thermal conductivity and high-frequency insulation properties of epoxy composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In present study, the epoxy resin (EP) samples co-doped with micron hexagonal boron nitride (h-BN) and nanoparticles including Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>, SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, and AIN were prepared by casting in the lab. The thermal conductivity, dielectric loss and breakdown strength of the co-doped epoxy resin samples were systematically investigated at different frequencies. Compared with pure EP, co-doped samples exhibited better thermal conductivity and higher breakdown strength. The optimum performance took placed in the EP samples co-doped with h-BN and Al<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>O<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>. The thermal conductivity and breakdown strength could reach 0.384 W/(m-K) and 110.8 kV/mm at 20 kHz, enhanced by 78.6% and 54.49%, respectively. All the results indicated that thermal conductivity and high frequency insulation properties could be improved significantly by micro-and nano-co-doping, rendering EP become attracted in the application of high frequency power transformers.

articleTitle: Simulation and Analysis of Stator Short-circuit Fault of Permanent Magnet Vernier Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to solve the stator interturn short circuit fault of the surface permanent magnet vernier motor, the magnetic flux density change of the motor air gap is calculated by the magnetic circuit permeability method, and the harmonic component caused by the stator short circuit winding in the air gap is analyzed. Taking 1/11 poles vernier motor as an example, the short-circuit fault model of the vernier motor is established, the electromagnetic characteristics of the motor under different short-circuit turns and different speed are calculated, the fault signal is extracted from the stator induced electromotive force, and the relationship between fault characteristic value, short circuit turns and motor speed is obtained. It is proved that PARK vector method can identify and detect inter-turn short circuit fault in single fault mode of vernier motor.

articleTitle: Research on Dual Active Bridge Control Method for Model Predictive Control without Feedforward Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Direct current transmission and distribution technology has been widely used in fields such as rail transit, new energy grid connection, and electric vehicle charging due to its high utilization rate of cable cross-section and low line loss. The DC converter is the core equipment for voltage conversion and power transmission. This article takes the dual active bridge (DAB) converter as the research object, and proposes a model predictive control without compensation to address the problem of long transient time response. Compared with traditional control schemes, this method has higher dynamic response ability because it eliminates the feedforward PI compensation link. Finally, simulation comparisons were conducted with other control schemes to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Hybrid Multi-Segment SVPWM with Simplified Implementation for Single-Phase Three-Level Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Single-phase converters are being widely used in new power systems, and in order to output high-quality voltage waveforms in power systems, multilevel converters are well known solutions. However, the high harmonics caused by the modulation strategy will seriously deteriorate the power quality. In this paper, the modulation strategy of single-phase three-level converter will be deeply discussed and investigated in order to solve the problems of poor harmonic performance of the converter and the balance of neutral point voltage. Firstly, the new hybrid SVPWM algorithm with more segments is analyzed to ensure that the algorithm can achieve the balance of neutral point voltage and good harmonic performance. Secondly, a one-dimensional space-vector modulation strategy is introduced into the algorithm, which is based on geometrical computation and has a simple calculation method with high versatility. Finally, through simulation and experiment, it is verified that the hybrid SVPWM algorithm with more segments under the one-dimensional space vector modulation strategy can not only improve the harmonic performance and realize the ability to balance neutral point voltage, but also simplify the modulation calculation process and improve the operation efficiency.

articleTitle: Deadbeat Predictive Current Control Based on a Novel Multi Parameter Identification for the Permanent-Mangent Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Online parameter identification algorithms allow the motor control system to adjust the control parameters in real application. By using the continuous parameter detection, the motor maintains the optimal performance under different operating conditions. The accuracy of the motor parameters is an important factor affecting the performance of deadbeat current predictive control(DPCC). Traditional identification methods are difficult to balance convergence speed and identification accuracy, which there is an under-ranking problem for the multi-parameter identification of a permanent magnet synchronous motor. In this paper, the sensitivity of the control parameters in DPCC is analysed and an improved hybrid online parameter identification method is proposed. Among the traditional identification methods, the least squares algorithm is fast in identification and the model reference adaptive method has high identification accuracy. The algorithm proposed in this paper combines the advantages of both, which stepwise identifies the model in different time scales, and introduces multiple new hibernation factors to enhance the algorithm's resistance to perturbation. Finally, the effectiveness of the identification method is proved by simulation comparison and experimental verification.

articleTitle: Dynamic Suppression Method for Circulating Current in Multi-Parallel Two-Level Inverters Based on MPC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Circulating current (CC) is a disadvantageous factor that must be eliminated in parallel two-level inverters, which will degrade the quality of the output current or even cause a system crash. Common mode voltage (CMV) is the main factor that generates CC. Conventional model predictive control (MPC) can achieve circulating current suppression by synthesizing zero CMV voltage vectors, but this type of method usually relies on the rich vector selection of three-level inverters and is difjicult to apply in two-level inverters. The current control methods have low current tracking accuracy and cannot suppress the fluctuation of the CC caused by the random variation of the CMV during the dead period. In this article, a multi-vector MPC method is proposed, which constructs a zero CMV combination vector to achieve CC suppression without changing the current tracking accuracy of the conventional three-vector MPC at all. Moreover, dynamic CC suppression according to the magnitude of CC amplitude is proposed, which can further reduce the CC and regulate the CC offset. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified with comprehensive simulation.

articleTitle: Gradient Degradation Behaviors of Silicone Rubber Under UV-B Radiation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Silicone rubber insulators always work at high altitude regions with strong UV -B radiation, which degrades the silicone rubber materials and threatens the safe operation of insulators. Therefore, this study conducted a 5OOh UV-B accelerated aging test to investigate the impact of UV - B irradiation on the silicone rubber materials. The results indicate that with the prolongation of aging time, on the surface of silicone rubber material, the C-H bond content decreases first and then increases due to competitive relationship between C-H breakage reactions and hydrogen abstraction reactions, while the Si-O-Si bond content increases due to silanol dehydration condensation reaction. The surface becomes rough and the particles are more obvious. On the other hand, as the irradiation depth increased, the C-H bond content of the silicone rubber material decreased owing to hydrogen abstraction reactions. The closer it was to the irradiation surface, the rougher the cross-section is. These results demonstrate that degradation behaviors of silicone rubber under UV-B radiation is gradient, which is important for operation state detection and assessment for outdoor insulators.

articleTitle: An IPT System with Double SS Compensation Topologies and Strong Misalignment Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: WPT technology has been applied to some extent in the fields of electric vehicles, medical equipment, aerospace and underwater operations. In response to the poor anti offset ability of traditional low order topology on magnetic coupling structures, this paper proposes an IPT system with double SS compensation topologies and strong misalignment tolerance, and the circuit topology, working principle and design method of the compensation topology are provided. Capable of ensuring constant current output and strong misalignment-tolerant capability when the coupling coefficient and load of the magnetic coupling mechanism change.

articleTitle: Collaborative Optimization Analysis of Wind-AACAES-Heat
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Advanced adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) devices are getting increasing attention, but the operating modes of compression and turbine units in them are complicated, which are affected by many factors such as heat transfer medium temperature, gas mass flow rate, heat exchanger heat transfer efficiency and so on. This paper establishes an AA-CAES dual-charge energy model for combined heat and power storage, considering the efficiency optimization in the energy release stage, coupling wind turbines (WTs) and unit combined heat and power (CHP) to analyze the role of different operating modes of AA-CAES, and constructs a quadratically constrained quadratic programming (QCQP) about the economic optimization of the system. The optimization results show that in the integrated energy system the AA-CAES combined heat and power storage is more advantageous than the traditional AA-CAES in participating in the wind power consumption, the results are more economical, and the operation of the CHP is more flexible.

articleTitle: AC Breakdown Characteristics of Combined Air Gap with Floating Conductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In practical engineering, there are combined air gaps formed by floating conductors, which exhibit more complex discharge characteristics compared to air gaps.
