In order to suppress eddy current losses in the motor rotor and provide suggestions for the material selection of low-temperature and high-speed permanent magnet motors. In this paper, a high-speed permanent magnet motor with a rated power of 40 kW and a rated speed of 35,000 r/min is used as a research object to test the electromagnetic performance of various components of the motor in a low-temperature environment. The composite structure of metal plating and sleeve applied on the outside of the permanent magnet is used to consider the changes of electromagnetic properties of the rotor components under low temperature environment, and the finite element method is used to study the influence law of the composite sleeve structure on the eddy current loss of the motor rotor, and to analyze the influence mechanism of the composite structure on the eddy current loss of the rotor. The research in this paper provides a reference for the material selection and design of composite sleeve structure for high-speed permanent magnet motors operating in low-temperature environments.

articleTitle: Diagnosis of Substation Equipment Operating Status Based on Target Detection and Information Extraction Technique in Infrared Image
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Infrared detection can promptly reflect abnormal temperatures in substation equipment, reducing the probability of equipment faults. Traditional infrared diagnostic methods rely on manual intervention, making it challenging to timely and effectively diagnose the status of a large number of substation equipment infrared image. To address the state diagnosis of substation equipment in infrared image, this paper proposes a method based on target detection and information extraction technique for substation equipment state diagnosis. Initially, a model based on the YOLOv5 algorithm is constructed to recognize and locate equipment and text in infrared image. The text regions are cropped using a clipping module and then subjected to text extraction based on EasyOCR. Subsequently, the correspondence between temperature measurement crosshair and equipment is automatically judged based on contained logical relationship. Finally, the status of substation equipment is diagnosed based on temperature threshold discrimination method. The infrared image collected from the scene are used for testing. The results indicate that the average precision of equipment detection is 91.54%, the average precision of text detection is 94.68%, and the accuracy of equipment status diagnosis is 91.23%. The experimental results show that the proposed method can preliminarily diagnose the status of equipment based on target detection and information extraction. It is useful to provide technical references for subsequent edge computing and online diagnosis of substation equipment in infrared image.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of the IPT System with High Misalignment Tolerance Based on BP Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Wireless power transfer technology does not require direct connection to transmit energy through electromagnetic field coupling, and has the characteristics of convenience, flexibility, high safety and reliability, and resistance to mechanical wear. In wireless power transfer system, the relative position deviation of the primary and secondary edges can cause drastic changes in magnetic parameters, causing system imbalance. And for magnetic coupling devices, there are parasitic capacitors in the upper and lower layers of each turn of the multi-layer coils, and the voltage difference between layers is significant, which is a significant factor affecting system efficiency and transmission of reactive power. To address the above issues, this article selects BP coils with high coupling and strong misalignment-tolerant characteristics, as well as LCC/S compensation topologies; Reducing interlayer voltage difference through layered compensation and improving system efficiency; Parallel capacitors are connected in front of the rectifier bridge to eliminate the problem of excessive voltage and current phase difference when the load increases.

articleTitle: Surface Fluorination of Nano-Alumina Fillers and Its Effect on the Dielectric Properties of UV-Cured Resin Matrix Composites
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: UV-cured resin is used in the manufacture of 3D-printed insulators due to their advantages of fast molding and high processing accuracy. Exploring the surface modification of nano-alumina and its application in UV -cured resin matrix composites is of exploratory significance. In this paper, Fluorosilane coupling agent (FAS17) was used to modify nano-alumina and fabricate UV -cured resin matrix composites samples. Measurements on the samples showed that the dielectric properties of the UV -cured resin matrix composites with modified nano-alumina were improved. After that, the first principles method was used to calculate the trap distribution, and the results agreed with the experimental data.

articleTitle: A Novel Data-Driven Transient Stability Assessment of Power Systems Based on Uncertain Data Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Transient stability analysis is crucial in power systems, and thus, data-driven methods for transient stability analysis have received extensive research attention due to their accuracy and efficiency in existing studies. However, traditional approaches primarily focus on improving models to enhance the accuracy of transient stability assessment, often overlooking the significance of the dataset itself. In response to this gap, this paper introduces a data-centric perspective to augment power system transient stability analysis. By employing adversarial training, our proposed method generates uncertain samples based on the given transient stability analysis model and then incorporates these samples into the training dataset, which could significantly improve the accuracy and robustness of the existing data-driven models. The proposed method was tested on the New England 39-bus system to demonstrate its effectiveness. The results indicate that enriching the training dataset with generated samples to challenge and refine the model provides a new perspective for improving data-driven transient stability analysis.

articleTitle: Two-Layer Optimal Control Model with Compensation Mechanism of Charging Price for Large-Scale Electric Vehicles Participating in Deep Peak Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid development of grid-connected renewable energy generation systems, the pressure and cost of deep peak regulation (DPR) in the power system have increased sharply. Electric vehicle (EV) is a special load with double characteristics of load and energy storage, which is growing most rapidly in power system in recent years. Therefore, in order to guide EVs to charge during DPR scenario and lower the pressure and cost of DPR in the power system, this paper provides a two-layer optimum control model with the compensation mechanism of the charging price for EVs to participate in DPR. The model aims to maximize the DPR interests of thermal power units for DPR (DPR-TPU) and EVs and minimize the shared cost of renewable power plants and regular thermal power units. Through cooperative or non-cooperative games, the EV dynamic charging price and compensation price for DPR, stepwise compensation price for DPR-TPU, and thermal power units output at different periods are optimized. Using 50,000 dispatchable EVs participating in DPR as an example, the proposed model is tested in a regional power grid. The results show that the optimal strategies can improve the technical and economic indicators of DPR-TPU while increasing the benefits of EVs.

articleTitle: Power Equipment Status Evaluation Technology Based on Multimodal Data Aggregation Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper innovatively proposes a four level refined modeling method based on the equipment status evaluation guidelines, which improves the granularity of equipment evaluation. A combination reasoning method based on lexical analysis is proposed in addition, which centers on devices and achieves aggregation and inference analysis based on multimodal data such as images, voiceprints, signals, etc. Our method quantifies the evaluation of device status through score calculation and divides it into health levels, which can break down data silos between systems, expand the range of data perception, and improve the comprehensiveness, accuracy, and reliability of device evaluation.

articleTitle: PM Synchronous Motor with an Integrated Common-Mode Voltage Filter Considering Parasitic Capacitance Distribution
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The common-mode voltage (CMV) arises from the simultaneous imbalance in the three-phase voltage output of the inverter. It is coupled with parasitic capacitance within the machine structure, which is related to the physical structure of the machine. This phenomenon induces leakage current and bearing current, potentially leading to motor system damage. Therefore, this paper proposes five different topologies of a motor with an integrated filter using partial motor windings to mitigate CMV, leakage current, and bearing current. Furthermore, considering the physical distribution of parasitic capacitance for minimizing CMV-related harms, an optimal topology with an integrated filter has been determined.

articleTitle: Influence of Thermal Aging on the Evolution of Dielectric and Physical Properties in Resin-impregnated Paper
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Resin-impregnated paper (RIP material) is a widely used internal insulation material in Ultra High Voltage (UHV) bushings, requiring high electrical insulation strength, excellent thermal stability, and long-term reliability. Understanding the complex degradation mechanisms of impregnated paper under the combined influence of thermal factors is crucial for enhancing the reliability and lifespan of such insulation systems. This study delves into the intricate degradation mechanisms affecting the insulation performance of impregnated paper under thermal stress. Through degradation experiments, impregnated paper samples with varying degradation times underwent frequency domain dielectric property testing and phase characteristic analysis. Significant degradation in the dielectric properties of the material was observed under the combined effects of electric and thermal fields, with a notable increase in dielectric and dissipation factors in the low-frequency region. Utilizing the Havriliak-Negami model, the fitting results revealed an increase in internal and interfacial polarizations under thermal stress. Fourier spectrum analysis indicated an increase in functional groups such as hydroxyl and methyl, a reduction in ether bonds, and an initial increase followed by a decrease in ester bonds. The study also employed molecular dynamics simulations to explain the material's degradation mechanism and correlated these findings with spectroscopic characteristics, elucidating the microscopic degradation process. These findings suggest molecular long-chain breakage and the generation of smaller molecules, leading to an increase in internal and interfacial polarization strength. The study demonstrates a good correlation between the phase structure evolution and dielectric performance before and after the degradation of RIP material. It unveils the degradation mechanisms of the material under the influence of thermal factors.

articleTitle: Clarification of Energy Storage Level Connotation of Internal Voltage Amplitude/Frequency and Active/Reactive Current in AC Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Oscillations of unknown mechanisms occur frequently in the new power system, which have great influences on system steady operation. In fact, system oscillation is a process of active/reactive power and energy exchange between units and networks characterized by internal voltage amplitude/frequency and active/reactive current. Since there is no clear understanding of the nature of active/reactive energy exchange behind system oscillation phenomenons, the existing oscillation analysis and suppression methods are only suitable for specific system operation scenarios. Taking a small disturbance dynamic process of converter interfaced system as an example, this paper thus aims to clarify the energy storage level connotations of internal voltage amplitude/frequency and active/reactive current. Firstly, the closed-loop dynamic process of system and the dynamic evolution behavior of AC electric variables are described. Then combined with simulation waveform, the active/reactive power imbalance driving mechanisms of units AC internal voltage evolution and networks AC current evolution are explained respectively. Finally, the energy storage level connotation of internal voltage amplitude/frequency and active/reactive current are revealed.

articleTitle: Design of Five-Phase Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor with Special-Shaped Spoke Magnetic Pole Array
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a five-phase modular stator permanent magnet synchronous motor with harmonic injection Spoke type magnetic pole array. This configuration has the following characteristics: first, the use of five-phase windings with modular stators gives the motor strong electromagnetic thermal isolation capabilities; second, the Spoke-type magnetic pole array used has a strong magnetization effect, and the soft magnetic field in the array The use of materials increases the self-inductance of the motor windings and enhances the motor's ability to suppress short-circuit current under winding short-circuit faults. In addition, harmonics are injected into the contour of the soft magnetic material to make the air gap magnetic field more sinusoidal, which solves the problem of serious stator iron loss caused by the large harmonic content of the Spoke magnetic pole array magnetic field. A schematic diagram of the proposed motor is given. The design principle of harmonic injection Spoke type magnetic pole array is given. Finally, the electromagnetic properties of the proposed motor were simulated and compared with those of the traditional Spoke pole array motor, verifying the advancement of the proposed configuration.

articleTitle: Low Conduction-Loss DC Circuit Breaker with Bidirectional Break Capability
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The Modular Multilevel Converter-based High Voltage Direct Current (MMC-HVDC) transmission system has become the most commonly used transmission technology in DC transmission projects. In order to save transmission and distribution costs, it often employs a half-bridge submodule combined with a DC circuit breaker for isolating DC-side short-circuit faults. The DC circuit breaker is crucial equipment for DC fault isolation. During a short-circuit fault on the DC side, the current can quickly exceed several times its rated value within milliseconds. Hybrid DC circuit breakers efficiently and safely interrupt DC power. However, traditional hybrid DC circuit breakers, which use IGBTs as forced commutation switches, incur high costs and suffer from kilowatt-level power losses. Therefore, this paper proposes a low conduction loss DC circuit breaker topology with bidirectional interruption capability. It utilizes thyristors and diode bridges as forced commutation switches and designs thyristor turn-off circuits and capacitor pre-charging strategies. The proposed topology offers advantages of high interruption efficiency, low conduction losses, and low cost. Simulation verification using the PSCAD/EMTDC platform confirms the effectiveness of the proposed topology.

articleTitle: Elimination of Field Winding Induced EMF in Stator Electrically-Excited Synchronous Machine Using Open-Winding Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, the elimination of field winding induced EMF ripple using open-winding inverter for stator electrically-excited synchronous machines (stator-EESMs) is presented. Due to the doubly salient topology, the induced EMF ripple exists in the field winding of stator electrically-excited synchronous machines. Although the induced EMF ripple can be reduced to an acceptable level by certain methods, the average torque is inevitably reduced as well. With the open-winding inverter, the DC-biased phase current can be generated and therefore the original field winding is removed. The results show that, by using open-winding inverter, the field winding induced EMF ripple is eliminated whilst the torque performances are effectively improved.

articleTitle: Fault Arc Detection Model Based on LSTM-Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to quickly and accurately detect electric vehicle series arc faults, this paper builds an electric vehicle fault arc experimental platform and obtains data samples of power supply terminal voltage and trunk current under different working conditions. At present, most detection models only perform fault analysis through current signal characteristics, ignoring voltage and other signal characteristics. Based on the traditional single-layer LSTM model, a series arc fault detection model combined with LSTM-Transformer is proposed, and the signal characteristics of voltage and current are used to identify faults. Experimental results show that the fault arc recognition rate of the model reaches about 97% under all working conditions. It provides a feasible scheme for arc fault detection in electric vehicle electrical system.

articleTitle: Optimization Scheduling Strategy for Electric Vehicle and Grid Interaction Considering Photovoltaic Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As the power system and intelligent vehicle technology advance, the interaction between the power grid and automotive networks becomes more intertwined. Electric vehicles (EVs) impact the grid, prompting the use of Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) technology. This enables EVs to optimize grid power allocation, aiming to minimize both charging costs and grid losses. Firstly, an EV scheduling model considering grid loss and charging and discharging cost is established. Further analysis of grid node performance and network loss sensitivity, combined with time-of-use electricity price policy to guide the charging and discharging strategy of electric vehicles based on optimal power flow analysis. Finally, the improved IEEE 33-bus system is used to verify the feasibility and accuracy of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Screening Model Considering the Cascading Failures Triggered by Cyber-Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Substations in the power grids are vulnerable to cyber-attacks, and thus can lead to multiple line contingencies. However, previous studies mainly focus on the single-stage contingencies, lacking of exploring the propagation stage after extreme events. This paper proposes a probabilistic bi-level screening model for identifying the vulnerable substation and lines with high risk, which considers the cascading failures triggered by extreme events. The simulations conducted on the IEEE 24-bus system and the IEEE 39-bus system validate the effectiveness of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Design of a Wireless Power Transfer System with Long Air Gap
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a multi-relay wireless power transfer (WPT) system suitable for millimeter-level extended air gaps in high-voltage environments. Feasibility is demonstrated through derivation, and a comparison of power and efficiency is conducted with systems employing different numbers of coils. The study highlights the comprehensive advantages of a five-coil system in terms of power transmission and efficiency. The coils utilize nanocrystalline magnetic cores, which are smaller and lighter than ferrite cores, effectively reducing the system's weight. Finite element electric field and magnetic field simulations confirm that the embedded system does not affect the insulation properties of insulators under high voltage. Experimental validation of the output characteristics shows that the optimal output efficiency can reach 50.9% under a 20V input.

articleTitle: Subspace-State-Based Short-Circuit Current Observer for Interturn Short-Circuit Faults in Symmetrical Six-Phase PMSMs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Interturn short-circuit fault (ISCF) is a serious fault type in machine system. This paper proposes a novel Luenberger state observer (LSD) of short-circuit current using the xy subspace states for symmetrical six-phase permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs). For six-phase control systems, the current symptoms in each subspace are affected by the ISCF. Compared to the dq subspace voltage equations, the xy subspace voltage equations are simpler. To reduce the complexity of the observer matrices, the short-circuit current observer is developed by the xy subspace states. Experimental results show the effectiveness of the proposed observer for different fault severities and operating conditions.

articleTitle: Reactive Molecular Dynamics of Atomic Oxygen Bombardment on Polyimide under Electric Field
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Polyimide (PI) possesses excellent insulating properties and is widely used in spacecraft electrical transmission devices and equipment. To deeply investigate the degradation mechanism of polyimide solid insulating materials under the bombardment of atomic oxygen (AO) in an electric field, the ReaxFF (reactive force field) reactive molecular dynamics method was employed. The erosion process of Kapton-type polyimide under the influence of an electric field was computationally simulated. Various electric field strengths were applied to the polyimide simulation system, ranging from 0.6, 0.8, 1.0, 1.2, to 1.4 V/nm. The results indicate that under a weaker electric field, the bombardment kinetic energy of AO is reduced, resulting in little change in the overall mass loss. However, a stronger electric field exacerbates the cleavage of polyimide, and the normalized mass loss increases with the simulation time. Material loss induced by atomic oxygen bombardment in an electric field environment is a primary cause of insulation failure in aerospace equipment.

articleTitle: Technical Requirement for Load current switches in MVDC system and Verification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: At present, in medium-voltage direct current (MVDC) system, the load current switching operation is mainly accomplished by using DC circuit breaker (DCCB) as load current switch (LCS). However, if the transient switching process of the load current is considered, the transient voltage established by the DCCB is much higher than the actual required transient voltage, which greatly increases the cost. To address this issue, this paper analyzes the technical requirement for load current switches in MVDC system and verifies it by proposing a new LCS. Through an analysis of different voltage requirements between HCB and LCS switching currents, the system requirement of LCS is revealed. Subsequently, a new LCS based on power electronic devices is proposed, and detailed descriptions of its topology, working principle, and operation flow are provided. In the end, the technical requirement for load current switches in MVDC system is verified based on theoretical analysis and simulation results, and performance advantages of proposed load current switch are demonstrated.

articleTitle: Analysis of Motion Characteristics and Field Strength Changes of Spherical Metal Particles in GIS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) is now widely used in UHV power transmission and transformation stations. When there is movement of foreign particles inside the enclosure, local electric field distortion will be caused, which will decrease the insulation strength of GIS causing serious accidents. This paper intended to establish a three-dimensional GIS electrostatic field model to study the trajectory of charged particles under power frequency overvoltage and its influence on the electric field in GIS, and to obtain the characteristics of partial discharge caused by it. For this purpose, COMSOL Multiphysics and MATLAB are used in this paper for the traditional mathematical physics equation model simulation and 3D model co-simulation. The results of the two methods were compared and the results showed that the motion range of charged particles is far greater than that using the traditional calculation method when the electric field distortion is considered, which needs enough attention in the subsequent simulation and experiment.

articleTitle: EV Charging Load Simulation Based on Traffic Equilibrium Considering Power and Transportation Networks Uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the development and popularization of electric vehicles (EVs), the simulation of charging behavior of EVs becomes more and more important. Firstly, considering the EV travel based on traffic equilibrium, the traffic network model is established and decomposed into user optimal path model and traffic assignment model. Secondly, the PDN model including renewable energy is established. Finally, the branch and price method and Monte Carlo algorithm are used to solve the problem. The case studies on Xi'an have verified the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Real Time Operating System Simulation Method Based on Cross-Platform Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This article introduces a method to simulate the operation of a real-time operating system on a non-real-time operating system. This method is based on cross-platform technology, establishing a micro sandbox in the cross-platform middleware, placing threads with real-time requirements in the sandbox, and uniformly scheduling them by the sandbox management program. The scheduling algorithm is adjusted according to the target simulated operating system to achieve accurate simulation and operation of real-time software on the host operating system. This method has achieved the expected goal in the simulation and debugging process of real-time software.

articleTitle: Tensile Stress Affecting Electrical Tree Growth in Epoxy Resin Under Temperature Gradient
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Under long-term operating conditions, epoxy resin insulation needs to withstand tensile stress and temperature gradients. The article aims to explore the correlation between the electrical tree behavior and tensile stress in epoxy resin under temperature gradient. The tensile stress is applied by a push-pull machine and set to 0, 10, 20, and 30 MPa. As the tensile stress increases, the electrical tree inception voltage decreases and the tree growth rate accelerates, making it easy to form branched electrical tree. The tensile stress aggravates the tree extension in the direction of mechanical stress. The temperature gradient accelerates the degradation of epoxy resin and changes their morphological characteristics of electrical tree. Local temperature rise on the high voltage side results in more severe degradation. The formation of internal defects and molecular chain behavior in epoxy resin affected by stress field and temperature gradient field is explored, and space charge transport behavior is a significant element affecting the tree growth.

articleTitle: Research on Temperature Prediction and Fault Early Warning of Transformer Bushings
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As a major component of power transformers, high-voltage bushings are susceptible to overheating failures due to factors such as the working environment, load changes, and equipment aging. High temperature not only damages the bushings themselves but also reduces insulation performance, increases the risk of electric shock and electrical breakdown, and can even trigger serious safety accidents such as fire and explosion. In order to detect and address bushings temperature abnormalities at an early stage, This paper presents A temperature prediction algorithm combining temporal convolutional neural network (TCN) and long short-term memory (LSTM) based on Attention mechanism is proposed. Additionally, an early warning model is established based on the prediction results. Statistical methods are utilized to analyze the distribution of prediction residuals and set the fault threshold interval. Finally, the actual bushing temperature data are input into the early warning model to evaluate the operating condition of the transformer bushing. The results demonstrate that the Attention-TCN-LSTM model exhibits faster convergence speed and higher prediction accuracy compared to other models. The established early warning model shows high sensitivity in assessing the operating condition of transformer bushings and can issue early warning information at the early stage of faults, providing sufficient time for maintenance personnel to prevent safety accidents resulting from deteriorating bushing faults and mitigating economic losses.

articleTitle: State of Temperature Estimation for a Lithium-ion Battery Cell using Adaptive Unsent Kalman Filter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Accurate state of temperature (SOT) estimation for lithium-ion battery is essential to guarantee the safety and long-term stable operation of electric vehicles. While the majority of current physical modeling techniques rely on various types of equivalent circuit models (ECM), challenges persist in accurately estimating with the electrochemical models. Therefore, this paper proposes a methodology for temperature estimation based on a restructured electrochemical-thermal coupling model, and employing the Adaptive Unscented Kalman Filter (AUKF) algorithm to enhance battery SOT estimation accuracy. This method initially establishes a Thermal Single Particle Model (TSPM) that integrates a Single Particle Model (SPM) with a Lumped Thermal Model (LTM). And the model's alignment with experimental data further reinforced the thermal model's precision. Then, to account for the impact of noise on computational accuracy, the AUKF algorithm is introduced to adaptively process noise and filter the temperature values by the model. Finally, the validation of the algorithm is conducted through a comparative analysis with the temperature predictions of an open-loop model. The results indicate that the reconstructed electrochemical-thermal coupling model demonstrates high effectiveness in battery temperature estimation. By integrating the AUKF, the accuracy of temperature predictions was significantly enhanced, with the temperature prediction error notably reduced from 0.28°C to 0.07°C, achieving a 61.74% improvement in estimation accuracy. This paper contributes to the research on optimizing the SOT estimation methods for lithium batteries.

articleTitle: Power Transmission and Distribution Service Solution With Grid-Side Alternative Energy Storage (G-AES) - Based on VCG Alternative Value Evaluation and Cost Recovery Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The identification of Grid-side Alternative Energy Storage (G-AES) as transmission and distribution asset attributes is a prerequisite for G-AES to be incorporated into the regulated transmission and distribution business and obtained stable permitted income. However, a quantitative evaluation mechanism and cost channelizing mechanism for the alternative value of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{G}$</tex> AES power transmission and distribution functions has not been established, then G-AES construction cost as well as operation and maintenance cost cannot be effectively included in the recovery of power transmission and distribution supervision business, which hinders the scale development of G-AES. Currently, G-AES is still in the pilot application stage. Therefore, this paper proposes a GAES transmission and distribution service solution framework, which uses VCG mechanism principle to evaluate G-AES alternative value, proposes a cost recovery mechanism based on investment effectiveness evaluation, and puts forward policy mechanism suggestions to effectively solve the problem of G-AES alternative value evaluation and cost recovery.

Author Keywords: Power transmission and distribution service solution

articleTitle: Current Phase Analysis of the Induction Heating System with an Intermediate Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Induction cooker, have a huge market because of their high efficiency, short heating time, safety and other advantages. Among the operating characteristics of induction cooktops, heating uniformity is a property of great concern, and there have been several studies based on the effect of different coil structures on the heating uniformity of induction cooker, in which the heating coil is divided into 2–3 regions to improve the heating uniformity, but the effect of the phase of the current in the coil on the heating uniformity has not been paid attention to in these studies. For this reason, a mutual inductance-based impedance phase model is proposed in this paper. By analyzing the circuit model, the phase angle of the primary and secondary currents is deduced. On this basis, finite element simulation is carried out to analyze the induction heating uniformity of induction cookers with different phases, and the phase range with more uniform heating is obtained by comparison.

articleTitle: Slot-pole combination and optimization of a flux-concentrating fault-tolerant permanent magnet vernier rim-driven motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The flux-concentrating fault-tolerant permanent magnet vernier rim-driven motor (FCFTPMV-RDM) achieves higher torque density by improving the fundamental and low-order harmonics of the air gap magnetic density. This paper mainly focuses on the impact of structural parameters on output torque (Te) and torque ripple under various slot-pole combinations to further enhance motor performance. Firstly, the structure of the motor is analyzed, and then potential slot-pole combinations are identified. The impacts of structural parameters on the Te and torque ripple of motors with different slot-pole combinations is analyzed using finite element analysis. It is concluded that the motor with slot-pole combinations of 12/36/11/25 has the highest Te and the lowest torque ripple. Finally, the electromagnetic performance of the motor is analyzed using finite element analysis.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Method for Multiple Reactive Power Sources with Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper focuses on the operation of new energy stations and energy storage scheduling in the steady-state level AVC system, and studies the optimization allocation strategy of reactive power for new energy stations and energy storage steady-state based on economic model predictive control; A dynamic reactive power control parameter adaptive optimization method is proposed considering the physical characteristics of the inverter of new energy units. The effectiveness of the proposed method was verified through example analysis. The research results can provide useful references for new energy stations with energy storage to participate in active support control of the power grid.

articleTitle: Research on the Optimization Method of LP-DSLIM Based on Sobol Sensitivity Analysis and Surrogate Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Long primary double-sided linear induction motors (LP-DSLIM) have important application prospect in high-speed and high-thrust occasions. In this paper, the electromagnetic field finite element software is used to parametrically model LP-DSLIM, and the Kriging surrogate model is established with electromagnetic thrust and thrust fluctuation as the optimization goals. According to the optimization goal, the Sobol sequence method was used to analyze the global sensitivity of the motor structural variables and screen the key decision variables. Finally, the multi-objective genetic algorithm is used for optimization, and the optimization results are verified in the finite element model, which provides a new idea for the optimal design of LP-DSLIM based on the finite element model.

articleTitle: An Active Dumping Current Controller Design for Current Source Converter in PMSM Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Current source inverter is considered as an excellent candidate for permanent magnet synchronous motor drive systems due to its superior output waveform and inherent short-circuit protection capability. However, due to its requirement for the DC bus to exhibit current-source characteristics, it often needs to be connected in series with a front-end. Considering the power quality on the grid side, a current source converter with bidirectional energy flow capability can be chosen as the front-end for current source inverter. In current source converter systems, there is a resonant issue in the grid-side filtering section, which includes parallel inductance and capacitance. Due to efficiency limitation, this study investigates active damping current controller as replacement for traditional passive damping method. For the proposed active damping current controller, the paper models it in the Laplace domain and considers dynamic performance, resonance suppression capability, and stability margin for designing the active damping loop. Additionally, decoupling term design in the synchronous rotating coordinate system is conducted, taking into account the impact of the active damping loop. Finally, simulations are carried out to validate the proposed control and solution, considering the efficiency of the system.

articleTitle: Overview of Topology Optimization for Flux-Switching Linear Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Due to high thrust density, robust structure and low cost, Flux-Switching Linear Machines (FSLMs) have received an intense amount of research interest over the last few decades. The purpose of this paper is to systematically review the research content FSLMs. Firstly, the structure and operation principle were introduced. Then, the various machine topologies of FSLMs to improve output thrust and reduce thrust ripple were summarized and compared. Finally, the main application fields and research hotspots of FSLMs were prospected.

articleTitle: Anti-Windup PI Control for Speed Loop of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Modified Integral State Prediction Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In recent years, windup phenomenon in permanent magnet synchronous motor speed control system has been widely concerned by people. With the deepening of scholars' research, more and more anti-windup schemes have been proposed. In this paper, the principle and disadvantages of three classical anti-windup schemes are analyzed, and a modified integral state prediction anti-windup scheme with compensation element is proposed. Compared with the classical methods, the novel scheme optimizes the transient response process of the system from the saturation range to the linear range, and improves the ceiling of the dynamic performance of the anti-windup PI controller. Finally, the validity and universality of the scheme are verified on the experimental platform.

articleTitle: Analysis of Residual Stress at the Curing Interface of Epoxy Resin Impregnated Paper for Dry-Type Bushing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The interfacial residual stress formed in the preparation of dry-type bushing is an important factor restricting its reliable operation. In this paper, the kinetic equation of epoxy resin impregnated paper curing is derived by using the non-isothermal DSC analysis method, and the dry-type bushing model is established by simulation software to derive the temperature, curing degree change, and interfacial residual stress distribution of dry-type bushing in the curing process. According to the results, the maximum value of the interface residual stress formed after curing occurs at the contact between the impregnated paper and the ends of the center capacitor, which is up to 10.9 Mpa. This result will be conducive to the efficient manufacturing and reliable operation of the dry-type bushing.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Light Load Frequency Limited Optimal Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, the critical conduction mode (CRM) control method of Buck converter is studied, and a light load frequency limited optimal control method is proposed. Based on high efficiency, high power density and frequency limit, CRM with wide output range is realized to ensure high efficiency of the whole load range. Frequency limited and soft switching are realized by using dead-time resonance, and theoretical derivation and control simulation are carried out. A 2kW experimental platform was built to verify the feasibility of the light load frequency limited optimal control method. Compared with the traditional high-power constant-frequency CRM mode, the efficiency is significantly improved at light load. Combining the two control methods can achieve more than 92.1 % efficiency in the full power range of 180W -2000W.

Author Keywords: light load frequency limited optimal control

articleTitle: A Double Closed-loop Vector Control Strategy for Dual Stator-Winding Induction Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the fields of wind power generation, ship shaft power generation, pipeline residual pressure power generation and flywheel energy storage, generators are needed to realize the conversion of mechanical energy to electrical energy. The difference between the dual stator-winding induction generator (DWIG) in this paper and the traditional induction generator studied is that the stator side is composed of two sets of windings, the power winding and the control winding, and the magnetic field of the motor rotor can be adjusted by the control winding, so as to keep the voltage and frequency of the output terminal of the power winding unchanged when the motor speed or load is changed by external influences. In this paper, the mathematical model of DWIG is established, the coupling relationship between the power winding, the control winding and the rotor winding is analyzed, and the mathematical model equation under the two-phase rotation dq coordinate system is derived. Secondly, a double closed-loop vector control strategy of power winding voltage outer loop and control winding current inner loop is proposed to maintain the stability of power winding terminal voltage and frequency by controlling the change of three-phase voltage of control winding. Finally, a simulation analysis model is built by using Simulink, and the closed-loop control performance under the condition of speed and load change is compared and analyzed, and the feasibility of the double closed-loop vector control strategy is verified.

articleTitle: Self-Excited Wound Field Flux Modulated Machine using fractional-slot concentrated winding
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a self-excited wound field flux modulated machine, where the magnetic flux variation in a differential frequency between the armature working rotating magnetic field frequency and the rotor rotation speed frequency is effectively utilized for the rotor field excitation. And a diode rectifier circuit on the rotor achieves the AC/DC conversion between the rotor harmonic winding and rotor field winding. In this paper, this new technique is applied during the design and analysis of wound field flux modulated machine with 12-teeth/l0- poles fractional-slot concentrated winding. Owing to its special winding structure, the stator of the proposed machine can generate sub-harmonic magnetic motive force (MMF) to excite harmonic winding in the rotor. Compared to the existed sub-harmonic excitation machine, the proposed machine can generate the sub-harmonic MMF without any extra equipment or winding.

Author Keywords: self-excited wound field flux modulated machine

articleTitle: Investigation Results and Evaluation Method of Electrical Energy Loss in the Devices of 110 kV and 220 kV Substations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the continuing development of world economy, especially with the rapid growth of emerging economies and the acceleration of industrialization, the consumption rate of energy is being propelled. The electrical energy losses generated during the transformation and transmission of electrical energy constitute a major part of the energy losses in power systems, as well as the carbon emissions. This paper investigates the situation of energy losses in four typical power substations (two 110 kV and two 220 kV) in Zhejiang Province, China, indicating that the losses power transformer and reactive power compensation equipment is the main part of substation's energy loss. Moreover, a simple but effective analytical model for substation's energy loss is established, considering both the constant loss and variable loss. This study can give a guidance to the energy loss estimation and carbon emission reduction in the operation of low-carbon oriented power substations.

articleTitle: Optimization of Multiple- Tx Magnetic Coupling Structure of Wireless Charging System based on Orthogonal method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: N on-resonant topology is widely used to enhance the anti-misalignment ability of wireless charging systems (WCS). Meanwhile, optimizing the magnetic coupler has also been proven to be an effective method for improving the anti-misalignment ability of WCSs. First, the working principle of the non-resonant WCS is analyzed, and a magnetic coupler with multiple transmitter coils is proposed to achieve strong anti-misalignment ability. Then, the parameters of the magnetic coupler are optimized using the orthogonal method. Finally, the simulation results show that the optimized magnetic coupler achieves mutual inductance fluctuations of less than 5% under a horizontal misalignment region of 140 mm. Besides, combining the non-resonance topology can further enhance the anti-misalignment ability of the WCS.

Author Keywords: magnetic coupler with multiple transmitter coils

articleTitle: Impedance Calculation of Twisted Cores in Power Lines at High Frequency by a Multi-Level PEEC Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Power lines are essential components of the electrical grid that transport electricity from power plants to homes, businesses, and industries. These lines typically consist of core, sheath, and armor. The core is usually made of several twisted copper strands, and its complex structure leads to a difficult impedance analysis for transient analysis in lightning protection. The analytical method and numerical method are two common strategies for twisted core impedance analysis. However, the analytical method does not consider the impact of helix pitch on the eddy current, and it leads to the calculation error. It is hard for the numerical method to build the model of twisted cores with hundreds of strands. It is also time-consuming for the numerical method to solve the impedance of the complex structure at high frequency. This work proposes a multi-level PEEC method to solve the impedance of twisted cores of power lines. The method can depict the helix structure of twisted cores and can calculate the impedance within a considerable time.

articleTitle: An Anti-Misalignment Electric Vehicle Wireless Charging System Based on Multi-Receivers with Paralleling Diode Rectifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Misalignment tolerance is a problem that needs to be handled for wireless charging of electric vehicles, especially the more challenging to correct door-to-door direction (X misalignment), since ideal parking cannot be ensured when an electric vehicle is parked. A multi-receiver electric vehicle wireless charging system with paralleling diode rectifies is proposed to improve the misalignment tolerance. Strong misalignment tolerance can be achieved by automatic mode switching of the system at various misalignment points, which is made possible by the clamping effect of the diodes. To confirm the viability of the suggested plan, experimental prototypes and mathematical models were constructed. The system achieves effective power transfer, and its maximum efficiency is 90.38%, based on the experimental data. Within a 100 mm misalignment of the receiving coil along <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$X$</tex>, the system maintains excellent efficiency over a wide range of misalignments, with an efficiency more than 90% and an output power fluctuation of less than 4.8%.

articleTitle: Roughness Characteristics of Slide Surface and its Effect on Contact Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To deeply understand the current conduction mechanism of pantograph-catenary system, the roughness characteristics of the slide surface and its effect on contact resistance were experimentally studied. Seven roughness parameters were used to reflect the roughness characteristics. They are arithmetic mean deviation of the contour (Ra), maximum peak height of the contour (Rp), peak count (Rpc), curvature radius (r), average width of the contour element (Rsm), valley depth (Rvk), and skew of the contour (Rsk), respectively. The influence degree of roughness parameters on contact resistance was determined. The variation of all the roughness parameters increases with the increase of contact current. With the increase of contact pressure, Rsm and Rvk decrease, and Rsk increases. With the increase of sliding speed, Rsm and Rsk increase, and Rvk decreases. The initial roughness has a significant effect on the roughness characteristics of the slide surface within the first 15 minutes of operation. The influence degree of roughness parameters on contact resistance is Rpc > Rvk > Rp > r > Ra > Rsm > Rsk.

articleTitle: Influences of High Temperature and Solid Particles on Streamer Discharge in Tree-line Faults
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The occurrence of wildfires and line tripping caused by tree-line faults has emerged as a critical issue in power grids. To investigate the mechanism of streamer discharge under wildfires and provide theoretical support for realistic simulation of tree-line faults, a two-dimensional axisymmetric streamer discharge fluid model has been established. The microscopic quantities that cannot be measured experimentally such as densities of electrons and positive/negative ions, electric field spatial distribution during discharge process are calculated. The reliability of the model is verified by comparison with the existing research results. The calculation results show that with the increase of temperature, the electric field required for the streamer discharge is reduced, and the streamer radius and velocity are increased. The polarization electric field generated around the solid particles is larger than the maximum electric field of the original streamer. The combined effects of high temperature and solid particles greatly promote the development of streamer discharge, further increasing the streamer velocity.

articleTitle: Credible Power Capacity Evaluation for Load-side Resources to Participate in Power System Primary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the gradual increase of the penetration rate of new energy with uncertainty in the power system, the conventional units that are the main force of primary frequency regulation (P FR) have been replaced, resulting in the weak capacity of the power system for primary frequency regulation. Due to the large investment in supplementary source-side resources, a large number of load-side resources existing in the power system can be used to participate in PFR. Due to the insufficient capacity of individual load-side resources, it is difficult for them to be directly controlled by the power system. This paper proposes using a Virtual Control Unit (VCU) to aggregate various load-side resources, providing P FR for the power system. Since the capacity of each load-side resource is uncertain, the total capacity of VCU is also an uncertain quantity. The VCU uses tagging to categorize load-side resources based on their capacity characteristics. It then employs a two- level aggregation method to aggregate these resources. Since When aggregating all kinds of load-side resources, the VCU needs to report the total capacity to the power grid, thus making it necessary to evaluate its credible power capacity. Through case study analysis, it is shown that the proposed strategy can effectively aggregate a large number of load-side resources to participate in P FR, proving its effectiveness. Further, by utilizing two-level aggregation of load-side resources with tagging, the power capacity characteristics can be parsed into mathematical expressions, greatly simplifying the aggregation difficulty, demonstrating its superiority. Additionally, after risk analysis, the capacity reported by the VCU to the power grid can ensure the maximum expected profit of the VCU, ensuring the sustainability of the strategy.

articleTitle: Adaptive Fractional-Order-Inductor Based SHC Reduction Method Considering Parameter Errors and Frequency Deviation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the context of a two-stage grid-connected inverter system, the presence of a second harmonic current (SHC) in the input current has negative effects on both system efficiency and battery lifespan. While previous research has focused on reducing SHC, little attention has been given to the impact of parameter errors and frequency deviation on suppression performance. This paper proposes an adaptive fractional-order-inductor (FOI) based control strategy, which effectively mitigates SHC. The accuracy of line frequency information from the grid is ensured through the utilization of a phase-locked loop (PLL). In situations where there are fluctuations in power grid frequency, an adaptive center frequency filter is employed to minimize the impact of frequency deviation. Furthermore, an adaptive third-order general integrator determines the proportion of SHC in the input current, enabling dynamic adjustment of FOI order as required. Furthermore, an improved virtual capacitor is introduced in parallel with the DC bus to improve system dynamic performance. Theoretical analysis is conducted to provide comprehensive insights into key parameter design methodology. Finally, a 500W experimental prototype is constructed and tested in laboratory conditions to validate both the feasibility and effectiveness of this proposed control method.

articleTitle: Simultaneous Rotor Time Constant and Speed Estimation for Speed-Sensorless IM Drives with a Shift Angle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: For speed sensorless induction motor drives, there are a number of methods for simultaneous rotor time constant and speed estimation. However, the coupling of speed and rotor time constant estimation is a well-known problem. To cope with this problem, this paper presents a simultaneous rotor time constant and speed estimation method with a shift angle. In contrast to existing methods, this paper analyzes the coupling between rotor time constant and speed based on the adaptive laws. Then, rotor time constant and speed are decoupled using a compensation method based on a shift angle. In the rotor flux estimation, the rotor position error, which is neglected in the conventional methods, is introduced to improve the estimation accuracy. By analyzing the selection of shift angle, it is proposed to remove the rotor time constant estimation under light load condition. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified on a 2.2kW IM setup.

articleTitle: Research on Economic Scheduling Methods Considering Risk Prevention Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to assess the costs and benefits of various electricity generation and consumption entities in the power system, it is necessary to conduct research and analysis on the game theory equilibrium points of the economic scheduling problem. With the widespread integration of new energy units and the gradual increase in awareness of green electricity consumption among users, both the supply and demand sides of the power system exhibit new characteristics. Firstly, the low marginal cost characteristics of new energy units and the demand for green electricity on the consumer side will impact the mathematical formulation of the economic scheduling problem. Additionally, traditional analytical methods face challenges such as multiple variables and difficulty in solving when addressing nonlinear equilibrium problems. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an economic scheduling mathematical model for power systems that considers the production and consumption of green electricity. Subsequently, an equilibrium solution algorithm based on the optimal response method within the framework of game theory is introduced. Through case analysis, the equilibrium situation of the economic scheduling problem in the presence of renewable energy production and consumption is evaluated. The study also provides relevant suggestions for investment planning on the power generation side of the power system.

articleTitle: A High Efficiency Active Class E Rectifier Over A Load Range
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper provides a parameter choosing method for the design of high efficiency active Class E rectifiers by releasing the capacitor and duty cycle. It is no longer consistent with the duty cycle <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> of the corresponding diode, but uses it as a variable to find a higher efficiency point. At the same time, the capacitor <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C$</tex> paralleled with the switch is also used as a design variable to further improve the rectifier's efficiency. Then an active Class E rectifier is designed, which can achieve a 20 V-2 A output with efficiency higher than 97.2% under a load range of 5 -20 Ω.

articleTitle: Research on MTPA Control of IPMSM for Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Interior permanent magnet synchronous motors are frequently utilized in electric vehicles due to their superior qualities, such as high-power density, uncomplicated structure, and rapid torque response. The maximum torque per ampere (MTPA) control approach is commonly employed in the low-speed range to reduce stator current and copper losses. This paper presents a novel approach based on the perturbation and observation (P&O) method to achieve MTPA control of electric motors. Unlike traditional methods, the proposed approach does not require measuring motor parameters and is less susceptible to changes in these parameters. It also utilizes a variable step size search algorithm to determine the optimal current angle efficiently. Simulation experiments were carried out to assess the efficacy of the proposed method, and the results demonstrate that it exhibits faster convergence, lower stator current, and better performance compared to traditional analytical methods and disturbance observation methods.

articleTitle: Disturbance Observer Based Model Predictive Control for Soft Open Point
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a full-order terminal sliding-mode disturbance observer-based model predictive control (FOTSMO-MPC) for the two-port soft open point (SOP). Considering the parameter variation and external disturbance, a full-order terminal sliding-mode observer is designed to estimate the disturbance in the current loop, which are used as compensation to raise the anti-disturbance of the SOP system. In addition, to raise the dynamic performance and robustness, a full-order terminal sliding-mode (FOTSMC) is designed in the outer loop. The integral type virtual control signal without chattering is designed to deal with unmatched uncertainties. Finally, the simulation proves the validity of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Harmonic Current Suppression for Open-End-Wingding PMSM Based on Complex Vector Proportional Integral Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Because of the existence of zero-sequence circuit, the Open-End-Winding Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (OEW-PMSM) with common DC bus generates the zero-sequence current (ZSC) during operation. If the inverters' tube voltage drop and dead time are considered, the harmonics of three-phase current will be further increased, which will affect the operating efficiency and stability of OEW-PMSM. The traditional proportional resonant (PR) controller can't suppress the ZSC and the harmonic components of three-phase current very well. Therefore, a suppression method based on quasi proportional resonant (QPR) controller and complex vector proportional integral (CVPI) controller is proposed, which can suppress the three-phase current harmonics and ZSC by suppressing the harmonics in the d-q axis current and suppressing the ZSC through the zero-axis closed loop controller. The simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can efficiently suppress the third, fifth and seventh harmonics of current and ZSC.

articleTitle: Parameter Design Method of the Magnetic Coupler for Wireless Charging System Using Metamodel of Optimal Prognosis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper addresses the parameter design problem of magnetic couplers and proposes a multi-objective optimization design method based on the Metamodel of Optimal Prognosis (MOP). The method involves mathematically fitting optimization objectives and design parameters using the optimal predictive metamodel, thereby establishing response surfaces for multi-objective optimization. By transforming finite element calculations of the magnetic coupler into numerical computations through fitting, the optimization process is accelerated. The parameters ultimately selected are verified through simulation, thus validating the effectiveness of the proposed optimization method.

articleTitle: A Detection Method of Gate Open-Circuit Failure in SiC MOSFETs Based on Internal Gate State Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Gate open-circuit failure caused by the cracking and liftoff of gate bond wires has been demonstrated to be a new failure mode of SiC MOSFETs, which can cause serious consequences such as the shoot-through fault and gate-oxide breakdown. To enhance the reliability and robustness of SiC MOSFETs, a fast and accurate detection scheme of such failure is required. This letter proposes a gate open-circuit failure detection method based on the internal gate state extraction. This state, although is unavailable externally, can be extracted from gate current pulses. The gate open-circuit failures are then detected by checking the inconsistency between the drive signal and the internal gate state. Experimental results validate that the proposed method can detect all types of gate open-circuit failures accurately within 55ns.

articleTitle: Coordinated Power and Structural Load Optimization for Offshore Wind Turbines with Nonlinear Model Predictive Generator Torque Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Modern large-scale offshore wind turbines (OWTs) with pronounced flexible structure, operating in the coupled aero-hydrodynamic loads, presents a challenge for generator torque control. This study proposes OWT generator torque nonlinear model predictive control (NMPC) strategy to coordinate optimization the power production and structural load. Firstly, the prediction model is established based on aero-elastic-servo models of OWT, which predict the dynamic generator torque control behaviors to provide a preview of power production and structural loads. Subsequently, the cost function is jointly formulated by enhancing power production, regulating tower damping, and restricting actuator motion. To effectively compute the cost function, the Fast Particle Swarm Optimization (F-PSO) is proposed. Finally, the aero-elastic-hydro-servo experiment using the developed generator torque NMPC is conducted for 10 MW monopile OWT. The result under turbulence wind, irregular wave, and wind-wave misalignment proves the coordinated optimization on power production and structural loads.

articleTitle: Effect of direct current electric field on water diffusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Moisture is a key factor affecting the electrical performance and material deterioration of power transformer oil-paper insulation. Therefore, it is of significant importance to study the diffusion law of moisture in oil-paper insulation to ensure the safe operation of transformers. However, the lack of suitable non-destructive testing means has led to few experimental studies on the diffusion law of electric field on moisture in insulating paper. For this purpose, utilizing the characteristics of non-destructive and full-range testing of terahertz spectroscopy, in this paper, an experimental study was carried out to investigate the effect of DC electric field on the diffusion of moisture in oil-immersed insulating cardboard. The results show that the electric field will inhibit the diffusion of moisture in oil-paper insulation. And the inhibition effect increases with the increase of electric field strength. The calculated diffusion coefficients tend to decrease with the increase of electric field, from 0 kV/mm to 1.2 kV/mm, the diffusion coefficients decrease about 6 times. This study is of significance for the subsequent study of moisture distribution in the presence of multi-physical fields and the formation and development of latent defects in transformer insulation.

articleTitle: Simulation of Thermal and Electrical Transient Field Distribution of a HVDC Cable Laid in a Tunnel
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The rapid development of high voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission technology has put forward increasingly higher requirements for the key technologies of HVDC cables. Compared to the steady-state operation characteristics, the performance of DC cables under transient working conditions is more worthy of attention. In this paper, the electrical and thermal transient field distribution of a 320 kV DC XLPE cable laid in a tunnel is simulated by finite element analysis (FEA) method under two typical conditions, load current fluctuation and surrounding temperature variation. The results show that the thermal and electrical field of the cable will be affected by the amplitude and duration of the transient load current, and the large thermal time constant enables the cable to transmit a certain short-term overload without being overheated. Besides, a short-time variation of the atmospheric temperature at the soil surface will not cause a noticeable change of the thermal and electrical field in the cable, but the change of the air temperature in the tunnel will affect the cable both thermally and electrically. Under transient conditions, attention should not only be paid to the temperature rise of the cable conductor, but also to the temperature gradient across the insulation.

articleTitle: The Influence of Delay on PWM and EMI in Parallel Inverter System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In systems with parallel inverters, when there are many inverters, a master-slave control method is commonly used. The control signals generated by the master controller are sent to each slave controller, which then independently controls the corresponding inverter. During this process, varying degrees of delay can occur, leading to differences in the actual power signals. By analyzing the delay of modulating wave and carrier wave, this paper reveals the influence of delay on pulse width modulation (PWM) and electromagnetic interference (EMI). Through theoretical derivation and simulation verification, we found that if there is a delay in the PWM, it will inevitably lead to voltage differences and circulating currents in the parallel-connected system, while also reducing the suppression effect of zero common mode voltage (ZCMV). If carrier synchronization is ensured and the delay between modulation waves meets certain conditions, PWM synchronization can be guaranteed without introducing other issues.

articleTitle: Simulation for the Underwater Power Supply System Based on Underwater Inverter Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the increasing global exploration of offshore oil and gas, underwater power supply systems have longer power supply distances and require more electrical equipment. So underwater power supply systems based on underwater transformers are challenging to meet extraction demands due to its high cost. In this case, the systems implementing the underwater inverter scheme have lower costs. This paper simulates the underwater power supply system based on an underwater inverter scheme. The load type is compressors. The motor control method is Constant Voltage-to-Frequency Ratio Control. The rectification section of the variable frequency drive uses non-controlled rectifier. The inverter section of the variable frequency drive uses an NPC/H-Bridge five-level inverter. Simulation for the motors' start-up process and harmonic analysis during the steady state. Compared with the scheme of the underwater transformer, the underwater inverter scheme has lower costs and lower harmonics.it is suitable for power supply systems with longer submarine cables.

articleTitle: Partial Power EV Fast Charging Station Based on Dual DC Buses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: For the fast charging of electric vehicles this paper proposes a new partial power system based on dual DC buses. This DC-DC converter topology uses a two-stage structure of a front-stage fixed frequency LLC converter and a back-stage T-type three-level converter to control tram charging. In this charging scheme, the structure of generating a low-voltage DC bus to supply power to the rear-stage voltage regulation circuit by the front-stage DC-DC converter can reduce the number of devices used. In this paper, the 100kW partial power charging station is taken as an example, and the simulation is built in MATLAB Simulink.

articleTitle: Evaluating Stability in Offshore Wind Farm Transmission Systems Using Hybrid DR-MMC Rectifier-Based HVDC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Recently, a hybrid rectifier combining a diode rectifier with a modular multilevel converter (DR-MMC) has been recognized as an advantageous solution for High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) systems, notable for its enhanced power transmission capabilities and cost efficiency. The integration of this innovative rectifier type into HVDC systems, especially for offshore wind farms (OWF), necessitates a comprehensive examination of system stability. In this paper, a DC impedance model for the DR-MMC rectifier is proposed. This model incorporates the impact of the connected OWF at the AC terminal on the DR-MMC rectifier's DC impedance. Following this, the AC impedance of the HVDC transmission system as seen from the onshore converter station is developed. Stability analysis for the onshore station connected to a weak AC grid is conducted using the general Nyquist criterion. How the simplification of the DC terminal influences the stability of the onshore AC system is investigated. The study shows that oversimplification of the offshore rectifier introduces inaccuracies into the stability analysis result. Validation of the impedance model and the stability analysis result is achieved through time-domain simulations in Matlab/Simulink.

articleTitle: Subsynchronous Oscillation Suppression Strategy for Doubly-Fed Wind Turbines Based on DPC-LADRC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: When large-scale wind turbines with Doubly-fed Induction Generator (DFIG) are connected to the grid, the risk of subsynchronous oscillation (SSO) in the system increases day by day, and the causes become more complex. In order to ensure that doubly-fed wind turbines can achieve stable power output, it is urgent to propose suppression measures for the corresponding SSO. Most of the traditional suppression strategies are based on the negative damping theory. The responses of the oscillating voltage and the oscillating current are consistent and do not take into account the impact of the oscillating voltage on the output power. This article first analyzes the impact of voltage oscillation on output power oscillation when SSO occurs, showing that under voltage-type SSO, current suppression alone cannot suppress power oscillation. Secondly, considering the characteristic changes of SSO, to achieve the suppression of output oscillation power, a suppression strategy based on DPC-LADRC is proposed. This strategy starts directly from the power point of view and suppresses it through linear active disturbance rejection (LADRC). Its control structure is simple; parameter tuning is easy; and it shows strong adaptability under changes in SSO characteristics. Finally, by building a DFIG grid-connected system oscillation suppression simulation model, the simulation results show that when the SSO amplitude and frequency change, stable power output can be achieved under the DPC-LADRC suppression effect, verifying the DFIG grid-connected system proposed in this article. Effectiveness of SSO suppression strategies.

Author Keywords: Doubly-fed Wind Power Generation System Subsy nchronous Oscillation
Direct Power Control Linear Active Distur bance Rejection Control

articleTitle: Influence of screen structure on high-frequency bandwidth and dv/dt noise immunity for PCB Rogowski coils
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: PCB Rogowski coil renowned for its non-saturation, flexibility and miniaturization advantages, plays a pivotal role in monitoring the condition of SiC devices. While the screen enhances the dv/dt noise immunity, it also poses a trade-off by reducing the high-frequency bandwidth of PCB Rogowski coil. Therefore, this paper analyzes the effect of screen structure on PCB Rogowski coils. Initially, an equivalent circuit model is presented and validated for effectively estimating the high-frequency bandwidth of PCB Rogowski coil. Subsequently, it is derived that the coupling capacitance between the coil and the dv/dt noise source conductor can linearly reflect the dv/dt noise immunity of the sensor. The paper then analyses the effects of diverse screen designs, including hole structure, screen height, inner and outer radius, on the coil using finite element analysis software. The simulation results are validated through experiments. Laws of simulation can be helpful for customized design of PCB Rogowski coils.

articleTitle: An Inverter Nonlinearity Compensation Method with Multi-Step Waves for Speed-Sensor less Induction Motor Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In induction motor control system, the nonlinear characteristics of the inverter will increase the harmonic content of the current, and also increase the output torque ripple of the motor. Since the nonlinearity of the inverter can cause the inaccuracy of the observer to the input signal, its adverse effect is obvious in sensorless control systems. Thus, the nonlinear compensation of the inverter is necessary to improve the performance of the control system. The traditional voltage compensation method will inevitably produce wrong compensation signal in the low current region.
