Thus, it is not practical to compensate the nonlinear problem of the inverter in practical applications. On this basis, the causes of inverter nonlinearity are analyzed in detail. The multi-step equidistant waves are used to compensate, and the compensating voltage signal is selected accurately by the command current. The experimental results show that the proposed voltage compensation method is more effective than the traditional compensation method.

articleTitle: Iterative Optimization Method for Prediction of No-Load Back-EMF in Permanent Magnet Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motors Based on Multilayer Perceptron
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents an analytical method for analyzing no-load back-EMF of a permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor and proposes a new method for predicting the optimal iterative step size based on Multilayer Perceptron. Taking the saturation and nonlinearity of magnetic material into account, the analytical model of the motor in the case of no-load is established by using the magnetic equivalent circuit method. The multilayer perceptron is used to sample and train the iteration step size with corresponding cycle index, and select the optimal step size of the iteration re-value. With optimal step size, the number of steps for iterative convergence can be drastically reduced, which improves the computational efficiency. The analytical results are verified by the finite element method and the experiment, which confirms the validity of the proposed model.

Author Keywords: permanent magnet assisted synchronous reluctance motor
lumped parameter magnetic circuit model;Multilayer Perceptron

articleTitle: A Gain-Based Variable Inductor Control Method for LLC Resonant Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents a gain proportion integration (GPI) controller to accurately adjust the resonant inductor of an LLC resonant converter. Firstly, the GPI controller is designed and compared with the traditional PI controller in the simulation performance of LLC resonant converter based on variable inductor (VI). The closed-loop control LLC converter based on VI using GPI controller shows good results in simulation, which can quickly reach a stable state with minimal error in steady state, and the interference caused by input voltage fluctuations is well suppressed. At the same time, the idea of system coupling is adopted to improve the performance of control. The proposed GPI controller has good dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Power Factor Optimization Method for Induction Motor High-Speed Drives
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The induction motor (1M) voltage closed-loop field-weakening method can achieve the maximum torque output capability. However, the active power that supplies the load and the reactive power that forms the magnetic field are confined by the voltage boundary, leading to power factor deterioration. To address this problem, the principle of optimal power distribution is derived for 1M high-speed drives. It is quantitatively proved that to maximize the power factor, the dq-axis stator currents should maintain a certain proportion. On this basis, the power factor optimization control is achieved by regulating the flux current through a closed-loop structure and a limit block. Compared with the conventional method, the power factor with the investigated method is effectively improved in the field-weakening region. The effectiveness of the proposed algorithm is demonstrated on a 3.7kW IM drive system.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Transformer Multi-Physical Field Distribution Compression Display System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: At present, the automation and informatization level of the manufacturing, operation and maintenance process of power equipment has gradually improved. However, digital twin technology has not been widely used in the field of power systems with higher realtime requirements for data collection, analysis and feedback. The main research content of this paper is mainly based on the transformer equipment in digital twin power equipment. Through finite element method calculation and correction of measured data, the internal field distribution of the equipment model is obtained, Based on the calculation results, the data is compressed and the three-dimensional model field distribution is plotted, allowing equipment maintenance personnel to observe the internal situation of the transformer equipment in real time through this platform, thereby helping planning decisions and responding quickly to faults.

articleTitle: Modeling, Evaluation, and Optimization of Active Common Mode EMI Filter Based on Phasor Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Active EMI filter (AEF) is able to attenuate common mode (CM) EMI and reduce the volume of EMI filters. However, very few researchers investigate the evaluation of the performance of their AEFs and how it is influenced by key parameters. This paper proposes a method based on phasor analysis to evaluate AEF's performance and degradation. Firstly, the phasor analysis is conducted based on a current sensing current compensating (CSCC) AEF. Then, the AEF and the CM noise path are modeled. Finally, this method can be used to evaluate and optimize the performance of AEF and analyze its degradation. It is explained that how AEF's performance is influenced in different frequency bands. The experiment verifies the method and shows that adequately designing AEF's parameters can optimize its performance and help the equipment to pass EMC standards.

articleTitle: Combination of Zero Common Mode and Spread Spectrum for Four-Module Motor Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In parallel three-phase inverters, zero common-mode voltage can theoretically be achieved through zero common-mode modulation techniques. The advantage of spread spectrum PWM over constant switching frequency PWM is its ability to eliminate peaks of EMI. Therefore, this paper proposes a modulation method that combines zero common-mode and variable switching frequency to simultaneously reduce common-mode EMI and differential-mode EMI. Under the premise of using the zero common-mode vector, this method uniformly changes the switching period within a certain range, employing a four-module motor as the load for modulation. Simulation results show that this strategy not only achieves zero common-mode voltage but also reduces conducted EMI by more than 20 dB, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Research on Insulation Defect Detection Method for Conductive Slip Rings Based on MEMS Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The insulation reliability of the space conductive slip ring (SR) is crucial for ensuring the safe electrical transmission of satellites. Currently, the lack of monitoring and warning operation mode in SR makes it challenging to meet the long-life, high-power development needs of future spacecraft. Using the finite element simulation (FES) method, this paper investigates the effects of electrode deformation defects and brush attachment defects on the surface electric field of the SR. The results indicate that defects located near the main insulation of the SR will cause significant distortion in the surface electric field. Furthermore, the optimal detection location was determined based on the peak value of the distorted electric field. Subsequently, the selected MEMS sensors were calibrated and tested for accuracy, with an error of less than 0.5 kV/m in the test range of 0–20 kV/m. Using the sensor, the surface electric field of an SR operated with electricity and containing defects was tested. The radiation range of the distorted electric field caused by the defects was investigated, and the influence of voltage level on the defect detection effect was further studied. The results demonstrate that, at a 300V SR voltage, the sensor effectively identifies defects when the distance is less than 3mm from the SR surface. At a detection distance of 1 mm, the sensor can effectively detect established defects at standard voltage levels. This paper provides guidance for the future application of MEMS electric field sensors in the space domain.

articleTitle: Multi-Swing Transient Stability Analysis of SGs/SynCons Near Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper reveals the multi-swing transient instability mechanism of synchronous generators (SGs) or condensers (SynCons) impacted by nearby wind farm (WF) dynamics. Firstly, the diverse influence of wind farm dynamics on SGs/SynCons' transient stability across different swing stages is analyzed based on an energy function. Then, a voltage vector diagram is established to illustrate that increased rotor angle of SGs/SynCons can cause voltage drops at the grid-connection point, which may repeatedly trigger Low Voltage Ride Through (LVRT) control of WFs post-fault. Under such cases, periodic oscillations or instability may occur if the transient energy within a cycle doesn't reduce considering the combined damping effects of renewable energy and inherent system damping. Finally, simulations validate the existence of the multi-swing transient instability of SGs/SynCons.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of DC Transfer Switch for ±800kV Ultra-High Voltage DC Project
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: DC transfer switch is a key equipment responsible for operating mode transfer and fault removal in UHV DC engineering, which directly affects the safe and reliable operation of the DC system. Aiming at the DC transfer switch in a ±800kV UHVDC transmission project in China, this paper is based on the engineering specification requirements and actual operation strategy. The simulation models of middle bus transfer switch(MBTS), neutral bus transfer switch(NBS) and neutral bus ground transfer switch(NBGS) are built in the electromagnetic transient environment. At the same time, combined with the conversion current requirements of each transfer switch and the actual parameters of the line, the current conversion process of the above three types of transfer switches is calculated and analyzed, and the configuration of each transfer switch is given, that is, the energy absorbed by the lightning arrester of the middle bus transfer switch in A converter station is 9.062MJ; and the absorbed energy of the neutral bus transfer switch arrester at converter station A and converter station B is 20.233MJ and 20.428MJ respectively, and the absorbed energy of the neutral bus grounding switch arrester at converter station A and converter station B is 8.022MJ and 8.124MJ respectively.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy for Power Imbalance in Bipolar MMC-HVDC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid development of MMC-HVDC technology, bipolar MMC-HVDC system will receive more and more attention. The types of power imbalance problems are more diverse in bipolar islanded large-scale renewable energy transmission system, which puts forward higher requirements for fault ride-through under AC and DC faults. Therefore, this paper considers these three kinds of power imbalance problems the fault ride-through problem of non-fault pole MMC over-current, DC overvoltage and DC overcurrent of bipolar system, and considers the cooperation of AC Chopper and bipolar converter control strategy to achieve the fault ride-through (FRT) of these three kinds of power imbalance problems.

articleTitle: Mathematical Analysis of Current on DC-Link Capacitor in Dual Three-Phase PMSM Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: For a motor drive system, the capacitor at the bus end is one of the main components. The DC bus capacitor is often used as an energy storage device to maintain the power balance between the AC side output power and the DC side input power of the driver system, and reduce the impact of the current ripple. Therefore, the reliability of the DC bus capacitor is one of the main factors affecting the drive system. The current ripple is high-order harmonics, which distorts the current, resulting in faster heating of the capacitor and damage to internal components. Therefore, the complete mathematical model of the DC-link capacitor current is critical for suppressing the capacitor current ripple and provides the necessary theoretical basis. Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motors are widely used due to high fault tolerance and low voltage characteristics. In this paper, a novel mathematical model of current ripple on DC-link capacitor is proposed for dual three-phase PMSM drive system, and the accuracy of the mathematical model is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Online Optimization of Multi-Degree-of-Freedom Inductor Current RMS For Modular Multilevel Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to improve the efficiency of the modular multilevel-neutral point clamped (MMC-NPC) three-level dual active bridge (DAB) dc-dc converter and to address the problem that optimization of multi-degree-of-freedom converters generally employs methods such as offline lookup tables. An online optimization strategy of multi-degree-of-freedom RMS inductor current of MMC-NPC three-level DAB dc-dc converter is proposed. Firstly, the optimization solution model of the dc-dc converter is established, and then it is solved by using the global optimal solver Gurobi, and the obtained results are put into the LSTM training, and the trained LSTM intelligences are equivalent to the fast agent prediction model, which can optimize the RMS value of the inductance current in the whole voltage and power ranges. Finally, the proposed online optimization strategy is validated in Matlab/Simulink simulation platform.

Author Keywords: the RMS value of inductor current

articleTitle: An Absolute Inductosyn Angle Measuring Method Based on Data Fusion Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the high-performance control algorithms used in modern motor drive systems, accurate information about the rotor position is indispensable. As a type of position sensor, inductosyn is widely used in industrial automation and other fields because it can work in harsh environments and have higher precision. However, the inductosyn is a multi-pole structure so only relative angles can be obtained. In view of this phenomenon, this paper proposes an absolute angle calculation method based on dual-fine channel data fusion algorithm. This method can obtain absolute angle by employing the signals of two multi-pole channels and has good resistance to interference. The simulation results verify the feasibility and effectiveness of the method, and show that the accuracy of this method is significantly improved compared to the previous method.

articleTitle: Effect of Applied Voltage on Electrohydrodynamic Behaviors in a Needle-to-Ring Actuator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Three-dimensional numerical studies are closer to real scenarios and provide a more valuable reference for the development of electrohydrodynamic (EHD) technology. This paper presents the results of computational simulations of a cylindrical EHD cascade actuator with needle-to-ring electrodes. The simulations account for the combined effects of injection, field-enhanced dissociation, and surface charge accumulation. A complete set of EHD equations is calculated according to a commercial software package for the finite element method. The study systematically compares the influence of applied voltages at 20 kV and 30 kV on charge and flow dynamics. The findings indicate that as the applied voltage increases, there is a notable transition in the fluid flow behavior from a two-dimensional to a three-dimensional mode.

articleTitle: Contact Force Tracking Control of Pantograph-Catenary System Based on Low-Pass Filtering Backstepping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to reduce the fluctuation of the pantograph-catenary contact force (PCCF) and improve the tracking accuracy of the high-speed train pantograph-catenary system (PCS), an active control strategy of PCCF based on low-pass filtering backstepping was proposed. Firstly, the three degree of freedom PCS model was established and transformed into a cascade form. According to the strict feedback structure of PCS, the controller was designed by backstepping. Then, the first-order derivative control law of virtual control quantity was designed directly by combining the dynamic surface control, which can avoid the “explosion of terms” in backstepping when calculating the first derivative of the virtual control quantity, simplify the controller design structure. A state reconstruction observer was designed to estimate the unmeasured state quantity of PCS. Finally, Lyapunov theory was used to prove the global asymptotic stability of the closed loop system. The simulation results show that proposed control strategy can effectively reduce PCCF fluctuation, improve the current collection quality of PCS, and is suitable for operating environments of different speeds.

articleTitle: Bidirectional Droop Control for the Hybrid AC/DC Microgrid with no Steady-State Deviation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents a novel bidirectional droop control scheme designed for Interlinking Converter (ILC) in a hybrid AC/DC microgrid, offering enhanced stability and eliminating steady-state deviation. The mathematical models for the bidirectional AC/DC converter and the control algorithm are developed, and their performance is rigorously evaluated through simulations using PSCAD/EMTDC. The results demonstrate robust stability, rapid response to dynamic conditions, and successful elimination of steady-state deviation. The bidirectional droop control outperforms conventional strategies, positioning it as an advanced approach for decentralized microgrid control. The findings have practical implications for improving reliability and efficiency in microgrid applications, signaling a significant step forward in microgrid control strategies.

articleTitle: Toughness enhancement method for grid reconfiguration integrated with mobile energy storage devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Distribution network resilience refers to the ability of a distribution network to withstand extreme disasters and restore power as quickly as possible. In this paper, we propose a two-stage distribution network resilience enhancement strategy that considers distribution network reconfiguration and mobile energy storage devices. In the disaster stage, a toughness enhancement model integrating dynamic distribution network reconfiguration and mobile energy storage devices is established, and a particle swarm algorithm optimisation model is constructed. Using distribution network reconfiguration and scheduling of mobile energy storage devices as the resilience enhancement method and minimising the amount of load loss in disaster as the objective, the particle swarm algorithm is used to solve the model, and finally, the feasibility of the proposed optimisation method is demonstrated through the arithmetic case analysis of the improved IEEE 33-node distribution network.

articleTitle: Analysis and Compensation of High-Current Error for Fiber-Optic Current Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The nonlinear relationship between the output of the fiber-optic current transformer and the current to be measured is derived by means of the mathematical model of the quarter-wave retarder and the spun elliptical birefringent fiber. The nonlinearity caused by the azimuth angle and retardation errors of the retarder, as well as the linear birefringence in the sensing fiber is determined to be the main factors leading to the basic measurement error, composite error, and maximum peak instantaneous error. The high-current measurement accuracy of the transformer can be improved by reducing the alignment error and phase delay error of the retarder and shortening the pitch of the spun elliptical birefringent fiber. Based on the DC equal ampere-turn method and linear interpolation, a nonlinear error measurement, modeling, and compensation method for fiber-optic current transformers is proposed. The linear response of the transformer to Faraday effect over a large dynamic range is obtained and the power frequency high-current measurement accuracy is improved by the error compensation. It is shown by test results that the scale factor error of the fiber-optic current transformer can satisfy the requirement of 0.2 accuracy class within the rated accuracy limit primary current.

articleTitle: A Frequency-Based Impedance Differential Protection Scheme for Undersea Observation Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Electric energy is the lifeblood of the operation of the undersea observation network. The operation of the undersea observation network and observation equipment is inseparable from electric energy. The undersea observation network studied in this paper is a single-stage constant voltage DC power supply mode, which uses a single-core copper wire of a photoelectric composite cable and seawater as a power transmission circuit. In order to clear faults efficiently, this paper proposes a frequency-based impedance differential protection scheme. The electrochemical process of electrode-seawater circuit is studied, the characteristics of submarine cable electrode seawater power supply parameters and frequency variation mechanism are revealed respectively. This paper establishes the broadband RC impedance model of the anode-seawater-cathode circuit. Based on the broadband impedance spectroscopy, an impedance differential protection scheme is proposed. The voltage and current of the branch unit are converted into impedance signals and expanded in the frequency domain, and appropriate frequency value is selected to design a differential protection criterion. The validity of the impedance differential protection scheme is proved by simulations in PSCAD/EMTDC. The scheme offers a theoretical basis and technical support for the safe, reliable, high-quality, and stable operation of deep sea facilities.

articleTitle: A Fault Current Characteristic Analisis Method of Grid-Forming Converter with Current Limiting
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Grid-forming converter can actively provide fast power support for the power system, and play a pivotal role in the new power system mainly based on new energy converters. Due to the weak overcurrent capability of the power electronics, the grid-constructing converter tends to operate in current-limiting mode under grid faults. In this paper, the transient analytical and numerical solutions for the filter inductance current are solved based on current limiting, taking into account the dynamic characteristics of the current loop; due to the fast nature of the current loop, the filter inductance current is therefore equated to a step function when solving for the fault output current in this paper. The fourth-order differential equation was reduced to the second order to simplify the solution, and the analytical solution of the grid-connect current was solved based on the state-space method; Numerical solutions for the grid-connect current taking into account the frequency dynamic characteristics are obtained for the grid-connect current based on the Runge-Kutta methods.

articleTitle: Research on a Variable-Step-Size Precise Modeling Method for Single-Phase Full-Bridge Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: When the traditional discrete mapping modeling method is used to analyze the switching converter, there are some problems such as long calculation time and large error due to the fixed step size. This paper takes the single-phase full-bridge inverter as an example and proposes a variable-step-size precise modeling method. Based on the traditional discrete mapping modeling method, this method effectively solves the problem of model error accumulation by calculating the exact time point of mode switching. At the same time, the proposed method can select the appropriate step size for each mode according to the characteristics of different modes, realize the segmented simulation between different modes, and improve the operation efficiency. The modeling results are consistent with the PSIM simulation, which shows that the modeling method proposed in this paper has sufficient accuracy. Besides, compared with the traditional method, the proposed method achieves a better balance between the operation efficiency and the operation accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Output Ripple of Switched Capacitor Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The resonant operation of zero-current-switching (ZCS) switched capacitor converters (SCCs) will cause a large ripple current to be transmitted to the output. In order to analyze and optimize the output voltage ripple, a general step-down ZCS SCC output model is summarized in this paper. Through mathematical analysis of the model, the expression of output voltage ripple based on dead-time and capacitance of the output filter are given. Furthermore, for multiphase parallelled ZCS SCC, in order to minimize output voltage ripple, the optimal phase-shift angle design is given. Finally, a 2-to-l SCC prototype is constructed and tested to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Experiment of a New Magnetron Sputtering Cathode Surface Magnetic Field Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Magnetron sputtering is widely used in the field of material surface modification of low-temperature plasma, in which the magnetic field design of the cathode directly affects the quality of film formation and process cost. In order to optimize the magnetic field of the existing magnetron sputtering target, a structure with alternate distribution of internal and external magnetic yokes and permanent magnets is designed, and the finite element simulation experiment is carried out by using the method of parameter control variables. By studying the influence of magnetic circuit structure parameters on the magnetic field strength and distribution uniformity of the target surface, the parameters of key components such as permanent magnets and magnetic yokes were optimized and determined. The simulation results show that with the design structure of the cathode, the uniformity of the horizontal magnetic induction intensity on the surface of the cathode is 49.4% and the target utilization rate is 50.3%, which effectively improves the magnetic field uniformity and target utilization.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of Low Loss Wireless Power Transfer System with Coaxial Rotatable Coil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper introduces the design method of non-contact Coaxial rotatable coils, which can be used to realize wireless power transfer and replace the connecting devices of traditional aircraft cables, and the method can effectively avoid the wear and tear of traditional cables and other problems. In this paper, the magnetic field and its own inductance, resistance and mutual coupling coefficient and other parameters are calculated by using three-dimensional modeling simulation software, and the perturbation situation encountered in its work is also simulated and analyzed. The equivalent circuit model of the wireless power transfer system is also established, and its loss, working efficiency and maximum efficiency point are analyzed and calculated, so as to come up with an effective way to increase the efficiency and reduce the loss. Finally, when the output power is 94W, the prototype's rotating efficiency achieved 93.20%.

articleTitle: A MPPT Method Based on Model Predictive Control for Three-Level Flying Capacitor Boost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This article proposed a novel control method suitable for Three-level flying capacitor boost (TLFCB), which is widely used in photovoltaic system. To improve reliability and dynamic response speed, this article used model predictive control (MPC) strategy as the inner loop to control the flying capacitor voltage and inductor current. Besides, a disturbance and observation algorithm with variable step size is proposed as the outer loop to provide the reference of the photovoltaic voltage. While realizing power point tracking, it can also detect the state variables within the system and accelerate dynamic response. The effectiveness of this method is proved by simulation results.

articleTitle: A Fast Dual Vector Model Predictive Voltage Control Strategy for the Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator based on T-type Three-level Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, a fast dual-vector model predictive voltage control (FDV-MPVC) strategy for the permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) based on the T-type three-level converter is proposed, which is expected to reduce the computation burden, eliminate the weighting factor, and improve the steady-state performance of conventional model predictive control method. Based on the sectors of spatial voltage vectors, only two voltage vectors are selected within five candidate vectors, avoiding testing all feasible voltage vectors, which reduces the computation burden and improves the steady-state performance of FDV-MPVC. In addition, the working characteristics of the redundant small vector are utilized to replace the midpoint potential balance cost function, eliminating the need for setting and adjusting weighting factors, while ensuring balanced midpoint potential. Furthermore, a modulation model is applied to calculate the duration of vectors, and an optimized vector selection strategy is introduced to reduce the switching frequency of the converter. A comprehensive analysis of the converter topology, PMSG model, and control system is presented. Simulation results demonstrate that the FDV-MPVC can efficiently achieve stable DC voltage output while maintaining good steady-state and dynamic-state performance.

articleTitle: Simulation Design of Series Resonant Power Supply for Submarine High-Voltage Cable Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The submarine cables are long and have a large capacitance. The existing cable voltage withstand test power supply is bulky and inconvenient for mobility to use in the field. This paper presents the design of a power electronic series resonant power supply consisting of a three-phase PWM rectifier, inverter, and a series-resonant circuit. The Circuit parameters were determined through MATLAB/Simulink simulation, and an adjustable frequency in the range of 30–300 Hz was developed. The power supply has a simple and compact structure, easy operation, and a wide range of applications, meeting the withstand voltage requirements for high-voltage electrical equipment. The paper also presents a prototype of a 10kVA power supply that has been built based on this research.

articleTitle: Tesla Check Valve Ventilation Blade Designed for Substation Ventilation Noise Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In recent years, the demand for electrical facilities has also increased dramatically. However, due to some substations built in the city In order to reduce noise, ensure fire protection and occupy land, many transformer houses are set up too narrow and sealed Closed, which is easy to lead to poor liquidity of the air conditioning system, poor cooling effect, and easy to lead to high temperature of the main transformer Question. The transformer of the power system will produce low frequency noise during operation, which will cause noise to the surrounding residents These problems have caused great harm to the normal and safe operation of the transformer.The feasibility of using Tesla check valve blades for ventilation and sound insulation was studied through Ansys software.The fluid flow (fluent) module and harmonic acoustic module in Ansys software are used to study the ventilation performance and sound insulation effect of Tesla check valve blades. By changing the spacing, tilt Angle, outside diameter, radian and other factors of the Tesla check valve blade, the data under different parameters can be obtained. Based on the calculated data such as pressure difference, wind speed and air flux, the variation law of ventilation performance and sound insulation effect under different parameters is studied. The ventilation performance and sound insulation effect of Tesla check valve blade and ordinary shutter blade are compared to find out the difference of ventilation performance and sound insulation effect of the two blades. Analyze the effects of each influence and summarize the different laws brought by different factors, and get the final plan. The ventilation performance is as follows: The greater the tilt Angle of the Tesla check valve, the worse the ventilation performance; The greater the spacing; The better the ventilation performance; The larger the outside diameter, the better the ventilation performance; The ventilation performance of Tesla check valve blades is slightly worse than that of ordinary shutter blades. The rules of sound insulation effect obtained are as follows: The greater the tilt Angle of Tesla check valve; The better the sound insulation effect; The gap at 90mm has the best sound insulation effect; The larger the outside diameter, the better the sound insulation effect; The sound insulation effect of Tesla check valve blades is significantly better than that of ordinary shutter blades.Transformer room ventilation and noise reduction have always been the research goals of many scholars, aiming at taking care of transformer room At the same time, reduce the noise interference to the surrounding residents. Study the ventilation performance of Tesla check valve blades Various rules of sound insulation effect, the advantages and disadvantages of the study are obtained, and the reference value is provided for the future research in this field.

articleTitle: Coordinated Power and Transportation System Based on Electic Vehicle Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the development of the times and the deterioration of the global environment, electric vehicles (EVs) may become more and more important in the future. In the transportation network (TN), EVs need to charge at electric vehicle charging stations (EVCSs). The EVCSs consume a large amount of electrical energy. In the power distribution network (PDN), EVCSs are considered as loads. Therefore, EVCS is ‘the bridge’ that couples transportation and power system. How can EVCSs optimize thier charging price to maximize the total profit of them? In this article, we will discuss this problem. Firstly, we find the connection among TN, PDN and EVCSs and model them. Then, the problem is solved by iterations. This article proposes the concept of virtual transportation network (VTN). We will plan routes on it.

articleTitle: Direct Look-Up Table Method for Field-Weakening Control of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Operation Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To operate a permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) in the field-weakening region, the voltage closed loop is the most common method with strong robustness and stability. However, the coefficients tuning of the additional PI regulator is a complex work because of no suitable theory. Also, it stills lead to instability if the coefficients are not appropriate. To solve it, a direct look-up table method is proposed for PMSM field-weakening control without using additional PI regulator. Through the relation of speed, torque and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{d}-\mathbf{axis}$</tex> current, a look-up table is designed to generate the required <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{d}-\mathbf{axis}$</tex> current reference, which can be adjusted dynamically according to different operation conditions. Compared to the traditional one, the proposed method has better current rapidity and stability to some extent, which is verified through experiments.

articleTitle: Impedance-Based Stability Analysis of DC Distribution Systems with Complex Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The impedance-based stability analysis method is widely used in DC distribution systems. However, most existing methods are based on the one-dimensional impedance transfer functions and overlook the system's complex network. This paper investigates the small-signal stability of DC distribution systems with complex networks. First, the small-signal equivalent circuit model of the system is established and the closed-loop transfer function from all input variables to bus node voltages is derived. Second, based on the control theory of multi-input multi-output systems, two system-level stability criteria based on admittance matrix sum and equivalent loop gain are proposed, respectively. Finally, a typical DC distribution system consisting of four nodes and four converters was designed for case analysis and simulation, and the results show the correctness of the proposed stability criteria.

articleTitle: A Wind Farm Model Including the LVRT Controller Using Vector Variable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The low-voltage ride-through (LVRT) is the ability of wind turbines to stay in grid. As wind generation grows, dynamics of wind farms under fault will have a greater impact on the power system. Thus, the LVRT process must be considered. Different from that of a single wind turbine, the wind farm's LVRT dynamic is the combined effect of all wind turbines. To accurately simulate the LVRT process, it is necessary to reflect each individual wind turbine's dynamics. Due to the large number of devices involved, a method for modeling wind farms considering LVRT process and related controller is proposed in this paper. A doubly-fed induction generator (DFIG) usually includes the crowbar and switching control strategies to satisfy the LVRT requirements, these components are considered in detail in this work. With the proposed method, LVRT process of the whole wind farm throughout the fault and the post-fault stage can be captured. Meanwhile, all wind turbines can be modeled with one submodule with vector variables using this method instead of modeling them one by one. It decreases the simulation time and modeling effort. The validity of the vector model is verified by comparing the Simscape model's simulation results. Time-domain simulation shows that this vector modeling method can conserve the LVRT dynamic of all wind turbines located within the wind farm.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design of a Six-Phase Low-Inertia Fault-Tolerant Permanent Magnet Synchronous Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Multiphase permanent magnet (PM) synchronous machine features the advantages of high reliability and high fault-tolerant capability, which has great potential in the fields like aviation servo and electric vehicles. In order to meet the design criteria of low moment of inertia and high post-fault torque performance, three different rotor structures are analyzed and compared for a low-inertia fault-tolerant permanent magnet synchronous machine(SLIFT-PMSM) by finite-element method. The influence of winding structure on torque performance is investigated, and the winding structure is optimized to improve the post-fault torque performance. The electromagnetic performance of the improved scheme is evaluated under both the normal and fault conditions.

articleTitle: Bridging Characteristics of Moist Cellulosic Particles in Flowing Transformer Oil
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The presence of cellulose impurities in transformer oil can compromise the insulation performance of transformers. Cellulose impurities, characterized by molecular structures containing significant amounts of hemicellulose and hydroxyl groups, tend to adsorb considerable moisture. The bridging behavior of particles in transformer oil is influenced by oil flow. Presently, the bridging characteristics of moisture-laden cellulose particles in flowing transformer oil are not well-defined. In this study, utilizing the established transformer oil circulation device and oil observation system for particles, we conducted research on the bridging characteristics of particles with varying moisture content and different electric field intensities in flowing transformer oil. The features of small bridges in flowing oil were extracted, and the influence of cellulose moisture content on the bridging in oil was elucidated from a force perspective. The results indicate that as cellulose moisture content increases, the electrical conductivity of particles rises, resulting in an increased dielectrophoretic force. Consequently, higher cellulose moisture content makes particles more likely to converge towards regions of higher electric field intensity, specifically the center of the electrodes. The center width of bridges increases, and the leakage current flowing through the electrode gap rises due to elevated cellulose moisture content.

articleTitle: Analysis and Design of High Step-Up Push-Pull Series-Resonant Converter with ZVS Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A push-pull series-resonant converter is studied for high step-up dc-dc voltage conversion, which reduces the inductor current stress by applying the resonant tank to the high-voltage side. However, the push-pull converter suffers from hard-switching and dramatic turn-off voltage spike due to the sudden change of current in leakage inductance. To prevent spike voltage and obtain zero-voltage switching, the excitation inductance and the quality factor are analyzed. A design method is proposed for soft-switching operation, which enables the converter to operate at a fixed frequency with a duty cycle smaller than 0.5. Finally, a 100 kHz 2 k W push-pull series-resonant converter prototype with 27 V dc input and 380 Vdc output is built with 98.3% peak efficiency. The experimental waveforms verify the feasibility of the zero-voltage switching.

articleTitle: Overview of Broadband Measurement Characteristics of Voltage Sensing Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: A high proportion of new energy and high-frequency power electronic equipment access to the new power system presents a large number of high harmonics, broadband oscillation, electromagnetic interference and voltage fluctuations and voltage flicker and other characteristics, the development of voltage sensing devices to ensure the accuracy of the measurement of industrial frequency and harmonic power measurement, the correct action of the relay protection device, transmission line over-voltage monitoring and other aspects of the important significance. To this end, several high-voltage measurement devices are outlined, the working principle and transmission characteristics of several different types of high-voltage measurement devices are compared and analyzed, and the technology enhancement methods are analyzed, and finally the advantages, disadvantages and adaptability of several high-voltage measurement devices are summarized and prospects are made for the practical application and future development of the device.

articleTitle: Research on Matching Interpolation Functions and Field Calculation Methods in Multi-Material Topology Optimization of Electric Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The Solid Isotropic Material with Penalization (SIMP) method is highly regarded in the field of topology optimization due to its ease of implementation and conceptual clarity. However, in the realm of multi-material topology optimization for electric motors, the non-linear characteristics of soft magnetic materials make the choice of interpolation function crucial, as it significantly impacts the computational results. Through analysis, it is revealed that the matching relationship between interpolation methods and magnetic field calculation methods is crucial, specifically, interpolation functions should not be placed in the denominator of the dependent variable for field calculations, as it leads to computational instability. To validate this hypothesis, it was confirmed that the permeability interpolation based on magnetic scalar potential electromagnetic field calculation is also stable.

articleTitle: Simulating Hundreds of Power Converters without Model Simplification: Is it Possible in Offline and Realtime Modes?
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The modern power converter-dominated power system requires high-accuracy electromagnetic transients (EMT) simulation in very large scale. State-of-the-art simulation systems can provide either high-accuracy EMT simulation for few power converters or root mean square (RMS) simulation for large-scale power systems. For modern converter-dominated power systems consisting of hundreds of grid-connected power converters, i.e. photovoltaic power station or wind farm, simplification of converter modeling is required, i.e. average model or aggregation model. Is it possible to simulate this kind of scenarios without any model simplification? The answer is: yes. In this paper a novel simulation platform and process targeting to solve this challenge is introduced and demonstrated by case studies. With the help of this simulation platform, multiple simulation studies and verifications, i.e., system stability, fault ride-through (FRT), etc. can be performed at the highest accuracy level.

articleTitle: Electrical Tree Degradation in Epoxy Resin under Bipolar Square Wave Voltage with High Frequency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Electrical tree induced by divergent electric field is detrimental to the safe operation of devices, especially the apparatus like solid state transformers used in smart grids where the epoxy resin is commonly employed as an insulating material that generally has to withstander harsh operating conditions involving bipolar square wave voltage with high frequency. In this study, we investigated the morphology, growing properties, fractal dimension, accumulated damage, initiation proportion and breakdown characteristics of electrical tree in epoxy resin under high-frequency bipolar square wave voltages. The electrical tree grew rapidly with treeing time after a period of slow propagation. The rate of growth, number of branches, fractal dimension, initiation proportion and accumulated damage all increased with voltage magnitude and duty cycle increasing. At 10 kV and frequencies higher than 20 kHz, bubble-like trees appeared due to the decomposition of epoxy resin before breakdown occurred. The intensive partial discharge, proved by luminescence, contributed to the propagation of electrical tree. This research provides valuable insights into the characteristics of electrical trees in epoxy resin under high-frequency bipolar square wave voltages.

articleTitle: Uneven Electrolyte Distribution in Lithium-Ion Batteries: Investigating the Phenomenon and Mechanism of Negative Electrode Lithium Plating
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries are widely utilized across various industries; however, safety incidents stemming from manufacturing defects remain a recurring issue. Despite this, research on defects occurring during the battery manufacturing process remains relatively limited. In this study, we employ a pseudo-two-dimensional model (P2D) to investigate the secondary reactions of lithium insertion and stripping at the negative electrode. By simulating charge and discharge processes under different levels of wetting, we explore the uneven distribution of lithium plating resulting from inadequate wetting and delve into its underlying mechanisms. Our findings reveal that as the degree of defects increases, the risk of lithium plating at the negative electrode gradually escalates. This escalation can be attributed to the constrained speed of lithium-ion transport within the defective region, while the transport rate in the normal region remains unaffected. Consequently, this leads to disparate lithium-ion concentrations between the adequately wetted normal region and the insufficiently wetted defective region, exacerbating the non-uniform distribution of lithium ions and substantially elevating the risk of lithium plating. Our study not only enhances understanding of defect mechanisms in lithium-ion batteries but also provides theoretical insights for improving battery manufacturing quality.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experimental Analysis of Insulator Fracture Failure at Extremely Low Temperature
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: At extremely low temperatures, the bonding interface between the metal components of the transmission line insulator and the cement adhesive is affected by the huge temperature difference and the extremely low temperature, resulting in structural fracture due to thermal expansion and contraction, which in turn affects the integrity and bearing capacity of the insulator. In order to study the principle of adhesive failure of insulators at extremely low temperatures, a simulation model of disc suspension insulators was established. The stress and strain of insulator metal accessories and the internal thermal stress of insulators in low-temperature environments were simulated and analyzed, and the mechanical strength and size change tests of insulators in different low-temperature environments were carried out. The results show that the extremely low temperature will increase the failure strength of the insulator metal attachment, but the plasticity and toughness will decrease and the brittleness will increase. If there are defects in the ball head and rod of the insulator steel foot during the casting process, brittle cracking may occur under the ultimate bearing capacity, resulting in a fracture of the steel foot. The volume of cement adhesive for insulators shrinks with the decrease in temperature, resulting in gaps in the internal bonding interface of the insulator, causing the internal structure of the insulator to loosen, and the strength of the insulator at extreme low temperatures decreases significantly.

Author Keywords: Insulator fracture failure at very low temperature
Mechanical strength failure test of insulator

articleTitle: Generator Stator Partial Discharge Pattern Recognition Method Based on BOVF and Active Learning QBC-Catboost
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Partial discharge(PD) of generator stator bars is an important basis for generator insulation diagnosis. The traditional supervised classification model requires a large number of labeled training samples, which has high requirements on sample quality, and it is difficult to construct and optimize the performance of conditional classifiers with few labeled samples. To solve the problems, this paper proposes a feature extraction method based on bag of visual features(BOVF) and active learning QBC-Catboost partial discharge pattern recognition model. First, the model constructs BOVF of PRPD through bag of visual words model, and then uses active learning query by committee (QBC) strategy and Catboost classifier to jointly measure sample value and complete value retrieval. Finally, BOVF -QBC-Catboost model realizes labeling cost constraint and recognition performance optimization. Based on laboratory conditions, five typical defective of stator bars were designed and defect samples were obtained to verify the validity of the model. The accuracy of BOVF can be improved by up to 5.3 % compared with the statistical characteristics of discharge. The recognition accuracy of QBC-Catboost model with 25% sample labeling rate can reach 98.4%, and the difference of recognition accuracy between QBC-Catboost model and fully labeled random sampling model is only 1.0%. The experimental results show that BOVF and QBC-Catboost recognition model can effectively mine discharge characteristics, complete value sample retrieval, effectively constrain the training cost, and realize the construction of high-performance classification model.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Resilience Assessment of Distribution Network In Extreme Weather
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The power system, as a vital infrastructure, is expected to withstand the impacts of rare yet severe events such as extreme weather. This paper introduces a comprehensive method for evaluating the resilience of distribution networks during extreme weather. First, the failure rate model of distribution network components is established, and the Monte Carlo method is used to simulate extreme weather and generate scenarios involving random failures within the distribution network caused by the typhoon. Subsequently, a resilience assessment system is formulated considering the entire process from fault occurrence to network recovery, incorporating indicators such as load loss rate, average recovery time of critical loads, resilience coefficient, and island continuity, and a comprehensive evaluation is obtained by subjective and objective weighting methods. The effectiveness of the proposed assessment method is then validated through simulation analysis using the modified IEEE 33-bus system.

articleTitle: Potential Assessment and Scheduling Method of TCLs Based on Human Body Exergy Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Given the intermittency and fluctuations issues generated by large-scale deployment of clean energy in the power grid, demand-side resources like the temperature control loads (TCLs) to smooth power grid fluctuations is beneficial to ensuring the power grid's stability. Exergy analysis can use human, interior, and outdoor parameters to assess the ideal level of thermal comfort for humans. The human body's ideal temperature range is displayed by an energy analysis, followed by TCLs' peak load capacity range. In this paper, a bottom-up optimization technique for TCLs' potential assessment and scheduling method is presented. Because the user side simply needs to give the bidding curve, it promotes user privacy and security while fully respecting the user's own desire. User's bidding curve is displayed through the utility function of the user. Decentralized TCLs are organized in the form of load aggregator (LA). LA gathers bidding curves from all users to assess the total potential and controls TCLs to attend demand response. A numerical example was used to investigate the mentioned method, which is based on the human body exergy model. The example analysis shows that the TCLs adjustment temperature obtained by exergy analysis is similar to the predicted mean vote (PMV) index, but because the parameters are more comprehensive, it is conducive to the fine description of the control potential. And the TCLs control mode based on bidding curve will not affect the user comfort.

articleTitle: A Method of Magnetic Core Partitioning Design for Flyback Planar Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This article is based on the planar transformer of Flyback converter, and proposes a magnetic core partitioning design method to address the problems of poor flexibility and low space utilization of its standard core shape, which can effectively improve the efficiency and power density of the transformer. Through theoretical analysis, the influence mechanism of core shape and size on transformer loss was elucidated, and the main directions of core design were summarized. Based on the power density, the basic shape was selected, and the process of establishing a transformer loss model was discussed in detail. 8 model constraint schemes were proposed according to different design requirements. The optimal solution of the model was obtained using MATLAB, and the partitioning basis and design principles of 4 core areas were explained. The standard core was optimized to be X-type, Finally, the feasibility and universality of the theory were verified through finite element simulation and experiments.

articleTitle: Parallel Open-Circuit Fault Diagnosis for Cascaded Full-Bridge NPC Inverter with Carrier Phase Shifted Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, a diagnosis method for open-circuit fault based on parallel operation structure is proposed for cascaded full-bridge neutral point clamped (NPC) inverter with carrier phase shifting SPWM (CPS-SPWM), which has small calculation and short diagnosis time. Multiple faulty devices with open-circuit in different submodules can be diagnosed independently. The variation rules of capacitor voltage are analyzed under the normal and faulty condition. On this basis, the fault is detected quickly through the voltage deviation, and the scope of fault diagnosis is reduced to two IGBTs. Then, the faulty IGBT is located by comparing the calculated deviation and actual capacitor voltage. Finally, the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed method is verified on the thirteen-level experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Grid-forming Hybrid Energy Storage with PLL for Improved Deadband Performance in Primary Frequency Regulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the wide adoption of environment-friendly renewable energy sources, the power converter needs to provide primary frequency regulation (PFR). Energy storage (ES) with grid-forming (GFM) control and fast frequency response are required for PFR. However, in GFM mode, active power is determined by the phase difference between the inverter terminal voltage and the point of common coupling voltage, causing spontaneous active power response in frequency deadband (FDB). In this paper, a strategy that adds a phase-locked loop (PLL) in the power synchronization control loop is proposed to restrict active power response in FDB, which can extend the lifespan of ES. Then, the proposed strategy is used in DC-coupled hybrid energy storage (HES), the slow-acting energy storage (SES) with larger capacity provides droop and damping for long-term frequency support with the control of GFM with PLL, and the fast-acting energy storage (FES) with smaller capacity provides inertia for short-term frequency support by following the SES's synchronization information. In addition, a step active power response with hysteresis is used in SES to maximize its advantages and decrease the times of the synchronous generator participation in PFR. Finally, the simulation results are provided to verify the proposed strategy's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Construction of a Real-type Empirical Platform for Flexible Interconnection of Source-grid-load-storage in Distribution Station Areas Facing Multi-flow Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the advancement of the construction of new power systems, the operating form of the power grid has changed from “source with load” dispatching model to the “source-grid-load-storage” coordinated, collaborative and interactive, and the application of new equipment and new technologies in the distribution network continues to move toward “energy-”Business is developing in the direction of multi-stream integration. Therefore, it is necessary to carry out adaptability testing and demonstration of new equipment and new technologies to improve the reliability and resource regulation capabilities of the distribution network. To this end, the construction of a real-type empirical platform for source-grid-load-storage flexible interconnection in distribution station areas oriented to multi-stream integration was studied. First, we analyze the construction ideas and content of the true-type empirical platform, then introduce the platform function implementation and testing methods, and finally select typical application scenarios to illustrate. The application of the real-type demonstration platform for source-grid-load-storage flexible interconnection in distribution station areas can solve the problem of insufficient assessment of new equipment in the distribution network and insufficient evaluation of new scenarios, and has broad application prospects.

Author Keywords: flexible interconnection in distribution station areas

articleTitle: Research on the Calculation Method of Geoelectric Field Environment Under Strong Geomagnetic Disturbance Events
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Geomagnetic disturbance events could induce geomagnetically induced currents(GIC), which directly damages primary equipment such as transformers and circuit breakers, posing a threat to power grid security. Strong geomagnetic disturbances(GMD) can be generated by late-time high-altitude nuclear electromagnetic pulses(HEMP-E3) and solar storm caused geomagnetic storms(SS-GMD), both of which lead to widespread strong disturbances in the geomagnetic field. Considering the construction of China's new power system and its complex geological structure, calculating the induced ground electric field under strong geomagnetic disturbance events is crucial. In this paper, we first analyze the similarities and differences in typical electric field waveforms under HEMP E3 and GMD environments. The calculation methods and geodetic models required for simulating induced ground electric fields under strong geomagnetic disturbance conditions are mentioned. Next, we discuss the method to obtain magnetic field data during strong geomagnetic disturbance events. Finally, two induced geoelectric field calculation models based on one-dimensional layered geodetic conductivity model and three-dimensional geodetic model are established. We simulate the temporal changes and visualize the distribution of induced ground electric fields under strong geomagnetic disturbance environments, and investigate the impact of magnetic field data and geodetic conductivity structure on the amplitude and direction of induced ground electric fields. This work can provide a reference for subsequent calculations of ground electric fields under HEMP E3 and the assessment of GIC in large and complex power grids.

articleTitle: Electric Power Load Forecasting Method Based on Contrastive Learning and Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Currently, as the proportion of new energy sources continues to increase, a large amount of uncertainty and randomness leads to a decline in the flexibility of the power grid companies' adjustment capabilities. Improving the accuracy of load forecasting can help power companies optimize generation planning, reduce the need for reserve capacity and lower operational costs. We propose a load forecasting method based on contrastive learning and attention mechanisms that can reduce load forecasting errors. Firstly, we proposes a contrastive learning method that constructs a pre-task to pretrain the Transformer encoder, which enables it to extract similarity features. Thereby it can reduce the redundancy of data and enhancing the correlation of samples. Secondly, we introduce a BVA(Bi-view attention module) that can perform weighted processing on feature vectors, making the information aggregated into the feature vectors more effective. Numerical case studies are conducted on real data sets, our proposed method can effectively reduce the error in load forecasting.

articleTitle: Analysis of DC ice-melting temperature rise characteristics and ice-shedding dynamic response of old OPGW lines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: OPGW has been widely used in the power grid. DC ice melting is one of the effective measures to prevent OPGW from icing accidents. Taking the old OPGW-48Bl-90 ground wire as the research object, the DC ice-melting entity model of OPGW under different operating conditions is established, and the temperature rise characteristics of OPGW during the DC ice-melting process are calculated. The influence of different ice thicknesses and external wind speed on the temperature distribution of OPGW is explored. The temperature change process of the OPGW center point is analyzed, and the OPGW temperature at ice-shedding time is obtained as the initial condition. At the same time, the influence of different ice thicknesses and external wind speeds on the dynamic response of OPGW at ice-shedding time is explored, and the dynamic response of old OPGW DC ice-shedding is analyzed. The results show that the radial temperature distribution of the old OPGW DC ice melting process is not uniform. The influence of ambient wind speed on temperature is nonlinear. The ambient wind speed will affect the temperature rise speed and ice melting time during the DC ice melting process of the ground wire; the higher the ice-melting current and the thicker the icing thickness, the higher the internal temperature of the ground wire at the ice-shedding time, and the larger the vertical maximum displacement of the OPGW midpoint. The vertical maximum vibration displacement of the OPGW midpoint increases with the increase of ice thickness.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Relay Suction Prediction Based on Improved Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Support vector regression (SVR), a machine learning method based on statistical learning theory, is an effective tool for sample training and data prediction. However, limited by its own principles and mechanisms, SVR often needs to adjust internal parameters when facing outliers and special experimental data in the data, and its accuracy and stability will be reduced. The model optimization of SVR by subjecting the data to outlier detection can improve the model performance. On this basis, this paper proposes a Grey Wolf Optimization (GWO) Support Vector Regression (SVR) algorithm based on isolation - based anomaly detection using Nearest - Neighbor Ensembles (iNNE). Firstly, outlier detection is carried out using the iNNE method, where the raw data are processed and outliers are removed; secondly, an improved kernel function is proposed to better map the input vectors from the low-dimensional space to the high-dimensional feature space; thirdly, parameter optimization of the SVR model is carried out by using the GWO algorithm to obtain the optimal parameters, and lastly, prediction is carried out on the electromagnetic relay suction dataset as an example, and is achieved by comparing the results with those of the un-optimized SVR, the traditional outlier detection method and the SVR before improving the kernel function are tested by comparing with the unoptimized SVR, the traditional outlier detection method and the SVR before improving the kernel function. The results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the computation speed and prediction accuracy.

Author Keywords: isolation - based anomaly detection using Nearest - Neighbor Ensembles (iNNE)

articleTitle: A Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis Method for Power Systems Based on Data Physical Models
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Cascade faults that cause power system collapse are usually caused by the further expansion of the harm caused by short-circuit fault events. To avoid cascading faults in the power system and ensure the safety of the power grid, it is necessary to effectively identify key information of simple faults in the early stages of the fault. This article proposes a method for diagnosing power system faults using a Data-Physical model, with the power system as the physical model and the BP neural network model as the data model. By utilizing the electrical parameters of non-faulty nodes to diagnose fault information in power systems, a fault set for diagnosing faults using non-faulty nodes is established. Then, a method using Zebra Optimization Algorithm to optimize the parameters of BP neural network is proposed to improve the matching degree between BP neural network and fault set. Finally, taking the “IEEE30 node” model as an example for fault detection. The results indicate that compared with the unoptimized BP neural network, the method proposed in this paper has a more accurate ability to diagnose faults in power systems.

articleTitle: Optimal SOP Configuration for Improving the Carrying Capacity of DG in Distributed Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rise of clean energy, the limitations of traditional thermal power generation are becoming increasingly apparent. The rapid growth of new energy installed capacity, especially distributed generation, presents numerous challenges to the distribution network. Soft open points (SOPs) offer a potential solution by regulating power flow and improving the penetration rate of distributed generation. However, the selection of SOP location and capacity significantly impacts the installed capacity of distributed generation. Therefore, it is necessary to study the configuration method of SOPs in order to enhance DG's carrying capacity in a multi-SOP scenario. This paper proposes a multi-SOP based optimization configuration model for maximizing DG's carrying capacity while considering safe operation constraints within the distribution network. To improve convergence and calculation efficiency, nonlinear constraints in this model are simplified and transformed into a convex optimization model that can be solved using commercial solvers. Finally, we verify the effectiveness of our proposed optimization model by analyzing a modified IEEE33 distribution network model and comparing it with traditional calculation methods.

articleTitle: Interval Observer-Based Attack Detection in Smart Grid Under FlexRay Communication Protocols
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, the detection of false data injection attacks (FDIA) in the smart grid based on interval observer is studied under the FlexRay communication protocol. The FDIA is highly stealthy and can modify the sensor data to affect system performance without being detected by common detection mechanisms. A cyber-attack detection mechanism against FDIA is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the smart grid is divided into several sub-areas for analysis and modeling, and a novel FlexRay communication protocol is designed to schedule the transmission of information in each sub-area. Next, an interval observer considering internal state boundaries and disturbances is designed based on the information after transmission to estimate the upper and lower bounds of the system states. An algorithm for attack detection against FDIA using interval residuals from interval observers is proposed. In addition, using the augmentation technique and the Lyapunov stability analysis method, sufficient conditions to ensure the stability of the estimation error system are given in the form of linear matrix inequality (LMI), and the interval observer gains are obtained by solving the LMI. Finally, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed method is verified by a simulation example.

articleTitle: State of Health and Remaining Useful Life Prediction of Li-ion Batteries Based on Improved Support Vector Regression
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The state of health (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) are both important parameters that reflect the degree of aging of Li-ion batteries. Support vector regression (SVR) has advantages in processing small sample data and time series analysis but is challenging to select kernel parameters. In this paper, we present an improved SVR model based on the Cauchy Variation Ant-lion Optimization (CALO) algorithm to enhance the prediction performance of SOH/RUL. Firstly, we conduct feature selection and select health factors based on correlation analysis. We then use the Ant-lion (ALO) algorithm to optimize kernel parameters and incorporate the self-adaptive T-distribution Cauchy variation into the ALO algorithm to improve its global convergence and local search ability. Finally, the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA) and Center for Advanced Life Cycle Engineering (CALCE) datasets are used to compare and validate the proposed method. The results demonstrate that the proposed method has a faster convergence speed and higher optimization accuracy, which can effectively enhance the accuracy and robustness of the SOH and RUL prediction of Li-ion batteries.

articleTitle: Coordinated Optimal Configuration Method of Wind Power Load Shedding Rate and Energy Storage Aiming at Active Frequency Support
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the increase of renewable energy, the system frequency modulation ability is insufficient, and the relevant departments require that renewable energy should have the active support ability of power system frequency change. Long-term active load shedding to achieve frequency support will cause power generation loss and economic damage; if the maximum output of the wind turbine is taken as the active support task by the energy storage, the amount of energy storage required is large. Therefore, this paper proposes a coordinated optimal allocation method of wind power load shedding rate and energy storage capacity with the goal of frequency active support. From the economic point of view, the optimal allocation relationship between wind power load shedding rate and energy storage capacity allocation is analyzed to find the optimal setting of load shedding rate and energy storage capacity.

articleTitle: A Variable Gain Discrete Time Sliding Mode Observer for MMC Capacitor Voltage Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC) is one of the main development directions in the future medium and low voltage DC transmission and distribution field. In engineering, capacitive voltage sensors are usually configured for all submodules to ensure high reliability measurement, but this makes the hardware structure more complex. This paper proposes a control algorithm for online adjustment of observer gain based on discrete-time sliding mode observer (DTSMO). A weighted error judgment energy function is defined and three modes are distinguished. A transition mode is introduced between the approaching mode and sliding mode, and the gain within each mode is adjusted online according to the size of each component error function. This algorithm suppresses the chattering of traditional DTSMO during parameter changes and reduces the voltage error of each observed SM, this observer can eliminate all capacitive voltage sensors within a single bridge arm, and is designed based on the consideration of uncertain parameters outside of MMC. Its stability and convergence have been mathematically proven. Finally, simulation and experimental results of hardware prototypes has verified that the proposed VDTSMO observer has good steady-state and transient performance.

articleTitle: Modeling and Analysis of Voltage Harmonic for Active Neutral-point-Clamped Five-Level H-Bridge Inverter in Consideration of Dead-time
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The active neutral-point-clamp five-level (ANPC-5L) multi-phase H-bridge inverter has the advantages of a simple interface to the ship's medium voltage DC network, the single H-bridge topology with nine levels of output voltage and switching frequency multiplication, etc. To prevent the bridge leg from passing through, dead time needs to be set for inverters. However, for the medium and high voltage inverter, the dead time is up to 10μs, which has a prominent impact on the output harmonics. To accurately analyze the influence of the dead time of the ANPC-5L H-bridge inverter on the output harmonics, it is necessary to analytically model and verifies the output voltage harmonics considering the dead time. In this paper, the principle of the phase-shifted PWM(PS-PWM) method of ANPC-5L H-bridge inverters were firstly introduced. Then, the analytical models of output voltage harmonics with and without considering the dead time were established based on the double Fourier series approach and the harmonic distribution of the dead-time effect was accurately characterized.
