Based on the above, the theoretical calculation results of output harmonic analysis modeling of ANPC-5L H -bridge topology considering dead-time are verified by offline simulation and experiment, and the correctness and feasibility of the theoretical modeling are verified. The results of this study can be used as a reference for quantitative analysis of output harmonics of ANPC-5L H-bridge inverter considering dead-time and extended to other multi-level inverters for harmonic analysis and modeling.

articleTitle: Electric Field Optimization for Enhanced Insulation in 10kV SiC MOSFET Power Modules Based on Chipwall Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The insulation ability is crucial for the long-term operation of medium voltage power modules, and the concentration of internal electric fields at insulation weak points of medium voltage power modules will have a strong impact on them. This article investigates new electric field concentration points in medium voltage power modules, in addition to traditional three-phase points, and proposes an electric field optimization method for verification. Technology computer aided design (TCAD) simulation analysis of the insulation weak area under the high DC voltage stress shows that the maximum electric field strength at the interface between the packaging material and the chip terminal is higher than 18 kV Imm, which will lead to insulation degradation of the silicon gel. Therefore, the optimization design is proposed, and the method of reducing the internal electric field stress of silicon gel by pasting the chip insulation wall(Chipwall) on the chip surface is verified through simulation. Finally, two types of 10kV power modules with or without chip insulation walls were fabricated and subjected to partial discharge (PD) testing to verify the insulation improvement of the optimized design. Through optimization, under 8.5kV DC, the partial discharge pulse of the power module withchip wall structure was much lower than that of themodule without chip wall, proving the effectiveness of chip wall for insulation enhancement.

articleTitle: Adjustable Potential Evaluation Strategy of Energy Storage Participating Grid Peak Shaving Regulation in Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Virtual power plant is an important application scenario of energy storage, and energy storage also closely combines virtual power plant with power grid, bringing innovation and reform of source network load. An assessment strategy of the adjustable potential of energy storage in virtual power plant is proposed in this paper. First, an assessment model of adjustable potential of individual energy storage is constructed to achieve quantitative assessment and classification of its potential. Then, the adjustable potential evaluation method of polymer energy storage is proposed to realize the calculation of its potential. Secondly, tap the adjustable potential of the reserve potential pool and evaluate its potential to realize the reuse of energy storage resources in the reserve potential pool. Finally, the potential of adjustable polymerization in the virtual power plant is evaluated, and the response time sequence of energy storage participating in the peak clipping regulation is arranged. The calculation model and evaluation strategy proposed in this paper can evaluate the adjustable potential of individual and aggregate resources, which is conducive to improving the accuracy, rationality and effectiveness of the declared capacity of virtual power plant, and can provide theoretical reference and application guidance for virtual power plant to participate in peak cutting regulation, resource scheduling, response capacity declaration, energy storage resource management, etc.

articleTitle: A bad data identification algorithm based on voltage code
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the increasing complexity of modern power systems, the quality and integrity of measurement data have become crucial for ensuring the system's normal operation. Research and application of bad data identification techniques in power systems are gaining more attention. This paper draws an analogy to base-n code in mathematics and computer science, proposing voltage code based on the impedance matrix of power network nodes. It analyzes the role of voltage code as a ‘weight’ reflecting the impact of current injection on voltage. An error phasor AU containing information about bad data is constructed by measuring current and voltage. The paper analyzes the different effects of various types and quantities of bad data on AU, revealing three distinct characteristics of AU. Based on these characteristics, an algorithm for identifying bad data using voltage code and the measurement data itself is proposed. This algorithm does not require redundant measurements and can quickly identify bad data during system operation. The effectiveness of this method is validated through simulations using the IEEE 39-node system as a typical case study.

articleTitle: Evaluaton on Configuration and Economic Performances of Large-Scale Wind Power to Ammonia System with Different Installation Locations and Operation Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The green ammonia system powered with wind energy generators not only improves the utilization of installed wind power systems, but also reduces ammonia plant carbon emissions. However, due to the fluctuation of renewable energy in wind turbine (WT) generation systems, the operating points of the wind power to ammonia (WPtA) system fluctuate in a wide range, which greatly reduces the overall operation efficiency and reliability of the system. To this end, this paper proposes a capacity optimization configuration model of WPtA system for GW-scale. By the proposed model, the minimum unit ammonia cost is adopted as the objective function considering the operation constraints and strategies of different system configuration and different installation sites to optimize the configurations of main components such as the capacity of electrolysis hydrogen production system, chemical energy storage system, hydrogen storage system and synthetic ammonia system. Taking the GW-scale WPtA system as an example, the impact of five different installation sites on the optimal configuration and economic performances of the system is discussed and compared with different strategies of the system configuration and operation.

articleTitle: Uncertainty Modeling of Electricity Indirect Carbon Emission Intensity at Grid-Connected Point of IES
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the low-carbon optimization scheduling of the grid-connected integrated energy system (IES), elucidating the carbon reduction responsibility of electricity consumers involves considering the electricity indirect carbon emissions resulting from grid electricity purchases. Nevertheless, based on the carbon emission flow theory, determining the electricity indirect carbon emission intensity at different power system nodes relies on real-time active power flow in the grid, posing challenges for accurate advance predictions. In order to achieve day-ahead robust low-carbon optimization, modeling the electricity indirect carbon emission intensity with budget uncertainty set requires obtaining the predicted values, predicted intervals, and uncertainty budgets. As an artificially defined virtual physical quantity, the modeling process of electricity indirect carbon emission intensity is different from that of the source-load parameters of real physical quantities, so a comparison of the methods for obtaining uncertain parameters for both is necessary. Firstly, the paper analyzes how to obtain the predicted values of electricity indirect carbon emission intensity. Subsequently, an analysis of the variation trend in electricity indirect carbon emission intensity under source-load changes is conducted to determine the prediction methods for the predicted interval. Following that, an analysis of the selection of uncertain budgets is conducted. Finally, conclusions are drawn, clarifying the similarities and differences in the methods of obtaining carbon uncertainty parameters and source-load uncertainty parameters.

articleTitle: Lifetime Prediction of Low Voltage Electrical Machines Based on Accelerated Aging Tests Under Periodic Temperature Profile
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Low-voltage electric machines (EMs) with high power density and compact volume represent the key target in transportation electrification. In order to safely carry out the designated mission profile throughout the life service, the EM should be conceived according to an appropriate trade-off between reliability and performance. Although the over-engineering of the electrical insulation ensures the reliability requirements, its adoption compromises the EM performance. Therefore, a shift towards physics of failure (PoF) methodologies applied to electrical insulation is often preferred to fulfill the demanded reliability standards, while achieving optimal performance. In literature, constant temperature thermal aging is often considered in EMs' design, although most EMs experience a variable temperature profile during their operations. Thus, in this paper, the accelerated thermal aging tests are performed at variable temperatures employing three periodic temperature profiles (TPs) and lifetime is predicted based on test results. Finally, a reliability assessment is conducted to achieve a more comprehensive EM design.

articleTitle: Quantitative Evaluation Method For Adjustable Resource Regulation Capacity Considering Power Grid Regulation Requirements
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The large-scale integration of renewable energy sources poses new challenges for power grid operation and dispatch. The introduction of a large amount of controllable loads and energy storage systems can reduce the peak-to-valley difference of the grid's net load and the difficulty of peak shaving, while improving the accuracy and efficiency of grid dispatch. Considering the requirements and capabilities of grid regulation, a quantitative evaluation method for the controllable resource regulation capability is proposed in this paper, which takes into account the grid regulation demand. Firstly, the historical data of the controllable resources are processed using the Isolation Forest algorithm to obtain the effective data set of the controllable resources. Then, the controllable resources of the source-load-storage system are classified according to the regulation capacity required by the grid in different dispatch cycles. Secondly, the Long short-term memory (LSTM) neural network model is used to predict the controllable time of each type of controllable resource. Thirdly, a quantitative method and evaluation index system for the controllable resource regulation capacity is established, which includes three quantification levels: steady-state performance, dynamic performance, and regulation potential. These are separately aggregated into quantitative sub-indices, and different weights are assigned to each sub-index to calculate the controllable resource's score on each sub-index. Finally, the feasibility of the proposed quantitative evaluation method is verified through case analysis.

articleTitle: Risk-Minimizing Real-Time Dispatch for Power Systems with High Proportion Variable Renewable Generators Based on Conditional GMM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Real-time dispatch plays a crucial role in managing the integration of large-scale variable renewable generation (VRG) into the grid. However, it necessitates enhanced requirements for renewable energy uncertainty modeling and risk management. This paper addresses this problem by realtime characterization of renewable uncertainties and building a risk-minimizing realtime dispatch model. The conditional Gaussian mixture model (CGMM) is employed to model VRGs, which can sufficiently capture multidimensional scenario-wise features. Specifically, time is modeled as a two-dimensional trigonometric series to account for the discreteness and periodicity of time features. We characterize the temporal correlation of unit output by modeling the joint distribution of prediction errors over continuous time intervals. Building upon that, we construct a two-stage risk-minimizing model for realtime dispatch, where the objective is to minimize the probability of constraint violation. The sample averaging approximation (SAA) technique is applied to transform the intractable model into a mixed-integer linear program problem. Numerical tests verify that the proposed model contributes to the efficient integration of VRGs while maintaining system stability and security.

articleTitle: Phase Identification Method for Low-Voltage Distribution Network Users Based on Optimization Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The accuracy of the phase connection relationship among low-voltage (LV) users significantly affects the optimization of the network operating status. Based on the electrical quantity data collected by smart meters, a method for phase identification of users in a low-voltage distribution network (L VDN) is proposed. First, a three-phase LinDistFlow model is established for the L VDN to obtain the coefficient between the square of the user node voltage and the square of the phase voltage on the secondary side of the transformer. This coefficient is characterized by a 0–1 distribution, which provides principle support for phase identification. Then, the phase identification problem is transformed into a 0–1 optimization problem and the Mixed-Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model is constructed. Finally, based on the historical data of voltage, active power, and reactive power collected by the smart meters at the LV side of the transformer and at each user within the LVDN, phase identification is achieved by solving the MILP model. The simulation example results show that the method has 100% identification accuracy and strong stability, which can effectively resist the interference of smart meter sampling error. At the same time, this method uses only the voltage and power data collected by the smart meters on the secondary side of the transformer and the user nodes for phase identification. It is of high practical engineering value because it works even when the LVDN topology, line parameters, and phase of all users are unknown.

articleTitle: Secure Transmission with a Full-Duplex Relay in Power Line Communications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the increasingly prominent security problems of Industrial Internet and the rapid development of computing technology, the security of power line communication (PLC) based on classical encryption technology faces new challenges. In this paper, a secure transmission scheme of PLC relay network based on full-duplex (FD) is proposed. In this scheme, the transmitter transmits the composite signal containing the information-bearing signal and the jamming signal. The relay forwards the received signal in the last time slot according to the amplify-and-forward (AF) strategy while receiving the signal transmitted by the transmitter. The receiver transmits the jamming signal while receiving the signal transmitted by the relay. Based on the lognormal correlated channel model and the Bernoulli-Gaussian noise model, we derive the closed-form expressions for average secrecy capacity (ASC), secrecy outage probability (SOP), and effective secrecy throughput (EST), assuming maximum ratio combining are utilized at the eavesdropper. According to the theoretical analysis, we find the optimal power allocation to improve the secrecy performance with the external eavesdropper or the untrusted relay. Furthermore, Monte-Carlo simulation is utilized to verify our analysis. Simulation results show that the proposed method is superior to the traditional scheme.

articleTitle: Static Voltage Stability Analysis of Renewable Energy Multi-Infeed Systems Based on Margin Index
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Substituting a high proportion of renewable energy sources for traditional synchronous generators can lead to a deterioration in the system's static voltage stability. This paper proposes extending margin-based voltage stability indices based on the load side Thevenin equivalent, to the renewable energy source side for assessing the static voltage stability of renewable energy multi-infeed systems. Firstly, a comprehensive analysis of both the load and renewable energy sources is conducted, and normalized expressions for three margin indices are derived based on a single-machine black-box system. Secondly, the characteristics of the margin indices are analyzed, validating their applicability in a single-infeed system. Thirdly, a method is introduced for conducting static stability analysis on the renewable energy source side of multi-infeed systems using Thevenin equivalent. Finally, the effectiveness of the indices under different growth scenarios is verified in a modified IEEE 39-node system, expanding the application scenarios of these indices.

articleTitle: Non-invasive Load Monitoring Based on CNN-LSTM-Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the large-scale deployment of smart meters at the receiving end of power, the idea of using non-invasive load monitoring (NILM) to realize intelligent electricity consumption, energy saving and emission reduction has attracted the attention of researchers. NILM technology can be used as one of the auxiliary services provided by power grid to users, which can improve users' awareness of energy saving and improve the accuracy of load forecasting. Traditional NILM technology has some problems, such as low resolution and slow decomposition speed. This paper proposes a deep learning model of CNN-LSTM-Attention model, which introduces Attention mechanism in the traditional CNN-LSTM model. Finally, the model is evaluated by using REDD data set, which proves that the model has good performance in the decomposition speed and precision of specific electrical equipment.

articleTitle: Time-Domain Stability Analysis and Improvement of Two-Stage Three-Phase Off-Grid Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Two-stage three-phase off-grid inverter could be connected to photovoltaic systems devices to provide reliable power supply for critical loads. However, this system has stability problems under disturbance. In this paper, a time-domain model of the two-stage three-phase off-grid inverter is first established, and based on the time-domain model, the stability of this two-stage three-phase inverter is analyzed based on Floquet theory, and further verified by simulation. To further improve the robustness and extend the stability region of two-stage three-phase off-grid inverters, a time-domain stability improvement method is proposed based on the time-domain stability criterion and eigenvalue sensitivity theory, as well as a new stability control strategy with additional inductor current feedback is obtained by using the proposed stability improvement method. Following, the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed control strategy are proved by comparing the stable region between the inverter with traditional PI control and the proposed control strategy. Finally, the conclusions are drawn. This paper provides a fast way to accurate analyze the stability of two-stage three-phase off-grid inverters and a easy way to improve the stability of two-stage three-phase off-grid inverter according to the real application requirements.

articleTitle: Characterization of Space Charge Transport in Power Module Packaging Systems Under Different Operating Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The electrode-substrate-packaging material triple region in power modules is a critical insulation weak point that has attracted significant attention. However, most existing studies on electric field characteristics within power modules ignore space charges or oversimplify the insulation structure, thereby lacking a thorough understanding of the charge distribution inside the packaging system. In this study, a surface potential decay test was employed to determine the charge transport characteristics of the packaging material. Subsequently, A physical model was developed to reproduce the actual structure of the power module, and a bipolar charge transport mathematical model was developed to study the charge and electric field distribution within the encapsulated system under off and on conditions. The findings reveal that charge injection leads to decreased electric fields in the triple region while increasing electric fields at the interface between packaging material and ceramic substrate regions. The AlN substrate packaging system exhibits higher charge density due to its high shallow trap density which facilitates the charge transport process. This study reveals the charging behavior in the power module under different working conditions and provides data support for optimizing the electric field design.

articleTitle: Research and Application of Surface Detection Device for Minor Oil Seepage Fault of Submarine Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: For oil seepage faults of oil-filled submarine cables with no damage to electrical insulation, fault troubleshooting has always been a worldwide problem. Under the background that electrical and hydraulic signals can not be accurately located, finding fault points from tens of kilometers of submarine cable routing is like looking for a needle in a haystack. Therefore, it is necessary to improve the detection efficiency and scope to meet the actual detection needs. This paper proposes a set of real-time fluorescence detection device for submarine cable oil seepage fault detection. By installing a surface operation platform to carry out fluorescence detection device, real-time detection of submarine cable insulation oil can be realized on the water surface, rapidly narrowing the scope of submarine cable oil seepage fault detection, and greatly improving the work efficiency of fault detection.

articleTitle: Equivalent Energy Storage Modeling of Steam Accumulator Towards Multi-Energy System in Textile Industry
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The textile industry typically requires industrial steam as a crucial energy source in the production process, which formulates a multi-energy system with steam and electric flows. As the disparity between peak and off-peak electricity prices persists and expands, the integration of an electric steam boiler with a steam accumulator (SA) who performs a storage-like characteristics offers a viable means to enhance the economic efficiency of industrial operations. Nevertheless, the intricate nature of energy transfer within the SA poses significant challenges in modeling and optimizing the multi energy system. Hence, this study constructs the mathematical model of SA's charging and discharging process, earns the mass flow rate and energy of steam based on temperature, proposes an equivalent energy storage model of SA towards the multi-energy system in textile industry, and portrays the calculation method for determining the scheduling boundary of the SA for better application on the modelling of the multi-energy system in textile industry. By employing empirical data from Changzhou Hongrui Changtai Textile Factory, the equivalent energy storage model of the SA is computed.

articleTitle: Problems and Countermeasures of Energy Storage Construction for Resource-Poor Provinces
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Maintaining the balance of the new power system is crucial, and energy storage plays a significant role in achieving this. Recently, China has been actively promoting the development and application of new energy storage by issuing relevant policy documents, which has further facilitated the participation of new energy storage in the electricity market. Provinces lacking primary resources are often highly dependent on external energy, and energy storage technology can effectively balance the relationship between supply and demand, which is of great significance for maintaining the stable operation of power grids. This paper analyzes the problems existing in the development of energy storage in some resource-poor areas of China, and conducts simulation calculations and profit and loss analysis of new energy storage from the perspective of the entire life cycle combined with the peak-valley time-of-use electricity price policy of a central-eastern province. Then some suggestions have been put forward to promote new energy storage to participate in the electricity market.

articleTitle: Platform Economy Enables Electricity Retail Trading Market: ——Take “Lai Tao Dian” retail trading platform in Yunnan Province as an example
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the full liberalization of general industrial and commercial users to participate in market-oriented transactions, the scale of the retail market will further grow rapidly. In 2021, Kunming Power Exchange Center established the “Lai Tao Dian” retail power trading platform to provide better services for retail users and power selling companies, demonstrating that the platform economy enables Yunnan's electricity retail market. In order to further promote the reform of national electricity sales side, this paper studies the characteristics of platform economy and the operation mode of power retail platform, and believes that the current platform economic practice can meet the needs of various power market players. The platform economy is conducive to promoting the reform of the power selling side, guiding the digital and intelligent transformation of the power selling industry, and laying a good foundation for the integration of the ecological value chain of the power selling industry. This paper puts forward suggestions on the continuous improvement of design, operation and governance capabilities of “Lai Tao Dian” platform.

articleTitle: Modal decomposition analysis of flow characteristics with a pump model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Reversible pump-turbines are currently the only commercially available large-scale energy storage devices, serving as the core components of pumped storage power stations. The safety and stability of these units have always been of concern, as their operational instability is often closely related to internal flow mechanisms. The complex fluid motion contains the vast majority of information in high-dimensional data. Thus, accurately extracting flow structures from complex flow fields and delving into their intrinsic mechanisms remain challenging. This paper introduces two flow field modal decomposition methods, Proper Orthogonal Decomposition (POD) and Dynamic Mode Decomposition (DMD), to reconstruct transient complex flow fields under pump operating conditions in pump-turbines. The aim is to study the characteristics of flow field evolution in a low-dimensional form. The results indicate that both methods can effectively capture the main features of the flow field, particularly in the blade region, showing distinct separation and vortex structures. This validates the feasibility of POD and DMD methods in achieving dimensionality reduction and reconstruction of complex flow fields.

articleTitle: Distributed Robust Optimization-Based Coordinated Day-Ahead Scheduling Method for Distribution-Microgrid Coordination
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Microgrids are essential for integrating new energy sources and enhancing distribution network reliability. Coordination among multiple microgrids is crucial for safe and economic operation. Coordinated dispatching requires a distributed approach considering uncertainties in new energy sources and discrete control devices. The method employs distributed robust optimization for uncertainty representation and the SDM-GS-ALM algorithm for discrete control. It approximates integer variables through convex hulls, ensuring convexity. The C&CG algorithm serves as the outer layer, embedding SDM-GS-ALM in various stages. This establishes a framework for distributed computation in coordinating distribution and microgrids. The proposed method's effectiveness is validated using the North American 5-node system with Aggregate equivalent method for line operation state consideration.

articleTitle: Optical Efficiency Optimization Algorithm for Heliostat Field in Solar Power Tower
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The optical efficiency of a heliostat cluster plays a pivotal role in determining the operational effectiveness of a concentrating solar power system. This study explicates the fundamental principles concerning the radial-staggered layout of heliostat fields and expounds upon the methodology employed in quantifying its optical efficiency. The focus lies in an improved algorithm for assessing shadowing and blocking losses using three-dimensional geometric projection, with a primary objective to ensure simulation accuracy while reducing computational costs. As such, the optical efficiency of individual heliostats can be swiftly assessed, enabling the optimization of hundreds or thousands of heliostat layouts. As a practical case study, simulation analysis and layout optimization of the solar power tower's heliostat field are conducted in Harbin, China, yielding the spatial-temporal distribution pattern of optical efficiency. After optimization, the blocking losses of the heliostat field for a 5-MW solar power tower are reduced by 84.3%, while the annual optical efficiency increased by 8.8%.

articleTitle: Robust Optimization Scheduling Strategy for Electrothermal Cogeneration Virtual Power Plant Considering Auxiliary Services
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the Northeast region of China, where the proportion of renewable energy is high and the climate is cold, there is a high demand for renewable energy integration and heating stability. Aggregating electric-thermal flexibility resources in the form of virtual power plants and participating in the ancillary service market can help address these challenges. This paper first establishes an operational benefit model for virtual power plants in cold regions based on the characteristics of their resource endowments. The model considers the compensation mechanism in the Northeast's ancillary service market. Next, considering the synergistic interaction between peak regulation in the ancillary service market and virtual power plants in cold regions, the model comprehensively considers the scheduling potential of various types of flexible adjustable devices, the demand response capability of flexible electric-heat loads, and the peak shaving and valley filling effect of energy storage devices. A two-stage robust optimization scheduling model is constructed for electric-heat integrated virtual power plants to obtain the economically optimal dispatch plan under the worst-case scenario. A robust coefficient is introduced to flexibly adjust the conservatism of the optimized dispatch plan. The C&CG algorithm and strong duality theory are used for solving. Finally, a case study is conducted using the measured data from a continuous 7-day period in December 2022 in a specific area of Jilin Province. The results demonstrate that the coordinated operation of electric-heat integrated virtual power plants can effectively reduce the peak-valley difference in the system and bring incremental operational benefits to the system.

articleTitle: Ultra-short-term probability prediction of photovoltaic power based on DTW-KMedoids similar day clustering and XGB-BiLSTM model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The precise estimation of the probability interval for photovoltaic power holds paramount importance in quantifying the uncertainties in photovoltaic power predictions. This is pivotal for ensuring the safe and efficient functioning of modern power systems and scheduling practices, thereby mitigating potential risks. This paper introduces a novel approach aimed at enhancing prediction efficacy. To achieve this goal, a multi-step process is proposed. Initially, the XGBoost algorithm is employed to scrutinize the interrelationships between various features. Subsequently, the DTW-KMedoids time series clustering algorithm is implemented to cluster photovoltaic power series based on distinctive weather conditions like sunny, cloudy, and rainy days, using historical data sets as a foundation. Ultimately, tailored to different clustering outcomes, the BiLSTM neural network model is introduced. This advanced model enables ultra-short-term probability forecasts for photovoltaic power with a high degree of temporal precision (15-minute intervals) by capitalizing on the inherent time series dependencies in both forward and backward directions. To bolster computational efficiency, a parallel acceleration platform is utilized for model construction and expedited training procedures. Leveraging real-world photovoltaic output data from a specific station area, the study demonstrates that the proposed DTW-KMedoids-XGB-BiLSTM model surpasses alternative prediction models in terms of forecast accuracy. Consequently, the model generates dependable interval probability predictions for photovoltaic power, thereby contributing to more reliable energy management practices.

articleTitle: Review of Power Grid Optimization Scheduling Methods Based On Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In recent years, with the introduction of energy conservation and emission reduction targets, the introduction of renewable energy has become an important initiative. However, due to the many factors that affect the new energy units, the traditional scheduling method becomes inappropriate. If a more intelligent scheduling method is not developed, the lack of flexible energy scheduling capacity will further lead to problems such as insufficient wind power consumption level, inefficient power grid decision-making, high operating costs, and unstable energy supply. In order to solve the above problems and improve the environmental protection, efficiency, economy and safety of the power grid, this paper summarizes the application of artificial intelligence in the field of power grid scheduling, analyzes SAC, A3C and TD3 algorithms in detail, analyzes their mechanism through the algorithm structure, and summarizes the advantages and disadvantages of each algorithm and its application scenarios. In addition, this paper also analyzes the application of artificial intelligence in unit combination, economic scheduling optimization and optimal power flow optimization. Different from other review papers, this paper deeply analyzes several problems that may arise in the application of the algorithm, and specifically analyzes the future optimization direction and corresponding optimization methods, so as to improve the level of experience combination, fault handling, comprehensive consideration, interpretability and other aspects of the future agent.

articleTitle: Nondestructive Inspection of Steel Plates By Using Magnetic Absorption Robot and SH EMAT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the widespread use of steel structures such as petroleum storage tanks, metal bridges, and ships, the demand for periodic inspections has steadily risen. Addressing the safety risks associated with manually carrying inspection equipment to elevated locations, this paper proposes a non-destructive testing method for steel plates utilizing a magnetic adsorption robot and SH-EMAT. Equipped with electromagnetic acoustic transducers, the robot is remotely controlled to conduct inspections at designated locations. Employing permanent magnetic wheels ensures ample adsorption force for the entire robot. The electromechanical control system is meticulously designed, and the electromagnetic acoustic transducers are tailored by the compact robot. Energy consumption experiments under various operating modes and slot defect detection experiments on a metal plate were conducted. The results demonstrate the robot's capability to navigate vertically on a steel plate and effectively detect slot defects exceeding 1mm in depth. These findings validate the feasibility and significance of employing a magnetically adsorptive robot with electromagnetic acoustic transducers for steel plate defect detection.

articleTitle: Research on Dynamic Breakdown Characteristics of Bus-Charging Current Switching Test on Disconnector
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The bus-charging current switching test duty 1 is an important test to assess the dynamic insulation performance of isolating distance for the GIS disconnector. When the design of the fixed and moving contacts of the GIS disconnector is unreasonable, it may directly cause the disconnector breakdown to earth during the closing and opening operation. This article relies on the ultra-high voltage fault diagnosis analysis and test task of State Grid Corporation of China, six 1100 kV GIS disconnectors are used as the research object to conduct the bus-charging current switching test on disconnector, a broadband transient voltage to earth waveform acquisition system and arc optical monitoring system are constructed, and the measurement results are excellent. The research shows that the closing resistor has a good effect on limiting the overvoltage during the test duty 1; the increase of the inflation pressure helps to reduce the prestrike gap distance; improving the movement speed of the disconnector contacts helps to reduce the overvoltage amplitude; the initial electric field distribution between the moving and fixed contacts will have a significant impact on the subsequent arc development process. This study can provide guidance for customers on the internal insulation coordination of GIS disconnector and improvement of insulation structure design.

articleTitle: Catkin-Derived N-Rich Carbon Nanotube as an Anode Material for Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are widely used as a new generation of high-efficiency energy storage batteries because of superior specific energy, excellent cycle life, and low self-discharge rate. Commercial graphite is currently the mainstream anode material for LIBs, but graphite's limitations hinder the development of LIBs. Because of environmental friendliness, high efficiency and low cost, biomass carbon is expected to replace graphite as the next generation of anode materials for LIBs. In this paper, N-doped catkin carbon nanotubes (CCNT) were prepared by high-temperature carbonization method using catkin as precursor. CCNT provides more active sites and lower impedance, favoring Li<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">+</sup>storage and transport. In addition, N-doped improves the conductivity and electrochemical stability of CCNT. Therefore, CCNT-based LIBs exhibits excellent cycling and rate performance, providing a new option for realizing high-performance and low-cost LIBs.

articleTitle: Discharge Identification Method Based on Optical Emission Spectroscopy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The emission spectrum of plasma discharges encapsulates abundant physical information, reflecting critical plasma parameters such as reactive groups, gas temperature, and electron density. It also serves as a foundational element for identifying discharge types. This study designs two discharge platforms for executing microwave jet discharges and pulsed spark discharges. Through emission spectrum analysis, it elucidates the variations in plasma gas temperature and electron density within air, argon, and helium, correlating these changes with power supply output and gas flow rate. Additionally, to assess the efficacy of machine learning in datasets of limited scale, the research establishes a discharge identification model utilizing Deep Neural Networks (DNN) and another model based on the Kmeans clustering algorithm for recognizing four types of discharges. The findings demonstrate a direct relationship between discharge power and gas temperature across all discharge types, inversely correlated with gas flow rate, albeit with minimal impact on pulsed helium discharges. Except for an increase in electron density with power supply output in pulsed argon discharges, the other discharge types showed a decrease in electron density as power output increased. The influence of gas flow rate on electron density was marginal across all discharge types. The Deep Neural Network model achieved a 100% accuracy rate in identifying microwave and pulsed discharges, outperforming the K-means clustering algorithm-based model, which attained a 71.25% recognition rate, indicating a superior performance on small-scale datasets. This method, which necessitates only the extraction of light intensity data from the emission spectrum for feature derivation, is applicable across various discharge types, presenting significant practical relevance.

articleTitle: Modeling of Vanadium Redox Flow Battery Under Different Operating Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The performance of vanadium flow batteries (VRFB) can be severely reduced when operating at low temperatures due to changing electrolyte properties. In this work, we develop a non-isothermal model of VRFB dynamics that takes into account changes in electrolyte viscosity depending on temperature. The model is using available experimental and numerical data from recent literature. Using this model, the operation of 5-kW VRFB at low (5°C) and room (25°C) ambient temperatures is analyzed in two modes: constant electrolyte flow rate and constant pump power. As a result, the power loss is observed at constant flow rate due to intensive pump operation, and the capacity loss is reached 12% in the initial cycles of VRFB operation at constant pump power of 50 W. The results of this study highlight the significant change in battery dynamic characteristics at low ambient temperatures, indicating the importance of developing optimal cycling strategies for specific climatic conditions.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control for Modular Multilevel Converter with Reduced Switching Frequency Based on Improved Insertion Priority of the Sub-modules
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: When modular multilevel converters are used in medium and high voltage variable frequency drive systems, the switching frequency should be limited. Capacitor voltage balancing strategy based on insertion priority of the sub-modules (SMs) can effectively reduce the switching frequency. However, this strategy does not consider the switching frequency balance of the SMs. In this paper, a capacitor balancing strategy based on improved insertion priority of SMs is proposed. It is implemented based on model predictive control. The capacitor voltage and switching frequency balancing of SMs can be achieved. The strategy first simplifies the insertion priority. When the arm current is positive, only the upper limit of the allowable voltage distribution band is applied. When the arm current is negative, only the lower limit of the allowable voltage distribution band is applied. Then, the SMs within each priority level are sorted. Re-adjust the sequence of SMs with switching frequency that are too high or too low to keep their switching frequency as consistent as possible. The MATLAB/Simulink simulation results of MMC-PMSM show that the proposed strategy significantly reduces and balances the switching frequency of the SMs while ensures good control performance.

articleTitle: Low Voltage Ride-Through Method of Actively-supported Photovoltaic Unit Based on LSTM Optimized virtual impedance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In view of the power Angle instability and overcurrent of inverters caused by power grid voltage drop caused by faults, a low voltage crossing method of active supported photovoltaic unit based on virtual impedance optimization of short and long time memory neural network (LSTM) is proposed. Firstly, the grid type active support control strategy of PV array is proposed based on the output characteristics of PV array. Secondly, based on the traditional virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology, the transient voltage regulation equation is introduced to build a three-order model of synchronous generator. Then, based on this, the time of switching virtual impedance is determined by judging the operating state of the system by fault discriminator, and the magnitude of switching virtual impedance is determined by LSTM-based offline fault discrimination method. Finally, a grid- connected PV power generation system was built based on the DIgSILENT/PowerFactory power system simulation platform for simulation and verification, and the superiority of the proposed method was verified by comparison.

articleTitle: Analysis on the Reactive Power Regulation of Inverter and Voltage in Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Recently, more and more distributed photo-voltaic power generation is connected to the distribution network, but while connecting to the distribution network, it will encounter the situation of overload or under load of the current, which may lead to high or low node voltage of the bus nodes in the distribution network, and in order to ensure the safe and stable operation of the distribution network system, there is a great necessity to analyze the distribution of the voltage in the distribution network. In this paper, the LinDistFlow model of distribution network is firstly introduced, and then, considering the difficulty of modeling, the distribution network current model in the form of correlation matrix is derived, and then, the current model is combined with the Q-V droop control and the inverter output reactive power to study the characteristics of the inverter reactive regulation curve and the voltage of the distribution network. The combined model is tested and compared using variability indices on an IEEE 33 system considering droop settings. The results show that the Q-V regulation curve incorporating inverter droop control in the distribution network studied in this paper can improve the voltage distribution of the distribution network well.

articleTitle: Research on Energy System Planning for Data Centers Based on Hydrogen Electric Coupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Scientific planning of data center energy systems can achieve energy conservation and carbon reduction, and orderly achieve” dual control” of energy consumption and” dual carbon” of society. However, existing planning research mainly focuses on pure electrochemical energy storage, without considering new energy storage modes of hydrogen electric coupling. Meanwhile, there are few studies that use pure green energy supply as a guide to integrate energy and storage resources for planning and modeling. Based on the concepts of green energy supply and hydrogen electricity coupling, the storage, conversion, and balance of multiple energy sources including electricity, heat, and cold were analyzed. A data center energy system optimization configuration model, including photovoltaic power generation, hydrogen energy storage, and electrochemical energy storage, was constructed from two dimensions: reducing costs and reducing external energy dependence. The numerical results show that compared with pure electrochemical energy storage, the new energy storage planning scheme based on hydrogen electric coupling has lower economic cost and external energy dependence, and the proposed model has a good realistic matching degree.

articleTitle: Research on Fault-Tolerant Reconstruction Technology for Aerospace Electromechanical Systems Based on CPLD
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To address the high reliability requirements of aviation electromechanical control systems, this paper focuses on exploring control reconfiguration strategies for aviation electromechanical control systems. The article first establishes a reconfiguration strategy combining redundancy switching with robustness and adaptive capabilities for typical electromechanical control systems. Building upon this foundation, a fault-tolerant strategy is proposed specifically for the core controller of electromechanical control systems in aviation.

articleTitle: Firm Solar Power Forecast through Battery Storage and PV Overbuilding with Solar Power Curve Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The decision-making of the managers of the photovoltaic (PV) plant is influenced by solar power forecasting. To mitigate errors in solar power forecasting, the firm solar power forecast strategy is proposed, the role of which is to ensure that the actual solar power fully meets the forecasted solar power. Specifically, the deviation between the actual and forecasted PV power is corrected through battery storage, PV overbuilding, and proactive curtailment. From the perspective of optimization, a mathematical model, which aims to minimize the equivalent annual cost of the PV-battery system, is formulated to implement the firm solar power forecast strategy. A case study in Heihe China is then conducted and the results indicate that the additional PV overbuilding with 1.12 MW and the installation of battery storage with a rated capacity of 2.61 MWh are required to obtain the firm solar power forecast at the lowest cost, which is 29.11% lower than that of the case where the PV plant with no overbuilding but with proactive PV curtailment and larger battery is assumed and set as a benchmark.

articleTitle: Wind-Photovoltaic-Storage Cooperative Bidding Strategy Based on Differential Evolutionary Game
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to solve the bidding problem of new energy grid-connected, this paper proposes a market model of joint participation of wind power, photovoltaic and storage in power generation side bidding to provide a stable power supply, and introduces evolutionary game theory into the bidding strategy of generators, so that a stable optimal bidding strategy can be obtained through dynamic evolution in an uncertain environment. In addition, a composite differential evolutionary game algorithm is proposed to solve the problem that the uncertainty of new energy output leads to the difficulty of solving the replicated dynamic equations of the evolutionary game. Finally, simulation results verify the economics and superiority of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Offshore Wind Turbine Vibration Characteristics an d Fast Detection Method based on Auto-correlation and Variational Mode Decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Due to factors such as harsh weather conditions and long-term external conditions during operation of offshore wind turbines, problems such as loose bolts and reduced tower stiffness have been caused. Rapid detection of a large number of wind turbine towers is a necessary means for operation, maintenance and repair. Using excitation and measurement information, the vibration excitation points, vibration bolt signals, etc. are processed through autocorrelation and variable mode decomposition methods to obtain the spectrum diagram of the vibration signal. Through comparative analysis of the spectra, it can be seen that when the bolt is loosened, free vibration will occur under pulse excitation, with the peak value at its natural frequency; when the bolt is completely loosened, the tower where the excitation point is located will have a peak value at its natural frequency; while the other excitation point will have a peak value at its natural frequency. The vibration effect of the tower will lead to changes in its vibration properties, an increase in the forced vibration component, and the proximity of the vibration spectra of the two towers. Through the calculation and analysis of the changing characteristics of the vibration spectrum of the relevant tower connected by bolts, it can provide theoretical and practical measurement methods for offline and online judgment and detection of local looseness of the tower.

articleTitle: Research on Multiobjective Optimization of Long-Stator Synchronous Linear Motors Structure for EMS Maglev Train
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The electro-magnetic suspension (EMS) high-speed maglev trains are currently the only commercially available high-speed magnetic suspension trains with advantages such as high efficiency and high speed. However, as the application and operation continue, the demand of usage can't be met by the existing operating speed. Therefore, it is inevitable to increase the speed of maglev trains. the structure of the existing long-stator linear synchronous motor (LSLSM) of the maglev train is designed according to the operating speed of 430 km/h. Therefore, its structure needs to be optimized for the operating conditions of 600 km/h and above. In this paper, firstly, the magnitude of propulsion force and suspension force, the magnitude of propulsion force and suspension force pulsation, and the suspension-to-weight ratio are taken as the optimization objectives, and then the weight factors are set according to the operating conditions of the maglev train respectively, and then Taguchi's method is used to design the orthogonal test scheme in combination with the signal/noise (S/N) ratio and the fuzzy theory. Finally, the optimization results are verified through finite element simulation comparison. The results show that: the magnitude of the propulsion force is increased by 5.22%, and the propulsion force suspension force fluctuation and propulsion force fluctuation are reduced by 38.66% and 30.48%, respectively; due to the optimization of the motor structure, the core of the LSLSM achieves a weight reduction of 32.06 kg, and the suspension-weight ratio is increased by 7.65%.

articleTitle: Research of Inherent Relationship between Contribution Proportion of Harmonic and Gear Ratio in FSCWPMSM
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The magnetic field modulation effect in fractional slot permanent magnet synchronous motors(FSCW PMSM) has received widespread academic attention in recent years, and the selection of the pole-slot combination will have a decisive impact on the performance of the motor. The Gear Ratio is a function closely related to the motor pole-slot combination, while the existing method of measuring the electromagnetic performance of motors based on the Gear Ratio has failed to accurately calculate contribution proportions of different harmonic field, since the existing theory does not conduct in-depth research on the distribution of harmonics in the modulated magnetic field, and cannot accurately calculate the proportion of each harmonic component. This article provides a more detailed elaboration and explanation of the relationship between the pole slot combination and the Gear Ratio in the FSCW PMSM after an in-depth analysis of the magnetic field modulation effect. Subsequently, the contribution proportion of different harmonics to torque has been accurately and quantitatively calculated based on different pole-slot combination. Then detailed analysis of the characteristic changes of magnetic field modulation effects in FSCW PMSM, thereby comparing the electromagnetic properties of the motors. The work of this paper is to analyze the electromagnetic performance of the motor from the perspective of magnetic field modulation, which is a supplement and expansion of the magnetic field modulation theory.

articleTitle: Research on Vibration Simulation of Anode Saturable Reactor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As a significant device in converter valve, the anode saturable reactor is stimulated by a continuous high-frequency current, which will cause the vibration of the reactor. In this paper, a full-size model is established for vibration analysis. First, a vibration experiment is proceeded and the magnetostrictive and magnetization characteristic of the silicon steel sheet are measured. Second, a model is established for simulation calculation. Third, the experiment data and the simulation results are compared. The results indicate that the model can basically fit the experiment vibration.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling Strategy of Distributied Electric Bus Charging Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The development of photovoltaic energy and electric vehicles in China has shown rapid growth in recent years. However, the transformer capacity in the charging station is limited, and the matching between power generation and installed capacity is not enough, resulting in photovoltaic power generation cannot be fully consumed. Moreover, large-scale intermittent electric vehicles and fluctuating photovoltaic power generation are connected to the grid, endangering the stability and safety of the power grid. Therefore, the power guidance of smart grids for electric vehicles has become particularly important. Firstly, this paper summarizes the process of responding to redundant photovoltaic generation of electric bus charging stations, and analyzes the charging demand of electric buses and the dispatching demand of photovoltaic consumption at stations from the two aspects of electric buses and electric bus stations operated by lines. On this basis, this paper analyzes the adjustable potential of electric bus charging at stations in different time periods, and establishes an electric bus charging model. Finally, this paper establishes a model of electric bus charging to consume photovoltaic power generation in the station. with the goal of minimizing the deviation between the sum of the total charging power of electric buses in the charging station in the station and the target value of demand response photovoltaic consumption, constructs the optimal scheduling models for electric bus charging to optimize the grid-connected charging time of electric buses and the amount of electricity in response to photovoltaic consumption, so as to maximize the utilization of photovoltaic power generation resources and ensure the stability and safety of the power grid.

articleTitle: Load Identification and Prediction Based on Feature Fusion and Lightweight Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Load identification and prediction is an important aspect of ensuring power supply-demand balance in power distribution areas, and it has significant guiding significance for the safe warning and stable operation of the power system. Affected by various other factors, the direct prediction model of power distribution area load usually has poor generalization ability and it is difficult to meet the load prediction requirements of complex power distribution areas. To improve the generalization ability of load prediction methods in power distribution areas, a load prediction method based on multi-environmental feature fusion, lightweight convolutional neural network, and convolutional long short-term memory network was proposed. Firstly, the environmental features were analyzed by principal component analysis (PCA), the input variables were reduced and corrected to extract the environmental feature main components that affect the load changes in the power distribution area. Based on lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) model, the power distribution area load was identified. Then, the identification results of power distribution area load and environmental feature main components were comprehensively analyzed. Based on bidirectional gated recurrent unit (BiGRU) network model, the sub-item load in power distribution areas was predicted. Finally, the prediction results of sub-item loads were linearly superimposed to obtain the final load prediction results of power distribution areas.

articleTitle: Driving Performance of an SDBI Actuator on Silicone Oils Under AC Electric Fields
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The non-toxicity, high temperature tolerance and voltage resistance of silicone oil make it a valuable electrical material. In electrohydrodynamic (EHD) pumps, the polarity-dependent properties of silicone jets promise a bright future in the field of eco-friendly microfluidics. Based on the previous exploration of the flow field characteristics of silicone fluids in surface dielectric barrier injection (SDBI) actuators, the present study addresses the velocity field data collected through the 2D-PIV technique, employing the momentum integration method to calculate the electric force of silicone wall jets under AC signals. The results demonstrate that the sign of the electric force varies with the signal polarity, and its magnitude accurately follows the signal waveform. The mean electric force increases quasi-linearly with voltage, and a signal with a voltage of 30 kV generates an electric force of about 2 mN/m to drive the silicone oil.

articleTitle: Resonance Suppression Method of the Interactive Current Based on Impedance Reshaping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This study discusses the problem of resonance suppression for multi-inverter systems with different parameters. The complex coupling of the system can lead to different types of resonance, resulting in a decrease in stability. Existing impedance reshaping methods are mostly for improving the input-grid current quality, neglecting other types of resonances. In the paper, a new energy cluster system model is established to analyze the resonance coupling relationship and to obtain the objective of system impedance reshaping. The parallel impedance is optimally designed to produce a suppression effect on different types of system resonance. Finally, the correctness of the related conclusions is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Asymmetric PM-Assisted Synchronous Reluctance Motor Based on NSGA-III
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Reluctance motor has the advantages of simple structure, low amount of permanent magnet and high stability. But reluctance motor's limited torque density hinders its widespread application. However, the problem of high torque ripple caused by the asymmetric topology of the permanent magnet still needs further optimization. Firstly, the structure of APMA-SynRM and the parameters to be optimized are introduced. The APMA-SynRM optimization steps are then designed. Then, the range of optimization variables is determined by parametric scanning of APMA-SynRM parameters, and the response surface of APMA-SynRM is established. The final optimal design was obtained by non-dominating genetic algorithm (NSGA-III), In conclusion, the comparison and analysis of the key performance indicators before and after APMA-SynRM optimization are presented.

articleTitle: Multi-Objective Optimization of Coil Arrays in Arrayed Wireless Power Transmission Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Array wireless power transmission (A WPT) systems use coil arrays as the coupling structure, which enables high power, high reliability power transmission. The coil array has numerous parameters and complex coupling mechanism, which makes it difficult to realize the optimal design. To solve this problem, this paper demonstrates a multi-objective optimization method for coil arrays. An analytical model of the coil array is established, and analytical expressions for the self inductance, mutual inductance and coupling coefficients are given. A multi-objective optimization process based on genetic algorithms and Pareto frontiers is proposed by the analytical model. The product of coupling coefficient and quality factor, and power surface density are chosen as the optimization objectives to find the optimal solution in the Pareto frontier. It is experimentally verified that the coil array designed by this method performs well with less output ripple and higher efficiency.

articleTitle: Injected Grid Current Quality Improvement Method for Grid-Connected Inverters Considering Inductor Nonlinearity
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Given that the photovoltaic (PV) output is usually intermittent and fluctuating, the grid-connected PV inverter may often operate at half load or even light load conditions, and the distortion of injected grid current deteriorates. Considering that the inductor made of magnetic powder core material behaves soft saturation and nonlinear characteristics, its inductance value can change with the current. Then, the current controller which is usually designed according to the rated power inductor value is relatively conservative and is not beneficial to the grid current quality when the inverter power changes. Therefore, this paper proposes an adaptive grid current quality improvement method for grid-connected inverter considering the inductor nonlinearity, which adaptively adjusts the current controller parameters at different power values on the premise of ensuring system stability. The inverter achieves better current harmonics suppression by increasing the system loop gain during power changes especially under low power conditions. The effectiveness of the improved method is verified through simulations and experiments.

articleTitle: Virtual Synchronous Generator Frequency Stability Control Based on Data-Driven Model
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The proposal of virtual synchronous generator (VSG) solves the problem of insufficient damping and moment of inertia in the grid-connected inverter, but when the system is disturbed, the stability of the system will be impacted. In this paper, frequency prediction base on data-driven model is added to the control module of VSG. Under the premise that the maximum capacity of energy storage release remains unchanged and the output power of the inverter does not exceed the rated capacity. Based on the limit value of the predicted frequency of the system after disturbance, and the advantage that the inverter parameters can be adjusted in real time, the setting interval of the virtual inertia and damping is increased, so as to improve the recovery effect of the output frequency of the system after disturbance. Finally, the validity of the model is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: DTP-PMSM fault-tolerant control strategy based on improved MRAS
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor (DTP-PMSM) is widely used in aeronautical electric propulsion systems, and vector space decoupling(VSD) is a common control method for them. On this basis, speed sensorless control and fault-tolerant control have also attracted many scholars' research. But the fault-tolerant control on the basis of MRAS is a difficult problem. This article presents a re-decoupling of the model for open-phase fault detection in DTP-PMSM. It proposes a method involving virtual voltage, which facilitates the reconstruction of the MRAS (Model Reference Adaptive System) with adjustable models. Furthermore, simple adjustments are made to the adaptive law. Finally, verification is conducted through SIMULINK simulations.

Author Keywords: dual three-phase permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Tensile Test and Defect Identification of Composites Insulator FRP Rod Materials Based on Acoustic Emission Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Using acoustic emission (AE) equipment to monitor the static tensile test of composites insulator FRP rod and its component materials, the acoustic emission signals of the three specimens in the tensile process were collected, and through the analysis of the acoustic emission parameters, a method that can be used for identifying the three types of damages, namely matrix cracking, interfacial delamination, and fiber breakage, was proposed. Firstly, the K-means clustering method is used for de noising, and then the random forest (RF) algorithm is used to establish a model to identify the three types of damage signals, namely matrix cracking, interfacial delamination and fiber fracture. The results show that this method can identify the three kinds of damage signals more accurately. For the acoustic emission signals generated by the stretching process of composites insulator FRP rod materials, the total recognition rate of the model reaches 87.3%.

articleTitle: Optimization of Integrated Energy System Capacity Configuration in Agricultural Parks Considering Diversified Utilization of Solar Energy
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In winter, due to the excessively high cost of conventional heating, numerous facility agriculture parks with high heating demand are left in an abandoned state. Given the above problems, this paper designs a cogeneration system considering the coupling of photovoltaic-photothermal-air source heat pump. The photothermal heat collection unit is used as an additional heating source of the system, and the air source heat pump is utilized as the combined heat and power equipment of the system. With the economic efficiency of the system for energy supply as the objective, a model is established to optimize the capacity configuration of the integrated energy system in agricultural park. Finally, taking the agricultural integrated energy system in North China as an example, the effectiveness of the photothermal heat collection unit and the air source heat pump in improving the diversified utilization of solar energy is verified, and the proposed optimization scheme for the integrated energy system capacity of agricultural park is verified to be economical.

articleTitle: Online Optimal Charging Strategy for Lithium-Ion Batteries Based on Model Predictive Control at Relatively High Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Conventional charging protocols of lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) are challenged with the balance between charging speed, battery safety, and cycle life, especially at relatively high temperatures. In this work, a novel online optimal charging method based on model predictive control (MPC) is addressed to handle the above issues. A new thermo-electric coupled equivalent circuit model which decomposes the cathode and the anode is constructed to precisely estimate the cell temperature and internal anode voltage. The model is then integrated into the MPC control framework to generate the optimum real-time applied current. The designed charging protocols consist of not only continuous current optimal charging (CCOC) but also pulsed current optimal charging (PCOC) which can moderate the cell heat generation and temperature rise. It can be concluded that the PCOC method significantly reduces the charging duration compared with the CCOC. Simulation results of the developed charge control algorithm under different initial SOCs and initial temperatures are also discussed, which verify the robustness of the proposed charging strategy.

articleTitle: Model Predictive Control Strategy for Energy Storage Smoothing Ability and Output Power Considering Smoothing Wind Power Fluctuation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The wind-storage combined system (WCS) can suppress wind power fluctuations and improve the economic viability of wind power grid connection. However, the output of energy storage is influenced by multiple factors. This article introduces the suppression capability index of energy storage batteries, designs a multi-objective optimization model for protecting energy storage batteries and ensuring grid-connected power suppression capability, proposes a model predictive control strategy (MPC) based on adaptive adjustment of energy storage charge state, and compares the proposed method with traditional model predictive control methods through simulation. The results show that under the same energy storage configuration ratio, the method proposed in this paper can effectively suppress wind power fluctuations, with better overall performance indicators compared to traditional model prediction methods. While optimizing wind power fluctuations, it also enhances the power support capacity of the energy storage system, balancing the trade-off between energy storage output and stability.

articleTitle: Research on a High-Precision and Fast Whole-Process Simulation Method Adapted to a High Proportion of new Energy Connected to the Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This is particularly relevant given the increasing ratio of distributed new energy access to the distribution network, which results in a more complex structure of the distribution network with a high proportion of new energy. The proposed method addresses the challenge of simulation difficulty in this context. The paper proposes a hybrid explicit and implicit simulation method to solve the problem of solving systems of differential equations in rigid systems. The electromechanical transient process is handled using the fourth-order explicit Runge-Kutta method with a small step size. For the medium- and long-term dynamic process, the implicit trapezoidal method with a large step size is employed. The hybrid simulation method ensures accuracy while improving efficiency. The improvement in simulation accuracy and speed of this hybrid simulation method compared with the traditional simulation method is verified by simulating the IEEE 33-node power distribution network

articleTitle: Symmetric Impedance Modeling of Power Controlled Grid Following Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The traditional impedance model three-phase grid following converter is asymmetric, it results the frequency coupling effects. Further more, it requires the impedance model of the converter to be represented by a second-order matrix, which makes the stability analysis more complicated. Therefore, based on strict mathematical proof, this paper proposes a modified instantaneous power calculation formula that makes the impedance model symmetrical while making power control accurate and simplifying the stability analysis. Finally, the effectiveness of the theoretical is verified by simulation results.

articleTitle: A Novel Modulation Algorithm for Efficient Heating of Air Conditioning Compressor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This research aims to improve the heating efficiency of compressor driven air conditioning systems in cold regions to combat the global warming and promote the energy efficiency. This study proposes a novel approach to efficiently heat the compressor by utilizing the losses of the electric motor. The energy conversion process during compressor preheating is analyzed firstly, and then the numerical relationships for the losses generated by the driver and the energy conversion within the compressor motor are established. To distribute energy effectively and adjust the heating power, a novel heating modulation algorithm is proposed. Additionally, the relationship between motor losses and input variables is explored using the finite element analysis. Experimental validation was conducted to determine the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Detuned Wireless Charging System with Constant Power Charging Ability and High-Misalignment Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In practical applications, wireless charging systems (WCS) should solve unavoidable misalignment problems and realize stable output over a wide load range. Therefore, a detuned WCS with solid anti-misalignment capacity and constant power (CP) output over a wide load range using the overlapping coil magnetic coupler (OCMC) and Buck converter is proposed in this paper. First, the system structure is designed, and then the relationship between the mutual inductance, load resistance, and output power is investigated. Second, the detailed coupling characteristic of the optimized OCMC is analyzed. Finally, the closed-loop workflow of the WCS is described, and simulation results are given.

articleTitle: A Partitioning Method for Distributed Generation Cluster of Distribution Power Grid with 5G Base Stations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents a distributed generation cluster partitioning method for a distribution power grid with 5G base stations.
