publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Doubly salient electromagnetic machine(DSEM), which is currently widely utilized in aircraft power supplies, electric vehicles, and agricultural machinery, has a simple and reliable structure. However, with the miniaturization, high-speed, and high-frequency development of motors, motor efficiency improvement has become an important factor restricting development. This research suggests a way to minimize copper loss by allocating field current and armature current efficiently to conserve energy. Firstly, this paper deeply analyses the loss components of DSEM and the impact of motor operating parameters on the losses. Moreover, an abridged parametric loss model was developed to elucidate the correlation between output efficiency and copper loss. Secondly, this paper explores the basic law of torque control by the combination of field current and armature current, and draws a cloud diagram between current and copper loss. Then, it's easy to observe the control parameters that minimize the losses and optimize the efficiency of DSEM. Ultimately, the validation findings demonstrate that the strategy can attain optimal management of DSEM.

articleTitle: Study on Electric Field Distribution of 500kV AC GIL Tri-post Insulator Affected by Metal Particles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Gas insulated transmission line (GIL) is of crucial importance in special transmission scenarios and plays an important part in the large AC/DC hybrid power grid. Metal particles generated during transportation and operation could seriously affect the internal insulation performance of the equipment, which may cause surface flashover, breakdown and other discharge faults. In this paper, the sources of metal particles in GIL are analyzed, and a 500 kV AC GIL 1:1 finite element model is established. The change of electric field distribution on the surface of tri-post insulator caused by suspended metal particles in GIL is studied. Also, the influence on electric field distribution on the surface of tri-post insulator with different metal particle shapes is analyzed. The conclusion can provide guidance for the suppression of metal particles in GIL.

articleTitle: An Efficiency Optimized Analysis Method for Synchronous Rectification Resonant Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Aiming to the issue of low efficiency caused by ZVS missing of phase shift modulation (PSM) under light load condition, an efficiency optimized analysis method (EDAM) for synchronous rectification resonant converters is proposed. EOAM is realized through the way of advance conduction of synchronous rectifier (SR). Benefit from the increase in SR early conduction time <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{\mathrm{R}})$</tex>, more and more energy can be fed back from the secondary side to the primary side. It helps to increase the resonant current to provide sufficient energy for the discharge process of the primary lagging leg switch, reduce the turning-on loss. However, it also results in the increasing of the conduction loss. Thus, the optimal SR early conduction time (TR_OP) corresponding to the optimal efficiency <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\eta_{\text{op}})$</tex> is obtained through the tradeoff between the reduced turning-on loss and the additional conduction loss. To verify the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis, a 500W experimental prototype of LCLC converter is built. Compared with the traditional method of without EOAM, the proposed EOAM can improve efficiency of light load (20% load) by more than 2% (93.757% to 95.821 %).

articleTitle: Minimum Loss Control Method of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Based on Strong Tracking Extended Kalman Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The conventional model of permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) neglects the impact of core loss, leading to reduced operational efficiency. To achieve minimum loss control, a robust tracking extended Kalman observer (STEKO) is proposed in this paper for realtime online observation of the iron loss current component, which can be incorporated into the minimum loss model. This proposed strategy can not only eliminate the complex parameter calculation required by traditional model-based minimum loss control methods but also address the limitations of extended Kalman observer (EKO) in handling sudden system changes. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method accurately computes the stator d-axis current with minimal losses and exhibits strong dynamic performance.

articleTitle: Distribution Network Topology Identification Based on Time Series Voltage Mutual Information and Probability Density Function
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Recognition of distribution network topology is usually based on switching and node related data. It is difficult to frequently interact with multi-dimensional and real-time data, but the reliability of the identification is not high only by uploading the switching quantity. In this paper, a topology identification method based on node voltage magnitude is investigated to accurately recognize the topology of distribution networks. First., take the example of a radial distribution network., mutual information is used to analyze the similarity of two nodes' timing voltages. Then., probability density distribution curves are used to determine whether multiple nodes are in the same branch. Next., the topology identification process is proposed: monitoring whether the topology is changed., determining which branch is disconnected., determining the exact location of the breakpoint., verifying whether the switch is correct., and reconstructing the topology. Finally., the IEEE33 node system is taken as an example and simulated in MATLAB for verification. The topology derived from the identification is accurate., proving the effectiveness of the method.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Magnetic Hysteresis Measurement and Modeling of Soft Ferrites Applied to Power Electronic Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Magnetic core is one of the key components of Power Electronic Transformers (PETs), and its magnetic hysteresis properties is vital for the accurate design and analysis of PETs. In this paper, measurement and modeling of magnetic hysteresis of soft ferrites at different temperatures are conducted. Jile-Atherton (J-A) model is utilized to model the magnetic hysteresis behavior. Firstly, a clarification on the correct form of the anhysteretic magnetization is made. Then, NeIder and Mead Simplex algorithm, a derivative free method, is employed to identify the parameters of the J-A model. A temperature-dependent J-A model is deduced by expressing the parameters as functions of temperature, and Curie temperature Tc and critical exponent β are introduced as the additional parameters. The simulation results and the area enclosed by BH data derived from the J-A model are compared with the measurement. Most of the results agree well with the measurement, the largest relative error is about 18.78<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>• Comparisons between the results acquired from the temperature-dependent J-A model and the measurement are made. This temperature-dependent J-A model shows good performance in predicting hysteresis behavior in lower temperature range. However, its performance in predicting hysteresis behavior in higher temperature range is not desired.

articleTitle: State of Health Estimation of Lithium-Ion Battery Based on Elman Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries have been very widely used in new energy electric vehicles with their high energy density and long service life. Its state of health (SOH) can largely affect the stable operation of electric vehicles. Therefore, It is of great importance to estimate the SOH of Ii-ion battery. In this paper, three features are extracted from the charging incremental capacity (IC) curve. The correlation between the selected features and the battery capacity is analyzed using Spearman's correlation coefficient and Pearson's correlation coefficient. An Elman neural network was developed to estimate the battery capacity, and the estimation results were analyzed by RMSE and MAE error indexes. SVM and BPNN are used as comparisons to verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Simulation Study on Temperature Distribution and Ampacity of HVDC Submarine Cable Laid in Cable Trench
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Steady-state ampacity and temperature are key parameters reflecting the operating status of high-voltage direct current (HVDC) submarine cables. A two-dimensional (2D) simulation model of the ±160 kV submarine cable in a trench-laying method has been established using COMSOL Multiphysics finite element software. The influence factors of temperature distribution, electric field distribution and ampacity of submarine cable are studied when the fluid medium of cable trench is air and water respectively. The results show that there are differences in the temperature difference across different radial inner and outer surfaces of the submarine cable insulation layer, with the greatest temperature difference occurring along the direction of gravity. The critical temperature difference for the reversal of the electric field distribution in the insulating layer, with the center acting as the pivot, is 7.4°C, and the field strength at the center remains constant at 10.0kV/mm. The steady-state ampacity, limited by the conductor temperature and the insulation layer temperature difference, shows a crossing point on the curve as the ambient temperature changes. Filling the cable trench with water significantly improve the ampacity. Increasing the width of the cable trench and reducing the thickness of the cover plate can improve the submarine cable's ampacity to a certain extent, with more pronounced effects when the fluid medium is water.

articleTitle: Research on Experiment Methods for Key Electrical Indicators of Megawatt Off-Board Chargers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to solve the problem of vacancies in the detection platform of megawatt-level off-board charger, this article proposes a key electrical index experiment method based on a hundred-kilowatt charging platform. Off-board chargers with output power of hundreds of millions and above are often realized by connecting and controlling multiple low-power charging modules. Therefore, this experiment method requires the establishment of a parametric model of the charging module in the megawatt charger, combined with the experimental calibration model of key electrical indicators of the actual charging module; then, an off-board charger is built by connecting and controlling a limited number of charging modules, and combined with The experimental calibration model of the actual charger; finally, the multi-dimensional gray prediction model is used to achieve the indicator prediction of the megawatt-level multi-charging module charger. The effectiveness of the indicator prediction results for the key electrical indicator tests of off-board chargers was verified through the experiment of actual chargers. The results show that this method is simple to implement and cost-controllable. It is an effective method to test key electrical indicators of megawatt chargers through data prediction and experimental verification.

articleTitle: Verification Method for Peak Voltage of Impulse Voltage Calibrator based on Diode Bias Compensation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The impulse voltage calibrator is the key piece of equipment for the traceability of impulse voltage measuring systems or digitizers. The uncertainty in the peak voltage and time parameters of the self-built impulse voltage calibrator are evaluated from the standard uncertainties in the components of the impulse forming network and charging voltage. The influence of the stray parameters of the pulse network on the uncertainty in the peak voltage is related to the evaluation method. In addition, the peak voltage of the calibrator varies with the connected load, and the stray capacitance of the load is difficult to accurately evaluate. This paper describes the feasibility and traceability of a peak voltage verification method for a self-built standard calibrator. Based on the unidirectional conduction characteristics of the diode, the peak value of the impulse voltage waveform is equivalent to the sum of the DC voltage, weak pulse voltage and instantaneous forward voltage drop of the diode. The circuit simulation method is used to determine the parameters of the verification circuit and the selection of diodes. An uncertainty evaluation method for the verification method is proposed. Compared with the GUM method, the method proposed in this paper has a smaller measurement uncertainty for higher voltages.

articleTitle: Research and Design of Wide Range High Voltage Input Series Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In high-voltage input applications, the switching device of a single ended flyback converter bears high voltage stress, which affects its safe and stable operation. To solve this problem, this article introduces the series flyback converter and analyzes its automatic average voltage characteristics. The topology exhibits good voltage sharing performance under both CCM and DCM mode. In order to verify the correctness of the analysis, a 200V~ 11 OOV two winding series flyback converter was designed, and the experimental results proved the correctness of the analysis and design.

articleTitle: Intelligent Power Trading Optimization Control System Based on Cloud-Cluster-Client Collaborative Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Smart home appliances have entered thousands of households. With smart home appliances controlled through apps, home energy management systems develop rapidly. However, large-scale appliances will pose a calculation burden. This article designs and develops an intelligent power consumption optimization control system based on cloud-cluster-client collaborative architecture. The system includes a cloud control platform, smart home cluster, and web application server, which can achieve communication management. When analyzing the real-time electricity prices, the management strategy can generate and issue regulation instructions to optimize the electricity consumption for smart homes. Meanwhile, the system enables consumers to have the lowest electricity bills while meeting various constraints. Finally, user energy-saving behavior can be promoted to realize the charging requirements. Numerical tests are conducted on air conditioners and EV s through software, which shows that the architecture can learn high system economics, using convenience and computational efficiency.

articleTitle: Transmission Process and Treatment Measures for Voltage Sags in Airport Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Governing voltage sag is of great significance in ensuring the normal operation of airport equipment and reducing economic losses. Based on historical data of airport operations, this paper classifies common electrical equipment according to their sensitivity and simulates the voltage sag at the airport and the output characteristics of typical high-sensitive equipment under different voltage sag conditions. The research shows that the inductance in the filter circuit for rectifier side directly affects the sensitivity of power electronics devices. Increasing the inductance can prolong the duration of current, which is beneficial for the capacitor to maintain voltage during voltage sag, making the DC voltage more stable. Based on this, a scheme of increasing the DC side filter inductance to manage voltage sag is proposed. Compared with measures such as UPS, DVR, and energy storage configuration, the scheme of increasing inductance has a good cost performance and is more advantageous for governing single-phase voltage sags that occur most frequently in the airport power system.

articleTitle: Optimised Scheduling Strategy for Source-Load-Storage Cooperation Considering Economic Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This research tackles the challenge of effectively managing the variable output of solar energy in electricity generation through the development of an optimized model for a Virtual Power Plant (VPP) integrating multiple microgrids (MMGs). The proposed approach introduces a real-time optimization method, incorporating provisions for designating a portion of the microgrid as a backup. The optimization model comprises two key phases: day-ahead planning and real-time adjustments. During the day-ahead planning phase, the objective is to optimize the VPP's profitability by determining optimal baseline and regulation capacity values for each hour of the subsequent day. Real-time adjustments aim to synchronize the VPP's electricity consumption with the dynamic regulation signal (RegD signal) at minimal cost. This real-time optimization process identifies the most efficient operational configurations for each microgrid and VPP resource. Simulation results validate the efficacy of this real-time optimization approach, showcasing its ability to enhance VPP revenue while upholding its crucial role in supporting grid frequency stability.

articleTitle: A Paralleled Harmonic Suppression Path for VSG Current Control Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology is able to provide inertial support to the grid, but at the same time becomes the emerging source of harmonic currents. To address this problem, this paper proposes a harmonic current suppression method for VSG with parallel compensation of the current loop output. The parallel compensation branch is implemented using the harmonic phase compensation control branch proposed in this paper, which effectively improves the harmonic current suppression capability of the virtual synchronous generator. This method not only overcomes the problem of reduced suppression due to small line impedance, but also has a simpler structure and better harmonic current suppression than the existing methods. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed improvement is verified by MATLAB simulations.

articleTitle: Position and Speed Observer for IPMSM with Hall Effect Sensors based on Extended EMF
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) is widely used in industrial fields such as AC speed regulation and servo drive due to its advantages of small size, high power density, and easy maintenance. Accurate rotor position and speed information play a crucial role in vector control. Compared with sensorless control and high-precision encoder control of PMSM, the Hall sensor is a guarantee of low cost and control performance. However, low-resolution Hall sensors reduce the accuracy of position and speed estimation in vector control systems. Therefore, this paper proposes a rotor position and speed estimation method of IPMSM with Hall sensors based on an extended electromotive force (EMF). The proposed method has high dynamic performance. Simulation results verify the effectiveness of the proposed scheme.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural Network-Based Model Predictive Control for Speed Regulation in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motors with an Extended Sliding Mode Load Torque Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the pursuit of enhancing control efficiency in Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor (PMSM) servo systems, this paper integrates a Model Predictive Control Speed Control (MPSC) approach into the speed loop control architecture. The predominant challenge in conventional MPC is its extensive computational demand, which also becomes significantly susceptible to load disturbances. To mitigate this, the paper introduces a discrete recurrent neural network (RNN) specifically aimed at reducing the computational burden associated with MPC. Additionally, an extended sliding mode load torque observer (ESMLTO) is developed for the PMSM drive system, focusing on mitigating load torque effects and bolstering overall system robustness. The viability and performance enhancement brought about by these proposed strategies are substantiated through a series of simulations and experimental validations.

Author Keywords: Extended Sliding Mode Load Torque Observer (ESMLTO)

articleTitle: Optimization-Based Parameter Determination for IGBT Models in Network Simulations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel methodology for determining the model parameters of semiconductor power devices. This method utilizes optimization techniques based on empirical data from actual double-pulse tests, implemented within simulation software to accurately derive model parameters. This approach enables precise replication of the device's switching behavior. Initially, the simulation model for the power semiconductor device and the double-pulse test circuit is constructed using PySpice in a simulation environment. Following this, actual double-pulse tests are conducted to gather extensive waveform data. Finally, these actual switching waveform data serve as the basis for optimizing the model parameters, with the unknown parameters in the model being optimized through iterative methods. This technique not only enhances the accuracy of the device's switching waveforms but also circumvents the need for additional equipment such as curve tracers and high-precision source meters.

articleTitle: Enhanced Control of Active Half-Bridge Type Four-Wire Vienna Rectifier under Unbalanced Grid Voltage Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In order to enhance the Vienna rectifier's performance during three-phase unbalanced voltage conditions and mitigate the deviation of the capacitor midpoint voltage, a novel active half-bridge four-wire Vienna rectifier topology is proposed. This paper first introduces 3-D unbalance coordinate transformation to establish a control strategy for the active half-bridge four-wire Vienna rectifier based on PI control method, aiming at managing the zero-sequence voltage under unbalanced grid voltage conditions. Through the detection of second harmonic component of the output voltage, a control law is formulated to regulate the input current amplitudes, thereby eliminating the second harmonic ripple. Additionally, Multiple Proportional-Resonant (MPR) control is applied to regulate the capacitor midpoint voltage. Simulation results under unbalanced grid voltage conditions confirm the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy in eliminating three-phase current distortion, suppressing the deviation of capacitor midpoint voltage, and obtaining minimal rectifier output voltage ripple.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation Analysis of Power Supply System for Deep Space Exploration Electric Propulsion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: At present, the power supply system of applied electric propulsion deep space exploration mission is faced with the problem of wide power range and voltage range adaptation, it is difficult to combine the characteristics of electric propulsion and power system to carry out joint research. On the basis of the analysis of the power system architecture of electric propulsion deep space probes, the reference and significance of the design of the power sub-system of electric propulsion deep space probes is discussed in this paper. In view of the characteristics of light weight, multi-thruster backup and high degree of autonomy for subsequent deep space exploration missions, the topological architecture of the power supply system suitable for deep space exploration missions is designed to solve the maximum power dynamic tracking problem of wide power (0-10kW) and voltage range (80-120V). The power supply system model is established by Saber, and three typical working models of deep space exploration are simulated and analyzed. The results show that the topology architecture is feasible. This study can be used as the basis for further research on wide voltage and wide power range power supply system.

articleTitle: Analysis of Magnetization Process of Nanocrystalline Alloy under High-Frequency Trapezoidal Wave Excitation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The investigation of the influence of non-sinusoidal excitation on the magnetization saturation process of nanocrystalline alloys is crucial for the operation of high-frequency transformers under complex working conditions. On the basis of G. Herzer's random anisotropy theory, this paper establishes a three-dimensional model of nanocrystalline alloy and uses the angular velocity of magnetic moment deflection as a parameter to describe the magnetization saturation process. The effects of non-sinusoidal trapezoidal wave excitation magnetic fields with different frequencies and amplitudes on the magnetization saturation process of the material were investigated through micromagnetism simulation. The results indicate that increasing the frequency or amplitude of the trapezoidal wave excitation accelerates the magnetic moment deflection and angular velocity. The angular velocity of magnetic moment deflection is more significantly affected by changes in frequency among them.

articleTitle: Optimization Design of Electromagnetic Vibration of Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor Considering Force Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, the fundamental reason for the influence of stator slot opening width on the amplitude of the equivalent concentrated force (ECF) on the stator teeth is discussed. And the structure parameters of motor are optimized to achieve low electromagnetic vibration by considering the force modulation effect. Firstly, a quantitative analysis is conducted on the higher-order and lower-order electromagnetic force amplitudes with different slot opening widths for a 12slot-l0pole permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM). The results show that the increasing opening width leads to an increase in both the higher-order and lower-order electromagnetic force amplitudes. Due to the opposite phase, there is a maximum value of the ECF amplitude on the stator teeth. In addition, structure parameters are optimized to reduce the higher-order electromagnetic force amplitude and increase the lower-order electromagnetic force amplitude, resulting in a decrease in the vibration acceleration amplitude at 2fe. Finally, the modal analysis experiment and vibration acceleration test are conducted on the original prototype. The simulation results have a good agreement with the experiment results, demonstrating the accuracy of the simulation model and the effectiveness of the calculation method.

articleTitle: Methodology for Quantifying Building Demand Response Potential for Market Access Judgments
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Market access judgment is a critical component of demand response (DR), employed for the early selection of target users and the reliability review of declared information. This necessitates the grid's ability to rapidly quantify the demand response potential (DRP) of different building. However, traditional approaches often develop potential quantification models tailored to individual objects, making it challenging to meet the potential quantification requirements of a large number of diverse buildings. To enhance model applicability, this paper proposes a data-driven method for quantifying the buildings DRP. Firstly, the input and output variables of the model are determined. Subsequently, a toolchain consisting of EnergyPlus, JEPlus, and Eppy is employed to construct a training dataset, and a backpropagation neural network (BPNN) model is trained based on this dataset to obtain a DRP quantification model applicable to a specific class of buildings. The effectiveness of the method is validated using a typical office building in Nanjing, with global temperature adjustment selected as the peak-shaving measure. According to the computational results, the developed potential quantification model achieves an MSE of 0.0096 and an R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>value of 0.9, demonstrating a good fitting performance. The proposed method considers the influence of different building scales, disturbance levels, meteorological conditions, and response periods on the building DRP.

articleTitle: Power Control Method for Composite Energy Storage Systems Utilizing Wavelet Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Due to the stochastic, intermittent, and fluctuating nature of wind speed variations, power fluctuations occur in wind power generation systems. Energy storage technology plays a crucial complementary role in renewable energy generation by mitigating these fluctuations. This paper focuses on the study of short-term output power fluctuations in the system. Firstly, based on the principles of a first-order low-pass filtering algorithm, the paper calculates, analyzes, and discusses the smoothing effects of different cutoff frequencies on wind power, while meeting the goal of smoothing power fluctuations in wind power generation systems. The cutoff frequency of the first-order low-pass filtering algorithm is determined to be 0.3. Secondly, through comparative analysis of reconstruction errors, the paper determines that the wavelet decomposition level used is 6. Based on the power characteristics of energy storage components, signals of different fluctuation frequencies are allocated to lithium iron phosphate batteries and supercapacitors for smoothing via control of power electronic devices. Thirdly, the paper optimizes the power allocation method for compound energy storage systems, considering the state of charge, and employs a fuzzy PI control method to control the charging and discharging of the energy storage system. Compared to traditional PI control methods, the working state of the energy storage devices is more stable, with a decrease of 1.87% in SOC fluctuation for lithium iron phosphate batteries and a decrease of 0.64 % for supercapacitors. This protects the use of energy storage equipment, and simulation validates the feasibility of this method.

articleTitle: Transient Stability Analysis of Virtual Synchronous Machine Considering the Damping Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Virtual synchronous machines (VSM) have become a promising solution for grid integration of renewable energy and energy storage systems. To replace the conventional synchronous machines with power-electronics-based VSMs, transient stability under large disturbances must be guaranteed. This paper reveals that the well-known equal area criterion (EAC) may lead to over-conservative prediction. On this basis, the phase portrait analysis is adopted to evaluate the VSM transient stability considering the damping effect. Hardware-in-loop (HIL) results are presented to verify the theoretical findings.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Parasitic Capacitance of MOSFET and Deadtime in High-Frequency ZVS Class-D Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper mainly analyzes the influence of the variation in the parasitic output capacitance (Coss) of MOSFET on the soft switching range of high-power and high-frequency full-bridge Class-D converters. Adjusting the input voltage is one of the important methods to regulate the output power of full-bridge Class-D converters. However, when the input voltage varies, the Coss of the MOSFET also changes. If the dead time cannot be adjusted instantly and properly, the converter risks losing zero-voltage switching (ZVS). This study examines the association between the load, switching frequency, and Coss, which affect the ZVS range of the converter. A theoretical calculation method for the dead time that ensures ZVS has been deduced and a 5kW/4MHz full-bridge Class-D converter prototype has been developed. Experimental results have verified the correctness of the estimated ZVS range.

articleTitle: Consequent-pole Flux Reversal Machine With Asymmetric Pole Towards High Torque Density and Low Torque Ripple
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Conventional flux reversal machine (FRM) suffers from significant pole flux leakage due to the direct mounting of permanent magnets (PM) under the stator teeth. In this paper, a novel consequent-pole FRM (AV-CPFRM) with asymmetric V-shaped PMs is proposed. The average torque of the proposed AV-CPFRM is enhanced by the flux focusing effect, and the torque ripple is reduced by adopting asymmetric structure. Then, the effect of asymmetric V-shaped magnets on the torque performance of the AV-CPFRM is investigated. Finally, the electromagnetic performance of the AV-CPFRM is compared with the conventional CP-FRM and consequent-pole FRM (V-CPFRM) with V-shaped PMs by the finite element analysis. The results indicate that the AV-CPFRM reduces torque ripple by 86.6% compared to the conventional CP-FRM while improving average torque by 11%.

articleTitle: Control Strategy of Voltage-Controlled Doubly-Fed Induction Generator Based on Model Predictive Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The conventional current-controlled doubly-fed induction generator utilizes phase-locked loop synchronization, depending on grid-connected point information. It exhibits characteristics of low inertia and damping, making it unsuitable for highly penetrated grid systems. The voltage-controlled doubly-fed induction generator (VC-DFIG), self-synchronized with the grid, offers voltage and frequency support, particularly suitable for weak grid operation. To enhance VC-DFIG's dynamic performance, this study proposes a model predictive control strategy. Modeling DFIG on a two-phase stationary coordinate system, employing virtual synchronous control, the structure integrates stator voltage outer loop and rotor current predictive control to establish rotor current prediction equations. Model predictive control replaces the traditional PI-controlled rotor current loop, improving system dynamic response and robustness while avoiding complex coordinate transformations and PI parameter rectifications. Theoretical analysis and an 11KW DFIG simulation platform validate the control strategy's effectiveness.

articleTitle: Discussion on Influencing Factors of Maximum Operating Temperature of Environment-Friendly Polypropylene Insulated Medium Voltage Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: When the environment-friendly polypropylene material is used in power cable insulation, there is no need for cross-linking and degassing during the production. Because of its simple process, low energy consumption and excellent mechanical & electrical properties, it has attracted widespread attention both in academia and industry. Compared with traditional XLPE insulated power cables, polypropylene insulated power cables have a higher melting point, so whether they can be applied to higher conductor temperatures than 90°C has become a key issue in cable design and development. In this paper, the deformation resistance, insulation oxidation resistance and accessory matching performance of polypropylene cable material are the main research directions, and the challenge of polypropylene insulated medium voltage cable at higher operating temperature (above 105°C) is analyzed. The results show that polypropylene insulated cable is prone to structural deformation, accelerated aging of materials and fitting of accessories when running at higher temperatures. The design and operation method of cable structure with low redundancy is proposed, which can provide a basis for the engineering application of polypropylene insulated cable.

articleTitle: Blockchain Green Electricity Accounting Method for Full-Caliber Green Electricity Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In the context of the low-carbon transformation of the power system, the green power trading market will be an important part of the national unified power market. With the participation of all kinds of trading subjects and the diversified green power demand on the user side, the current green power accounting method in green power trading needs further in-depth research in terms of improving flexibility and certification credibility, and it is urgent to extend the green power accounting method to meet the full-caliber green power trading demand and credible traceability certification method. To this end, the paper proposes a green power accounting method for green power transactions based on blockchain technology. By combining the ideas of “certificate and power unification” and “certificate and power separation”, a refined green power accounting method for green power transactions is designed to meet the demand for green power accounting in full-caliber green power transactions; meanwhile, from the perspective of blockchain technology, the green power accounting business involves the subject, type, smart contract and on-chain process. At the same time, from the perspective of blockchain technology, it designs the main body involved in green power accounting business, smart contract and on-chain process, eliminates the trust problem of transaction main body and realizes the automatic execution of green power accounting and credible traceability of green power environmental value.

articleTitle: Design of 200N Magnetic Levitation Single-Sided Voice Coil Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To address the smooth operation of cables in the high-precision lithography machine wafer stage, this paper introduces a specialized magnetic levitation single-sided voice coil motor designed to generate a continuous 200N lifting force in the vertical direction. Structural optimization of the motor's Halbach permanent magnet array is performed using JMAG to obtain a motor capable of producing the maximum levitation force within specified dimensions. Based on this motor, two final design solutions are proposed, with a focus on reducing the winding volume and the volume of the permanent magnet, respectively. The performance of the motors under both schemes is compared, and the changes in levitation force with a tilted rotor angle for both scenarios are analyzed. Conclusions are drawn based on the findings.

articleTitle: Comparison of Electromagnetic Properties Between Hybrid Rotor and Spoke-Type Rotor of PM Machines
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents models of two types of permanent magnet (PM) mahines which called hybrid rotor mahcine and spoke-type rotor mahcine. These two types of mahcines have different significant advantages in output performance under different operating conditions. For revealing the influence of pole numbers and rotor sizes on the performance between the hybrid rotor and spoke-type rotor of PM machines, this paper reserch on the torque profile, air-gap magnetic density, back electromotive force (back-EMF) and eddy loss have been investigated, and the influence of reluctance torque on output was analyzed. The results indicate that the sinusoidal characterisitic of radial magenetic flux density and back-EMF of hybrid rotor machine is better and the loss is less under the large pole numbers and small size operation condition. The comparison results also show that the hybrid rotor PM machine has higher torque density and lower ripple under small rotor size and less pole nmubers operation condition, which is caused by the flux-focusing effect of surface mounted PM. However, in the case of large rotor sizes, hybrid rotor PM machine do not have advantage in average torque, but ripple is still relatively low.

articleTitle: An Ultra-Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting Model Based on Meteorological Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Wind energy as a renewable energy has been widely used. However, wind power is affected by meteorological and other factors with strong randomness and volatility. It is of great significance to study how to improve the accuracy of wind power forecasting to promote wind power grid integration and power system dispatch. This paper takes wind power forecasting as the research objective and proposes a historical observation window size selection method, a meteorological feature selection method, and an ultra-short-term wind power forecasting model based on SVR-LSTM. Finally, the validity of the ultra-short-term wind power forecasting method is verified with the actual operation data of a particular wind farm. The experimental results show that the combined model has the highest prediction accuracy than the single prediction models.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis and Verification of Permanent Magnet Wind Generators Stator
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: With the rapid advancement of permanent magnet wind generators, the semi-direct drive high speed scheme has become the prevailing approach. With the increase of motor speed, it is prone to resonate with the stator structure, which affects the safe and stable operation of the motor, so it is necessary to carry out modal analysis of the motor in the design stage. The present study establishes a finite element model for the stator of an 8WM permanent magnet wind generator. Subsequently, modal analysis is conducted using the finite element analysis method to determine the natural frequency and vibration mode of the motor stator structure. Finally, a hammering modal test is performed to validate the accuracy of the finite element analysis. The results demonstrate that under rated working conditions, there exists a significant disparity in both frequency and mode between electromagnetic excitation and structural vibration in permanent magnet motors, thereby eliminating any possibility of resonance. Consequently, it can be concluded that the design of the motor's stator structure is rational.

articleTitle: A Zero-Input-Current-Ripple High Voltage Gain DC-DC Converter With Y-Source Coupled Inductor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In this paper, a zero-input-current-ripple (ZICR) DC-DC converter is proposed. The proposed converter benefits like significant voltage gain and enhanced efficiency. ZICR is achieved by adding a ZICR structure, which consists of a capacitor, an inductor, and a coupled inductor. The presence of the capacitor results in an average zero current passing through the ZICR structure. Therefore, a small size magnetic core can be used to design the inductor and coupled inductor, which can reduce the volume and copper loss of the magnetic components. In addition, merging a voltage multiplier with a Y-source coupled inductor to derive high boost capacity. The inherent passive clamping circuit effectively alleviates the turn off voltage spike of the switch. All diodes achieve zero current switching (ZCS) turn off by utilizing capacitors to absorb leakage energy. Then, the reverse recovery issues are mitigated. An in-depth elaboration is provided for the operating principle of the converter. Ultimately, a prototype with 200-W, 32–380 V, 50-kHz is developed to validate the realizability of the proposed converter. Within the output power range of 40-200W, the overall efficiency of the prototype with the ZICR structure is higher than that without this structure. The peak efficiency of the proposed converter, both in the presence and absence of the ZICR structure, stands at 95.9% and 95.6%, respectively.

articleTitle: Analytical Modeling and Calculation of High-Speed Surface Mounted PMSM Based on Subdomain Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper proposes a slotless analytical subdomain model of surface mounted PMSM based on Carter coefficient. This model is simplified from an open-slot motor and only needs to solve fourth-order linear equations under each harmonic order, which can avoid strong coupling of the entire coefficient matrix and high-order matrix inversion operation. This model can solve the partial differential equations of each subspace much easier, which can avoid the potential problems during complicated calculation, making it has better robustness. What's more, this model makes it convenient to quickly and accurately conduct a qualitative analysis on a series of surface mounted PMSM with different parameters. The comparison with finite element method shows that the subdomain method presented in this paper has low error and fast calculation speed.

Author Keywords: surface mounted permanent magnet synchronous motor

articleTitle: Bipolar Flyback Single-Stage PFC Converter Without Rectifier Bridge
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: An AC-DC Flyback converter which can be used not only for positive input voltage, but also for negative input voltage is proposed. It only needs to add an LCD (inductance, capacitance and diode) network on secondary side of transformer belongs to traditional Flyback converter, and capable of transforming the positive or negative input voltage into positive output one without adding a rectifier bridge. It can be easily applied to the AC-DC power factor correction circuit or the back-stage converter of the converter cascaded system. This paper investigates the operating modes and principles of the system when the input voltage is positive and negative, and designs the voltage feedback control strategy. The results indicate that, different from the traditional Flyback converter, the newly presented power stage could increase and decrease the input voltage, have the same output voltage waveform at the positive and negative input voltage, and has good dynamic characteristics under the modulation of closed-loop manipulation method. Experimental results prove the correctness of the topology proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Influence of Ambient Temperature on the Optical Fiber characteristics of Fiber Optic Current Transformer Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Fiber optic current transformer (FOCT) has become an important measuring equipment in Ultra-high voltage(UHV) converter station, because it has the advantages of large dynamic range, nonmagnetic saturation, digital and analog interface output. Previous studies mainly focused on the uniform temperature change of sensing optical fiber and optical fiber 1/4 wave plate, but under complex working conditions, the fiber optic current transformer is disturbed by the nonuniform temperature of the surrounding environment for a long time, and the characteristic analysis of sensing optical fiber at uniform temperature can not fully reflect the change of FOCT ratio error. Therefore, this paper uses the COMSOL finite element simulation software to model the part of the optical fiber leading from the lower side of the sensing fiber ring, and analyzes that the sensing optical fiber will produce nonuniform stress under the influence of nonuniform temperature, which will affect the FOCT measurement ratio error. When the current of the current-carrying conductor is 3000A, FOCT meets the error requirement of 0.2% in the environment temperature range of -80.0~7.9 °C, and the FOCT ratio error is not zero when the initial temperature is 25°C. That is to say, with the increase of wire current, the low temperature characteristic of FOCT ratio error will increase, while the high temperature characteristic will decrease.

articleTitle: A Medium Frequency DC-DC Converter with Auxiliary Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: DC/DC converter is the core equipment for distributed photovoltaic power generation to connect to the medium voltage DC grid. A low switching loss medium frequency DC/DC converter is proposed, which contains a main power circuit and an auxiliary control circuit and contains a total of one three-level bridge arm and two two-level bridge arms. The main power circuit transmits approximately 90% of the power, with the switching devices operating at frequency of 500 Hz. Auxiliary circuit transmits the remaining small part of the power, by means of high frequency chopping of part of the switches in the auxiliary circuit, the current waveform is approximated as a trapezoidal waveform, which reduces the peak value of the current, and the switching loss generated by the high frequency chopping is also small because the current flowing through the auxiliary circuit is small. The current flowing through the switching devices in the common bridge arm is the sum of the current of the two circuits, but it can realize ZCS, and therefore the loss of the whole converter is small. The paper describes the operation principle of the converter in detail, analyzes the parameter design method, discusses the influence of different parameters for converter in detail, and carries out the simulation verification by PLECS.

articleTitle: A Review Of Conical Rotor Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Conical rotor motors are magnetically more complicated than cylindrical ones. The conical shape enables adjustment of the air gap through the axial displacement of the rotor and also results in an axial component of the magnetic force on the rotor, which enables many unique functions for the conical rotor motor. This paper reviews the research trends and key technologies of conical rotor motors from aspects such as structural topology, model simplification, optimization design, and application.

articleTitle: Flux-Weakening Control of IPMSM Based on Complex Vector Decoupling
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The interior permanent magnet synchronous motor (IPMSM) is widely used in the drive system of new energy vehicles. Vector control is usually used to drive IPMSM, but there is a dynamic coupling problem of dq axis current. In order to solve the problem of serious current coupling when IPMSM is running at high speed under flux-weakening control, the complex vector model of the motor is established, and the complex vector decoupling strategy is proposed. In this paper, a 40kW power permanent magnet synchronous motor simulation platform is designed, and the complex vector decoupling strategy is theoretically analyzed to improve the current loop performance. On this basis, a variable load experiment is carried out to verify the correctness of the complex vector decoupling strategy. At the same time, combined with the phenomenon of inductance change in the actual motor, the decoupling performance of feedback decoupling and complex vector decoupling under the same working condition with different inductance is compared, which verifies the excellent parameter robustness of the complex vector decoupling strategy.

articleTitle: An Analytical Solution for Magnetic Field Distribution of Rectangular Magnets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper presents a three-dimensional analytical solution for the magnetic field distribution of permanent magnet mechanisms with rectangular magnets. The model is based on the magnetic vector potential theory for the permanent magnet via the equivalent current. Analytical expressions of the magnetic flux intensity for a single magnet and the total magnets are deduced. Green formula and Simpson method are applied to solve the analytical expressions. The results agree well with those calculated by the finite element method. The proposed analytical model can provide a reference for the design and optimization of permanent magnetic mechanisms with rectangular magnets.

articleTitle: Helmet Detection for Substation Personnel Based on LG-YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Helmet detection is important for power safety management in substations, but manually checking is low efficiency. Therefore, a lightweight real-time object detection model LG-YOLOv8 for helmet detection is proposed in this paper. Firstly, a lightweight cross-stage partial feature extraction structure LGBlock is proposed to replace the original C2f module, based on the Ghost module and Efficient Channel Attention mechanism. Secondly, The Bi-directional Feature Pyramid Network (BiFPN) is introduced to replace the original Path Aggregation Network (PANet) in the Neck, enhancing the network's ability to represent multi-scale features. Finally, we use SIoU to improve the bounding box regression loss function in the Head, improving model recognition accuracy and adaptability to complex scenes. Extensive experiments are conducted on the public SHWDv2 dataset to verify the performance. Compared to the benchmark model, the number of parameters, computational complexity, and model size of the proposed LG-YOLOv8 are respectively reduced by 50.2%, 35.8%, 48.6%. It can be better deployed on mobile terminals for substation safety monitoring.

articleTitle: Research on the Power Control of MMC-PET System Based on VSG and PBC
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Power Electronic Transformer (PET) is a new type of power electronic device with flexible topology access, which has a wide range of application prospects in AC and DC microgrids. For the control of the MMC-PET system, which is cascaded by a modular multilevel converter (MMC) and dual active bridge (DAB), the traditional PI control method lacks damping inertia, has poor dynamic performance, and is unable to modulate the frequency actively. This paper proposes a current and voltage control technique based on virtual synchronous generators (VSG) theory and passivity-based control (PBC) theory. Firstly, the basic topology and working principle of MMC-PET are introduced, and the mathematical models of MMC and DAB are analyzed. Secondly, the passivity of MMC is investigated, and the passive controller is combined with the VSG control with primary FM to optimize the MMC-PET control so that the MMC-PET system has the function of primary FM with better robustness. Finally, the MMC-PET system model is constructed in Matlab/Simulink. The simulation experiments of the above VSG and PBC control methods are carried out under the working conditions of frequency fluctuation and load change in the power grid. The results show the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed MMC-PET system model and control method.

articleTitle: Loss Calculation and Thermal Investigation of Motors for Aviation Electric Fuel Pumps Under All Working Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper calculates the losses of the wet-type asymmetric dual-three-phase PMSM used in aviation electric fuel pumps, and analyzes the heat generation of the motor. First, accurately calculate the losses of each part of the motor, including iron losses, eddy current losses, copper losses, viscous losses and other factors. The losses under the three working conditions are compared and analyzed, and the results show that the viscous loss is greatly affected by the speed. Then, the temperature rise of the motor under different working conditions is calculated based on the calculated losses. The results show that the temperature rise of the motor is within a reasonable range and meet industrial requirements.

articleTitle: Experimental Research on Reliability of AC/DC Weak Current Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Magneto-sensitive sensors are currently widely used in smart grids because of its wide bandwidth, high sensitivity, and small size properties. However, due to their susceptibility to environmental temperature, humidity, and magnetic field interference, long-term operation in complex environments may result in measurement failure. The range of weak currents in smart grids generally falls within the range of microamps to hundreds of milliamps. In this paper, a 0.3A current sensor was selected as the research object to study the effects of temperature, humidity, and magnetic field on its measurement performance. Accelerated aging tests were conducted under temperature, humidity, and magnetic field interference. Based on the experimental results and life prediction model, the reliability operating life of magneto-sensitive sensors under different working conditions was derived. This will provides reference data for subsequent sensor failure updates.

articleTitle: Adaptive VSG Grid-connected Control Strategy Based on Moment of Inertia and Damping Coefficient
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of determining the optimal values for rotational inertia <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> and damping coefficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$D$</tex> in traditional virtual synchronous generator (VSG) technology, which can lead to poor system dynamic performance. To enhance the transient stability of the system, this paper proposes a VSG control strategy based on adaptive parameters and a droop strategy. Firstly, the paper establishes a mathematical model of the VSG control scheme to analyse the relationship between the active dynamic response characteristics of the system and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$J$</tex> and D. Secondly, the paper combines the adaptive parameter optimisation algorithm with the droop control strategy to optimise the VSG control strategy. Finally, the paper conducts simulation experiments using MATLAB/Simulink to compare the control effects of fixed-parameter VSG control, adaptive VSG control, and the proposed control strategy. The experiments focus on power fluctuation suppression and frequency oscillation recovery in the case of active power perturbation. The results verify the feasibility of the proposed control strategy.

articleTitle: A Coupled Hydraulic Balance Operation Method for District Heating Networks to Improve Flexibility of Multi-Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The district heating networks (DHN), an important component of multi-energy systems. Its natural passive heat storage characteristics can provide flexibility for the power grid and promote the consumption of renewable energy connected to the grid. Currently, most of flexibility improving method using DHN's thermal storage haven't considered the hydraulic balance of the complex topology networks, and directly sets the flow rate of each pipe. This leading to that the flexibility improving method may not take effects in practical application since the hydraulic balance may not be satisfied. This paper proposed a pipe network coupled flow regulation method to improve the flexibility of district heating networks. A hydraulic balance model corresponding to the resistance coefficients of all pipelines of the pipe network is proposed, and the simulation accuracy of flow rate for main and branch road under different pressure drops is verified experimentally. The relationship between pipe resistance coefficient, pump work and flow distribution in the final topology pipe network when the flexibility of the district heating networks is enhanced by flow regulation is obtained. This method can realize hydraulic balance regulation when DHN flow regulation is used to provide flexibility for power system.

articleTitle: Current Diversion Monitoring Method Based on Temperature-Current Mapping for Multi-Break GCB
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Existing pumped storage power station generator outlet circuit breakers (GCB) mostly use SF6 circuit breakers, multi-break parallel design of vacuum circuit breakers is an effective way to solve the problem of insufficient rated current of vacuum interrupters. In this paper, a temperature-current mapping monitoring method for multi-break GCBs is proposed. Firstly, the electromagnetic-thermal multi-physical field coupling model of multi-break GCB based on the finite element method is established. The thermal field distribution law under the influence of different steady state currents, ambient temperature and other multi-factors is studied, and the temperature-current mapping model is constructed by using neural network. Take 24kV/16kA/125kA multi-break GCB as an example, monitor the temperature at the soft connection of GCB and the ambient temperature inside the equipment. Back-calculation of shunt current by temperature-current mapping model and comparison analysis with actual current magnitude. The neural network is then compensated and calibrated to achieve on-line monitoring of shunt currents in multi-break GCBs. The online monitoring method of temperature-current mapping is not only applicable to the current monitoring of multi-break GCBs, but can also provide a reference for the current monitoring of high-current devices.

articleTitle: Analysis of Nonisolation Characteristics and Effect of Electric Field Couplers in Dynamic CPT Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The nonisolated characteristic of capacitive couplers in capacitive power transfer (CPT) systems can lead to significant voltage discrepancies between the two sides. This paper analyzes the reverse current phenomena caused by the nonisolated characteristic in dynamic capacitive power transfer (DCPT) systems. A capacitive coupler model that considers the voltage between two transmitters (operating and standby) of the DCPT system is developed. In the DCPT system designed within this paper, the RMS voltage to ground for the two ports on the standby transmitters is calculated to be 1577.62V and 1557.68V, respectively. When the standby inverter is activated, the reverse-biased diode of the MOSFETs within the inverter is momentarily turned off at the initial moment, which is akin to a circuit break. According to the calculation results presented in this paper, the potential becomes larger than <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{dc}}$</tex> or drops below OV to turn the diode on, thereby switching on the diode of the standby inverter and generating reverse current. The model proposed in this paper elucidates the mechanism behind the reverse current generation in the standby inverter, and its accuracy is validated through simulation research.

articleTitle: Peak Shaving Strategy of Electric Vehicle in Industrial Park Considering Differentiated Subjective Willingness
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As a typical flexibility resource, electric vehicles (EVs) have considerable load storage capacity if scheduled properly. This paper established a two-level optimization model of EV for optimal load scheduling of industrial large users, in which the upper model searched the optimal price incentive strategy on which basis the lower model give the optimal scheduling strategy of EV. To portray the external characteristics of the EV aggregation, a virtual battery (VB) based EV power capacity model was established to conduct peak shaving for the industrial user. The subjective willingness of EV owners was a modification to the VB model. The subjective willingness was quantified through fuzzy evaluation and the value determined the EV response rate which affected the available power capacity of the VB. The optimal price incentive coefficient was sought by particle swarm optimization (PSO) to reach the balance between the subjective satisfaction of the EV owner and the revenue of the industrial user, then the charging/discharging strategy of the EV was optimized through the modified VB model and the total revenue of industrial user was calculated considering the profits of peak load shaving the costs of price incentive. We validated the model with real-world load data, proving that the EV optimal scheduling model is practical and profitable, and that an optimal price incentive strategy can increase the total revenue of industry users.

articleTitle: A High-Gain Interleaved Active-Clamped Bidirectional Flyback Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In recent years, the world has been increasingly concerned about energy scarcity and environmental pollution. This has led to a greater emphasis on developing renewable energy sources. To address the challenges of renewable energy variability, an effective solution is to use energy storage systems. To establish a seamless connection between the energy storage system and the grid, the incorporation of a bidirectional DC-DC converter is imperative. Flyback converters emerge as the preferred choice owing to their uncomplicated circuit structure, electrical isolation, compact dimensions, cost-effectiveness, and straightforward installation procedures. The interleaved parallel Flyback converter plays a pivotal role in minimizing current ripple and mitigating voltage and current stresses, concurrently enhancing power density and rating. Nevertheless, the presence of leakage inductance in the transformer results in voltage spikes generated by the Flyback converter. This paper introduces a novel high-gain interleaved active-clamped bidirectional Flyback converter, and meticulously analyzes its operating principles. The study elucidates the parameter design process and conducts simulations based on the designated parameters. The simulation results align with the theoretical analysis, affirming the feasibility of the proposed converter.

articleTitle: Simplified SVM Strategy for Suppressing Common Mode Voltages for Modular Multilevel Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: To solve the problem of traditional Space Vector Modulation (SVM) strategy's difficulty in extending to high-level Modular Multilevel Converter (MMC), and to suppress the common-mode voltage generated during the implementation of MMC modulation strategy, this paper proposes a simplified Space Vector Modulation (SVM) strategy based on mutated coordinate system, the boundary switching state is derived by judging the area where the space vector is located, and then the correction parameter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$K$</tex> is introduced to correct the boundary switching state, so as to improve the speed of the strategy and complete the common mode voltage suppression. Simulation results show that the strategy is simple to implement and can suppress the MMC common-mode voltage within the minimum variation range.

articleTitle: LightGBM Based Fault Diagnosis of the Canned Motor Pump Based with Stray Flux
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The static closed structure and complex working conditions of the canned motor pump severely limit the traditional motor fault detection method. In order to detect the status of the canned motor pump, and the stray flux condition monitoring as a non-invasive detection method reflects the operating status of the motor, it is suitable for canned motor pumps. This paper proposes a fault diagnosis method based on stray flux with LightGBM algorithm. Firstly, the topology and working principle of the motor are introduced, and the corresponding mapping relationship between stray flux and air gap flux is verified. Then, the distribution law of stray flux under different faults is obtained based on the finite element model. Then, it is proposed to rely on the frequency energy distribution decomposed by wavelet packet energy as the eigenvalues and use the LightGBM algorithm to train the data for fault diagnosis. Finally, an experimental testbench was built for different fault experiments and feature extraction and training were conducted, which proved the correctness of the diagnostic method.

articleTitle: Comparison of PLL and without PLL control for grid-connected VSCs under large disturbances
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Grid-connected voltage source converters (VSCs) typically utilize phase-locked loops (PLL) for synchronization. However, this approach may lead to transient synchronization instability under weak grid conditions, especially during significant disturbances such as large power steps or asymmetric faults, etc. The transient synchronization instability issues resulting from PLL and weak grid interactions can be avoided by using a natural abc frame without PLL control structure. In this paper, the transient characteristics of VSC with and without PLL control strategies are compared by considering two common large disturbance scenarios: 1) large power step and 2) asymmetric faults. The PSCAD/EMTDC time-domain simulation results are also provided.

articleTitle: A Sensorless Control Method for LCI-fed Electrically Excited Synchronous Motors Based on Improved Sliding Mode Observer
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Load Commutated Inverter (LCI)-fed electrically excited synchronous motor, utilizes thyristor as switching device, so it is extensively used in the field of high-power transmission. An improved sliding mode observer is proposed in this paper, and whose stability is analyzed by Lyapunov function. A sigmoid function with a boundary layer is used to substitute the signum function which can reduce the chattering problem caused by the conventional sliding mode observer. Also, introduce a simple sliding mode adaptive gain related to the motor speed in order to reduce the influence of motor speed change on rotor position estimation accuracy. Finally, an improved phase-locked loop is used to extract rotor position information. The system model is established by MATLAB/Simulink, and the simulation results validate both effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed high-speed rotor position detection method.

articleTitle: Thermal Analysis and Optimization of Homopolar Inductor Machine for Flywheel Pulsed Power Supply Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: As a key component of flywheel pulsed power supply system to realize energy conversion, homopolar inductor machine (HIM) is considered as a strong competitor among all the electrical machines due to its merits of simple structure, robust rotor and rotor flywheel integration. However, in order to further improve the power density of the machine, it is required to work under high speed and high electromagnetic load., which will cause high loss density., high temperature rise., and bring the risk of fatal error. Addressing the issue., the several thermal optimization methods are applied and examined. First., the topology and operation principle of the HIM is explained. Then the finite element (FE) model and heat source model is obtained., and performance and loss distribution is calculated. Finally., a rotor pole slotting method and a novel cooling channel is proposed., and the temperature rise inside the HIM is examined using FE thermal analysis. The results show that the temperature of HIM can be effectively suppressed by the proposed method and cooling channel in this work.

articleTitle: Research on Inter-Turn Short Circuit Fault Diagnosis Method of Switched Reluctance Motor for Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Addressing the challenges of a complex operating environment, slow recognition response times, and the high cost associated with inter-turn short circuit faults (ISCF) in switched reluctance motors (SRM), this article introduces a novel fault diagnosis method based on the interacting multiple model (IMM) algorithm. Equivalent circuit models corresponding to different operating states of ISCF in each phase of the SRM were developed. The Kalman filter was employed to estimate the model's state, with the residual signal utilized for fault localization and detection. Simulation and experimental results demonstrate that the proposed fault diagnosis method significantly mitigates the impact of intricate scenarios, enhances the anti-interference capability in diagnosing SRM stator winding ISCF, and enables precise and rapid identification of fault information.

articleTitle: Analysis of MMF of the PMSM with the Same Number of Poles and Slots Considering Different Number of Winding Turns
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The abundant winding magnetomotive force (MMF) harmonics generated by the fractional slot concentrated windings (FSCWs) in permanent magnet synchronous machines (PMSMs) affect rotor losses, vibration, and noise of the machine. Because the size and spatial position of the slots of the PMSM with the same number of poles and slots are different from the conventional PMSMs, the distribution of the winding MMF harmonics is more complicated. This paper proposes a model for calculating the MMF harmonic distribution based on the vector method, while considering the different topologies and the different number of windings turns in different slot sizes. The validity of the proposed model is verified by the Fourier decomposition of the MMF distribution. Based on the proposed model, the characteristics of the winding MMF harmonics of the PMSM with the same number of poles and slots with different topologies are analyzed.

Author Keywords: The PMSM with the same number of poles and slots

articleTitle: Active Disturbance Rejection Control of a Counter-rotating Permanent Magnet Synchronous Motor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: Counter-rotating permanent magnet synchronous motors (CRPMSM) have the advantages of high efficiency and high torque density to drive the co-axial counter-rotating propeller for vessels. In this paper., the active disturbance rejection control (ADRC) method for CRPMSMs is studied. The mathematical models of the CRPMSM., speed loop and current loop controller based on the active disturbance rejection technology are established. In order to alleviate the speed fluctuation of CRPMSM due to unsmooth fal function in NLSEF, the linear proportional gain is used to substitute the fal function. The simulation results show that the ADRC system of CRPMSM has the advantages of fast response and strong anti-interference ability under the load variation condition and speed abrupt change of two rotors of CRPMSM.

articleTitle: Composite Control of Single-Phase Grid Connected Voltage Source Inverter using a Novel Phase-Locked Loop
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: The core component of the new energy grid connection are inverters, and their performance will directly affect the stability and robustness of the power grid. When using traditional control methods for inverters, low-frequency oscillations often occur due to the mutual influence between the inverter and the grid impedance, which can cause distortion of the grid connected current. At the same time, traditional inverters have shortcomings in tracking and locking the voltage rate and phase transformation of the power grid, and may even cause phase locking errors due to the limited degrees of freedom of the phase-locked loop itself. By adopting a composite control strategy of mixed damping and voltage improved feedforward compensation, the stability of the grid connected system is improved and the distortion rate of the grid connected current is reduced, meeting the harmonic standards for grid connection during the period; Adopting an improved anti Park transform phase-locked loop to eliminate oscillation components and solve problems such as computation delay. Finally, the effectiveness of the above control strategy was verified through MATLAB simulation.

articleTitle: Full-Bridge LLC Resonant Converter with Super-Twisting Non-Singular Fast Terminal Sliding Mode Control
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE 7th International Electrical and Energy Conference (CIEEC)
abstract: In response to the problem of large dynamic overshoot in the traditional proportional-integral (PI) control of full-bridge LLC resonant converters, a novel control strategy based on the super-twisting non-singular fast terminal sliding mode (STNFTSM) is proposed. Firstly, this paper describes the basic principles of LLC resonant converters. Then, an improved super-twisting algorithm is proposed, and the STNFTSM controller is designed based on it.
